**Goal.** A mathematical argument, from facts known for sure, for how to derive an optimal smaller network from a
larger trained one. The first example is the curve family of InceptionV1 layer 3b. The theory is stated for any
family, any group and any layer where possible.

**How to read.** Part A holds the starting points in three tiers: FACTS (true of every network of the kind
defined, with a proof here or a cited source), DEFINITIONS (interpretability objects made into mathematical objects)
and HYPOTHESES (named premises we believe but have not proved). Part B holds theorems. Each theorem names the
hypotheses its proof uses. A theorem tagged "(under: none)" holds for every network of the kind defined. Part C is
the only place for numbers: how far InceptionV1 is from each hypothesis. Part D is where the math leads. The Appendix
holds the triage of the old papers (`PAPER.md`, `NEURON-MATH.md`), which are the record of this work and are not cited
as proof.

# Part 0: the fixed target

**Trunk T5** (confirmed by Shonu on 2026-10-28; exact text in `DECISIONS.md` section 1; it replaces T4, described
next as a record). As T4, with one more input: a map M of N on P, a finite list of typed claims about N and P (Part
A.7), each with an error that anyone can compute from N and P in polynomial time. The developer's groups are unions of
the map's districts. How the map is found is outside the trunk. The exactness promise applies only when M is complete
for the zoom (Definition DM6, Shonu's decision on card 3-19): then, with every error 0, the rule is an exact closed form.
With some error positive, the rule has a bound in the list of errors. Part B.M starts the work: a map splits a grouping
into its regions (Theorem TM1). The first form of T5, without completeness, conflicted with T43 under the
polynomial-time reading of "closed form" (Theorem TM3: the map "one district, every image" has error 0). With complete
maps and the two-sided blend claim, T43's big groups have no complete error-0 map, and groups without a bad pair are
folded by a formula (Theorem TM5, Corollary TM5.1). Scope today: groups in the last hidden layer, two logits for groups
coarsened below their size; elsewhere no map is complete yet.

**Trunk T4** (confirmed by Shonu on 2026-10-27, replaced by T5 on 2026-10-28; exact text in `DECISIONS.md` section 1; it replaces T\*\*\*,
described next as a record). Given a network N, base inputs P and a zoom chosen by the developer (nested groupings
G_0, ..., G_m: each group is a set of N's units in one layer with a target size; units in no group are kept), a rule
that reads N, P and the zoom and does not train returns, for each level, the network with the least D_P in which each
group is replaced by its number of new units, each reading only that group's units. Switching levels is instant after
a one-time computation. The rule is an exact closed form at eps(N) = 0 and has a bound in eps(N) otherwise. Part B.W
defines the classes of builds and starts the work on T4. The least build over any new units (the object of T\*\*\*)
becomes the reference class (a) of Definition D50, and Hypothesis H-group says that the two agree for clean
networks.

**Trunk T\*\*\*** (confirmed by Shonu on 2026-10-25, replaced by T4 on 2026-10-27; exact text in `DECISIONS.md` section 1). Given a network N, a mix
P (the generalist mix or a developer's mix) and sizes (k_1, ..., k_L), one per hidden layer, a rule that reads N and P
and does not train returns a network of the same kind as N, with k_l units in layer l, built from any new units, with
the least distillation loss D_P. After a one-time computation per mix (the zoom), switching to another size list is
instant (its cost does not grow with N). When N is perfectly clean (cleanliness distance eps(N) = 0) the rule is an
exact closed form; when eps(N) > 0 it comes with a proved bound that depends only on eps(N) and is 0 at eps = 0. Two
earlier versions are kept in `DECISIONS.md` as a record: the draft T\* (Part B.T was written against it) and T\*\*
(no input data; Part B.C was written against it, and its Theorem T24 is why the mix came back). Part B.Z defines the
zoom and starts the work on T\*\*\*.
The question behind T\*\*\* (Shonu, 2026-10-25): distillation trained to the end converges to the least-KL small
network on the mix; what is that network, and is it a fold of the network's own units when the network is clean?
Part B.F states this as Conjecture D25.

Distances in `DECISIONS.md` are counted from the old trunk T\*; the nodes above the current trunk T\*\*\* (R-least, R-nest, R-root
and R-score, decided; R-goal, dropped; R-cleannet and R-fold, pending) are listed there. Every result of Parts B and D is about a smaller
or simpler question than T\*. `DECISIONS.md` names each step away
from T\* as a node (a restriction), says who chose it, and gives every result its path of nodes. Read every tag
"(under: ...)" together with that path. A tag "(under: none)" means "no hypothesis beyond the class and objective of
its Part", and the path says what that class and objective are. The Facts of Part A hold for every network. Among
the results of Parts B and D before Part B.T, only Proposition T1' has an empty path, and it is about units that read

Theorem T12 is one step away: a floor on the squared logit objective D2 (in place of D_P), not shown to be reached by

**The lens of each section (2026-10-26).** Shonu: "Folds and other interpretability stuff ... They're really just my

Part A.5 and Part B.K (2026-10-26) start the work on the right definition of clean. A.5 states it as a list of
principles motivated by the essay; two of them have graded entries in eps(N) so far. B.K proves (Theorem T43) that
one family of networks that satisfy these principles (all of them at one hidden layer; all but the gate principle
Q4 at more layers), with mixes symmetric under the networks' own symmetry, keeps the hardness of T22. For these
networks the hard instance is carried by the mix alone: the network depends only on its size, not on the instance.
Revision 2 of A.5 (2026-10-26, later) replaces D39 by D42, because D39 made clean networks rare (Theorem T44: exact
symmetry holds only on a null set) while the essay says trained networks are clean. Under D42 the perfectly clean
networks contain a non-empty open set (Theorem T45), and the detector networks at one hidden layer are still perfectly clean, so T43
still refutes the hardness conjecture for clean networks (Remark A.5.3).
Revision 3 (2026-10-26, evening, A.6): Shonu: "when we say clean, we really mean interpretable", and "the first principle
is actually exploration". After exploring InceptionV1 the way the essay does, A.6 defines a clean network as one
whose units are READ (their readers turn on with them) and have ONE JOB (every route by which a unit is built feeds
the same readers). B.R proves its basic properties. The read part has two forms: in the weak form T43's hardness still stands
(comment (g) of D45); in the agreement form T43's networks are outside the class (Proposition T50), and whether the
hardness holds there is Conjecture D47. In the agreement form of D45 it does not apply (Proposition T50).

Part B.T works at T\* itself, under the readings stated at its start (in particular: "trained network" means any
network of the kind, and "image mix" means any finite list of points). Three of its results are proved conflicts
under those readings. Theorem T23:
for some networks (three logits) no build of width 2 reaches the infimum of D_P, so "the least" does not exist.
Theorem T20: for some networks the least builds of widths 1 and 2 do not nest, so "least at every k" and "the B_k
nest" cannot both hold for every network. Theorem T22: no algorithm returns a least build (even within a small stated
eps) in polynomial time for every network and every mix, unless P = NP. On the positive side, for two logits, one
hidden layer and a finite mix, a least build exists (Theorem T19). For the objective D2 an exact finite rule finds it,
at a cost that grows like n^{d k}, and for D_P the problem splits into finitely many convex pieces (Theorem T21). The choices these theorems force are in `DECISIONS.md` section 3. Theorem T14 (linear chains,
objective D2) is a separate and narrower hardness result.

# Part A: starting points

## A.0 Setting

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| x | an input (an image), drawn from an input law P on the input space X |
| L | the layer that holds the family (for the first example: 3b) |
| A(x) | the input field that the family's units read: C channels over a grid of positions p (for the curve family: the output of 3b's 5 x 5 bottleneck) |
| z_i(x, p) | pre-activation of unit i of layer L at position p: z_i(x, p) = <K_i, A(x)[p + Omega]> + b_i, with kernel K_i on the window Omega and bias b_i |
| h_i(x, p) | output of unit i: h_i = relu(z_i), relu(t) = max(t, 0) |
| M_b | the fixed pooling map in front of reader branch b (for 3b: a 3 x 3 max-pool with stride 2, and for one branch a second 3 x 3 max-pool after it) |
| u_b(x) | the input of reader branch b at pooled position p: u_b(x, p) = W_b (M_b h(x))(p), with W_b a matrix (Fact F10) |
| y(x) | the network's logits. q(x) = softmax(y(x)) |
| F | a family: a subset of the units of layer L, with N members |

Everything above layer L is a fixed function of the field h(x). A **build** changes only the family and the weights
that read it (Definition D6). The intact network is the reference ("the teacher").

## A.1 Facts

**Fact F1 (layer equations).** Convolution and linear maps are linear. ReLU is positively homogeneous and piecewise
linear: relu(c t) = c relu(t) for c >= 0. Max-pool is positively homogeneous and piecewise linear: on each set of
inputs with a fixed arg-max pattern it is a linear selection. Softmax is smooth.
Source: definitions.

**Fact F2 (one ReLU carries a sum exactly when the terms agree in sign).** relu(a + b) = relu(a) + relu(b) if and
only if a b >= 0.
Proof: case split on the signs. Lean: `relu_add_iff` (`Coarse/Basic.lean`).

**Fact F3 (shifts on the stride lattice).** Let sigma be the total stride of the layers below L. Shifting the input
by s = sigma m (m an integer vector) shifts every field of layer L by m: h_i(tau_s x, p) = h_i(x, p - m), for
positions whose receptive field stays inside the image.
Proof: each convolution, ReLU and pool commutes with shifts by multiples of its own stride. A composition commutes
with shifts by multiples of the product of the strides. Zero padding breaks this at borders.
Comment: shifts by other amounts, and all rotations, are not symmetries of the architecture.

**Fact F4 (a ReLU layer whose units each fire alone has only permutation symmetries).** Let S be a set of
non-negative vectors in R^n (the outputs of a ReLU layer that occur) that contains a positive multiple of every
basis vector e_j (each unit fires alone on some input). If an orthogonal matrix Q maps S into S, then Q is a
permutation matrix.
Proof. For each j, Q (c e_j) lies in S, so column j of Q is non-negative. So Q has non-negative entries. A
non-negative orthogonal matrix has exactly one non-zero entry in each column, equal to 1: the columns are
non-negative and pairwise orthogonal, so their supports are disjoint, and each has norm 1. So Q is a permutation
matrix. QED.
Comment: without the premise the statement is false (if all outputs lie in a thin cone around (1, 1, 1), every
rotation about that axis maps the cone into itself). The consequence we use: under the premise, no rotation acts on the
channel index of a ReLU layer, so a rotation symmetry must act on the input plane (Definition D2).
Lean: `fires_alone_nonneg` (non-negativity, `Coarse/Model.lean`) and `nonneg_orth_col_single` (permutation,
`Coarse/Basic.lean`).

**Fact F5 (second order of the distillation loss).** For logits y and a change delta,
KL(softmax(y) || softmax(y + delta)) = 1/2 delta^T Pi(y) delta + O(|delta|^3), with
Pi(y) = diag(q) - q q^T, q = softmax(y). Pi(y) is positive semi-definite with the all-ones vector in its kernel.
Proof. KL(q || q') = A(y + delta) - A(y) - q^T delta with A the log-sum-exp function. A has gradient q and Hessian
diag(q) - q q^T (the covariance of the one-hot label under q). Taylor's theorem gives the expansion. QED.

**Fact F6 (group averaging cannot hurt a convex invariant objective).** If a finite group acts on builds, and an
objective J is convex and invariant under the action, then J at the group average of a build is at most J at the
build.
Proof: Jensen's inequality, then invariance. Lean: `reynolds_le` (`Coarse/Basic.lean`).

**Fact F7 (balance under gradient flow).** For a ReLU unit with incoming weights a (with bias) and outgoing weights
c, gradient flow on any loss that depends only on the network's function (no weight decay) keeps |a|^2 - |c|^2
constant in time.
Proof. Positive homogeneity gives, for every loss l, <a, grad_a l> = <c, grad_c l> (scale a up by e^t and c down by
e^-t: the function does not change, so the derivative in t is zero). Under gradient flow,
d/dt |a|^2 = -2 <a, grad_a l> = -2 <c, grad_c l> = d/dt |c|^2. QED. Source: Du, Hu and Lee 2018.

**Fact F8 (the weights at a stationary point are data moments).** If theta is a stationary point of the training
loss sum over the data of l(theta; x, y) + (lambda/2) |theta|^2, then lambda theta = - sum over the data of
grad_theta l.
Proof: set the gradient to zero. QED.

**Fact F9 (the weights do not fix second moments).** Let theta satisfy the stationarity condition of F8 for a data
measure P_train (a finite or infinite mass on labelled inputs). Let Q be any measure on inputs, with each input
labelled by y drawn from the network's own prediction q(x). Then theta satisfies the same condition for P_train + Q
in expectation over the labels, and the second moment of the gradient increases by the Fisher matrix of Q,
E_Q E_{y ~ q(x)} grad_theta l grad_theta l^T, which is non-zero whenever Q gives mass to inputs where q(x) is not
one-hot and the gradient is not zero.
Proof. For the cross-entropy loss, grad_theta l = -grad_theta log q_y(x). Its mean over y ~ q(x) is
-sum_y grad q_y(x) = -grad sum_y q_y(x) = 0 (the score has mean zero). So adding Q adds zero to the mean gradient and
adds the Fisher matrix of Q to the second moment. QED.
Comment: so a rule that reads only the weights cannot recover the data's second moments in general (Corollary
T0.1 turns this into a statement about the coarse write).

**Fact F10 (InceptionV1's readers of 3b are pointwise after their pooling).** The four input branches of layer 4a
read 3b through 1 x 1 convolutions: three read M_1 h = the 3 x 3, stride 2 max-pool of the 3b field, and the fourth
reads M_4 h = a second 3 x 3 max-pool (stride 1) of M_1 h. In total 192 + 96 + 16 + 64 = 368 reader inputs. So, for
each branch b, the readers' input at pooled position p is W_b (M_b h)(p).
Source: the architecture (Szegedy et al. 2015).

**Fact F11 (the distillation loss is at most a quarter of the squared centred logit change).** For logits y and any
change delta in R^n, 0 <= KL(softmax(y) || softmax(y + delta)) <= (1/4) |P_perp delta|^2, with
P_perp = I - (1/n) 1 1^T (it removes the mean).
Proof. Let H(y) = diag(q) - q q^T, q = softmax(y). For any vector v, v^T H v is the variance of v_Y with Y drawn from q.
Variance lemma: v^T H v <= (1/2) |v|^2. Proof of the lemma: v^T H v = (1/2) sum over i, j of q_i q_j (v_i - v_j)^2.
The terms with i = j are zero. For i != j, (v_i - v_j)^2 <= 2 (v_i^2 + v_j^2). So
v^T H v <= sum over i != j of q_i q_j (v_i^2 + v_j^2) = 2 sum_i q_i (1 - q_i) v_i^2 <= (1/2) |v|^2, because
q_i (1 - q_i) <= 1/4. Now KL(q || q') = A(y + delta) - A(y) - q^T delta with A the log-sum-exp function (Fact F5).
Taylor's theorem with integral remainder gives KL = integral_0^1 (1 - t) delta^T H(y + t delta) delta dt. H 1 = 0, so
delta^T H delta = (P_perp delta)^T H (P_perp delta) <= (1/2) |P_perp delta|^2 at every point. The integral of (1 - t)
is 1/2. QED.
Lean: `softmax_var_le` (`Coarse/Fold.lean`, the variance lemma in its finite form). The Taylor step is by hand.

**Fact F12 (three examples of residual stream) (added 2026-10-29, Part B.V).** A residual network keeps a **stream**: one
vector h_l in R^d per position after block l, with h_l = h_(l-1) + f_l(h_(l-1)) for the block's map f_l. Networks
differ in what else acts on the stream. Three examples (not a classification: a post-norm transformer, with a norm on
the stream itself, is none of them):
1. A ReLU on the stream. torchvision's ResNet (`BasicBlock.forward` and `Bottleneck.forward` in
   `torchvision/models/resnet.py`): `out += identity`, then `out = self.relu(out)`. So h_l = relu(h_(l-1) + f_l(h_(l-1)))
   (with a 1 x 1 projection in place of h_(l-1) where the width changes). Every coordinate of the stream passes a ReLU at
   every block.
2. A filter per coordinate on the stream. torchvision's ConvNeXt (`CNBlock` in `torchvision/models/convnext.py`): the
   block is a depthwise 7 x 7 convolution (`groups=dim`), then LayerNorm, Linear, GELU, Linear and a layer scale, and
   `result += input`. The first map that reads the stream acts on each coordinate (channel) separately.
3. A pure stream. Each block reads the stream only through a norm followed by linear maps, and writes by a linear map
   that is added. torchvision's ViT (`EncoderBlock.forward` in `torchvision/models/vision_transformer.py`:
   `x = self.ln_1(input)`, attention, `x = x + input`, `y = self.ln_2(x)`, MLP, `return x + y`) and the pre-norm
   transformers of language modelling are of this kind; both also read the stream through a final norm before the logits
(ViT's `encoder.ln`, GPT's `ln_f`).
Proof: the code cited. In kinds 1 and 2 some map acts on single coordinates of the stream. In kind 3 nothing does after
Fact F13 part 1 folds each norm's per-coordinate gain and shift into the readers.

**Fact F13 (the norm on a pure stream) (added 2026-10-29, Part B.V).** For eps >= 0 let
n_eps(h) = h / (|h|^2 + eps)^(1/2) (for eps = 0, on h != 0).
1. (RMSNorm.) An RMSNorm of width d with gain gamma and constant eps_0 is gamma (.) h / (|h|^2 / d + eps_0)^(1/2)
   = d^(1/2) diag(gamma) n_(d eps_0)(h). So a reader R applied after it equals the reader d^(1/2) R diag(gamma) applied
   after n_(d eps_0).
2. (LayerNorm.) LayerNorm(h) = RMSNorm(C h) + beta with C = I - (1/d) 1 1^T. Suppose every map that reads the stream
   reads it through a LayerNorm (every block and the logits). Replace the input's first write e(x) by C e(x) and every
   write W_l g + c_l by C W_l g + C c_l. The new network computes the same function, its stream is C h_l, and on
   C R^d each LayerNorm is the RMSNorm of part 1 plus beta, which folds into the reader's bias.
3. (Rotation.) For an orthogonal Q, n_eps(Q h) = Q n_eps(h). Hence in a network of Definition DV1, replacing e, W_l and
   c_l by Q e, Q W_l and Q c_l, and every read matrix R_l and the logit matrix U by R_l Q^T and U Q^T, gives the same
   function, with stream Q h_l.
Proof. (1) Multiply numerator and denominator by d^(1/2). (2) The stream is the sum of the first write and the block
writes, so by linearity the new stream is C h_l if the block's inside values are unchanged. LayerNorm reads h only
through C h, and C C = C, so every LayerNorm sees the same value in both networks; by induction over the blocks the
inside values are the same and the logits are the same. On C R^d, C h = h, so LayerNorm is RMSNorm plus beta there.
(3) |Q h| = |h|, so n_eps(Q h) = Q h / (|h|^2 + eps)^(1/2) = Q n_eps(h). By induction the rotated stream is Q h_l, and
each read R_l Q^T n_eps(Q h_(l-1)) = R_l Q^T Q n_eps(h_(l-1)) = R_l n_eps(h_(l-1)) is unchanged; the logits likewise.
QED.
Lean: `norm_rot` (part 3, the rotation step) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`. Parts 1 and 2 are identities of
linear algebra, checked in `model/tv_regions.py` (check A).
Comment. Parts 1 to 3 are the computational invariance used by SliceGPT (A.4). They say that in kind 3 the function has no
special basis: only quantities that do not change under a rotation of the stream (the inner products among the read
vectors, the write vectors, the first write and the biases) are features of the function. Trained weights may still
pick a basis.

**Fact F14 (angles in the stream) (added 2026-10-29, Part B.V.3).** Let N be a network of Definition DV1 and A an
invertible d x d matrix. Let N^A be N with first write A e, writes A W_l and A c_l, read matrices R_l A^(-1) and logit
matrix U A^(-1), and everything else N's.
1. (No norm.) In the no-norm form, N^A's stream is A h_l, its inside values are N's, and its logits are N's, at every
   input.
2. (Norm.) In the norm form, if N^A's stream before norm l is A h_(l-1)(x), then its read there is s_l(x) times N's
   read, with s_l(x) = ((|h_(l-1)(x)|^2 + eps_l) / (|A h_(l-1)(x)|^2 + eps_l))^(1/2). So N^A computes N's logits at every
   x of P where |A h_(l-1)(x)| = |h_(l-1)(x)| for l = 1, ..., L + 1; for an orthogonal A this holds at every input
   (Fact F13 part 3).
Proof. (1) Induction on l: the read is R_l A^(-1) A h_(l-1) = R_l h_(l-1), so the inside values are N's, and the
stream is A h_(l-1) + A W_l g_l + A c_l = A h_l; the logits are U A^(-1) A h_L + c_y. (2) R_l A^(-1) n_(eps_l)(A h) =
R_l h / (|A h|^2 + eps_l)^(1/2) = s_l R_l n_(eps_l)(h). Where s_l = 1 at every norm, the induction of part 1 goes
through. QED.
Lean: `gl_read` (part 1's read step) and `norm_scale_read` (part 2's read step) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`.
Comment. If S_1, ..., S_m are subspaces whose sum is direct, some A maps them to pairwise orthogonal subspaces (extend
a basis made of bases of the S_j to a basis of R^d, and map it to an orthonormal basis). So without norms the function
computed by N, and the class of cuts that drop a given part (Lemma TV10), do not see an angle between areas; all
families of subspaces of given dimensions whose sum is direct are equivalent under GL(d). The claim errors of DM11 to
DM14 are not: they use orthogonal projections and are unchanged only under rotations. (Families whose sum is not
direct have finer invariants under GL(d), for example the cross-ratio of four lines in a plane.) With norms an angle
acts on a read only through one number per norm, the stream's size |A h|; this is the temperature of Theorem TV1.

## A.2 Definitions

**Definition D1 (feature).** The feature of unit i at position p is its response function
f_{i,p}: X -> [0, inf), f_{i,p}(x) = h_i(x, p). Features are compared in L2(P): <f, g>_P = E_P[f(x) g(x)].
Comment: this needs no basis in channel space, so Fact F4 does not constrain it.

**Definition D2 (group action on inputs).** Let G be a group of transformations of the image plane: the special
Euclidean group SE(2) (rotations and shifts) or a subgroup. G acts on inputs that are functions on the plane by
(g . x)(v) = x(g^-1 v), and on features by (g . f)(x) = f(g^-1 . x).
Comment: on a pixel grid with borders, only shifts on the stride lattice and quarter turns act without loss. The
other elements act exactly only in the plane model (Definition D8).

**Definition D3 (family and its parameter).** A family is a set of units F = {1, ..., N} with a group G, a template
feature f_0 (the template unit at the origin), group elements g_1, ..., g_N and positive weights m_1, ..., m_N. The
members are N samples of the field g -> g . f_0. With positions, member i at position p is the feature
f_{i,p} = (tau_p g_i) . f_0, with tau_p the shift by p. The weights define the family's measure
mu_F = sum_i m_i delta_{g_i} on G (used in Part D).

**Definition D4 (clean).** A family is eps-clean under law P if
max_{i, p} | f_{i,p} - (tau_p g_i) . f_0 |_P <= eps |f_0|_P. It is exactly clean if eps = 0.

**Definition D5 (readers, edges and circuits).** The readers of a family are the units of the next layer with a
non-zero weight from some member. The edge from family F to a reader family R is the pair (W_RF, D_R): the weight
block from F to R and the gate pattern D_R(x) = 1[pre-activation of R > 0]. A circuit is a chain of edges. On one
input, a circuit acts as the product of its weight blocks and gates. By Fact F1 this is a linear map on each set of
inputs with fixed gates and fixed pool selections.

**Definition D6 (build).** A width-k build of family F replaces the N members by k new units of layer L,
c_a(x, p) = relu(<K'_a, A(x)[p + Omega]> + b'_a), and replaces their write columns. It may also change the readers'
other weights, according to a declared bench:
| Bench | What may change |
|---|---|
| frozen | only the new units and their write columns |
| biases | also the readers' biases |
| re-route | also the readers' weights on all other units of layer L |
A build has two parts:
1. **WHAT**: target signals t_a = sum_i lambda_{a,i} h_i (combinations of the members' outputs at the same position,
   before pooling), and the write.
2. **HOW**: a choice of (K'_a, b'_a) such that one unit of layer L computes t_a.
A WHAT is **realizable** when a HOW computes it exactly.

**Definition D7 (distillation objective).** For a law P and a build B,
D_P(B) = E_{x ~ P} KL(softmax(y(x)) || softmax(y_B(x))). The optimal width-k build for P minimises D_P over the
bench's builds. The generalist objective takes P = P_train. Training a width-k network by distillation on P is one
approximate solver of this minimisation, not its definition.

**Definition D8 (the plane model).** Positions p range over the plane R^2 with Lebesgue measure. Inputs are fields on
the plane (band-limited, so that every element of SE(2) acts on them without loss). Every layer below L commutes with
all shifts of the plane (so F3 holds for all shifts). Rotations are NOT required to commute with the layers below L
(oriented filters do not); the rotation structure enters only through H-clean. The pooling maps M_b commute with
rotations about any point (for example the identity, or an average over a disc). Readers act pointwise after M_b, as
in F10.

**Definition D9 (ideal tangent-element detectors and their co-activity on one curve).** A detector of width w for
the tangent element (v, phi) responds to a rendered curve with
w^-3 integral over the curve's arc length of k((v(s) - v) / w, (phi(s) - phi) / w) ds, with k a fixed smooth bump of
integral 1. As w -> 0 this converges only in the sense of distributions, so the ideal case is defined directly: the
co-activity on one random curve of the ideal detectors at the tangent elements (0, 0) and (v, phi) is the pair
occupation density of the curve at those two elements (the density of pairs of arc-length points, one at each
element). In the linearised setting of B.2 the curve is a graph over the first coordinate, which equals arc length, so
for a curve through (0, 0) the occupation density at v = (s, y) and angle phi is the joint density of (y(s), phi(s)).
Finite-width detectors are modelled by independent Gaussian errors of standard deviation w_y (position across the
curve) and w_phi (angle) added to BOTH elements.

**Definition D10 (fold ladder and tree).** A fold ladder of a network is a list of levels j = 1, ..., r, a build B_j
for each level (Definition D6 or D11) with width k_j(l) at built layer l, k_j(l) < k_{j+1}(l), and merge matrices
M^l_{i <- j} (k_i(l) x k_j(l)) for every pair of levels i < j, such that at every built layer l the units of B_i are the
units of B_j multiplied by M^l_{i <- j}, and merges compose: M^l_{i <- j} M^l_{j <- j'} = M^l_{i <- j'}. Level i is a
parent level of level j. Call a unit of a built layer **non-negative** when it is a non-negative combination of the
full network's members in that layer (a read with non-negative coefficients, like a detector made of detectors). The
ladder is a **tree** between levels i < j when, at every built layer, each level has a basis of non-negative units in
which every parent unit is a non-negative combination of AT LEAST TWO child units, with disjoint sets of children for
different parents. Both conditions are needed for the word to mean something: without "at least two" each parent
can be its own single child, and without "non-negative units" any level of at least twice the parent's width works
(take the children p_s + e_s and p_s - e_s, so that p_s is half their sum). To **fold** a network to width k is to take
the level of width k.

**Definition D11 (gated chain).** Fix a finite set of positions Pos with weights rho(p) >= 0, and a feature map
a: X x Pos -> R^d (for example the input field read around p, with one entry equal to 1 for the biases). A gated chain
of depth m and widths N_1, ..., N_m has four parts.
1. A gate path: real functions g_1, ..., g_m on X x Pos. They may be any functions of the input, but they are computed
   by a path that does not read the value path (items 2 to 4), so a build cannot change them.
2. A first family: v_1(x, p) = g_1(x, p) K^T a(x, p) in R^{N_1}, with K a d x N_1 matrix (column i is the kernel of
   member i). So every member of the family shares the gate g_1.
3. Edges: v_{l+1}(x, p) = g_{l+1}(x, p) w_l v_l(x, p), with w_l an N_{l+1} x N_l matrix, the same at every position
   (the edge is pointwise in position, like the 1 x 1 readers of Fact F10).
4. A readout: y(x) = H sum_p rho(p) v_m(x, p) + c, with H an n_y x N_m matrix and c in R^{n_y}.
A width-(k_1, ..., k_m) build keeps the gate path and the feature map, and replaces K, w_l, H, c by any K' (d x k_1),
w'_l (k_{l+1} x k_l), H' (n_y x k_m), c' (the frozen bench of D6 does not apply: all value weights are free). The
**logit distillation objective** of a build is D2_P(B) = 1/2 E_P |P_perp (y_B(x) - y(x))|^2, with P_perp as in Fact F11.
Comment: the nonlinearity of a gated chain lives only in its gate path. Within one input the value path is linear.
Gated linear units (Dauphin et al. 2017; the SwiGLU layers of current language models, Shazeer 2020) and the norm
nonlinearities of rotation-equivariant networks (Worrall et al. 2017) have a similar shape, with two differences: there
each unit or each group of units has its own gate, and the gates are computed from the value path itself. So those
networks are not gated chains as they stand. A ReLU unit is a unit whose gate is its own sign, so a ReLU layer is not
a family with a shared gate (Proposition T1'). The gate path is kept by every build at full size: the theorems of B.4
fold the value path, not the gate path.

**Definition D12 (self-gated chain, self-contained build, forced reads).** A **self-gated chain** has items 2 to 4 of
Definition D11 (first family, pointwise edges, readout), with gates computed from its own value path instead of a
separate gate path. Write z(x, p) = K^T a(x, p) for the first family's pre-activations, W_1 = I and
W_l = w_{l-1} ... w_1 (N_l x N_1) for l >= 2. There are read matrices S_1 (N_1 x r_1) and S_{l+1} (N_l x r_{l+1}) for
l = 1, ..., m - 1, and fixed functions phi_l: R^{r_l} -> R, such that
g_1(x, p) = phi_1(S_1^T z(x, p)) and g_{l+1}(x, p) = phi_{l+1}(S_{l+1}^T v_l(x, p)).
The **forced read space** is the subspace R of R^{N_1} spanned by the columns of S_1 and of W_l^T S_{l+1}
(l = 1, ..., m - 1): every read that some gate takes, pulled back to the first family. Write r = dim R.
A **self-contained build** of widths (k_1, ..., k_m) has K', w'_l, H', c' as in D11, read matrices S'_1 (k_1 x r_1)
and S'_{l+1} (k_l x r_{l+1}), and the same functions phi_l. Its gates are computed from its own units:
g'_1 = phi_1(S'_1^T K'^T a) and g'_{l+1} = phi_{l+1}(S'_{l+1}^T v'_l). Nothing else is kept. With W'_l defined like W_l,
the build is **read-faithful** when its effective read kernels equal the network's: K' S'_1 = K S_1 and
K' W'_l^T S'_{l+1} = K W_l^T S_{l+1} for l = 1, ..., m - 1.
Comment: a single ReLU unit is the case N_1 = 1, S_1 = 1, phi_1(t) = 1[t > 0]: then g_1 z = relu(z). A ReLU layer of
N units is outside this definition, which has one scalar gate per layer and position. In a generalisation with one gate
per unit, every member's own read would be forced and R would be the whole space. Inside the definition, r limits the
read-faithful fold at uniform width (Theorem T11). Corollary T11.1 removes the limit with r extra units below the top.

**Definition D13 (spatial gated chain and its visible subspaces).** A **spatial gated chain** is a gated chain
(Definition D11) whose edges may mix nearby positions. Positions Pos are a finite subset of Z^2 (or of a group), so
that p + q is defined. Fix a finite set Q of offsets (the window). Then
v_{l+1}(x, p) = g_{l+1}(x, p) sum_{q in Q} w_l(q) v_l(x, p + q), with one N_{l+1} x N_l matrix w_l(q) per offset, and
v_l(x, p') = 0 when p' is not in Pos (zero padding). The first layer and the readout are as in D11. The first layer may
read raw input patches, so every layer between the input and the readout is part of the chain. Gates are either given
by a gate path (as in D11) or self-gated with reads at the same position, g_{l+1}(x, p) = phi_{l+1}(S_{l+1}^T v_l(x, p))
and g_1(x, p) = phi_1(S_1^T z(x, p)) (as in D12). A build has widths (k_1, ..., k_m), K', w'_l(q), H', c' (and read
matrices S'_l when self-gated).
For a matrix U (n_y x k) with orthonormal columns, the **visible subspaces** O_m, ..., O_1 (O_l a subspace of R^{N_l},
read as a space of row vectors, that is, of reads of layer l) are defined from the top down:
O_m = the row space of U^T P_perp H, and for l < m, O_l = the span of all r^T w_l(q) with r in O_{l+1} and q in Q,
plus the columns of S_{l+1} when the chain is self-gated. For the first layer, O_1 also contains the columns of S_1.
The O_l are the smallest system of spaces of reads that contains the top reads and the gates' reads and is closed under
the pulled-back edge maps. The **reachable space** Rch_l (l >= 2) is the smallest subspace V of R^{N_l} with
P(v_l(x, p) in V for every p) = 1, and Rch_1 is the same for z(x, p). It exists: among the subspaces with this property
take one of least dimension; its intersection with any other has the property too (two events of probability one), so
by minimality it lies in every other. The **visible width** of layer l is d_l = the dimension of O_l
restricted to Rch_l (the space of the functions r^T on Rch_l, r in O_l).
Comment: d_l <= dim O_l, and dim O_m <= k, dim O_l <= dim O_{l+1} + r_{l+1} with pointwise edges (Q = {0}) for l >= 2,
and dim O_1 <= dim O_2 + r_2 + r_1. Builds pad with zeros like the network. Gates that read a pre-activation through a
window (the ReLU and GLU shapes) are outside this definition. With a
window of |Q| offsets, dim O_l can be up to |Q| dim O_{l+1} plus the gate reads, so the widths can grow toward the
input. In linear systems theory (literature table) the minimal state space is the part that is both reachable and
observable. Here the layers play the role of time steps, and the offsets give several maps per step.

**Definition D14 (kept features, seen mean, seen floor).** For a self-contained build (Definition D12) with first-layer
kernel K' (d x k_1), the **kept features** are w(x, p) = K'^T a(x, p) and W(x) = (w(x, p))_{p in Pos+}, with
Pos+ = {p : rho(p) > 0}. With V = col(K'), the **seen mean** is m_V(x) = E_P[y | W] and the **seen floor** is
F(V) = 1/2 E_P |P_perp (y - m_V)|^2. (Both depend on K' only through V: Lemma T17a.) Under H-gauss the kernel is
**linear-seen** when E_P[a(x, p) | w(x, p)] is almost surely a linear function of w(x, p).
Comment: a build's switches are functions of its kept features (Lemma T17a). So the best switch is a question about
what the kept features can predict of the network's switch arguments.

## A.3 Hypotheses

**Hypothesis H-clean.** The family is eps-clean (Definition D4) with members at equally spaced angles: g_i is the
rotation by 2 pi i / N about the unit's position. The theorems of Part B are proved at eps = 0. Conjecture T4 part 2 is
the stability statement for eps > 0.

**Hypothesis H-sym.** In the plane model, the input law P is invariant under rotations about any point and under
all shifts: g . x has the same law as x for every g in SE(2). Its distance is
eps_sym = max over g in the family's group of sup over test functions f with |f| <= 1 of |E f(g . x) - E f(x)|
(twice the total-variation distance between the law of g . x and the law of x). This is the eps_sym of Conjecture T4.
Comment: on square pixel images no law has this invariance, so for InceptionV1 H-sym is a statement about how close
the network's own layer-L statistics come to it (Part C).

**Hypothesis H-read.** The readers treat the family symmetrically: there is a permutation R of the reader channels,
of order N, such that W_{., i+1} = R W_{., i} for every member column, and the metric of Part B satisfies
G_{gamma . x}(gamma p, gamma p') = R G_x(p, p') R^T, with gamma the rotation by 2 pi / N about a fixed point acting on
inputs and positions.
Comment: by Fact F4 a symmetry of the next ReLU layer whose units each fire alone must be a permutation, so R is a
permutation and not a general orthogonal map.

**Hypothesis H-kron.** The data object of Theorem T0 (for all readers of all branches stacked, Setting of B.0)
factorises exactly: T = E_P sum_{p, p'} h(x, p) h(x, p')^T (x) G_x(p, p') equals C (x) M for one N x N matrix C and one
r x r matrix M (both positive definite).
Comment: this is an exact factorisation. K-FAC's independence assumption (activity independent of the output metric)
gives only a sum over position pairs of Kronecker products, so H-kron is stronger. A constant metric G = M (x) K with
one pooling for all branches gives H-kron, with C = E sum K(p, p') h(x, p) h(x, p')^T. With different pools per branch
it is an extra restriction.

**Hypothesis H-pool.** The pooling in front of the readers commutes with the read: the pooled output of a coarse unit
t = Lambda h equals Lambda times the pooled member outputs. This holds when the pooling is linear.
Comment: InceptionV1 max-pools 3b, and max-pool of a sum is not the sum of max-pools, so H-pool is an approximation
there (Part C).

**Hypothesis H-contour.** The part of the input that drives the family is a field of smooth contours: random curves
drawn by the curvature process (position v, angle phi, curvature kappa, arc length s; dv/ds = (cos phi, sin phi),
dphi/ds = kappa, dkappa = sigma dB_s with B a Brownian motion, and the curvature kappa_0 at the start drawn from a law
nu with variance tau^2 > 0, independent of B), on an independent background. Rendering: near each curve, the input
field is a fixed function of the signed distance to the curve and of the local curve angle.
Comment: curvature persists over short arcs in this law. Mumford's direction process (dphi = sigma dB_s) is the
classical alternative. Theorem T3 shows that the two laws predict different pairings.

**Hypothesis H-stat.** The large network's weights are a stationary point of its training loss (the premise of
Facts F8 and F9).

**Hypothesis H-joint (several families).** The families A_1, ..., A_F share one N and one labelling (member i of every
family sits at angle 2 pi i / N), each is exactly clean under the same rotation, one reader permutation R satisfies
H-read for every family, and H-kron holds for all FN members stacked, with one M.

**Hypothesis H-shot (contours add).** The members' responses add over the curves in an image, the curves form a
Poisson process, and its intensity is the same in every image. (By Campbell's theorem the covariance of two responses
is then the single-curve pair term.)

**Hypothesis H-detector.** Each curve member responds like a finite-width detector of Definition D9 at its own tangent
element, with independent errors, and with a fixed angle label.

**Hypothesis H-gram (co-activity from the weights).** The family's co-activity matrix C is proportional to the
Gram matrix of the members' kernels.
Comment: this is what a weights-only check of Conjecture D1 needs. It is a strong assumption and is named so it can be
measured.

**Hypothesis H-gate (shared gates).** The part of the network above the input field is a gated chain (Definition
D11): one gate per family per position, computed by a gate path that does not read the value path. Every build keeps
the gate path unchanged and at full size.
Comment: this is the restriction under which Part B.4 closes the fold. It replaces "one unit per gate" (ReLU) by "one
gate per family".

**Hypothesis H-eq (an equivariant chain).** A gated chain with N_l = N for every l, and a map gamma that acts on inputs
(x -> gamma . x) and on positions (a permutation p -> gamma p of Pos) with gamma^N = identity, such that:
1. (H-clean for the first family, finite form) z_{i+1}(gamma . x, gamma p) = z_i(x, p), with z(x, p) = K^T a(x, p) and
   member indices mod N;
2. the gates and the pool are invariant: g_l(gamma . x, gamma p) = g_l(x, p) and rho(gamma p) = rho(p);
3. (H-read for every edge, with R the member shift) w_l Pi = Pi w_l, with Pi the cyclic shift on members,
   (Pi v)_{i+1} = v_i;
4. the readout is equivariant: H Pi = R_y H for a permutation R_y of the n_y logits.

**Hypothesis H-symN (finite symmetry of the input law).** gamma . x has the same law as x.
Comment: this is the finite-group form of H-sym. It needs no plane model when the input space carries an exact action
of Z_N (for example images sampled on a polar grid). On square pixel grids an exact action exists only for N = 1, 2, 4.

**Hypothesis H-selfgate (gates read the value path through fixed reads).** The part of the network above the input
field is a self-gated chain (Definition D12). Part B.5 compares the self-contained builds of D12, which compute their
gates from their own units with the network's functions phi_l and keep nothing at full size.
Comment: H-gate keeps a separate gate path at full size in every build. H-selfgate removes that path. The price is
that a build which changes the reads changes the gates, and then the value path is no longer linear in the build.
Part B.5 handles the builds that keep the reads (read-faithful builds) exactly, and gives a lower bound for all builds.

**Hypothesis H-sgate (spatial gated chain).** The part of the network above the raw input is a spatial gated chain
(Definition D13), with gates from a gate path that every build keeps, or self-gated with reads at the same position.
Comment: this allows the spatial kernels of the lower layers (a stem), which H-gate and H-selfgate exclude.

**Hypothesis H-gauss (a Gaussian input field with independent positions).** Under P, the vectors a(x, p), p in Pos+,
are independent and have one Gaussian law N(m_a, Sigma). Sigma may be singular, for example when one entry of a is the
constant 1.
Comment: this is a hypothesis about the input field of the chain, not about the network. It makes the part of the input
that a build does not keep independent of what it keeps, and that gives the seen mean of Definition D14 a closed form
(Part B.7). Image features are not Gaussian and nearby positions are dependent; Part C defines the distance.

**Hypothesis H-dialfit.** In the curve-family crush of InceptionV1 layer 3b (one family of ten units replaced by one
trained coarse unit, `family.py`), the trained coarse unit is at the fixed point of Corollary T38.2 on the crush's
training mix: on its firing positions, its pre-activation equals the least-squares affine fit, from its own 5 x 5
input window, of the family's output seen through the coarse unit's own write (the target t of T38.2, with the readers
the four input convolutions of layer 4a). The fixed point predicts a slope of 1 between the pre-activation and the fit.
The distance is eps_dial = 1 - corr, with corr the correlation of the pre-activation with the fit on the firing
positions; the slope is reported beside it.
Comment: two premises of T38.2 do not hold for the crush. Every reader of 4a sees 3b after a 3 x 3 max pool, so the
unit's output does not reach the readers unpooled; and the crush has no bias shift d, so gamma = 0 (T38.2's last
sentence). The crush was also trained on KL through the rest of the network, not on T38.2's local score. So this is a
hypothesis, not a consequence of T38.2, and a failure is not surprising. A first version used the plain summed output
of the ten members as the target (the case W = c = all ones); Part C records both.

**Hypothesis H-front (a gate in front of the family) (proposed; node R-gatefold, PENDING).** N has two hidden
layers, with layer-1 output h(x) in R^m. There is a unit of layer 1, the gate q (a coordinate of h), and a number
Delta_0 such that N's gap equals Delta_0 at every point x of the support of P with q(x) = 0. The gate's region is
G = {x in supp P : q(x) > 0}, and P(G) > 0 and P(supp P \ G) > 0.
Comment: this is the essay's "gate in front of the car detectors" in a plain ReLU network. For example, it holds when
the members that N reads are silent wherever the gate is silent; the hypothesis itself only asks that N's gap is
constant there. With a symmetry group Gamma, "Gamma fixes the gate" means pi_1(gamma) fixes the unit q for every gamma
(Definition D20). It is a claim about N and the mix, not about builds. Shonu confirmed this reading of "fold" on
2026-10-26 (`DECISIONS.md` card 3-4).

**Hypothesis H-flatgate (the gate is flat on its region) (proposed; node R-flatgate, PENDING).** Under H-front,
the gate takes one value q_1 > 0 at every point of G.
Comment: a convenience. A ReLU gate is rarely constant where it fires. It makes the least-squares fit on G
realisable by one unit whenever the fitted values minus Delta_0 have one strict sign on G (Lemma T39a).

**Hypothesis H-route (InceptionV1 is clean under D45, as measured by the estimator of Part C) (proposed; nodes
R-cleannet and R-explaw, PENDING).** Let pi-hat, lambda-hat and the pair index pi-hat(u_1, u_2) be the estimators of
pi, lambda (Definition D45) and the pair index (Definition D46) stated in the Part C row of H-route, with its stated
approximations (readers, pools, sample sizes), and the base law of the ImageNet validation images (option (i) of node
R-explaw). For the 12 units drawn there from each of blocks 3b, 4c and 4e of lucid InceptionV1: (1) the median of
pi-hat over the 36 units is at most 1/4 of the median pair index over the consecutive pairs of drawn units; (2)
lambda-hat > 0 for at least 9 in 10 of them; (3) for the same units of one random initialisation of the same
architecture (lucent's initialiser, seed 0), lambda-hat > 0 for at most 3 in 4. (The statement as first written did
not fix the denominator; the script divides by the live units. Part C reports both readings.) The numbers 1/4, 9 in 10 and 3 in 4
were fixed before the measurement. Its distance is the triple of measured values.
Comment: this is a statement about one trained network, one random draw and a stated sample, so it is evidence for
the definition, not a theorem about trained networks. (1) and (2) say that trained units are read and have one job;
(3) says that the read index separates a trained network from an untrained one, which the packing index alone does
not (observation 4 of A.6).

**Hypothesis H-agree (the excess read separates trained from untrained, InceptionV1) (proposed; nodes R-cleannet and
R-explaw, PENDING).** Let xi-hat be the estimator of the excess read xi (Definition D45, item 2') stated in the Part C
row of H-agree, with the base law of the ImageNet validation images. For 12 units drawn uniformly (a fresh draw, seed
stated there) from each of blocks 3b, 4c and 4e of lucid InceptionV1: (1) xi-hat > 0 for at least 9 in 10 of the
trained units; (2) for the same units of one random initialisation (lucent's initialiser, seed 0), xi-hat > 0 for at
most 3 in 4; (3) the trained median of |xi-hat| is at least 5 times the random median. The numbers were fixed before
the measurement. A lab run on other units of 3b and 4e (`research/clean/explore/s11_excess.py`) came first; this
draw does not reuse its units, and 4c was not in it.

**Hypothesis H-typical (trained networks are nearly clean) (proposed; node R-cleannet, PENDING).** Fix a kind
(architecture, compact input domain X) and a law Q_0 on its weights (the initial law used to train N). Let N_0 be
drawn from Q_0. Then, entry by entry, eps(N) <= theta E_{Q_0}[eps(N_0)] (Definition D42), with theta = 1/2, a number
fixed before any measurement. Its distance is the largest entry of eps(N) divided by the matching entry of
E_{Q_0}[eps(N_0)] (Part C).
Comment: this is the second half of criterion C6. It is an acceptance test of D42 as much as a hypothesis about N:
the essay's title is the claim, and if the test fails, the definition (or its base measure, comment of D41) is in
question before the networks are. Part C adds a second control, a network of the same size trained to give the same
unit two unrelated jobs; that control is a measurement, not part of the statement.

**Hypothesis H-group (the developer's class loses nothing on families).** Let N have one hidden layer and two logits,
let N be perfectly clean for a group Gamma (Definition D20) with families F_1, ..., F_q (the orbits of Aut_X(N),
Definition D38), let P be a finite mix, and let k >= 1. Then there are sizes k_F >= 0 with sum k such that, at the
grouping G whose groups are the families with these sizes (Definition D50), V_b(G) equals the least D_P over all
builds of width k of N's kind with any new units (it is reached, Theorem T19).
Comment: Shonu's test (2026-10-27) of whether class (b) loses anything when N is clean. It is trivially true when one
family's rows span the input space (Theorem T54 part 3: then (b) at that family is every unit), so it has content
only for families of low rank. Theorem T25 fails it: its one family has rows that do not span R^2, and the least unit
reads an input that N ignores. For real networks D38 gives one-unit families (no exact symmetry), so testing H-group
on them needs the relaxed families of node R-cleannet.

**Hypothesis H-recur (step by step is optimal for some tree).** Let N have one hidden layer and two logits and be
perfectly clean for a group Gamma (Definition D20), let P be a finite mix, and let G\* be a target grouping in which
every group has at least two units and target size 1. Then there is a zoom G_0, ..., G_m = G\* with G_0 the grouping
with no groups (take B_0 = N), in which every step changes exactly one group, and that group has exactly two children
and target size 1, and an (r) sequence along it (Definition D50) with D_P(B_j) = V_b(G_j) at every level j. Targets
with other sizes are open.
Comment: Theorem T55 makes each such step cheap; the open part is the tree. For the detector networks with the mixes
of Theorem T43 it holds along every zoom of this form when the target's groups have no bad pair (Corollary T60.1);
targets whose groups contain a bad pair, and other mixes, are open.

**Hypothesis H-freefam (the families of a clean network are free on its own mix).** Let N be perfectly clean for a
group Gamma (Definition D20), with families from Definition D38, and let P be N's training mix. Then every family is
free on P (Definition D55): for any two firing points of members whose midpoint is in P, the gap at the midpoint is not
below the average of the gaps at the two points (in the language of the essay: the blend of two curves is another
curve, so some member fires on it).
Comment: the detector networks of D40 with T43's mixes fail it on purpose: their families are discrete alternatives
whose blends the mix marks "nothing". If H-freefam holds for a family, Corollary T59.2's kind of coarse unit (a
presence unit) is the candidate; if it fails, Theorem T62 says presence units can be impossible. Part C measures the
share of conflicting segments.

## A.4 Literature and compatibility with "clean"

Every borrowed result or framing is listed here, with the assumption it makes about how networks represent things.
A framing that splits a clean family into sparse directions across units does not enter the chain of logic.

Its concepts enter as hypotheses, never as facts |

## A.5 What a clean network is: criteria and principles (proposed; node R-cleannet, PENDING)

(Section A.6 replaces the definitions of this section as the definition of clean, 2026-10-26 evening. The criteria
below still apply to it.)

Shonu (2026-10-26) made this the goal of the session: "not making a stronger version of clean, but just a good
version of what a clean network is". He added three requirements the same day. Clean is a property of the network
alone ("what I'm aiming for is for this thing to be able to be done on the things a network can do"). It may need
several numbers ("you might need to have multiple metrics to describe cleanliness which the error bounds can depend
on"). And it is "more of an object which satisfies a bunch of principles than a single principle". The essay agrees
on the second point: "distilling everything into one 'cleanliness' score should be taken as a broad pointer to the
regime a neural network is in, rather than something precise". So clean is a structure with several parts, and
eps(N) is a list with one entry per part. The trunk's words ("a bound that depends only on eps(N)") read the same way
when eps(N) is a list. Definition D20 (one symmetry group) becomes one principle among several (Q1 below).

**Revision 2 (2026-10-26, later): why D39 is replaced.** Shonu: the essay's title says networks "are already clean",
yet under D39 clean networks are rare and do not describe real networks, so the definition must change. No theorem
of this paper said clean networks are rare. D39 made them rare in one place, and strict in two more. (1) Its families
are orbits of an exact symmetry group (Definition D38), and exact symmetry holds only on a set of measure zero
(Theorem T44). (2) Its entries take a supremum over all of X, and most of X (for images, the pixel box) is inputs the
network never meets. (3) Its entries take the worst pair, while the essay counts a share ("roughly 90% of neuron poles have one main
job"). And the symmetry was not the essay's: no sentence of the essay mentions symmetry, equivariance or mirror images
(its two uses of "rotation" are a rotation of the activation basis and an attack that must survive rotation).
Symmetry came from the curves example and the equivariance papers of the literature table. Shonu also kept C1 (asked
whether the training inputs could enter): "it's not really an objective metric where we can actually compare
networks. if you take what the essay says at face value, you should be able to determine if a network is clean by
interpreting the neurons and circuits themselves (as they sort of do through interp tools) rather than needing extra
data. i think we can achieve the same thing but using foundational mathematical principles". And: look at the essay
"for inspiration for these mathematical things you create since the essay itself does go against some standard
interp methodologies". Definitions D41 and D42 below are the result. Each principle is judged on a unit's whole
target, not at its peak (the essay: "a blind maximum tests the neuron's center, not its breadth"), and each is read
from the weights and signs of the circuit, as the essay reads neurons by their votes and their readers.

**Criteria for a definition of clean.** These are requirements on the definition, not on a network.

| | Criterion | Source |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | It is a property of N and of the input domain X of N's kind, and of nothing else: no mix, no build, not the optimum. (If it used the optimum, "clean makes the optimum easy to find" would hold by definition.) | Shonu, 2026-10-26 |
| C2 | It is graded: eps(N) is a list of non-negative numbers, one per principle, and N is perfectly clean when every entry is 0 | the trunk; Shonu, 2026-10-26 |
| C3 | Each principle is motivated by a sentence of the essay about real networks (the sentences motivate the rules; they do not state them) | Shonu: a definition "which reflects how neural networks actually are" |
| C4 | It covers families with no exact symmetry (the essay's ear units: "pale, wavy, and head-side ear neurons all feed one hanging-ears neuron") | the essay, "A City vs a Knot" |
| C5 | It excludes networks whose readers vote for and against two units that are on together, as the broken line of Lemma T22a does (Remark A.5.2). "One unit per memorised point" cannot be a principle: in Theorem T43 the network is the same for every hard instance, so whether its units "memorise" is a property of the pair (N, P), which C1 excludes | the essay: "A neuron is built from votes"; Theorem T43 |
| C6 | It is typical. Perfect cleanliness must not be an equation that holds only on a set of measure zero: the perfectly clean networks must contain a non-empty open set of networks (Theorem T45: the margin-clean networks), and a small change of the weights must keep a margin-clean network perfectly clean. And well-trained networks must score low (Hypothesis H-typical; a random network and a network that packs unrelated jobs into one unit are the controls) | the essay's title, "Neural Networks Are Already Clean"; Shonu, 2026-10-26 |
| C7 | Each entry is a weighted share over units, not the worst unit | the essay: "roughly 90% of neuron poles have one main job" |
| C8 | Each entry is a number in [0, 1] that does not change when the units of a layer are permuted or a unit's incoming weights and bias are scaled by c > 0 and its outgoing weights by 1/c. So two networks of one kind can be compared | Shonu, 2026-10-26: "an objective metric where we can actually compare networks" |

**Definition D38 (input domain, regions, readers, families) (proposed; node R-cleannet, PENDING).** The input domain
X of N's kind is a closed convex set in R^d that holds every input the network is meant for (for images, the pixel
box; for the toy networks of Part B, R^d unless a section says otherwise). For a hidden unit u with pre-activation z_u
(a function of the input x), its **region** is R_u = {x in X : z_u(x) > 0} and its **peak** is m_u = the supremum of
z_u over X. Two units of one layer are **apart** on X when their regions do not meet, and **nested** when one region
contains the other. A **reader** of a unit of layer l is a unit of layer l + 1, or, for l = L, a logit difference
y_c - y_c' for any two classes c != c'. Let N be in reduced form (Definition D20). Its **symmetry group**
Aut_X(N) is the set of tuples (A, pi_1, ..., pi_L, sigma): A an orthogonal map of R^d with A X = X, pi_l a
permutation of the units of layer l, sigma a permutation of the classes, such that the conditions of Definition D20
hold with rho_0 = A (W_1 A = pi_1 W_1, W_l pi_{l-1} = pi_l W_l, pi_l b_l = b_l, W_out pi_L = sigma W_out,
sigma c = c). It is a group under composition and depends only on N and X. The **families** of N are the orbits of
the units of each layer under Aut_X(N).
Comment: this fixes the referee's point that a group and a family structure chosen freely make every network
"clean" (the trivial group with single-unit families). Here both are functions of (N, X). The price: a real network
has no exact symmetry, so its group is trivial, its families are single units, and the principles about families
say nothing. That is criterion C4, the main open part of the definition.

**Definition D39 (principles of a clean network, first revision; superseded by Definition D42, kept because Lemma
T43a and Theorem T43 refer to it) (proposed; node R-cleannet, PENDING).** Let N be in reduced form,
with input domain X and its families (Definition D38). N satisfies:
1. **Q1 (moved copies)** when some family has two or more members, that is, when Aut_X(N) moves some unit. This is
   the content of Definition D20 once the group is N's own. No entry: the graded version (distance to the nearest
   network with a given symmetry, as in D21) is left for a later revision. Essay: rotated copies of one unit
   (literature table, "Naturally Occurring Equivariance").
2. **Q2 (siblings are alternatives)**, in two forms, both open for Shonu's choice. *Strict:* any two members of one
   family are apart on X. *Broad* (for a bounded X): each member u has a point of X where z_u reaches m_u and every sibling is strictly
   below it there. Entry (for the strict form): eps_2 = the largest, over pairs u != v of one family, of the supremum
   over X of min(z_u, z_v), divided by max(m_u, m_v), and 0 if that supremum is not positive; when a supremum or a
   peak is infinite the entry is 1 if the pair meets on X and 0 if not. Essay: "an ambulance neuron might have a taxi
   on its negative pole, and a taxi an ambulance"; a neuron "separates two subtle patterns at its positive and
   negative poles". The strict form excludes broadly tuned families: if a member is on at a sibling's peak input,
   the two are on together there. The paper's own detector model (Definition D9, Hypothesis H-gram) and the curve
   units have such overlap, so the strict form is likely too strong for real networks.
3. **Q3 (votes agree where units are on together)** if no reader (any logit difference y_c - y_c', or any unit of the
   next layer) reads two units that are on together somewhere on X with weights of opposite signs. Entry: eps_3 = the
   largest, over readers and pairs u, v that the reader reads with opposite signs, of the same ratio as in Q2. Essay:
   "A neuron is built from votes: each input weight votes for its positive side or its negative side". A reader may
   vote against an alternative (the taxi on the ambulance's negative pole): opposite signs are allowed on units that
   are apart.
4. **Q4 (a gate in front)** if every unit of layer l >= 2 reads, with a positive weight, a unit of layer l - 1 whose
   region contains its own and is not all of X (a unit that is on everywhere would make the condition empty). Essay:
   "a neuron in front of them acts as a gate". (The gate work of Part B.G is parked.)
5. **Q5 (the coarse unit is present)** if every family of a layer l < L is read, with positive weights only, by one
   unit of layer l + 1 that is on wherever a member of the family is on. Essay: "pale, wavy, and head-side ear
   neurons all feed one hanging-ears neuron".
The cleanliness list so far is eps(N) = (eps_2, eps_3). Entries for Q1, Q4 and Q5 are not defined in this revision:
those are used only as exact conditions. N is **perfectly clean under D39** (strict or broad) when Q1 to Q5 hold,
with Q2 in that form.
Comment: what D39 does not settle. (a) Criterion C4: families without exact symmetry (Definition D38, comment). Two
routes: families as the sets that one coarse reader summarises (Q5 read backwards), or as maximal sets of pairwise
apart units that share a reader. (b) Strict or broad Q2. (c) Two candidates from the essay were set aside because, as
stated there, they need inputs: the neuron basis as the rotation in which few units carry most activity, and
"generalization should be local" (it needs a distance between inputs that N does not supply). Both may have forms that
use only N; none is proposed here. (d) The entries depend on X. Two half-spaces whose normals are not antiparallel are
both on far out in R^d, so Q2 and Q3 can fail on R^d and hold on a bounded X. X is part of the kind of N, as the
trunk's "network of the same kind" already requires; which X is right for a given kind is not settled here.

**Remark A.5.1 (the networks of Part B under D39).** For the toy networks, X is R^d or the convex hull of the mix's
support (the smallest convex domain that holds the mix). Each verdict below holds for both, except the broad
form of Q2, which needs finite peaks and is read on the hull. A failure is shown by a
point of the hull where both units are on. (The check `model/ta5_principles.py` repeats these by exact arithmetic.)

| Network | Symmetry | Q1 | Q2 strict | Q2 broad | Q3 | Q4, Q5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T20 (relu(x - 1), relu(-x - 1)) | mirror swaps the two units | yes | yes: x > 1 and x < -1 are apart | yes | yes: both read with +1 | nothing to check (L = 1) |
| broken line of Lemma T22a (the teachers of T22 and T23) | moves no unit (the units have distinct thresholds along one direction) | no | empty | empty | no (Remark A.5.2) | nothing to check |
| T32 | 90-degree turns | yes | no: relu(x_1 - 1), relu(x_2 - 1) are both 1 at the mix point (2, 2) | yes: at (2, 0) the first is 1 and the second is off | yes: all reads +1 | nothing to check |
| T33 | 90-degree turns about the x_3 axis | yes | no: relu(x_1 + x_3/2 - 1), relu(x_2 + x_3/2 - 1) are both 1/2 at (1/2, 1/2, 2), the midpoint of the mix points (1, 0, 2) and (0, 1, 2) | not checked | yes | nothing to check |
| T34 | 90-degree turns about the x_3 axis | yes | no: the first two family-A units are both 1 at (1, 1, 2), the midpoint of (2, 0, 2) and (0, 2, 2) | not checked | yes | nothing to check |
| detector networks of Definition D40 | contains the block permutations | yes | yes (Lemma T43a part 2) | yes | yes | L = 1: nothing to check; L >= 2: Q5 yes, Q4 no |

So the strict form of Q2 separates T32 to T34 (whose turned members overlap) from T20, in line with Shonu's guess
("we're likely including some sort of networks which we don't really care about"). The broad form does not separate
T32. Which form is right is the choice (b) above. Q3 excludes the broken-line teachers of T22 and T23 in both forms.
The detector networks are clean on their domain X = {sum of block norms <= 1}; on a product domain such as a box,
two detectors of different blocks are on together, and strict Q2 fails for their families. Theorem T43 shows that
these clean networks keep the hardness of T22.

**Remark A.5.2 (why Q3 excludes the broken line).** The units of Lemma T22a are relu(v^T x - s_(j)) for one direction
v, so any two are nested: both are on at the point of the mix with the largest v^T x, which lies in any X that holds
the mix. The gap reads unit j with weight mu_j - mu_{j-1}, the change of slope at the kink (with mu_0 = 0, so the first
weight is mu_1). In T22, a midpoint's value v^T m_uv lies strictly between v^T x_u and v^T x_v, so the sorted labels
contain 2, 0, 2: the slope goes down and then up, and two units are read with opposite signs. So Q3 fails. Q3 holds
for this network exactly when every weight mu_j - mu_{j-1} (j >= 1) has one sign, that is, when the broken line,
including its flat left tail, is convex or concave on all of R.

**Definition D41 (the target of a unit, the votes of a reader, the use of a unit) (proposed; node R-cleannet,
PENDING).** Let N be a plain ReLU network in reduced form (Definition D20), with an input domain X (Definition D38)
that is compact and convex with non-empty interior. (A network that is not in reduced form is first put in it; so
everything below is a function of the reduced form.) Let lambda be Lebesgue measure on X. For a hidden unit u with
output h_u = relu(z_u):
1. Its **mass** is M_u = the integral of h_u over X with respect to lambda. The unit is **live** when M_u > 0. The
   **target** of a live unit is the law mu_u on X with density h_u / M_u with respect to lambda. So every input where
   u is on belongs to its target, and an input weighs in proportion to how strongly u fires there.
2. A **reader** of a unit of layer l is a unit r of layer l + 1, or, for l = L, a logit difference y_c - y_c' with
   c < c'. Reader r adds the **votes** a_{r,v}(x) = W_{rv} h_v(x) of all units v of layer l before its own
   nonlinearity (for a logit difference, W_{rv} = W_out[c, v] - W_out[c', v]). Its **cancelled share** at x is
   kappa_r(x) = (sum_v |a_{r,v}(x)| - |sum_v a_{r,v}(x)|) / sum_v |a_{r,v}(x)|, and kappa_r(x) = 0 when every vote is 0.
3. The **use** of a live unit u of layer l is omega_u = M_u |col_u|, with col_u the column of W_{l+1} at u, or, for
   l = L, the column of P_perp W_out at u (the part of the column that changes logit differences; P_perp as in Fact
   F11). The **read share** of a reader r in u is pi_{ru} = |W_{ru}| / sum_{r'} |W_{r'u}|, the sum over all counted
   readers r' of u, and pi_{ru} = 0 when that sum is 0. The counted readers of u are the live units of layer l + 1,
   or, for l = L, all logit differences (a unit of layer l + 1 that is never on passes no vote further, so it is not
   counted).
Comment. By Lemma T45a, kappa_r(x) lies in [0, 1] and is 0 exactly when the non-zero votes at x have one sign. M_u
is finite because h_u is continuous and X is compact. Every object is a function of the reduced form, so it does not
change when the units of a layer are permuted, or when a unit's incoming weights and bias are scaled by c > 0 and its
outgoing weights by 1/c (both give the same reduced form). Reduced form is needed here: without it, scaling a reader
r by c changes the columns col_u of the units it reads, and with them omega_u and pi_{ru}, while the function stays
the same. (Referee report 21's example: on X = [-1, 1], layer 1 relu(x) and relu(x + 1/2), layer 2
relu(h_1 - h_2 + 1) and relu(c h_1), logits (h_3 + h_4 / c, 0); as c grows, eps_V of D42 computed on these weights
goes to 0.) Each object uses only N and X (criterion C1).
Sources in the essay. The target: "I find it more accurate to think of a neuron as a target, with meaning growing out
from the center in every direction", and "a blind maximum tests the neuron's center, not its breadth" (so the target
is the whole region with its weights, not the peak alone, and not a top slice). The votes: "each input weight votes
for its positive side or its negative side, and the votes add up before the nonlinearity". The base measure lambda is
the one measure that X alone supplies. The essay also warns that feature visualization without transformation
robustness is "reward hacked in deeper layers": on the pixel box, much of a deep unit's target may lie on inputs that
no camera makes. Whether the kind of N should carry a group of small transformations that smooths the base measure is
open (item (d) in the comment of D39).

**Definition D42 (principles of a clean network, second revision) (proposed; node R-cleannet, PENDING).** Let N be a
plain ReLU network in reduced form with L hidden layers, and X as in Definition D41 (compact, convex, non-empty
interior). All sums below run over live units (Definition D41), and a weighted mean whose total weight is 0 (for
example, over an empty set) is 0. The cleanliness list is
eps(N) = (eps_V, eps_G, eps_B), with:
1. **V (votes agree on every target).** eps_V = the omega-weighted mean, over live units u of all hidden layers, of
   sum over the readers r of u of pi_{ru} E_{mu_u}[kappa_r]. So eps_V = 0 when, on the target of every unit, every
   reader of that unit hears votes of one sign.
2. **G (a gate in front).** For a live unit u of a layer l >= 2, g_u = the least, over the units v of layer l - 1
   with W_{uv} > 0, of mu_u({x : h_v(x) = 0}), and g_u = 1 if there is no such v. eps_G = the omega-weighted mean of
   g_u over live units of layers 2 to L. So g_u = 0 when some unit that u reads with a positive vote is on across all
   of u's target.
3. **B (built upon).** For a live unit u of a layer l <= L - 1, b_u = the least, over the units r of layer l + 1 with
   W_{ru} > 0, of mu_u({x : h_r(x) = 0}), and b_u = 1 if there is no such r. eps_B = the omega-weighted mean of b_u
   over live units of layers 1 to L - 1. So b_u = 0 when some reader takes u's vote with a positive sign and is on
   across all of u's target.
N is **perfectly clean under D42** when eps(N) = (0, 0, 0). Each entry lies in [0, 1] (Lemma T45a part 1 for
eps_V; the others are means of measures of sets) and is unchanged by the moves of the comment of D41, so the entries
of two networks of one kind compare (criteria C7, C8). No principle uses a family, so criterion C4 is met by
construction: the ear units of the essay are judged one by one, by their readers.
Sources in the essay, one per principle. V: "A neuron is built from votes"; "the V neuron's negative side is an O";
"an ambulance neuron might have a taxi on its negative pole". A reader may vote against a unit, as long as that unit
is off where the reader's other votes come in. V is also the test for the one failure the essay names, "arbitrary
packing", "neurons learning unrelated things together because they rarely interfere": if u fires on two unrelated
inputs A and B and a reader wants only A, the reader must cancel u at B with another unit that is on at B, so on u's
target that reader hears votes of both signs. And a unit is judged by how its own readers use it, not by our
categories ("Through our categories it was cats and cars, and it looked like a mess; it was a V the whole time"). G:
"often its job is to gate a region of the network"; "Now I think of them more as control flow"; "a neuron in front of
them acts as a gate". B: "a network's parts are built to be read, and built upon, by its downstream readers"; "If you
don't understand exactly what a neuron does, you can study what it connects to, the ecosystem around it".
Comment (what changed from D39, and why). Q1 (moved copies) is no longer a principle, for the reasons of Revision 2
above. Symmetry stays available as a hypothesis (D20, D21, H-clean, H-eq) where a section needs it; the name
"perfectly clean for Gamma" in D20 now means "exactly symmetric for Gamma", and is not D42's "perfectly clean". Q2
(siblings apart) is dropped: siblings may overlap, as broadly tuned real families do (the essay: "it's hard to
overstate how much neurons are analogizers"; "if a weak activation looks unrelated, don't be too worried unless you've
looked at it carefully"). What Q2 aimed at, a reader telling alternatives apart, is part of V. Q3 becomes V, Q4 becomes
G and Q5 becomes B, each graded and judged on targets instead of on all of X. What D42 does not settle: (a) the base
measure (comment of D41); (b) that trained networks score low (Hypothesis H-typical, Part C); (c) G and B ask for one
gate or one reader that covers the whole target; the essay's growth picture ("as a neuron grows, it sprouts offshoots
the way a tree branch sprouts sub-branches") may call for a cover by several units, which is not written here; (d) G
accepts a gate that is on everywhere (D39's Q4 excluded it, but that exclusion is not stable under small changes of
the weights); (e) the entries are not continuous in the weights. G and B are sign conditions: on X = [-1, 1], with v_1 = relu(x + 2)
on everywhere and u = relu(-h_{v_2} + 1/2 + delta h_{v_1}), g_u = 1 for delta <= 0 and g_u = 0 for every delta > 0
(referee report 21). And eps_V can leave 0 under every small change: relu(x) and relu(-x), read with +1 and -1 by the logit
difference, are never on together, but adding delta > 0 to both biases makes them overlap on (-delta, delta), and
eps_V becomes positive (of order delta^2 here, so in this example eps_V is continuous; the zero set is what fails to
be open). So the perfectly clean set is not open; Theorem T45 shows that it contains an open set. A graded G, for example the share of u's positive
votes that come from one unit, would be continuous; it is not written here; (f) the gated units of language models (gate times value, and
the essay's "double negative" regime) are outside plain ReLU networks; (g) at layer L every logit difference is a
reader, so eps_V = 0 there asks that two last-layer units that are on together rank every pair of classes the same
way: (W_out[c, u] - W_out[c', u]) (W_out[c, v] - W_out[c', v]) >= 0 for every c, c'. With many classes this is much
stronger than V at the hidden layers, because it counts pairs of classes that do not matter at x. Which readers
belong at layer L is open.
(h) V counts ordinary inhibition as cancellation, and that conflicts with the essay's own example. Take the essay's
ambulance unit: it reads a car-body unit with a positive weight and a taxi-sign unit with a negative weight ("an
ambulance neuron might have a taxi on its negative pole"). On a taxi both units are on, so on the car-body unit's
target the ambulance reader hears votes of both signs, and eps_V > 0. The essay presents this circuit as clean: the
negative side "tells us what distinction matters at this point in the circuit". So V, read on the targets of the
units a reader reads, penalises the very distinction the essay calls clean. (The sentence above, "a reader may vote
against a unit, as long as that unit is off where the reader's other votes come in", is this paper's reading, not a
sentence of the essay.) A candidate repair, for Shonu's decision (card 3-6): judge each reader's votes on the
reader's OWN target (the essay: "Everything feeding into it makes its own small semantic judgment, and the maximum
is where they all agree most"), with a logit difference read in both orientations, its target having density
(y_c - y_c')_+; and let B, extended to the last layer with logit differences as readers, carry the test for arbitrary
packing (a packed unit has no positive reader that is on across its whole target, because each reader cancels one
half). Check E9 of `model/t45_clean.py` (one hidden layer on the unit square) finds: under D42's V both the ambulance
circuit and a packing circuit score above 0, the packing circuit higher; under the candidate, the ambulance circuit
has B = 0 and a smaller, still positive V, the packing circuit has B > 0, the teachers of T22 and T23 still score
V > 0, and T20 and T32 still score 0. So the candidate separates the two circuits by B, not by V. Theorem T45 holds
for the candidate too (margin-clean networks have kappa_r = 0 at every input), and so do the verdicts of Remark A.5.3
for V; the extended B is new and its verdicts for the Part B networks are not written here.

**Remark A.5.3 (the networks of Part B under D42).** Take any compact convex X with non-empty interior that holds
the mix (for example a ball around it). The verdicts below hold for every such X. (The check `model/t45_clean.py` repeats the
sign arguments in exact arithmetic and the measure of the D40 case numerically.)

| Network | eps_V | eps_G | eps_B | Perfectly clean under D42? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T20 | 0: its reader reads both units with +1 | 0 (L = 1) | 0 (L = 1) | yes |
| teachers of T22 and T23 (broken lines of Lemma T22a) | > 0 (below) | 0 (L = 1) | 0 (L = 1) | no |
| T32, T33, T34 | 0: every read is +1 | 0 (L = 1) | 0 (L = 1) | yes (D39's strict Q2 excluded them) |
| detector networks of D40, L = 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | yes |
| detector networks of D40, L >= 2 | 0 | > 0: g_f = 1 - 1/(kappa m) | 0 | no |

Broken lines: let x* be the point of the mix with the largest v^T x. Every unit relu(v^T x - s_(j)), j <= n - 1, is
on at x* with margin, so all of them are on in a neighbourhood U of x* in X, and U has positive measure because X is
convex with non-empty interior. Remark A.5.2 gives, for the teacher of T22, a reader that reads two of them with
opposite signs. For the teacher of T23 the first logit difference has the slope changes (-1, 0, -1, 0, 6) along v
(with its sixth point last), so it too reads two units with opposite signs. So kappa_r > 0 on U, and U has positive
mass under every target, and eps_V > 0. (A broken line of Lemma T22a with convex or concave labels reads every unit
with one sign and has eps_V = 0, Remark A.5.2: the verdict is about these two teachers, not every broken line.) Detector networks with L >= 2: each
layer-1 unit is read by f with weight 1, and f is on wherever that unit is on, so b = 0; the copies above f read the
unit below, which is on across their targets, so their g is 0. On the domain of D40 the layer-1 units are apart (Lemma T43a part 2), so on the region of d_(j,i) the output h_f
equals d_(j,i), and the mass of h_f there is the integral of d_(j,i) over X. A rotation Q inside block j with
Q^T x~_i = x~_i' keeps the block norms, so it maps X onto X and keeps lambda, and d_(j,i) composed with Q is d_(j,i');
so the integrals of d_(j,i) and d_(j,i') are equal, and a permutation of the blocks does the same across blocks. Each
