w^T x + b <= -1 at every other vertex point. A bad pair has at most one vertex in the clique, so at its midpoint
w^T x + b <= 0. So Delta_B* = 2 at the clique's vertices and at no other point is it non-zero; every midpoint and every
clique vertex is fitted exactly (l1), and each of the other N_V - kappa vertices costs l_0. So L(B*) = Gamma.
Any build with L(B) < Gamma + 1/16 gives a colorful clique. Let C = {v : Delta_B(x_v) > delta}. If |C| <= kappa - 1, then
at least N_V - kappa + 1 vertex points have Delta_B <= delta < 2, and there l(Delta_B; 2) >= l(delta; 2) >= l_0 - delta
by (l2) and (l3). So L(B) >= (N_V - kappa + 1)(l_0 - delta) = Gamma + l_0 - 1/16 >= Gamma + 1/16. If C holds a bad pair
u, v, the midpoint step gives Delta_B(m_uv) > delta > 0, and by (l4), cosh z >= 1 + z^2 / 2 and
log(1 + y) >= y / (1 + y), the loss there is at least log cosh(delta / 2) >= delta^2 / 12 (delta <= 1). With weight M
this gives L(B) >= N_V + 1 > Gamma + 1/16. So C has at least kappa vertices, no two of the same color, every two
adjacent: C is a colorful clique of exactly kappa vertices.
The reduction. Run the algorithm with eps = 1 / (32 Z). If G has a colorful clique, inf D_P <= Gamma / Z, so the
returned B has L(B) <= Gamma + 1/32 < Gamma + 1/16, and C is a colorful clique. If G has none, no set C is one. So the
answer is "yes" exactly when the set C of the returned build (computed with rational arithmetic) is a colorful clique
of kappa vertices. The reduction takes polynomial time, so a polynomial algorithm for TRUNK-1 decides Multicolored
Clique, which gives part 1. In the reduction d = 2 kappa and S is polynomial in |V|, so a running time
rho(d) S^{o(d)} becomes rho(2 kappa) |V|^{o(kappa)}, which gives part 2.
(4) The mix has n >= N_V points. If G has a colorful clique, a build with D_P(B) <= (1 + 1 / (16 n)) inf D_P has
L(B) <= Gamma + Gamma / (16 n) < Gamma + 1/16, since Gamma < N_V <= n (l_0 < 1; for D2, Gamma = N_V - kappa). So C is a
colorful clique, and the same decision procedure works.
(3) For D2_P the per-point loss is (f - t)^2 / 4. It satisfies (l1) and (l2); on f <= delta <= 1 its slope toward
t = 2 is at most 1 in absolute value, so l(delta; 2) >= l(0; 2) - delta with l(0; 2) = 1 >= 1/8; and at label 0 it is
at least delta^2 / 4 >= delta^2 / 12 when f > delta. Also l(0; 2) = 1 gives Gamma = N_V - kappa < N_V + 1 - 1/16. The
same constants and steps apply. QED.
Lean: `mono_mid_ge_min` (the midpoint step), `broken_line_interp` (the teacher). The reduction itself is not in Lean:
complexity classes and running times are not in the Lean library in usable form.

**Remark B.T.3 (what the theorems leave open, and the decisions they force).** Theorem T23 shows that "the least"
need not exist (three logits, one hidden layer, width 2). Theorem T20 shows that "least at every k" and "the B_k nest"
cannot both hold for every network, already for one hidden layer and two logits. Theorem T22 shows that "least",
"fast" and "for every network and every mix" cannot all hold unless P = NP; under the Exponential Time Hypothesis no
algorithm with running time rho(d) S^{o(d)} exists. Theorem T19 shows that the least exists for two logits, one
hidden layer and a finite mix, and Theorem T21 gives an exact rule there for D2 (cost near n^{d k}) and a reduction to
finitely many convex problems for D_P. Each theorem's premises are the places where a choice can be made; `DECISIONS.md`
sections 2 and 3 list them. The setting of the hard instances is not that of real images: their points are
artificial and their teacher has one unit fewer than the number of points. A property of real networks or real mixes that excludes such
instances is one way out, and it has to be named before it can be proved.

## B.C The new trunk: a goal, no data, and what "best" can mean

This section starts the work on the trunk T\*\* (Part 0; `DECISIONS.md` section 1). T\*\* takes a network N, a goal
G and sizes (k_1, ..., k_L), and asks for the best build for G by a rule that reads only N and G. The first question
is what "best" can mean when no input data is given. Plan: `~/.claude/plans/okay-i-think-last-fancy-cosmos.md`.

**Definition D18 (goal; goal score on an input law).** A **goal** is a vector g in R^{n_y} with g >= 0 and g != 0:
how much each of N's output classes matters. The **generalist** goal is g = 1. For an input law mu and a build B, the **goal-weighted law** is mu^g(dx) = w_g(x) mu(dx) / E_mu w_g, with w_g(x) = sum_c g_c q_c(x) and q(x) = softmax(y_N(x))
(inputs count in proportion to how much N assigns them to the goal's classes). The **goal score of B on mu** is
S_{mu, g}(B) = E_{mu^g} KL(q(x) || softmax(y_B(x))). That a goal acts by reweighting inputs, and not inside the
pointwise loss, is a choice (node R-goal, PENDING). Since every q_c(x) > 0 and g != 0, w_g(x) > 0 for every x. For
the generalist goal, S_{mu, 1} = D_mu (Definition D7).

**Definition D19 (well-trained on a labelled law).** A labelled law Q is an input law mu with a label law y | x. A
network N is **well-trained on Q** if it minimises the expected cross-entropy E_Q[-log softmax(y_N(x))_y] among all
networks of its kind. It is **optimal on Q** if it minimises this among all measurable maps from inputs to probability
vectors. Optimal implies well-trained.

**Lemma T24a (a network is optimal exactly on its own labels) (under: none).** For every input law mu, let Q_mu label
each x by y drawn from q(x) = softmax(y_N(x)). Then N is optimal on Q_mu, so well-trained on Q_mu. Conversely, if N is
optimal on a labelled law Q with input law mu, then Q = Q_mu (the label law equals q(x) for mu-almost every x). So
"a law on which N is optimal" means the same as "an input law mu, labelled by N".
Proof. For a labelled law Q with label law r(x) and any map p from inputs to probability vectors,
E_Q[-log p_y(x)] = E_mu [H(r(x)) + KL(r(x) || p(x))] (Gibbs's identity). This is least exactly when p = r for
mu-almost every x. With r = q this gives the first claim. If N is optimal on Q, then q = r for mu-almost every x,
which is the converse. QED.
Lean: none, by hand. Gibbs's inequality for one input is the non-negativity of KL, used throughout; the integral
step is standard.

**Theorem T24 (the score on the training law is not fixed by the network) (under: none).** Let N be the network of
Theorem T20 (d = 1, n_y = 2, logits (T(x), 0), T(x) = relu(x - 1) + relu(-x - 1)). Its two hidden units are mirror
images under x -> -x, and its readout gives them equal weight, so N is equivariant under the mirror. Take the
generalist goal and builds of width 1.
1. Let mu_1 be uniform on {-3, ..., 3} and mu_2 uniform on {0, 1, 2, 3}. N is optimal on Q_{mu_1} and on Q_{mu_2}
   (Lemma T24a). For S_{mu, 1} = D_mu and also for D2_mu, no build is best for both mu_1 and mu_2.
2. For D2, the same holds for two laws that are themselves mirror-symmetric: mu_3 with weights proportional to
   (1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 1, 1) and mu_4 with weights proportional to (3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3) on -3, ..., 3. Every best build
   for mu_3 has a unit equal on {-3, ..., 3} up to scale to relu(x - 14/11) or relu(-14/11 - x). Every best build for
   mu_4 has a unit whose data vector is non-zero at exactly one of the points x = 3 or x = -3.
3. So no rule that reads only N and g returns a best build for the score on the training law, for every law on which N
   is optimal (by Lemma T24a: for every input law), even for a mirror-equivariant N and, in the D2 case,
   mirror-symmetric laws.
Proof. (1) Under mu_2 the points are 0, 1, 2, 3, where T = (0, 0, 1, 2) = relu(x - 1). The build with gap relu(x - 1)
has value 0, so the best value is 0, reached only by builds whose gap equals T at these four points. Take a width-1 gap
alpha relu(w x + b) + gamma equal to (0, 0, 1, 2) at 0, 1, 2, 3. A constant gap (w = 0 or alpha = 0) cannot be equal
to it. Otherwise, with t = -b / w and beta = alpha |w|, the second differences at x = 1 and x = 2 are beta h_t(1) = 1
and beta h_t(2) = 0 (identity of T20), so t lies in (0, 1]. If w < 0 the gap is beta relu(t - x) + gamma, constant
for x >= t, so it takes one value at x = 2 and x = 3, but T takes 1 and 2 there. So w > 0 and the gap is
beta relu(x - t) + gamma. At x = 0 this gives gamma = 0, at x = 1 it gives beta (1 - t) = 0, so t = 1, and then
beta = 1. So the gap is relu(x - 1) on all of R.
So the only best build for mu_2 (as a function) is relu(x - 1). Under mu_1 a best build exists (Theorem T19), and a
build whose unit is equal on P up to scale to relu(x - 1) is not best, by Theorem T20 part 2 (for D_P by the certified
bound, for D2 exactly: 85/26 > 16/5). So no build is best for both. The same holds in every input dimension, by placing
the points on a line (as in T20 part 4).
(2) For a unit relu(x - t) with the kink t in one of the eight pieces cut by the points (or at a point), the data
vector on {-3, ..., 3} is affine in t, the best (alpha, gamma) solves 2 x 2 linear equations, and the least weighted
residual V(t) is a rational function of t on each piece. The units relu(t - x) give the mirrored values, because both
laws and T are mirror-symmetric, and a constant unit gives the constant build. Write V for the residual with the unnormalised weights (the score is V divided by 4 times the total weight). The exact
minimum of V over every piece (critical points and ends, computed exactly in `model/t24_score.py`) is as follows.
For mu_3 it is 46/11, at t = 14/11 only. By hand: for t in (1, 2) the unit is zero at x <= 1, so
V >= min over gamma of [(gamma - 2)^2 + (gamma - 1)^2 + 9 gamma^2] = 46/11 (at gamma = 3/11), with equality only if the
unit fits x = 2, 3 exactly: alpha (2 - t) = 8/11 and alpha (3 - t) = 19/11, which forces t = 14/11. Every other piece
and the constant build give strictly more (next value 235/56). For mu_4 it is 6, reached exactly when the kink lies in
[2, 3), where the data vector is a positive multiple of the indicator of x = 3. By hand: such a unit fits x = 3
exactly, and the rest gives min over gamma of [3 (gamma - 2)^2 + (gamma - 1)^2 + 3 gamma^2 + (gamma - 1)^2] = 6 (at
gamma = 1). At t = 3 the unit is zero on the points, the build is constant and V = 90/11, so 6 is only approached
there. Every other piece gives strictly more (next value 585/94). The two sets of units do not meet. (3) A rule that reads only N and g
returns one build for both laws of part 1 (or of part 2), and no build is best for both. By Lemma T24a, "every law on
which N is optimal" is "every input law, labelled by N", so part 3 says: no such rule is best for every input law. QED.
Lean: `t20_d2_gap_a`, `t20_d2_competitor` (the D2 inequalities of part 1). The rational minimisation of part 2 is in the check; it is not in
Lean (sums of rational functions on eight pieces).

**Corollary T24.1 (the worst case over consistent laws is the worst single input) (under: none).** For every network N,
goal g and build B, the supremum of S_{mu, g}(B) over all input laws mu (each labelled by N; by Lemma T24a these are
exactly the laws on which N is optimal) equals sup over x of KL(q(x) || softmax(y_B(x))). This does not depend on g:
under the worst case, every goal gives the same score.
Proof. By Lemma T24a, N is optimal on Q_mu for every mu, in particular for the point mass at any x, where mu_g is that
same point mass (w_g(x) > 0), so S equals KL at x. Every S_{mu, g}(B) is an average of these values, so it is at most
their supremum. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (an average is at most the supremum).

**Remark B.C.1 (what T24 forces).** The trunk T\*\* asks for a score defined from N and G alone. Theorem T24 and its
corollary sort the ways to get one. (ii) Score on the training law, with "well-trained" a property of the pair (N, Q):
being optimal on Q does not fix the best build (T24), not even for a mirror-equivariant network and mirror-symmetric
laws (T24 part 2, for D2). By Lemma T24a, optimality puts no condition on the input law at all, so (ii) needs a
property that restricts the input law, for example one that comes from how the network
was trained (the old log's per-neuron imprints of SGD, `PAPER.md` Statement 35.2, evidence only), or one that singles
out natural images. (iii) Worst case over every law on which N is optimal: this is the worst single input over the
whole input space (Corollary T24.1). It is defined from N alone, but it is driven by inputs that are not images, and
it ignores the goal, because the goal of D18 acts by reweighting inputs. To keep the goal, (iii) needs a pointwise
loss that carries g (a new definition, node R-goal).
(i) An intrinsic score: an input law, or a comparison on N's own units, built from N by a fixed rule. Data-free
distillation builds input laws from a network alone (literature table), but by optimisation with free choices
(priors, step counts, statistics of normalisation layers); we know of no rule that is fixed by N with no free choices.
A candidate must be stated before anything can be proved under it. The choice was node R-score of
`DECISIONS.md`. Shonu decided it by making a mix an input of the trunk (T\*\*\*): the score is KL on the given mix.

**Definition D20 (perfectly clean network, for a symmetry group) (proposed; node R-cleannet, PENDING).** Let Gamma be
a finite group that acts on inputs by orthogonal matrices rho_0(gamma) (for images: rotations by multiples of 90
degrees and reflections of the pixel grid, which permute pixels exactly; finer rotations do not, see node R-plane; in
one input dimension, the mirror x -> -x). First put N in **reduced form**: delete every hidden unit that is not read (its column in the next layer's weights,
or in W_out, is zero; deleting it does not change the function), merge units with equal (w, b) (adding their outgoing
weights), and rescale every unit with (w, b) != 0 to |(w, b)| = 1, moving the positive scale into its outgoing weights
(relu is positively homogeneous). A plain ReLU network N in reduced form, with hidden layers 1, ..., L, weights W_l,
biases b_l and readout (W_out, c), is **perfectly clean for Gamma** if Gamma acts faithfully on the units of layer 1
(no gamma other than the identity fixes every unit of layer 1) and:
1. (Families.) For every hidden layer l there is a group homomorphism pi_l from Gamma to the permutation matrices of
   layer l such that W_l rho_{l-1}(gamma) = pi_l(gamma) W_l and pi_l(gamma) b_l = b_l, with rho_l = pi_l. Then
   the layer map commutes with Gamma: relu(W_l rho_{l-1}(gamma) h + b_l) = pi_l(gamma) relu(W_l h + b_l). A **family**
   is an orbit of units under pi_l. Each member is the template unit moved by gamma.
2. (Readers.) The readout treats every family symmetrically: W_out pi_L(gamma) = sigma(gamma) W_out and
   sigma(gamma) c = c for a group homomorphism sigma from Gamma to the permutations of the classes (sigma = identity
   for classes that do not change under Gamma).
3. (Built to be read.) Every hidden unit is read. In reduced form this holds by construction; it is listed because it
   is the essay's phrase.
This states the symmetry part of the essay's "clean" (families of moved copies, read the same way by their readers;
the Distill equivariance work in the literature table) for a whole network. It is the whole-network form of H-clean,
H-read and H-eq, with each unit's own relu in place of a shared gate. It does not cover families without an exact
symmetry (the essay's ear neurons are an example). The group is part of the definition: the faithfulness condition
rules out a group that acts only on input coordinates the network ignores (which would make every network
perfectly clean). Without reduced form the definition would depend on how units are scaled: relu(2x) + 2 relu(-x) is
mirror-invariant as a function, and becomes perfectly clean only after rescaling. Whether the hard instances of
Theorem T22 can be made perfectly clean for a non-trivial group is open; if they can, T22's conflict holds inside the
clean class too.

**Definition D21 (cleanliness distance, from the weights) (proposed; node R-cleannet, PENDING).** For a network N in
reduced form and a group Gamma as in D20 (Gamma is an input of eps; in T\*\*, eps(N) means eps_Gamma(N) for the
symmetry group of the input domain, for images the pixel-grid symmetries),
eps_Gamma(N) = min over the homomorphisms pi_l, sigma of the largest of the relative defects
|W_l rho_{l-1}(gamma) - pi_l(gamma) W_l| / |W_l|, |pi_l(gamma) b_l - b_l| / (|b_l| + |W_l|),
|W_out pi_L(gamma) - sigma(gamma) W_out| / |W_out| and |sigma(gamma) c - c| / (|c| + |W_out|),
over every layer l and every gamma in Gamma (Frobenius norms), and +infinity if Gamma does not act faithfully on the
units of layer 1 through the minimising pi_1. It uses only the weights. It is 0 exactly when N is perfectly clean for
Gamma (D20), because the minimum over the finitely many homomorphisms is reached. (It jumps when a unit's outgoing
weights reach zero, because reduced form deletes the unit; a continuous version is left for the bound of T\*\*.) The bound promised by T\*\* for eps > 0 is to be stated in terms of eps_Gamma(N).
Example: the network of Theorems T20 and T24 is perfectly clean for the mirror group {x, -x} (pi swaps its two units,
sigma is the identity), so eps = 0 for it. So Theorem T24 is a statement about a perfectly clean network.

## B.Z The zoom: folds of the network's own units, chosen by the mix

The trunk is now T\*\*\* (`DECISIONS.md` section 1): the mix P is an input again (Shonu: "the generalist mix and a
developer-defined mix are ultimately just mixes in general"), and Shonu's picture of the product is a **zoom**: from a
sample, "fold up the neurons and choos[e] which neurons to fold". This section makes the zoom a mathematical object
and asks whether the best builds of T\*\*\* are zooms.

**Definition D22 (fold) (proposed; node R-fold).** This section is for networks with one hidden layer (L = 1). Let N
have hidden units h_i(x) = relu(z_i(x)), z_i(x) = w_i^T x + b_i, i = 1, ..., n. A **fold** of a group S of these
units is a unit relu(sum_{i in S} m_i z_i(x) - tau) with every m_i >= 0 and tau >= 0: a unit whose pre-activation is a
non-negative mix of the group's pre-activations, with its threshold possibly raised (no new positive offset).
Equivalently (by expanding the sum), a fold of S is relu(w^T x + b) with (w, b) in the closed convex cone spanned by
the vectors (w_i, b_i), i in S, and the vector (0, -1). Theorem T29 shows that, when the members of S have a common silent
input (Z_S not empty) and inputs range over all of R^d, these are exactly the single ReLU units that fire only where
some member of S fires. A build is a **fold build** if every
hidden unit is a fold of some group. It is close in spirit to Definition D10's non-negative units (a detector made of
detectors) and to the essay's coarse unit ("one 'curves & loops' neuron instead of ten curve detectors"); a fold is a
single ReLU unit, while a non-negative sum of the members' outputs is not one (Proposition T1').

**Remark B.Z.0 (why non-negative and no new offset).** Both conditions are needed to keep a fold from reading what N
does not use. Add to the network of Theorem T25 a third unit relu(x_2 - 100) with output weight (delta, 0),
delta != 0. It never fires on the mix of T25 (there x_2 <= 2), so N is unchanged on P, and N stays perfectly clean for
the mirror (the new unit is fixed by it). With a free offset, the fold relu(z_3 + 100) = relu(x_2) would copy N on P,
as in T25. With a negative weight, the fold relu(-z_3) = relu(100 - x_2) equals 100 - x_2 on P, and with output
weight -1 and offset 100 it again gives x_2 on P. With m >= 0 and tau >= 0, a fold of this unit is relu(m (x_2 - 100) - tau),
which is 0 on P. (Pointed out by referee report 14.)

**Definition D23 (zoom, cut, switching cost).** A **zoom** of N (with L = 1) is a rooted tree whose leaves are N's hidden
units and whose internal nodes each have at least two children, together with, for every node v, a fold of the
group S_v of leaves below v (its non-negative mix m_v; a leaf carries its own unit), an output weight vector
a_v in R^{n_y} and an output offset c_v in R^{n_y}. A **cut** is a set of nodes that meets every root-to-leaf path exactly once. The build of a cut C is
y_C(x) = sum_{v in C} (a_v relu(m_v^T z_{S_v}(x)) + c_v): a fold build in which each unit reads only its own group,
and the groups of a cut are disjoint. It has |C| hidden units. Switching from cut C to cut C'
changes only the nodes in C and C' that differ, so it costs a number of operations proportional to that difference.
That can be of the order of n (for example from the root to all leaves), the same as writing out the new build; a
stored table of least builds, one per width, switches at the same cost. What a tree saves is storage, because nodes
are shared between cuts. The zoom is **exact for P** at the widths it serves if, for each width k in a stated set,
some cut of size k, with the stored node parameters (including the node offsets c_v, summed over the cut), gives a
least build of width k (least over the class named in the statement). Exactness is a property to prove for each zoom;
in particular the node offsets must fit every served cut at once.

**Remark B.Z.1 (T20 is a zoom, for D2).** In Theorem T20, z_1 = x - 1 and z_2 = -x - 1, so a fold of both units is
relu((m_1 - m_2) x - (m_1 + m_2)) with m_1, m_2 >= 0: an outward unit, active only beyond a kink t with |t| >= 1. For D2
the least builds of width 1 are known exactly: the residual sum is 16/5 (times 1/28), reached only by the units
relu(x - 8/5) and relu(-x - 8/5) (exact minimisation over every piece, as in T24 part 2). The first is
relu(10 x - 16) / 10 with 10 x - 16 = 13 z_1 + 3 z_2, a fold; the second is the mirror fold 3 z_1 + 13 z_2. Take the
tree with a root r and the two leaves. The leaves carry N's units with output weights (1, 0) and offsets 0; the root
carries a least width-1 build, with its own output weight and offset (the two cuts {r} and {leaves} share no node, so
the offsets do not interact). So for D2 the least builds at widths 1 and 2 are the two cuts of one zoom. For D_P the
least width-1 build exists (Theorem T19); numerically its kink is near 3/2 (outward, so a fold), but this is not
certified here. In one input dimension the group condition is empty, so this example does not test it.

**Theorem T25 (a least build need not be a fold, even for a perfectly clean network and a symmetric mix) (under:
none).** Let d = 2 and let N have the two hidden units relu(x_1 - 1) and relu(-x_1 - 1), logits (T(x_1), 0) with
T(s) = relu(s - 1) + relu(-s - 1). Let P be uniform on the seven points (s, T(s)), s = -3, ..., 3. Let Gamma be the
mirror (x_1, x_2) -> (-x_1, x_2).
1. N is perfectly clean for Gamma (Definition D20), and P is invariant under Gamma.
2. The build of width 1 with gap relu(x_2) has D_P = 0 and D2_P = 0, so it is a least build of width 1.
3. Every fold build of width 1 has D_P > 0 and D2_P > 0. So no least build of width 1 is a fold build.
Proof. (1) Gamma acts by rho_0 = diag(-1, 1), which is orthogonal. With W_1 the rows (1, 0) and (-1, 0) and b = (-1, -1),
W_1 rho_0 = pi W_1 with pi the swap, and pi b = b. The readout gives both units the weight (1, 0), so
W_out pi = W_out, with sigma the identity. The swap is not the identity, so Gamma acts faithfully on the units, and
both units are read. In reduced form the units are rescaled by the same positive number, which keeps all of this.
(The reduced form also keeps the function.) The point (s, T(s)) goes to (-s, T(s)) = (-s, T(-s)), which is in P. (2) On
P, x_2 = T(x_1) >= 0, so relu(x_2) = T(x_1), the gap of N, at every point of P; by (l1) the value is 0. (3) A fold
build of width 1 has gap alpha relu(m_1 z_1 + m_2 z_2 + beta) + gamma, which depends on the input only through x_1.
On P the first coordinates are -3, ..., 3, each once, and N's gap there is T. So its value equals the value of the
same build in Theorem T20 (d = 1, P uniform on -3, ..., 3), which is at least the least value there. That least value
is reached (Theorem T19) and is positive. Indeed, value 0 needs the gap to equal T at all seven points (by (l1)), so
its second differences at -2, ..., 2 equal those of T, which are 1 at -1 and at 1 and 0 elsewhere. A width-1 gap has
second differences beta h_t, whose support is at most two adjacent points (identity of T20), and -1 and 1 are not
adjacent. So no width-1 build has value 0. QED.
Lean: `t25_mirror` (the equivariance identities of part 1), `relu_second_diff` (the second-difference step of part 3).

**Remark B.Z.2 (what T25 means, and the decision it forces).** The unrestricted least build copies N on the mix by
reading an input feature that N does not use at all (x_2), because on this mix that feature happens to equal the
answer. It is best on P and has nothing to do with N's units: it uses a feature that is correct on P but not part of
N's computation. A fold build in the sense of D22 reads the input only through non-negative mixes of N's own
pre-activations, so it cannot use x_2 here, and Remark B.Z.0 shows that a fold of a unit that is silent on P alone is silent on P too (a fold of a group
that mixes silent and active units can still vary with the silent unit's input on P). So T\*\*\*'s "built from any new units" and Shonu's zoom ("fold up the neurons") disagree. The ways out are
T25's premises: (a) restrict builds to folds of N's units (the zoom, D22, D23); (b) keep any new units but require a
property of the mix that removes such accidental features (for example, that the part of the input N does not use is
independent of the part it uses); (c) keep any new units and accept builds that use such features. This is node
R-fold of `DECISIONS.md`. Two cautions. Under (a), "a fold cannot use a feature N does not use" is shown here only for
these two examples; a general statement needs a definition of "the features N uses on P" and a proof. Under (b), the
property is not shown to make the least build a fold: with an independent extra input, averaging over it can let one
unit imitate two kinks (Jensen: E (g - T)^2 = E (gbar - T)^2 + E Var(g | x_1)), so (b) is a conjecture that may fail.

### Why folds: the project's goals, made formal

Shonu asked for the case for folds to come from the project's goals, not from design rules: "based on us not wanting
to do training ... based on us wanting to fold up something which already exists and something that people download
once and can do a bunch of different times". The three goals are stated below as conditions on a rule, and the
theorems after them show what each condition forces. Everything here is for one hidden layer, as in D22 and D23.

**Definition D24 (three conditions on a rule).** A rule takes N, a mix P and a width k (the input size d, the
number of logits n_y and one hidden layer are fixed), and returns a set of builds.
1. (G1, the network's weights are used.) The rule **uses N's weights** if there are two networks N, N' whose logits
   agree at every point of some mix P, but for which the rule returns different builds on P. A rule that returns the
   same builds whenever the logits agree on P depends on N only through N's answers on P; call it a **distillation
   rule** (it fits a small network to N's labels). G1 is a necessary condition for "using the training already in N";
   it does not single out a class of builds.
2. (G2, a use adds no new distinction.) A unit u **reads only through N** if u(x) = u(x') whenever z(x) = z(x'),
   where z = (z_1, ..., z_n) are N's pre-activations. A rule satisfies G2 if every unit of every build it returns
   reads only through N (a choice to state it unit by unit: a sum of units can read only through N while its units do
   not). G2 restricts nothing when N's first-layer weights span R^d (then z determines x), which is the usual case.
3. (G3, coarse units cover fine units.) A single ReLU unit u **covers** a group S of N's units if u(x) = 0 at every x
   in R^d where every member of S is silent (z_i(x) <= 0 for all i in S): the coarse unit fires only where some fine
   unit fires (one reading of the essay's recursive generalization: a coarse neuron covers its offshoots).

**Theorem T26 (any new units give a distillation rule; folds use the weights) (under: none).**
1. For every class of builds that does not depend on N, in particular all builds of width k, the least value of D_P
   (and of D2_P) and the set of least builds depend on N only through the logits y_N(x) at the points of P. So
   "the least build over any new units" is a distillation rule.
2. "The least build over fold builds of width 1" uses N's weights. Let N_1 be the network of T20 (units relu(x - 1),
   relu(-x - 1), output weights (1, 0), offset 0) and N_2 the network with units relu(x + 3), relu(x + 1), relu(x - 1),
   output weights (-1, 0), (1, 0), (1, 0) and offset (2, 0). They have the same logits at every point of
   {-3, ..., 3}. For the mix P' on these points with weights proportional to (3, 3, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1), the least D2 over
   fold builds of width 1 (one group: the whole hidden layer) is 26/7 for N_1 and 84/11 for N_2 (residual sums with
   the unnormalised weights). Different least values mean the two sets of least builds are disjoint.
Proof. (1) D_P(B) = sum_j pi_j KL(softmax(y_N(x_j)) || softmax(y_B(x_j))), and D2 likewise, so N enters only through
the values y_N(x_j). (2) N_2's gap at x = -3, ..., 3 is 2 - relu(x + 3) + relu(x + 1) + relu(x - 1) =
(2, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2) = T. Folds (Definition D22) are relu(w x + b) with (w, b) in the cone of the members' (w_i, b_i),
with b lowered. For N_1 the cone of (1, -1) and (-1, -1), lowered, is {b <= -|w|}: rising units with kink t >= 1,
falling units with kink t <= -1, and the zero unit. For N_2 the cone of (1, 3), (1, 1), (1, -1), lowered, is
{w >= 0, b <= 3 w}: rising units with kink t >= -3, and the zero unit. On each piece cut by the points the least
weighted residual is a rational function of the kink, minimised exactly over the allowed kinks (`model/t26_weights.py`):
26/7 for N_1 (equal to the least over all width-1 builds) and 84/11 for N_2. QED.
Lean: none, by hand. Part 1 is one line; part 2 is an exact rational minimisation, done in the check.

**Theorem T27 (exact cost of the fold rule) (under: two logits, one hidden layer, a finite mix).** Let P have n_P
points, and let the allowed groups S_1, ..., S_G have at most s members each.
1. The least D_P (and D2_P) over fold builds of width k, each unit a fold of one allowed group, is reached, and equals
   the minimum, over at most (2 G R)^k choices, of a convex problem over a polyhedron, with
   R <= 2 sum_{i=0}^{s'} C(n_P - 1, i) and s' = min(s, d) (the vectors zeta_j span a space of dimension at most
   min(s, d) + 1). For D2 with rational data a least fold build with rational weights exists. So for a fixed list of
   small groups (a zoom over families) the exact rule's cost is polynomial in n_P, with an exponent of order
   min(s, d) k; G^k counts the group choices.
2. For large groups this is no easier than the unrestricted problem: see Proposition T27.1.
Proof. (1) A fold of S is relu(u^T zeta(x)) with u = (m, tau) >= 0 in R^{s+1} and zeta(x) = (z_S(x), -1), a
homogeneous linear function of u. For a unit with output weight alpha, alpha relu(u^T zeta) = s'' relu(|alpha| u^T zeta)
with s'' the sign of alpha, and |alpha| u >= 0, so signs absorb as in T19. For a fixed sign, group and active set A,
the unit's data vector is linear in u on the closed polyhedral cone {u >= 0 : u^T zeta_j >= 0 for j in A,
u^T zeta_j <= 0 otherwise}. As in T19 and T21 the gap vectors form a finite union of closed polyhedral cones (so a
least build exists, by coercivity), each piece is a convex problem, and only active sets of full-dimensional regions
of the arrangement of n_P hyperplanes through 0, restricted to the span of the zeta_j (dimension at most
min(s, d) + 1), are needed; the orthant only removes regions. The D2 rationality is T21 part 3. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (as T21).

**Proposition T27.1 (the hardness of T22 carries over to folds of large groups) (under: none).** There is no
algorithm that, given N with one hidden layer and two logits, a group S of its units, a finite mix and a rational
eps > 0, returns a fold build of width 1 of S within eps of the least such value, in time rho(s) S_in^{o(s)} (S_in the
input bit length), unless the Exponential Time Hypothesis fails; and none in polynomial time unless P = NP.
Proof. Take T22's points, labels, weights and constants (input dimension d = 2 kappa). Let S be the 2 d units
relu(e_l^T x) and relu(-e_l^T x), l = 1, ..., d, and let N be the network of Lemma T22a for the labels t_j - 1^T x_j,
plus the units of S with output weights +1 and -1 (they add back 1^T x, so N's gap equals t_j at every point). The
members of S are all silent only at x = 0, so Z_S = {0} is not empty, and the folds of S are exactly the units
relu(w^T x + b) with b <= 0 (the cone of (+-e_l, 0) and (0, -1)). T22's build for a clique has
b = 1 - 2 / eta <= 0 (eta <= 1), so it is a fold of S, and the other direction of T22's proof holds for every width-1
build, in particular for folds. So T22's reduction goes through for folds of S, with s = 2 d. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (a reuse of T22's reduction).

**Theorem T28 (one download, every mix) (under: none).**
1. A unit relu(w^T x + b) reads only through N if and only if w = W^T m for some m in R^n (W the matrix with rows w_i),
   that is, the unit is relu(m^T z(x) + beta): a fold in the linear-span sense (any signs, any offset).
2. (Small mixes.) If P has at most d + 1 affinely independent points, then for EVERY network N with two logits there
   is a build of width 1 with D_P = 0 and D2_P = 0, found from N's answers on P alone (it does not depend on N's
   weights).
3. (Capacity.) With one fixed group of at most s members for each unit, a fold build of width k has a gap that is
   a one-hidden-layer network on the (s + 1)-dimensional inputs zeta(x), with W = k (s + 2) + 1 numbers in the gap,
   so the class of gaps has pseudo-dimension O(W log W) (Bartlett, Harvey, Liaw and Mehrabian 2019, for a fixed
   architecture with piecewise-linear activations). Choosing a group per unit among G adds O(k log G). A single any-unit relu(w^T x + b) already has
   pseudo-dimension at least d + 1 (its level sets {relu(w^T x + b) > r}, r > 0, are all half-spaces of R^d).
Proof. (1) If w = W^T m, then w^T x + b = m^T z(x) + (b - m^T b_N), a function of z. If w is not in the row space of
W, there is v with W v = 0 and w^T v != 0; then z(x + t v) = z(x) for every t, while w^T (x + t v) + b takes every real
value, so the unit takes two different values on one fibre of z. (2) Let c = min_j Delta_N(x_j). Affinely independent
points let us solve w^T x_j + b = Delta_N(x_j) - c >= 0 for all j. Then relu(w^T x + b) + c equals N's gap on P, and
the value is 0 by (l1). Only the values Delta_N(x_j) were used. (3) The fold build is that network composed with the
fixed map zeta; composing with a fixed map does not raise the pseudo-dimension. The half-space statement is the
classical VC dimension d + 1 of half-spaces in R^d. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (a kernel vector argument; a linear solve; a cited bound).
Comment: part 2 says that for a developer's sample of at most d + 1 affinely independent images (d is the input
size of the layer), the unrestricted problem has a perfect answer for every network, built from its answers alone.
Affine independence is needed: seven collinear points in any dimension keep T20's positive least value. Part 1 shows
that G2 is a real restriction only when N's first-layer weights do not span R^d; in Remark B.Z.0's network they do,
so relu(x_2) passes G2 there. No sample-size theorem is claimed: turning part 3 into one needs a bounded loss, and KL
with unbounded logits is not bounded.

**Theorem T29 (covering units are exactly the folds) (under: none).** Let S be a group of N's units whose common
silent set Z_S = {x in R^d : z_i(x) <= 0 for all i in S} is not empty. A single ReLU unit relu(w^T x + b) covers S
(D24) if and only if
w^T x + b = sum_{i in S} m_i z_i(x) - tau for all x, with m >= 0 and tau >= 0, that is, if and only if it is a fold
of S (Definition D22). If Z_S is empty, every unit covers S.
Proof. If w^T x + b = sum m_i z_i(x) - tau with m, tau >= 0, then on Z_S every z_i <= 0, so w^T x + b <= 0 and the
unit is 0. Conversely, the unit covers S exactly when w^T x + b <= 0 holds on the non-empty polyhedron
{x : w_i^T x <= -b_i, i in S}. By the affine form of Farkas's lemma (literature table) there are m >= 0 with
w = sum m_i w_i and -b >= -sum m_i b_i, i.e. tau = sum m_i b_i - b >= 0. QED.
Lean: `fold_covers` (the direction "a fold covers its group", for finite groups). The converse rests on the cited
lemma.
Comment: a covering unit automatically reads only through N (its w is in the span of the w_i), so G3 implies G2 for
groups with a common silent set. The two conditions of D22 (non-negative mix, offset only lowered) are not choices
once G3 is accepted: they are what "covers" means for a single ReLU unit on all of R^d. The three premises matter:
a non-negative sum of the members' outputs covers S but is not one ReLU unit (Proposition T1'); if Z_S is empty every
unit covers S; and on a bounded domain covering is weaker (on [-3, 3]^2 with S = {relu(x_1 - 1)}, the unit
relu(x_1 + x_2 / 10 - 3/2) covers S and is not a fold).

**Corollary T30 (what the three conditions do) (under: none).** For networks with one hidden layer:
1. The least build over any new units is a distillation rule: it fails G1 (T26 part 1). On mixes of at most d + 1
   affinely independent points it copies every network perfectly from its answers alone (T28 part 2).
2. G3 forces folds: for a group with a common silent set, on all of R^d, the single ReLU units that cover the group are
   exactly its folds (T29). This is the only one of the three conditions that singles out folds.
3. G1 is necessary but not sufficient: folds satisfy it (T26 part 2), and so do other classes that depend on N's weights
   (for example a subset of N's units). G2 is implied by G3 and restricts nothing when N's first-layer weights span R^d.
4. The exact fold rule costs an exponent of order min(s, d) k for groups of at most s members (T27), so it is small
   for a zoom over small families; for large groups it is as hard as the unrestricted problem (Proposition T27.1).
So the case for folds rests on G3, one reading of "fold up what already exists"; the other two conditions rule out
the unrestricted rule but do not single out folds.
Proof. Collect the cited parts. QED.
Lean: none, a collection of the results above.

**Remark B.Z.3 (what this does not show).** It does not show that G1 or G2 force folds (Corollary T30). It does not
show a sample-size advantage (T28 comment). It does not show that folds lose nothing. T25 shows that the best fold
build can be worse on the mix than the best build over any units; T26 part 1 and T28 part 2 say what such a better
build is (an answer that does not use N's weights). Whether, for a perfectly clean network, the least fold build is as
good as the least build over any units, once accidental features of the sample are excluded, is open (and needs a
definition of "accidental"). The essay's crush is evidence
that it may be (the retrained 10-unit 3b layer has one "curves & loops" unit, which looks like a fold of the curve
detectors), but a statement and a proof are not written yet. Everything here is for one hidden layer.

## B.F Fold optimality: what distillation converges to, for clean networks

Shonu's framing (2026-10-25, late night): distillation, trained to the end, converges to the least-KL small network
on the mix. The trunk T\*\*\* asks for that optimum, over any new units. The project's question is what that optimum
is, and the conjecture is that for a clean network it is a fold of the network's own units (the essay: a small model
trained on the same data has coarse versions of the large model's neurons). Folds are not imposed (node R-fold); they
are the conjectured answer.

**Lemma T31 (with a full-rank first layer, every unit is a loose fold) (under: none).** Let N have one hidden layer
with pre-activations z_i(x) = w_i^T x + b_i. If the w_i span R^d, then every unit relu(w^T x + b) equals
relu(m^T z(x) + beta) for some m in R^n and beta in R. So the least build over any new units is the least build over
units that read only N's pre-activations, with any signs and any offset.
Proof. Since the w_i span R^d, w = sum m_i w_i for some m. Then w^T x + b = m^T z(x) + (b - m^T b_N), with b_N the
vector of the b_i. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (one line of linear algebra).
Comment: Theorem T25's failure (the least build reads x_2, which N ignores) needs a first layer that does not span
R^d. With a full-rank first layer the remaining question is narrower: are the least units **covering** folds (D22:
non-negative mix, threshold only raised) of **one family** each? Theorem T20's least width-1 unit for D2,
relu(13 z_1 + 3 z_2), is one (Remark B.Z.1). Conjecture D25 states the general claim.

**Lemma T32a (dual certificates for a piece of builds) (under: none).** Let P put weights pi_i > 0 on n points, let
t in R^n, and let a piece be the set of gap vectors g = sum_j s_j L_j theta_j + gamma 1, with fixed signs s_j, fixed
matrices L_j, theta_j in the closed polyhedral cone {theta : R_j theta <= 0}, and gamma free.
1. If v in R^n has sum_i pi_i v_i = 0 and, for every j, s_j L_j^T (pi v) is a non-negative combination of the rows of
   R_j (pi v is the vector with entries pi_i v_i), then every g in the piece has
   sum_i pi_i (g_i - t_i)^2 >= 2 sum_i pi_i v_i t_i - sum_i pi_i v_i^2.
2. Let K be a closed polyhedral cone of units theta = (w, b) with non-empty interior, and x~_i = (x_i, 1). Every theta
   in K lies in the closure of an open cell {theta in int K : sign(theta^T x~_i) = e_i for all i} for some sign vector
   e with no zero entry, and in the closed cell (all strict inequalities made weak) the data vector of the unit is the
   masked vector (theta^T x~_i if e_i = +1, else 0), equal to relu(theta^T x~_i). So the closed cells of the sign
   vectors whose open cell is not empty cover K, with the right data vectors.
Proof. (1) For a = t - g, sum pi (a - v)^2 >= 0 gives sum pi a^2 >= 2 sum pi v a - sum pi v^2. Here
sum pi v g = gamma sum pi v + sum_j theta_j^T (s_j L_j^T (pi v)) = sum_j mu_j^T (R_j theta_j) <= 0 for the
non-negative coefficients mu_j, so sum pi v a >= sum pi v t. (2) The finitely many hyperplanes theta^T x~_i = 0 cut
int K into open cells, whose closures cover the closure of int K, which is K. In the closure of a cell, theta^T x~_i
>= 0 where e_i = +1 and <= 0 where e_i = -1, so relu(theta^T x~_i) equals the masked value. QED.
Lean: `cert_ineq` (the completing-the-square inequality of part 1; the duality step and part 2 are by hand).
Comment: Theorems T32, T33 and T34 use this lemma. Their checks verify the cone memberships of part 1 exactly (by
Caratheodory, with at most d + 1 generators at a time), confirm each non-empty open cell by a rational interior point,
and confirm each empty one by a Gordan certificate (a non-negative combination of its strict inequality rows equal to
zero), so the list of cells is exact.

**Theorem T32 (the least build of a perfectly clean network need not be made of covering folds) (under: none).** Let
N have the four hidden units relu(x_1 - 1), relu(x_2 - 1), relu(-x_1 - 1), relu(-x_2 - 1) in R^2 and logits
(sum of the four units, 0), so its gap is their sum. N is perfectly clean for the rotation by 90 degrees (Definition D20: the rotation permutes the
four units cyclically and the readout sums them), and its first-layer weights span R^2. Let P be uniform on the eight
points (+-2, 0), (0, +-2), (+-2, +-2), which the rotation permutes. At width 2:
1. some build has D2_P <= 3/80;
2. every build of width 2 whose two hidden units are covering folds of the family (Definition D22) has D2_P >= 1/24.
So no least build of width 2 (for D2) is made of covering folds, and Conjecture D25 is false.
Proof. (1) The build relu(-4/5 x_1 + 4/5 x_2 - 8/5) - relu(-3/10 x_1 + 3/10 x_2) + 8/5 has D2_P = 3/80 exactly
(`model/t32_cover_gap.py`). Both its units point along the diagonal (-1, 1). The first is exactly a covering fold
(b = -(|w_1| + |w_2|)); the second fires on the centre square, where every member of the family is silent. (2) The members'
common silent set is the square |x_1| <= 1, |x_2| <= 1, which is not empty; by Theorem T29 the covering folds are the
units relu(w^T x + b) with b <= -(|w_1| + |w_2|). Absorb each output weight's size into its unit (the covering cone is
a cone), so a build is s_1 relu(theta_1^T x~) + s_2 relu(theta_2^T x~) + gamma with signs s_j. Split by the signs, by
the active set A_j of each unit on P, and by the signs of w_{j,1}, w_{j,2} (which make the covering condition linear):
on each piece the data vector of unit j is linear in theta_j and the constraints are linear, so D2_P is a convex
quadratic over a polyhedron. Every build lies in some piece. For a piece write unit j's data vector as L_j theta_j, with
theta_j in the closed cone {R_j theta <= 0}, and use Lemma T32a. The check finds such a v for every piece (the exact
residual of the least-squares problem on the face where the numerical optimum lies), verifies the two cone
memberships exactly (by Caratheodory, at most three generators at a time), and finds 2 v^T t - |v|^2 >= 4/3 in all
1176 pieces, i.e. D2_P >= 1/24. The list of pieces is exact too: the 24 full-dimensional covering cells are each
confirmed by a rational interior point, and every other sign pattern by a Gordan certificate (a positive combination
of at most four constraint rows equal to zero). Every covering build lies in the closure of one of these cells, with
the same data vector (Lemma T32a part 2). This is an exhaustive, exact computer-assisted proof. QED.
Lean: none, by exhaustive exact enumeration in the check; it is not in Lean (thousands of rational quadratic
programs).

**Theorem T33 (the least build of a perfectly clean network need not be made of broad folds: it can use the family's
negative side) (under: none).** Let N have the four hidden units relu(w_i^T x - 1) in R^3 with
w_i = (1, 0, 1/2), (0, 1, 1/2), (-1, 0, 1/2), (0, -1, 1/2), and logits (sum of the four units, 0). N is perfectly clean
for the rotation by 90 degrees about the x_3 axis (Definition D20), and its first-layer weights span R^3. Let P be the
orbits of (-1, 2, -2), (2, 1, -1) and (1, 0, 2) under that rotation, with weights 3, 1, 2 per point of each orbit
(normalised); P is invariant. At width 1:
1. the build with gap 1 - relu(-x_3 / 2) has D_P = 0 and D2_P = 0 (N's gap on P is 0, 1/2 and 1 on the three
   orbits, at heights -2, -1 and 2);
2. every build of width 1 whose unit is a broad fold of the family (Conjecture D26: relu(sum m_i z_i + beta),
   m >= 0, beta free) has D2_P >= 1/468, and D_P > 0.
So no least build of width 1 (for D2, and for D_P, whose least value is also 0 here) is made of broad folds, and
Conjecture D26 is false.
Proof. (1) At heights -2, -1, 2 the build gives 1 - 1, 1 - 1/2, 1 - 0, which are N's values (exact check,
`model/t33_broad_gap.py`). (2) Since sum m_i w_i = (m_1 - m_3, m_2 - m_4, (sum m_i) / 2) and sum m_i >= |m_1 - m_3| +
|m_2 - m_4|, a unit relu(w^T x + b) is a broad fold exactly when w_3 >= (|w_1| + |w_2|) / 2 (b free). Split this cone by
the signs of w_1, w_2, and the units by their output sign and active set on P: each piece is a convex quadratic over a
closed polyhedral cone, and the check gives every piece an exact dual certificate (Lemma T32a, weighted) with a positive
lower bound; the least is 1/468. The list of
pieces is exact (rational interior points for the cells, Gordan certificates for the empty sign patterns). For D_P: the least value over any builds is 0 (part 1), and every broad
build has D_P > 0, because D_P = 0 forces the gap to equal N's gap at every point of P, which forces D2_P = 0. So no
least build (for D_P) is made of broad folds. QED.
Lean: none, by exhaustive exact enumeration in the check.
Comment: the target rises with height and bends down (it is concave in x_3 on P). Every broad fold leans up
(w_3 >= 0), and one ReLU leaning up with any output sign gives a convex rising or a concave falling profile, never a
concave rising one. The least build uses the unit relu(-x_3 / 2), a non-negative mix of the NEGATED pre-activations:
the family's negative side (the essay: "The negative side tells us what distinction matters").

**Theorem T34 (the least build of a perfectly clean network need not be made of signed folds of one family)
(under: none).** Let N have two families in R^3: A, the units relu(w_i^T x - 1) with w_i = (1, 0, 1/2), (0, 1, 1/2),
(-1, 0, 1/2), (0, -1, 1/2); and B, the units relu(v_k^T x - 1) with v_k = (1, 1, -1/2), (-1, 1, -1/2), (-1, -1, -1/2),
(1, -1, -1/2). Logits (sum of all eight units, 0). N is perfectly clean for the rotation by 90 degrees about the x_3 axis
(each family is an orbit; the readout sums them; in reduced form the two families get different positive scales,
which the rotation preserves), and its first-layer weights span R^3. Let P be
uniform on the orbits of (2, 0, 2), (-1, 2, 0) and (1, -1, 0) (twelve points; N's gap is 2, 3 and 1 on them). At
width 1:
1. the build relu(-11/3 x_1 + 11/9 x_2 - 10/9 x_3 - 44/9) + 16/9 has D2_P = 25/216;
2. every build of width 1 whose unit is a signed fold of one family (Conjecture D27) has D2_P >= 7/60 > 25/216;
3. for D_P: some explicit width-1 build has a D_P value below a lower bound that holds for every build of width 1
   whose unit is a signed fold of one family (both certified with interval arithmetic, `model/t34_kl.py`).
So no least build of width 1 (for D2, and for D_P) is made of signed folds of one family, and Conjecture D27 is false.
Proof. (1) Exact evaluation (`model/t34_signed_gap.py`). (2) The signed folds of one family are the units
relu(w^T x + b) with w in cone(A), -cone(A), cone(B) or -cone(B), and b free. cone(A) = {w_3 >= (|w_1| + |w_2|) / 2}
(as in T33), and cone(B) = {w_3 <= 0, max(|w_1|, |w_2|) <= -2 w_3}, because the vectors (+-1, +-1) are the corners of
the square [-1, 1]^2, whose convex hull is that square. Since |w_1| + |w_2| >= max(|w_1|, |w_2|), cone(A) lies in
-cone(B) and -cone(A) in cone(B), so the union is {|w_3| >= max(|w_1|, |w_2|) / 2}: two convex cones (w_3 >= 0 and
w_3 <= 0), each given by four linear inequalities. The unit of part 1 has |w_3| = 10/9 < 11/6 = max(|w_1|, |w_2|) / 2,
so it is not a signed fold of either family. Split by the cone (two), the output sign and the active set on P: each
piece is a convex quadratic over a closed polyhedral cone, and the check gives every piece an exact dual certificate (Lemma T32a)
with a lower bound of at least 7/60, over an exact list of 636 pieces. (3) The same pieces, with the Fenchel
bound log(1 + e^f) >= s f + H(s): for a rational v meeting the conditions of Lemma T32a part 1 (weighted) and with
s = q - v in (0, 1)^n, where q = sigma(N's gap), every build of the piece has D_P >= sum_i pi_i (H(q_i - v_i) - H(q_i)).
The check finds such a v for every piece and evaluates the bound and the explicit build's D_P with interval
arithmetic (mpmath, 50 digits). QED.
Lean: none, by exhaustive exact enumeration in the check.
Comment: the least unit reads a direction that mixes the two families (it is neither family's positive nor negative
side). With a full-rank first layer it is still a mix of N's pre-activations (Lemma T31), but no longer a mix within
one family.

**Corollary T35 (for networks clean in the sense of D20, least builds need not be folds of one family, nor covering
folds of any group) (under: a perfectly clean network for Gamma, a full-rank first layer, a Gamma-invariant mix).**
There exist perfectly clean networks (Definition D20) with full-rank first layers and invariant mixes such that:
1. (T32: R^2, one family of four, width 2, D2.) Every build whose units are covering folds is worse than an explicit
   build (1/24 against 3/80, a relative gap of at least 1/9). The explicit build has one unit that fires where every
   member is silent. In R^2 every direction is a non-negative mix of this family, so this instance tests thresholds
   only.
2. (T33: R^3, one family of four, width 1, D2 and D_P.) No least build is made of broad folds; the least build
   (value 0) reads the family's negative side.
3. (T34: R^3, two families of four, width 1, D2 and D_P.) No least build is made of signed folds of one family; an
   explicit better build has a unit that mixes the two families.
Since covering folds of any group are broad folds of the whole layer (a group's cone lies in the layer's cone), part 2
shows that no least build there is made of covering folds of any group, for D2 and for D_P. On the other hand, with
free thresholds the family structure carries all the content: if the first-layer weights positively span R^d (as in
T32 and T34), every unit is a broad fold of the whole layer, so "folds of any group, threshold free" restricts nothing
(T34's unit is in fact a covering fold of a group that takes units from both families). And T20 shows that on other
instances the least build can be a covering fold. So the statement proved is an existence statement: least builds need
not be folds of one family, nor covering folds of any group.
Proof. Theorems T32, T33, T34; for "any group": a fold of a group S is relu(w^T x + b) with (w, b) in cone(S) and b
lowered, and cone(S) lies in the cone of the whole layer; if the layer's weights positively span R^d, that cone is
R^d and, with b free, every unit is a broad fold. QED.
Lean: none, a collection of the results above.

**Remark B.F.1 (the fork, and what the instances lack).** The claim "for clean networks, distillation converges to
folds of the network's families" fails at eps = 0 when "clean" means D20, for the trunk's own score D_P (T33, T34)
and for D2 (T32, T33, T34). The ways around it are the premises of T32 to T34:
(a) a stronger notion of clean, which these instances fail. The candidate from the essay: a coarse unit of each family
    is itself present in the network ("pale, wavy, and head-side ear neurons all feed one hanging-ears neuron"); none
    of the three networks has one. It needs a definition readable from the weights, and then a check that T32 to T34
    fail under it.
(b) folds as a restriction, accepting a loss at eps = 0: in T32 at least 1/9 relative (1/24 against at most 3/80); in
    T33 from 0 to at least 1/468 (D2); in T34 from at most 25/216 to at least 7/60 (D2).
(c) keep any new units and characterise the optimum directly (the best ReLU-ridge approximation of a sum of ReLU
    ridges), with the explicit builds above (a diagonal pair, a downward unit, a sideways unit) as the first data.
(d) folds of groups that cross families, with free thresholds. Not a way out: when the layer's weights positively
    span R^d this class is every unit (Corollary T35), so it says nothing; with covering thresholds it fails (T33).
(e) the objective: not a way out either, since T33 and T34 hold for D_P, the trunk's score.
(f) larger mixes, more layers, more classes: a counterexample in a special case refutes the general claim, but
    natural mixes and depth may still favour folds in some weaker sense, which would have to be stated first.
This is node R-foldopt of `DECISIONS.md`. Its premises rest on nodes Shonu has not decided (R-cleannet for D20,
R-fullrank, R-symN); option (a) is a proposal to replace R-cleannet.

## B.O What the optimum is in clean networks: symmetry first

Shonu (2026-10-25): "We need to understand what actually is the optimum within clean neural nets ... not just
mathematically but also with some sort of real interpretation." Corollary T35 says what the optimum is not. This
section starts on what it is, beginning with the one structure that clean networks give for free: symmetry.

**Lemma T36 (the objective and the least builds are symmetric) (under: none).** Let Gamma be a finite group acting on
inputs by orthogonal maps rho_0(gamma) and on classes by permutations sigma(gamma). Let the mix P be invariant
(P(rho_0(gamma) x) = P(x)), and let N be equivariant on the support of P: y_N(rho_0(gamma) x) = sigma(gamma) y_N(x)
for every x with P(x) > 0. (This holds when N is perfectly clean for Gamma, Definition D20, since D20 makes every layer
commute with Gamma; only the equivariance is used.) Builds are the one-hidden-layer builds of Definition D15. For a
build B and gamma in Gamma let (gamma . B)(x) = sigma(gamma) y_B(rho_0(gamma)^{-1} x): the build with every unit's
weight w_j replaced by rho_0(gamma) w_j and every output weight a_j and the offset c by sigma(gamma) a_j and
sigma(gamma) c. Then gamma . B is a build of the same widths, D_P(gamma . B) = D_P(B) and D2_P(gamma . B) = D2_P(B).
So Gamma maps least builds to least builds.
Proof. relu((rho_0 w)^T x + b) = relu(w^T rho_0^{-1} x + b), since rho_0 is orthogonal, so gamma . B is the build
described. Substitute x = rho_0 x': P(rho_0 x') = P(x') and y_N(rho_0 x') = sigma y_N(x') on the support of P, so
D_P(gamma . B) = sum_x' P(x') KL(softmax(sigma y_N(x')) || softmax(sigma y_B(x'))), and KL is unchanged when both
arguments are permuted the same way. The same for D2. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (a change of variables over a finite sum).

**Definition D28 (isotropy of a build).** In the setting of Lemma T36, the isotropy of a build B is the set of gamma in
Gamma with (gamma . B)(x) = y_B(x) for every x with P(x) > 0. It is a subgroup because the support of P is
Gamma-invariant. It is defined by the build's values on the mix, not by its parameters. Isotropy Gamma: the coarse
network treats all members alike on the mix. Trivial isotropy: its images under Gamma are |Gamma| different builds on
the mix, all with the same score.

**Lemma T37 (finite symmetric criticality) (under: none).** Let K be a finite group of orthogonal linear maps of the
parameter space of builds of fixed widths (for example generated by the maps of Lemma T36 and by permutations of the
units of a layer), and let f be D_P or D2_P as a function of the parameters, so that f(g theta) = f(theta) for every g
in K. Let theta be fixed by K, and let f be differentiable at theta (true when no point of P sits exactly on a kink of
a unit). If theta is a critical point of f restricted to the fixed subspace Fix(K), then theta is a critical point of
f. (This is the finite, orthogonal case of the principle of symmetric criticality of Palais 1979.)
Proof. Differentiating f(g theta') = f(theta') at theta' = theta gives g^T grad f(g theta) = grad f(theta); with
g theta = theta and g orthogonal, grad f(theta) = g grad f(theta) for every g, so grad f(theta) lies in Fix(K).
Criticality on Fix(K) means grad f(theta) is orthogonal to Fix(K). So grad f(theta) = 0. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (two lines of linear algebra).
Comment: the lemma gives critical points, not minimisers: symmetric critical points can be saddles. It does not apply
at a build with a point of P on a kink. Among the exact builds of Part B, two are proved least: T20's (its isotropy
under the mirror x -> -x is trivial: the mirror image is the other least build) and T33's (value 0, so least; its
unit lies on the rotation axis, so its isotropy is the whole rotation group). T32's and T34's builds are only proved
to beat the folds (T32: D2 at most 3/80; T34: at most 25/216), not to be least, so their symmetry says nothing about the
optimum. So a least build can keep the whole group (T33) or break it (T20).

**Theorem T38 (first-order structure of a least build: every unit is a regression of the rest of the residual on its
own region) (under: two logits, one hidden layer, a finite mix).** Let B be a least build of width k for D2_P, or a
least build among the builds with the same output signs, with gap g(x) = sum_j s_j relu(theta_j^T x~) + gamma (output
sizes absorbed into theta_j, signs s_j in {+1, -1}), and residual r_i = g(x_i) - Delta_N(x_i) on the points of P. For
each unit j let A_j be the points where it fires (theta_j^T x~_i > 0) and K_j the points on its kink
(theta_j^T x~_i = 0). Then:
1. sum_i pi_i r_i = 0: for D2, the build's average gap equals N's average gap over the mix;
2. for every unit j there are weights lambda_i in [0, 1] (i in K_j) with
   sum_{i in A_j} pi_i r_i x~_i + sum_{i in K_j} lambda_i pi_i r_i x~_i = 0: on its region (the kink points counted with
   a weight), the residual is orthogonal to every affine function of the input. Equivalently, for D2 and with no kink
   points, s_j theta_j^T x~ is a pi-weighted least-squares affine fit on A_j of the partial residual
   Delta_N - (g - s_j relu(theta_j^T x~)): N's gap minus the other units and the constant (a backfitting fixed point).
For D_P the same holds with r_i = sigma(g(x_i)) - sigma(Delta_N(x_i)), the difference of the class probabilities; part
1 then says the build's average class probability equals N's.
Proof. The objective is F(theta, gamma) = sum_i pi_i l(g(x_i); Delta_N(x_i)), with l smooth in g and derivative
r_i / 2 (D2, l = (g - t)^2 / 4) or r_i (KL). F is differentiable in gamma, with derivative proportional to
sum_i pi_i r_i, which is 0 at a minimum: part 1. For part 2 fix j. Moving theta_j to theta_j + e v (e > 0 small), the
one-sided derivative of relu(theta_j^T x~_i) is v^T x~_i on A_j, relu(v^T x~_i) on K_j and 0 elsewhere, so at a local
minimum, for every v,
   phi(v) = a^T v + sum_{i in K_j} b_i relu(v^T x~_i) >= 0, with a = s_j sum_{i in A_j} pi_i r_i x~_i and
   b_i = s_j pi_i r_i.
Split K_j into K+ (b_i > 0) and K- (b_i <= 0). For i in K-, relu(u) >= 0 gives b_i relu(u) <= 0, so
h(v) = a^T v + sum_{i in K+} b_i relu(v^T x~_i) >= phi(v) >= 0 for every v. Since b_i > 0 on K+ and
relu(u) = max over mu in [0, 1] of mu u, h(v) = max over y in C of y^T v, with
C = {a + sum_{i in K+} mu_i b_i x~_i : mu in [0, 1]^{K+}}, a compact convex set. If 0 were not in C, the point of C
nearest 0, call it y0, would satisfy y^T y0 >= |y0|^2 > 0 for all y in C, so h(-y0) < 0, a contradiction. So 0 is in C:
there are mu_i in [0, 1] with a + sum_{K+} mu_i b_i x~_i = 0. Take lambda_i = mu_i on K+ and lambda_i = 0 on K-, and
divide by s_j: part 2. With no kink points, on A_j the gap is s_j theta_j^T x~ + (g - s_j relu(theta_j^T x~)), so
part 2 is the normal equation of the stated least-squares fit. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (one-sided derivatives and the nearest-point argument for a compact convex set).
Comment: the proof gives more than part 2: the condition holds with lambda_i = 0 on every kink point where
s_j r_i <= 0. Part 2 is only a necessary condition: it says what every least build satisfies, not which regions A_j the
units take. Choosing the regions is the hard part (Theorem T22).

**Corollary T38.1 (width 1: a fit on the region, the average off it) (under: two logits, one hidden layer, a finite
mix).** Let B be a least build of width 1 for D2_P, with gap s relu(theta^T x~) + gamma, theta = (w, b), w not 0, firing
set A, kink set K and silent set Q (the other points of P). Then there are lambda_i in [0, 1] (i in K) such that:
1. the affine piece s theta^T x~ + gamma is a weighted least-squares affine fit of N's gap on A and K, with weight pi_i
   on A and lambda_i pi_i on K;
2. if the weights pi_i on Q and (1 - lambda_i) pi_i on K are not all 0, gamma is the weighted average of N's gap on Q
   and K with those weights;
3. on the hyperplane E = {x : theta^T x~ = 0} the affine piece takes the value gamma.
The fit in 1 is unique as an affine function on R^d when the vectors x~_i with positive weight span R^{d+1}; then 1 to
3 tie the region to the two fits: the least-squares fit on the region, extended to E, equals the average off it. For a
least build for D_P the same holds with "least-squares affine fit of N's gap" replaced by "logistic fit of N's class
probabilities" and "gamma is the weighted average of N's gap" by "sigma(gamma) is the weighted average of N's class
probability".
Proof. On K the unit is 0, so the gap there is gamma, which is also the affine piece's value. So T38 part 2,
sum_A pi r x~ + sum_K lambda pi r x~ = 0 with r the residual of the affine piece on A and K, is the normal equation of
the weighted fit in 1, and least squares is convex, so a solution of its normal equations is a fit. Its last
coordinate is sum_A pi r + sum_K lambda pi r = 0. Subtracting it from T38 part 1 gives
sum_Q pi r + sum_K (1 - lambda) pi r = 0, and on Q and K the gap is gamma: that is 2. On E, theta^T x~ = 0: that is 3.
For D_P replace the normal equations by the score equations of logistic regression with soft labels, which are also
convex. QED.
Lean: none, by hand.

**Corollary T38.2 (a unit inside a deep network fits the family's output seen through its own write) (under: two
logits, one hidden layer, a finite mix).** Take the setting of B.0 at one layer, with these extra conditions: the
metric G is the identity at each position (the plain squared error at the readers); the coarse unit's output reaches
the readers without pooling; and the build may also shift the readers' biases by any d in R^r (a widening of B.0's
builds). The points are the pairs (x, p), with the unit's input window x~(x, p) (a 1 appended) and weights from P. The
family sends a(x, p) = W h(x, p) in R^r to the readers, and the coarse unit, with read theta and a fixed non-zero write
c in R^r, sends c relu(theta^T x~(x, p)). Write t(x, p) = c^T a(x, p) / |c|^2, the family's output seen through c. Then
a least (theta, d) for the mean of |a - c relu(theta^T x~) - d|^2 gives, with gamma = c^T d / |c|^2, a least point of
the width-1 problem with target t and output sign +1. So T38 holds for it (with fixed signs), and when no point is on
the kink and the silent set carries weight, so does Corollary T38.1 with N's gap replaced by t. If the build has no
bias shift (d = 0), the same holds with gamma fixed at 0 and part 1 of T38 dropped.
Proof. Split d = gamma c + d' with c^T d' = 0, and a = t c + a' with c^T a' = 0. Then
a - c relu(theta^T x~) - d = (t - relu(theta^T x~) - gamma) c + (a' - d'), and the two parts are orthogonal, so the
squared norm is |c|^2 (t - relu(theta^T x~) - gamma)^2 + |a' - d'|^2. The second term does not depend on (theta, gamma),
and (theta, d) -> (theta, gamma, d') is a bijection. So minimise the first part, which is |c|^2 times the width-1
squared error with target t and sign +1. With d = 0 the same split holds with gamma = 0. QED.
Lean: none, a two-line orthogonal split, checked with sympy (`model/t38_write.py`).
Comment: T38 applied to the summed member output a = sum_i relu(z_i) is the case W = c = all ones. A trained coarse unit
is trained through the rest of the network (KL), not on this local score, so whether it sits at this fixed point is a
hypothesis (H-dialfit).

**Corollary T38.3 (when the readers mix positions, the unit's first-order condition weighs errors at all coupled
positions) (under: a finite mix).** Take the setting of T38.2 without its first two extra conditions: any metric G of
B.0 (so G_x(p, p') may couple different positions, with G_x(p', p) = G_x(p, p')^T as in B.0), and any linear map from
the unit's outputs to the readers. To keep the notation short, take the unit's output to reach position p unpooled.
Let e_x(p) = a(x, p) - c relu(theta^T x~(x, p)) - d, and define the error seen by the unit at p as
rho_x(p) = c^T sum_{p'} G_x(p, p') e_x(p'). At a local minimum of
E_P sum_{p, p'} e_x(p)^T G_x(p, p') e_x(p') in (theta, d):
1. E_P sum_p sum_{p'} G_x(p, p') e_x(p') = 0;
2. there are weights lambda in [0, 1] on the kink points (the (x, p) with theta^T x~(x, p) = 0) such that
   E_P [sum over firing p of rho_x(p) x~(x, p) + sum over kink p of lambda rho_x(p) x~(x, p)] = 0.
Proof. The objective is a quadratic function of d and of the unit's outputs u_x(p) = relu(theta^T x~(x, p)). Its
derivative in d gives 1. Its derivative in u_x(p) is -2 rho_x(p) times the weight of x, using
G_x(p', p) = G_x(p, p')^T. Then the proof of T38 part 2, with r_i replaced by -rho and the points by the pairs (x, p),
gives 2. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (the first-order condition of T38 with a different smooth outer function).
Comment: rho_x(p) contains the errors at every p' that G couples to p, including the unit's own outputs there, so 2 is
a least-squares normal equation with correlated errors. It is not a fit of a fixed target. With G the identity at each
position it reduces to the first-order form of T38.2.

**Definition D31 (dial and detector).** For a build and a mix P, a unit is a dial if its firing set carries at least
half of the weight of P, and a detector otherwise. (The essay's words: a dial, "where the middle matters"; a detector,
"where it mostly doesn't".)

**Remark B.O.2 (reading the optimum at width 1).** T38 says what every least build satisfies, unit by unit: unit j's
affine piece is a least-squares (for KL: logistic) fit of N's gap minus the other units, on its own region. At width 1
(Corollary T38.1) this has a clean reading: the unit marks out a half-space; on it the build is a least-squares affine
fit of N; off it the build is N's average there; and the fit, extended to the boundary, meets that average. A dial
(Definition D31) is then a linear summary of N over most of the mix, and a detector a linear summary over a small part
with the average elsewhere. T33's least build is an exact instance: its single unit fires on two of the three orbits
and fits N exactly there, and the constant equals N's value on the third orbit. With two or more units the same reading
holds only when the firing sets are nested or disjoint on P; in general the build on A_j is not affine and the build
where no unit fires is not N's average. A least build need not respect the network's symmetry: T20's least build has
trivial isotropy. This is the structure of hinging-hyperplane models (Breiman 1993, literature table): a sum of hinges,
each fitted on its own side by least squares to what the other hinges leave (backfitting).

## B.S The shape of the optimum: the output set and its pieces

Shonu (2026-10-26): "we need to mathematically derive what the general mathematical form/object is for what the small
network optimum is ... once we move forward, it's likely going to be a more special case of this thing". This section
names that object for plain ReLU builds on a finite mix (any depth, any number of logits). D35 and D36 name the point
that distillation on the mix is trying to reach: distillation is a local search for it, and it can stop in a wrong
piece or, when no least build exists (T23), push the weights without bound. The section collects what the proofs of
T19, T21 and T38 already built and adds one general bound (T42). It adds language, not new structure: its results are
bookkeeping. Table B.S.3 says which earlier results are special cases and which are analogues in another class.

**Setting of B.S.** N is a plain ReLU network with L hidden layers, input dimension d and n_y logits (Definition D15
and its deeper form). P is a finite mix with support x_1, ..., x_n and weights pi_i > 0. A **build of widths
k = (k_1, ..., k_L)** is a plain ReLU network with the same L, d and n_y and k_l units in hidden layer l, with any
weights. For a network B write Y_B for the n x n_y matrix with rows y_B(x_i), and Yhat_B = Y_B P_perp for its centred
form (P_perp as in Fact F11, acting on the logit axis). On centred matrices use the weighted norm
||V||_P^2 = sum_i pi_i |V_i|^2 (V_i the rows). Softmax depends on y only through P_perp y, so D_P(B) and D2_P(B) are
functions of Yhat_B, and D2_P(B) = (1/2) ||Yhat_B - Yhat_N||_P^2.

**Definition D35 (output set).** O_k(P) = {Yhat_B : B a build of widths k}, a subset of the centred n x n_y matrices.
It contains 0 (the build with all weights 0).

**Definition D36 (the optimum).** D*_k(N; P) = the infimum of D_P(B) over builds of widths k, that is, the infimum
over O_k(P) of the divergence V -> D_P at V (D_P measured from Yhat_N). D2*_k(N; P) is the same for D2_P, and
delta_k(N) = sqrt(2 D2*_k(N; P)) is the norm distance from Yhat_N to O_k(P). A **least build** is a build that reaches
the infimum; its output is a point of O_k(P) where the divergence from Yhat_N is least. Attainment: Theorem T19 (two
logits, one hidden layer); it can fail (Theorem T23).

**Definition D37 (activation pattern, piece, optimal pattern).** The activation pattern of a build B is the list
sigma(B) = (A_{l,j}), one set A_{l,j} = {i : the pre-activation of unit j of layer l at x_i is > 0} for each hidden
unit. For a pattern sigma, the piece O_sigma is the set of Yhat_B over the builds B with sigma(B) = sigma, and
D*_sigma is the infimum of D_P over O_sigma (+infinity if O_sigma is empty). A pattern sigma is **optimal** if
D*_sigma = D*_k.

**Theorem T41 (the optimum is a minimum over finitely many pieces) (under: a finite mix).** In the setting of B.S:
1. O_k(P) is the union of the pieces O_sigma over the finitely many patterns sigma (at most 2^{n (k_1 + ... + k_L)}).
2. D*_k = the minimum over sigma of D*_sigma. So an optimal pattern always exists, also when no least build exists.
3. Inside a piece, the activations are fixed masks: with D_{l,i} the 0-1 diagonal matrix of the pattern at x_i and
   layer l, the hidden vector of layer l at x_i is D_{l,i} (W_l h_{l-1}(x_i) + b_l). So each row of Y_B is multi-affine
   in (layer 1, ..., layer L, head): affine in the weights and biases of any one layer, or of the head, when the others
   are fixed. With the other layers fixed, the sign conditions of sigma are linear in (W_l, b_l), so each such slice of
   the parameter set of the piece is a polyhedron.
4. For any rule that returns a build B_R with pattern sigma_R, the error of the rule,
   D_P(B_R) - D*_k, is at least D*_{sigma_R} - D*_k >= 0, with equality in the first step when B_R reaches
   D*_{sigma_R}. So the error is 0 only if sigma_R is an optimal pattern.
Proof. 1: every build has a pattern, and there are at most two choices (fires or not) for each of the n points at
each of the k_1 + ... + k_L units. 2: an infimum over a finite union is the least of the infima over the parts, and a
finite set of extended reals has a least element. 3: when the pattern is fixed, relu(t) = t on the points where the
unit fires and 0 elsewhere, which is multiplication by D_{l,i}. With the other layers fixed, h_l is affine in
(W_l, b_l), every later layer and the head are affine in h_l, and the head is affine in its own weights. The sign
conditions of layer l are linear in (W_l, b_l) when h_{l-1} is fixed. 4: B_R lies in O_{sigma_R}, so
D_P(B_R) >= D*_{sigma_R}, and D*_{sigma_R} >= D*_k by part 2. QED.
Lean: `t41_min_over_pieces` (part 2, over any finite index set, in extended reals) and `t41_error` (part 4) in
`lean/coarse/Coarse/Shape.lean`. Parts 1 and 3 by hand (counting, and the evaluation of relu on a fixed sign).
Comment: part 4 is Shonu's error ("error in what the optimal small network would be") made exact, as a difference of
objective values. That is the one notion of a rule's error used in this paper. For one hidden layer and two logits
(Corollary T41.1) the piece problem is a finite set of convex problems, so there "which piece" carries the difficulty.
In general it does not: with three logits the infimum can fail to be reached inside one fixed piece (T23's minimising
sequence keeps one pattern), and for L >= 2 the piece problem is a non-convex multi-affine problem.

**Corollary T41.1 (one hidden layer: the sign-fixed parts of a piece have closed convex closures, and the piece
problem is a projection) (under: two logits, one hidden layer, a finite mix).** Take L = 1 and n_y = 2. For signs s and
sets A_1, ..., A_k let R(s, A) = {sum_j s_j E_{A_j} theta_j + gamma 1 : theta_j in Theta_{A_j}, gamma real}, with
Theta_A and E_A = diag(1_A) X~ as in the proof of T19. Write C_A = {theta : X~_i theta > 0 for i in A, <= 0 for i not
in A} (the cell of A) and O_{sigma, s} for the gap vectors of the builds with pattern sigma = (A_1, ..., A_k) and
output signs s (so the gap-vector form of O_sigma is the union of the O_{sigma, s} over the 2^k sign vectors s).
Then:
1. the set of gap vectors of builds of width k is the union of the closed polyhedral cones R(s, A) (T19). Every point
   of R(s, A) is the gap vector of a build with signs s and a pattern (A'_j) with A'_j contained in A_j;
2. (closure) if every cell C_{A_j} is non-empty, R(s, A) is the closure of O_{sigma, s}. Then D*_sigma is the least,
   over the 2^k sign vectors s, of the least value of D_P (or D2_P) over R(s, A), and each of these is the minimum of a
   convex function over a polyhedron (T21). If some cell is empty, O_sigma is empty. O_sigma itself is a union of 2^k
   such parts, and no convexity is claimed for it;
3. for D2_P, if a least point of R(s, A) satisfies every constraint theta_j in Theta_{A_j} strictly, it is the
   pi-weighted orthogonal projection of N's gap vector onto the linear span V(A) = the span of the columns of
   E_{A_1}, ..., E_{A_k} and of 1, and its normal equations are the equations of Theorem T38 parts 1 and 2 with no kink
   points.
Proof. 1: the proof of T19. For theta in Theta_A the true firing set of the unit is a subset of A, and its data vector
is E_A theta, because at a point with X~_i theta = 0 both are 0. 2: O_{sigma, s} is contained in R(s, A), which is
closed, so its closure is too. Conversely let theta_j in Theta_{A_j} and theta0_j in C_{A_j}. For t in (0, 1] the point
(1 - t) theta_j + t theta0_j is in C_{A_j}: on A_j it is a non-negative number plus a positive one, and off A_j it is
a sum of two numbers <= 0. Its gap vector depends continuously on t and tends to the gap vector of (theta_j) as t -> 0.
So R(s, A) lies in the closure. D_P and D2_P are continuous in the gap vector, so the infimum over O_{sigma, s} equals
the least value over its closure R(s, A), which is reached (T21). An empty cell means no build has that pattern.
3: write F(theta, gamma) for D2_P of the gap sum_j s_j E_{A_j} theta_j + gamma 1, a convex function on the whole space
of (theta, gamma). If no constraint is active at a least point, that point is interior to the constraint set, so it is
a local minimum of F on the whole space, and a local minimum of a convex function is a global one. The image of the
whole space under the linear map (theta, gamma) -> gap vector is V(A), so the least gap vector is the least point of
(1/4) sum pi (v - Delta_N)^2 over V(A): the pi-weighted projection. Its normal equations say that the residual is
pi-orthogonal to every column of E_{A_j} and to 1, which are the equations of T38 parts 1 and 2 with no kink points.
QED.
Lean: none, by hand (the cited proofs, a segment argument, and the normal equations of a weighted projection).

**Corollary T41.2 (two hidden layers with layer 1 kept) (under: two logits, a finite mix, first layer kept).** For
the builds of the setting of B.G, Corollary T41.1 holds on the points z_x = h(x) in place of x.
Proof. Lemma T39 part 0, whose proof uses only that the build keeps layer 1 (not H-front): the objective is the
one-hidden-layer objective on the points z_x. QED.
Lean: none, by hand.

**Theorem T42 (the optimum distance moves at most as far as the network: a transfer bound) (under: a finite
mix).** In the setting of B.S, take two networks N and N' with the same L, d and n_y, the same mix P and the same
widths k. Let dist(N, N') = ||Yhat_N - Yhat_N'||_P (the output distance on the mix; dist^2 / 2 is D2_P between them).
Then:
1. |delta_k(N) - delta_k(N')| <= dist(N, N');
2. if a build B' of widths k satisfies ||Yhat_B' - Yhat_N'||_P <= delta_k(N') + eta, then
   ||Yhat_B' - Yhat_N||_P <= delta_k(N) + 2 dist(N, N') + eta;
