not change the minimum. Hence the minimum in (1) is min over rank(A) <= k of E_P |(M - A) c|^2 =
min |(M - A) Sigma^(1/2)|_F^2. Since rank(A Sigma^(1/2)) <= k, this is at least the Eckart-Young value sum over i > k of
sigma_i^2. It is attained: B* = sum over i <= k of sigma_i u_i v_i^T, A* = B* (Sigma^(1/2))^+; the v_i with sigma_i > 0
lie in the row space of M Sigma^(1/2), inside the range of Sigma^(1/2), so A* Sigma^(1/2) = B*. The row space of A* is
span{(Sigma^(1/2))^+ v_i}, which gives (2); the spans grow with k. (3) P_perp has rank C - 1, so rank M <= C - 1. QED.
Lean: none (Mathlib has no singular value decomposition in this form, so a Lean proof is not practical); the steps are standard (Eckart and
Young 1936; reduced-rank regression, Izenman 1975), checked in `model/tv_regions.py` (check F: the closed form against
random subspaces and a local search).
Comment. This is not principal components of the stream. Sigma alone (SliceGPT's choice, A.4) keeps the directions with
the most energy; TV3 weighs them by what the logits read (M). A direction with much energy that the logits barely read
is dropped first. And the closed form minimises the readout error, the quantity in TV2's bound, not D_P itself.

**Corollary TV3.1 (an area that no block reads, cut to C - 1 directions under the energy claims) (under: pure-stream
networks; area cuts; areas read only by the logits).** For a grouping G of areas with eps_br(S) = 0, take V_S = V*_(C-1)
of TV3 for each S (when k_S >= C - 1). If the energy claims (S minus V*_(C-1), l) on the complement of the rule's own
choice have error 0 for every S and l (or in the no-norm form), B^a of Theorem TV2 is exact on P. With two logits, under
the same energy claims, every such area can be cut to one direction exactly. When C - 1 >= dim S this says nothing.
Proof. TV3 part 3 gives eps_ro(S, V_S) = 0; Theorem TV2 part 2. QED.
Lean: none needed.
Comment. The energy condition is the price of the norm: the directions that the logits do not read are unread, and TV1
says when they can go.

**Proposition TV4 (switching across a zoom of readout areas) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts; areas read only
by the logits).** Let G_0, ..., G_m be a zoom whose groups are areas with eps_br = 0, each group of G_(j+1) the sum of
groups of G_j, and suppose that at each level the energy claims of Theorem TV2 hold.
1. The one-time computation is, for each level j and each group S, a subspace V_S and L*(S, V_S) (by TV3 in closed form,
   or from the map's claims). After it, switching to level j selects stored weights, at a cost that does not grow with
   the size of N. TV3's V*_k is a way to find areas, and how M is found is outside the trunk: for a map that holds V_S
   as an area and the readout claim (S, V_S), TV2's bound is in that claim's error. (If the rule computes V*_k itself,
   eps_ro(S, V*_k) is not an error of a claim of M, and the bound is not in M's errors.)
2. The bound of TV2 at level j is a sum over the groups of G_j; a group that appears at two levels with the same V_S has
   the same term and the same premises.
3. (Children.) If S1, ..., Sr are pairwise orthogonal subspaces inside S with own part O = S minus their sum, and
   V = V1 + ... + Vr + V_O with V_i inside S_i and V_O inside O, then eps_ro(S, V)^(1/2) <= sum over i of
   eps_ro(S_i, V_i)^(1/2) + eps_ro(O, V_O)^(1/2). By TV3, no such cut of S with dim V <= k has a smaller error than
   V*_k.
Proof. (1) and (2): B^a at G_j is determined by the V_S, L*(S, V_S) and N (Theorem TV2). (3) Take L = sum over i of
L*(S_i, V_i) P_(V_i) + L*(O, V_O) P_(V_O). Since U P_S = sum over i of U P_(S_i) + U P_O and P_(V_i) P_V = P_(V_i), the
residual is the sum of the children's residuals, and Minkowski's inequality bounds its norm. The last sentence is TV3
part 1. QED.
Lean: none needed (bookkeeping).
Comment. A cut built from the children (for example, as an illustration that no proof uses: keep the "dog" and "cat"
directions of an "animal" area) is the
tree-shaped reading of a coarse area, and part 3 prices it against the best cut of the parent. T5 asks the groups to
nest, not the cuts. Inside one area TV3's cuts nest in k anyway.

**Lemma TV5 (the readout kernel) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Let K be the intersection over
l = 1, ..., L of ker R_l (the vectors that every block read matrix sends to 0).
1. A subspace S has eps_br(S) = 0 exactly when S lies in K. So the areas that no block reads are the subspaces of K.
2. If q_1 + ... + q_L >= d, then K = {0} for all read matrices outside a closed set of Lebesgue measure zero.
3. Hence, at error 0, TV2 to TV4 come to this: keep K perp whole and replace K (or subspaces of it) by fewer
   directions; with S = K and V = V*_(C-1) of TV3, the cut is exact when the energy claims (K minus V, l) have error 0.
   For weights outside the null set of part 2 there is no nonzero such area.
Proof. (1) eps_br(S) = sum over l of |R_l P_S|_F^2 is 0 exactly when R_l P_S = 0 for every l, that is, S lies in every
ker R_l. (2) K = ker Rbar, with Rbar the (q_1 + ... + q_L) x d matrix that stacks the R_l. K = {0} exactly when Rbar
has rank d, that is, when some d x d minor of Rbar is not 0. The sum of the squares of all d x d minors is a polynomial
in the entries of the R_l, and it is not the zero polynomial when q_1 + ... + q_L >= d (it is positive at an Rbar
whose first d rows are the identity). The zero set of a polynomial that is not identically 0 is closed and has measure
zero. (3) Part 1, Theorem TV2 for the area family {K} (or any family of subspaces of K, which part 1 makes areas that no block reads), and Corollary TV3.1. QED.
Lean: none needed (part 1 is the definition; part 2 is the standard fact that a nonzero polynomial vanishes on a null
set); checked in `model/tv_regions.py` (check K: random read matrices have K = {0}).
Comment. A transformer's MLP block alone has q_l = 4d read rows, so for generic weights no direction of the stream is
unread by the blocks, and the same holds for Theorem TV1's unread D (which lies in K and in ker U). The planted check
network has K != {0} by construction. The essay's unread dimension is unread only approximately (its readers have
small weights on it), so for real networks the case that matters is the graded one, Theorem TV6, and B.V's exact
results are its error-0 end.

### B.V.2 The graded case: blocks that read the cut part a little (added 2026-10-29, later)

Lemma TV5 shows that the exact results above cover almost no real network: every direction is read a little by some
block. This part handles that case.
1. Theorem TV6: for the cuts of its statement, the loss is at most a quarter of the square of (what the logits lose
   directly) plus (each block's leak, carried to the logits). The leak of a neuron is how much its read changes
   because the cut part is gone, computed from N, P and the cut's reads. The carrying runs through the stream: errors
   grow by (I + T_l) per block, not by T_l, and without a norm T_l is non-zero only along the area graph (a neuron
   that reads area B and writes area A). With a norm, T_l couples every area, because a change anywhere changes the
   size that every norm divides by.
2. Proposition TV7: no bound in the errors of claims made one block at a time, even errors that do not change under
   rescaling, can tend to 0 with them. One block writes a tiny value taken from the cut part; the logits read it with
   a large weight.
3. Definition DM14 and Corollary TV6.1: a claim whose error is a leak carried to the logits. In its errors alone, the
   loss of the projection cut has a bound that is 0 when they are 0. Its errors carry N's gains, as the quiet claim
   DM9 does.
4. Proposition TV8: when the cut's stream error is checked to stay small, the norm's coupling in TV6 can use each
   neuron's largest read on P instead of the length of its read vector.

**Theorem TV6 (the graded cut: leaks carried along the stream) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Let N be as in
Definition DV1, D a subspace of R^d, Pi = P_(D perp), and A_1, ..., A_m an orthogonal decomposition of R^d (the areas
of the bound; any decomposition is allowed). Let B be a re-fit area cut that drops D (Definition DV2) with these
choices: first write Pi e, writes Pi W_l and Pi c_l, block read vectors r'_(l,i) in D perp and biases b'_(l,i), norm
constants eps'_l > 0 (in the norm form), a logit matrix U' whose rows lie in D perp, and N's logit bias c_y. Let Lip_l
be the Lipschitz constant of sigma_l. Write h_l for N's stream, n = n_(eps_l) and n' = n_(eps'_l) at block l (l = L + 1
for the logits), and on P:
   nu'_l(x) = (|Pi h_(l-1)(x)|^2 + eps'_l)^(1/2),   rho_l = min over x in P of nu'_l(x) > 0,
   leak_(l,i)(x) = r'_(l,i) . n'(Pi h_(l-1)(x)) + b'_(l,i) - r_(l,i) . n(h_(l-1)(x)) - b_(l,i),
   lambda_l[A](x) = Lip_l sum over i of |P_A Pi w_(l,i)| |leak_(l,i)(x)|,
   T_l[A, B] = (Lip_l / rho_l) sum over i of |P_A Pi w_(l,i)| (|P_B r'_(l,i)| + |r'_(l,i)|),
   omega(x) = P_perp (U' n'(Pi h_L(x)) - U n(h_L(x))),   u_A = (|P_perp U' P_A| + |P_perp U'|) / rho_(L+1),
   M_l = (I + T_L)(I + T_(L-1)) ... (I + T_(l+1))   (M_L = I),
with |.| the Euclidean norm of a vector and the operator norm of a matrix, ||f|| = (E_P |f(x)|^2)^(1/2), and ||lambda_l||
the vector of the ||lambda_l[A]||. Then:
1. D_P(B) <= (1/4) (||omega|| + sum over l = 1, ..., L of u^T M_l ||lambda_l||)^2.
2. (No norm.) In the no-norm form, part 1 holds with nu'_l = rho_l = 1, T_l[A, B] = Lip_l sum over i of
   |P_A Pi w_(l,i)| |P_B r'_(l,i)| and u_A = |P_perp U' P_A|. So T_l[A, B] > 0 only if some neuron of block l reads B
   with its cut read vector r'_(l,i) and writes A. Call this an edge B -> A at block l of the cut's **area graph**. A
   leak into area A at block l adds to the bound only if there are blocks l < m_1 < ... < m_j and areas
   A = A_0, A_1, ..., A_j with an edge A_(t-1) -> A_t at block m_t, and u_(A_j) > 0. Leaks with no such path add
   nothing.
3. (Zero leak.) If every leak_(l,i) is 0 on P, the bound is (1/4) ||omega||^2. For the projection reads r' = Pi r,
   b' = b and eps'_l = eps_l + c_l(D), every leak is 0 when no block reads D (R_l P_D = 0) and the energy claims (D, l)
   have error 0 for l = 1, ..., L.
Proof. Let ht_l be the cut's stream in R^d (the induction of Lemma TV0, with the cut's reads and biases) and
delta_l = ht_l - Pi h_l, which lies in D perp; delta_0 = Pi e - Pi e = 0. Write e_l[A](x) = |P_A delta_l(x)|. Fix x in P
and a block l.
(a) A lemma on the norm. For a, a' in R^d and eps' > 0, with nu'(z) = (|z|^2 + eps')^(1/2):
n'(a') - n'(a) = (a' - a) / nu'(a) + a' (1 / nu'(a') - 1 / nu'(a)), and nu' is 1-Lipschitz, so
|a'| |1 / nu'(a') - 1 / nu'(a)| = (|a'| / nu'(a')) |nu'(a) - nu'(a')| / nu'(a) <= |a' - a| / nu'(a). Hence, for any vector
r, |r . (n'(a') - n'(a))| <= (|r . (a' - a)| + |r| |a' - a|) / nu'(a).
(b) The read of neuron i changes by
Delta_i = r'_i . n'(ht_(l-1)) + b'_i - r_i . n(h_(l-1)) - b_i = r'_i . (n'(ht_(l-1)) - n'(Pi h_(l-1))) + leak_i.
By (a) with a = Pi h_(l-1), a' = ht_(l-1), a' - a = delta_(l-1):
|Delta_i| <= |leak_i| + (|r'_i . delta_(l-1)| + |r'_i| |delta_(l-1)|) / rho_l. Since delta = sum over B of P_B delta and
r'_i . delta = sum over B of (P_B r'_i) . (P_B delta), |r'_i . delta| <= sum over B of |P_B r'_i| e_(l-1)[B], and
|delta| <= sum over B of e_(l-1)[B].
(c) The inside values change by |gt_i - g_i| <= Lip_l |Delta_i|, and delta_l = delta_(l-1) + Pi W_l (gt_l - g_l)
(the bias writes are Pi c_l in both). So e_l[A] <= e_(l-1)[A] + Lip_l sum over i of |P_A Pi w_i| |Delta_i|. With (b):
e_l <= (I + T_l) e_(l-1) + lambda_l, entry by entry, at every x. All entries of T_l are >= 0, so by induction
e_L(x) <= sum over l of M_l lambda_l(x).
(d) At the logits, P_perp (y_B - y_N) = omega + P_perp U' (n'(ht_L) - n'(Pi h_L)) (both use the bias c_y). By the
decomposition in (a), |P_perp U' (n'(ht_L) - n'(Pi h_L))| <= (|P_perp U' delta_L| + |P_perp U'| |delta_L|) / rho_(L+1)
<= u^T e_L, using |n'(.)| <= 1. So |P_perp (y_B - y_N)(x)| <= |omega(x)| + sum over l of u^T M_l lambda_l(x).
(e) The right side is a sum of functions with constant coefficients >= 0. Minkowski's inequality for ||.|| gives
||P_perp (y_B - y_N)|| <= ||omega|| + sum over l of u^T M_l ||lambda_l||. Fact F11 gives part 1.
(2) Without a norm, n' and n are the identity, so n'(ht) - n'(Pi h) = delta exactly and step (a) has no second term.
The path statement: entry A of u^T M_l is a sum, over sequences of areas A = B_l, B_(l+1), ..., B_L, of u_(B_L) times
the product over m = l + 1, ..., L of (I + T_m)[B_m, B_(m-1)]. A non-zero term needs, at every block m, either
B_m = B_(m-1) or an edge B_(m-1) -> B_m at block m, and u > 0 at the end; dropping the blocks where the area stays gives
the path of part 2.
(3) The bound with every lambda_l = 0 is (1/4) ||omega||^2. For the projection reads, leak_i = (r_i . Pi h)(1 / nu' -
1 / nu) - r_i . P_D h / nu with nu = (|h|^2 + eps_l)^(1/2); if R_l P_D = 0 the second term is 0, and if
|P_D h|^2 = c_l(D) on P then nu' = nu (Pythagoras), so the first is 0. QED.
Lean: `nu_lip` (nu' is 1-Lipschitz, in the form |(p^2 + eps)^(1/2) - (q^2 + eps)^(1/2)| <= |p - q|) and `scale_step`
(the step x |1 / B - 1 / A| <= t / A of (a)) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`; the reverse triangle step, the
recursion over blocks and the path expansion are by hand; checked in `model/tv_graded.py`.
Comment (what the stream does). The factor (I + T_l), not T_l, is the identity path of the stream: a block with small
gain passes an error on almost unchanged instead of multiplying it by its gain. Without a norm each entry of u^T M_l is
a sum over paths of the cut's area graph, so an area with no path to an area the logits read adds 0. This is where the
map's write and read structure enters a bound in B.V. How small the bound is for a given map is not shown. With norms
the second term of T_l joins every area to every area that a neuron writes: the norm couples the whole stream, as in
Theorem TV1, with strength 1 / rho_l (Proposition TV8 weakens this coupling for neurons that read little). When the
leaks are 0 and the S of Theorem TV2 are areas no block reads, with the energy claim (D, L + 1) also of error 0 and U'
TV2's logit read, omega is TV2's residual; so TV2 is the case of zero leak. The bound uses N's Lipschitz constants and
norms; Proposition TV7 shows that no bound in errors of claims made one block at a time exists.

**Proposition TV7 (no graded bound from claims made one block at a time) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts; a
gain counterexample).** For every s > 0 there is c(s) > 0 with the following property. For every delta in (0, 1]
there is a network N_delta of Definition DV1 (norm form with eps_l = 1, one block of one neuron, sigma = the identity,
two logits, d = 3) with an area family and a map M_delta that holds, for every area A of the family, its block-read
claim (both forms of DM11) and the write claims of every writer, and, for the grouping G = {D} with k_D = 0, the
readout claim (D, {0}) and the energy claims (D, l), such that every claim of M_delta has error at most delta^2 and
V_area(G) >= c(s). The two forms of the block-read error do not change under the symmetries of Fact F1 and of stream
scaling (DM11). So no bound that depends only on the errors of claims of the types of DM11 to DM13 and tends to 0 as
they tend to 0 holds for area cuts. This is the reading of T5's graded clause used in Proposition TE5; it is stricter
than T5's literal words ("0 when all of them are 0"). A bound that also uses N's gains, as Theorem TV6 does, is not
excluded.
Proof. P = {-1, 1}^2 with equal weights, x = (x1, x2). e(x) = x1 e_1 + x2 e_2, so |h_0|^2 = 2 on P; let
nu_0 = (2 + 1)^(1/2). The block: one neuron with read vector delta e_2, write vector e_3, bias 0, c_1 = 0. Its read is
delta x2 / nu_0, so h_1 = x1 e_1 + x2 e_2 + (delta x2 / nu_0) e_3 and |h_1|^2 = 2 + delta^2 / 3 on P; let
nu_1 = (|h_1|^2 + 1)^(1/2). Logits y = U n(h_1) with rows t e_3^T and 0, c_y = 0, where t = s nu_0 nu_1 / delta; then
y_N(x) = (s x2, 0).
The map. Areas: span(e_1, e_2), its children span(e_1) and D = span(e_2), and span(e_3) (laminar). Write claims: the
first write inside span(e_1, e_2) and the neuron inside span(e_3), errors 0 (c_1 = 0 writes nothing). Block-read
claims: the only read vector is delta e_2, so the areas span(e_1) and span(e_3) have both errors 0, and D and
span(e_1, e_2) have eps_br = delta^2 and eps_br^w = (|e_3|^2 / E_P |h_1|^2) delta^2 E_P |n(h_0)|^2 =
(2 / 3) delta^2 / (2 + delta^2 / 3) <= delta^2. Readout claim (D, {0}): U P_D = 0, error 0. Energy claims (D, l),
l = 1, 2: |P_D h_0|^2 = |P_D h_1|^2 = x2^2 = 1 on P, errors 0.
Now let B be any re-fit area cut at G (any block read vector in D perp, any biases, norm constants and logits). It
drops D, so its first write is x1 e_1, and its block read, its write and its logits are functions of x1 alone. At the
two points with the same x1, N's distributions are q_+ = softmax(s, 0) and q_- = softmax(-s, 0), and B gives one
distribution p. For any p, (1/2)(KL(q_+ || p) + KL(q_- || p)) = (1/2)(KL(q_+ || m) + KL(q_- || m)) + KL(m || p) with
m = (q_+ + q_-) / 2 (expand the logarithms). So D_P(B) >= c(s) = (1/2)(KL(q_+ || m) + KL(q_- || m)), which is > 0 since
q_+ != q_- for s > 0, and does not depend on delta. The family is not one network under a symmetry: the share
|P_(e_3) h_1|^2 / |h_1|^2 = (delta^2 / 3) / (2 + delta^2 / 3) changes with delta, and rotations, the rescaling of Fact F1
and stream scaling keep it. QED.
Lean: none needed (the identity for the mean of KL divergences is a direct expansion); checked in `model/tv_graded.py`
(check C: every listed error, and the least loss of cuts that see x1 only staying at c(s) while delta falls).
Comment. The neuron writes a value of size about delta that comes from D, and the logits read it with weight about
1 / delta, so N relies on a small value of its stream. Every claim of DM11 to DM13 sees one read or one write at a
time; only a quantity that carries the leak through the logits' weight sees the loss. This is Proposition TE5's
mechanism (a tiny leak read with a large weight) in the stream.

**Corollary TV6.1 (a graded bound in the carried leak errors alone) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts; carried
leak claims).** Let D and the areas be as in Theorem TV6 with every eps_l > 0, and let B_D be the projection cut of D
with reads Pi r, N's biases, eps'_l = eps_l + c_l(D) and logit matrix U Pi. Then
   D_P(B_D) <= (1/4) (sum over l = 1, ..., L + 1 of eps_cl(D, l)^(1/2))^2,
with eps_cl the errors of the carried leak claims (Definition DM14). The bound depends only on those errors and is 0
when they are all 0.
Proof. eps'_l >= eps_l > 0, so rho_l > 0. The quantities of DM14 are the terms of Theorem TV6 part 1 for B_D:
||omega|| = eps_cl(D, L + 1)^(1/2) and u^T M_l ||lambda_l|| = eps_cl(D, l)^(1/2). QED.
Lean: none needed.
Comment. The bound holds by construction: the claim errors are TV6's terms. When D is the dropped part of a cut at G
(a sum of members of the map's decomposition with dim V_S <= k_S for each S), B_D is a re-fit area cut at G, so the
bound also bounds V_area(G); in units of N's constants that is budget k + 1 (Lemma TV12). Corollary TV6.2 puts it in
T5's form. What it does not give is the least-loss build itself when the errors are above 0. It puts N's gains (Lipschitz
constants, write norms, 1 / rho_l) inside the claim's error, as the quiet claim DM9 does at the last layer; Proposition
TV7 shows that some such carrying is needed.

**Proposition TV8 (the norm couples only through each neuron's read) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** In the
norm form, let B, D and the areas be as in Theorem TV6, and let eta in (0, 1]. For block l and neuron i let
a_(l,i) = max over x in P of |r'_(l,i) . n'(Pi h_(l-1)(x))|, and a_U = max over x in P of |P_perp U' n'(Pi h_L(x))|. Let
T^eta_l and u^eta be T_l and u of TV6 with the coupling term |r'_(l,i)| replaced by a_(l,i) + 2 eta |r'_(l,i)|, and
|P_perp U'| in u replaced by a_U + 2 eta |P_perp U'|. Define, at every x in P, ehat_0 = 0 and
ehat_l = (I + T^eta_l) ehat_(l-1) + lambda_l(x). If sum over A of ehat_l[A](x) <= eta rho_(l+1) for every l = 0, ..., L
and every x in P, then
   D_P(B) <= (1/4) (||omega|| + sum over l of (u^eta)^T M^eta_l ||lambda_l||)^2,
with M^eta_l the products of (I + T^eta_m) as in TV6. The premise is computed from N, P and the cut alone.
Proof. A second-order form of step (a) of TV6: by its decomposition, r . (n'(a') - n'(a)) = r . (a' - a) / nu'(a) +
(r . n'(a')) (nu'(a) - nu'(a')) / nu'(a), and |r . n'(a')| <= |r . n'(a)| + |r . (n'(a') - n'(a))| <= |r . n'(a)| +
2 |r| |a' - a| / nu'(a) by step (a). So
   |r . (n'(a') - n'(a))| <= (|r . (a' - a)| + |r . n'(a)| |a' - a|) / nu'(a) + 2 |r| |a' - a|^2 / nu'(a)^2.
Induction on l: suppose e_m(x) <= ehat_m(x) entry by entry for m < l. Then |delta_(l-1)(x)| <= sum over A of
e_(l-1)[A](x) <= eta rho_l <= eta nu'_l(x), so the last term is at most 2 eta |r| |delta_(l-1)| / nu'_l(x), and with
|r'_i . n'(Pi h_(l-1))| <= a_(l,i) step (b) of TV6 holds with |r'_i| replaced by a_(l,i) + 2 eta |r'_i|. Steps (c) give
e_l(x) <= (I + T^eta_l) e_(l-1)(x) + lambda_l(x) <= ehat_l(x). At the logits the same form with |delta_L| <= eta rho_(L+1)
gives |P_perp U' (n'(ht_L) - n'(Pi h_L))| <= (u^eta)^T e_L. Steps (d) and (e) of TV6 finish. QED.
Lean: `scale_step` and `nu_lip` (the steps of (a)); the second-order step and the induction are by hand; checked in
`model/tv_graded.py` (check E).
Comment. a_(l,i) is the neuron's largest read on P. A neuron that reads little couples little, so with norms the bound
comes closer to the area graph; it never follows it exactly, since the coupling is at least 2 eta |r'_(l,i)| > 0. The
premise, computed from N, P, the cut and eta, asks that the cut's stream error, as bounded, stay a small part of the
stream's size. TV8's coupling a_(l,i) + 2 eta |r'_(l,i)| is smaller than TV6's |r'_(l,i)| only
when a_(l,i) < (1 - 2 eta) |r'_(l,i)|, so never for eta >= 1/2; both bounds hold, so one may use the smaller. This replaces Conjecture DV2 (route
corrected by the referee, round 2).

### B.V.3 Overlap and cancellation (added 2026-10-29, round 2)

Shonu (answering card 3-23, where the quantum picture is his analogy, not a step of any proof): "residual streams are a little bit different ... you can still have overlaps and have
meanings not be crowded ... I don't need the calculations to not affect other things. I just need to ... be able to
work at the end of the day with these individual concepts", and: "Some operations affect other operations, but you can
create a quantum algorithm specifically in order to cancel out those terms". This part makes both sentences into
mathematics.
1. Fact F14 (Part A) and Lemma TV10: without norms an angle between two areas is not a property of the function; a cut
   is fixed by the part it drops alone. With norms an angle acts through one number per norm: the stream's size.
2. Lemma TV11: the line between overlap and crowding. A reader can keep reading a set of areas exactly while it
   ignores a dropped part exactly when the two meet only in 0.
3. Theorem TV9: the build can cancel a leak. Each re-fit read of a cut has a least leak, in closed form (a weighted
   least-squares fit of N's read on what the cut keeps). If every read of N is an affine function of the kept content
   on P, the cut is exact, whatever weight N's blocks and logits put on the dropped part (Proposition TV9.1).
   Proposition TV9.2 gives the matching limit: no cut recovers what the first write loses.
4. Lemma TV12: a re-set norm constant is one more stream direction that holds a constant and is never read. So a
   re-set constant and such a direction are the same thing (node R-normconst, a reading of DV2's class).
5. Lemma TV13: the network's own cancelling. Without norms, the logit change of any cut is exactly a signed sum, over
   blocks, of each leak carried through the products (I + J_m) of the cut's later blocks. Theorem TV6 is this sum with
   every sign and every slope replaced by its largest size.
6. Proposition TV14: the same signed sum with N's own slopes, computed from N, P and the cut's reads with no run of the
   cut, gives the logit change up to a remainder of second order in the leaks, bounded point by point.
7. Definition DM15 and Corollary TV6.2: completeness for area maps, and T5's two promises for complete area maps.
   Conjecture DV3 (D.15) asks for TV14 in the norm form.

**Theorem TV9 (re-fit reads that cancel the leak) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Let N be as in Definition
DV1, D a subspace of R^d, Pi = P_(D perp), and fix norm constants eps'_l = eps_l + c_l > 0 with c_l >= 0 (in the
no-norm form n' is the identity). Part 3 uses Lipschitz sigma_l (it uses Theorem TV6); parts 1, 2 and 4 do not.
For l = 1, ..., L + 1 let z_l(x) = n'_l(Pi h_(l-1)(x)), a vector in D perp (the cut's normed read of N's own stream,
projected), and for a neuron i of block l <= L let t_(l,i)(x) = r_(l,i) . n_l(h_(l-1)(x)) + b_(l,i) (N's read). Write
E for E_P, zbar_l = E z_l, Z_l = E (z_l - zbar_l)(z_l - zbar_l)^T, c_(l,i) = E (z_l - zbar_l)(t_(l,i) - E t_(l,i)), and
(.)^+ for the pseudo-inverse.
1. Over r' in D perp and b' in R, the least value of ||leak_(l,i)||^2 = E (r' . z_l + b' - t_(l,i))^2 is
   Var_P(t_(l,i)) - c_(l,i)^T Z_l^+ c_(l,i). It is attained at r*_(l,i) = Z_l^+ c_(l,i), which lies in D perp, and
   b*_(l,i) = E t_(l,i) - r*_(l,i) . zbar_l.
2. In the same way, over C x d matrices U' with rows in D perp and biases c'_y, the least ||omega||^2, with
   omega(x) = P_perp (U' z_(L+1)(x) + c'_y - U n_(L+1)(h_L(x)) - c_y), is attained by the least-squares fit of each
   coordinate of P_perp (U n_(L+1)(h_L) + c_y) on z_(L+1), with the same formula.
3. Let B* be the re-fit area cut that drops D (Definition DV2) with first write Pi e, writes Pi W_l and Pi c_l, the
   constants eps'_l, the reads r*, biases b*, and the logits of part 2. Theorem TV6 holds for B* with its leaks, which
   are the least possible for each neuron (part 1) and for the logits (part 2), with omega as in part 2 (a logit bias
   c'_y in place of c_y changes no step of TV6's proof).
4. (The cancel case.) If every t_(l,i) and every coordinate of P_perp (U n_(L+1)(h_L) + c_y) is an affine function of
   z_l (of z_(L+1) at the logits) on P, then B* computes softmax(y_N) at every point of P, so D_P(B*) = 0, and
   V_area(G) = 0 for every grouping G at which some cut drops D.
Proof. (1) For fixed r', the best b' is E t - r' . zbar, and then E (r' . z + b' - t)^2 = E ((r' . (z - zbar)) -
(t - E t))^2 = r'^T Z r' - 2 r'^T c + Var(t). This quadratic in r' is bounded below (it is a mean of squares), so c lies
in the range of Z, and its least value is Var(t) - c^T Z^+ c, attained at r* = Z^+ c (the normal equations
Z r' = c). Each z_l(x) lies in D perp, so the range of Z lies in D perp, and so does Z^+ c. For every r',
r' . z_l(x) = (Pi r') . z_l(x), so the minimum over r' in D perp equals the minimum over all r'.
(2) The same computation, one coordinate at a time; P_perp acts on the target only. (3) Theorem TV6 holds for every
re-fit area cut with reads in D perp and constants eps'_l > 0, and its proof uses the logit bias only in step (d),
where both networks' biases enter omega. (4) Under the premise, part 1 gives leak 0 for every neuron and part 2 gives
omega = 0. Then the read of every neuron of block 1 of B* equals N's, so the inside values agree and B*'s stream is
Pi h_1; by induction over the blocks B*'s stream is Pi h_l, and its logits equal N's after P_perp. So D_P(B*) = 0 (no
Lipschitz constant is used). QED.
Lean: `ols_le` (the least-squares fit is a nearest point: the projection onto the span of the fitted functions is no
farther from the target than any element of that span) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`; the normal equations are
standard; checked in `model/tv_cancel.py` (check E) and in `model/tv_graded.py` (its re-fit cut is B*).
Comment (what is cancelled). The projection read r' = Pi r of Theorem TV6 part 3 leaves the leak
-r . P_D h / nu, the read of the dropped part. The read r* adds to Pi r the part of that leak that the kept content
predicts on P, so the build cancels it: this is "a quantum algorithm ... to cancel out those terms" with the cut as the
algorithm. It cancels exactly the part that the kept content predicts, and no more: part 1 is the least leak. TV9 does
not choose the reads to minimise TV6's bound (its T_l also depends on r'), and it is not the least-loss cut: the reads
are fitted on N's projected stream Pi h_(l-1), while the cut runs on its own stream.
Comment (scope of part 4). P is finite. If at some l the points z_l(x), x in P, are affinely independent in D perp
(generic when |P| <= dim(D perp) + 1), every function on P is affine in z_l there, and part 4's premise holds by
interpolation. So part 4 says something about N only when |P| > dim(D perp) + 1. Proposition TV9.2's lower bound is 0
in the same regime. In the norm form the premise depends on the build's constants eps'_l through z_l = n'(Pi h).

**Proposition TV9.1 (a copy the cut can read instead) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** For every s > 0 there
is a network N_s of Definition DV1 (no-norm form, d = 3, one block of one neuron, sigma the identity, two logits) and
D = span(e_2) such that the projection cut of D (Theorem TV6 part 3) has D_P = log 2 - H(softmax(s, 0)) > 0 (H the
entropy), while B* of Theorem TV9 has D_P = 0.
Proof. P = {-1, 1} with equal weights. e(x) = x e_1 + x e_2: the area span(e_2) holds a copy of span(e_1). The block's
neuron reads e_2 and writes e_3 (bias 0, c_1 = 0), so h_1 = x e_1 + x e_2 + x e_3. The logits read U = (s e_3^T; 0),
so y_N(x) = (s x, 0). The projection cut reads Pi e_2 = 0, so it writes 0 and its logits are (0, 0) at both points;
D_P = (1/2)(KL(softmax(s, 0) || u) + KL(softmax(-s, 0) || u)) with u uniform, which is log 2 - H(softmax(s, 0)) by
symmetry, and is > 0 for s > 0. For B*: z_1 = Pi h_0 = x e_1 and t = x, an affine (linear) function of z_1; z_2 =
Pi h_1 = x e_1 + x e_3 and P_perp (s x, 0) is linear in z_2. Theorem TV9 part 4. QED.
Lean: none needed (finite computation); checked in `model/tv_cancel.py` (check F).
Comment. Proposition TV7's network has the same shape, with the dropped content x2 independent of the kept content
x1; there no cut does better than c(s). The difference between the two is whether the kept content predicts the
dropped content. Proposition TV9.2 makes this exact at the first write.

**Proposition TV9.2 (what no cut can recover) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Let B be any network whose
logits at x are a function of Pi e(x) alone; every re-fit area cut that drops D is one (its stream starts at Pi e(x)),
and so is every such cut with a constant direction added (Lemma TV12). With q(x) = softmax(y_N(x)) and, for each value
v of Pi e on P, qbar(v) the P-weighted mean of q over the points x of P with Pi e(x) = v,
   D_P(B) >= E_P KL(q(x) || qbar(Pi e(x))).
The bound is 0 when Pi e is one-to-one on P. It is the least loss over all functions of Pi e; cuts need not reach it.
Proof. B's distribution is p(Pi e(x)) for some function p. (For a re-fit area cut: its stream starts at Pi e(x)
(Lemma TV0), and every later value is computed from it by fixed maps.) On a set F of points with the same Pi e, with total weight
pi_F, sum over x in F of pi_x KL(q(x) || p) = sum over x in F of pi_x KL(q(x) || qbar) + pi_F KL(qbar || p) (expand the
logarithms; the cross term is sum pi_x q(x) . (log qbar - log p) = pi_F qbar . (log qbar - log p)). The last term is
>= 0. Sum over the sets F. QED.
Lean: none needed (the identity for the mean of KL divergences is a direct expansion, as in Proposition TV7); checked
in `model/tv_cancel.py` (check F).
Comment. TV9.2 and Theorem TV6 for B* bound the least loss of the cuts that drop D from both sides: below, what the
first write loses; above, what the best reads fail to cancel, carried to the logits. TV7's c(s) is TV9.2's bound for
its network.

**Lemma TV10 (without norms, a cut is fixed by what it drops) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts; the no-norm form).** In the no-norm
form, let D be a subspace and K any complement of D (K + D = R^d, K meets D only in 0), and let Pi_K be the projection
onto K along D. An **oblique cut** is a re-fit area cut of Definition DV2 with Pi replaced by Pi_K: first write
Pi_K e, writes Pi_K W_l and Pi_K c_l, block reads and logit reads any linear functions on K, any biases. Then the set
of logit functions of x computed by oblique cuts along K equals the set computed by re-fit area cuts that drop D
(K = D perp).
Proof. Pi_K is 0 on D, so Pi_K = Pi_K Pi with Pi = P_(D perp), and its restriction J to D perp is a one-to-one linear
map onto K (its kernel D meets D perp only in 0, and the dimensions agree). Given a re-fit cut with stream ht_l in
D perp, reads r', logit matrix U' and biases, let the oblique cut have reads r'' with r'' . J z = r' . z (that is,
r'' = (J^(-1))^T r' on K), logits U'' = U' J^(-1), and the same biases. By induction J ht_l is its stream: J ht_0 =
J Pi e = Pi_K e; its reads at J ht_(l-1) are r' . ht_(l-1), so its inside values are the same; and J ht_l =
J ht_(l-1) + J Pi (W_l gt_l + c_l) = J ht_(l-1) + Pi_K (W_l gt_l + c_l). Its logits are U' ht_L plus the same bias. The
converse uses J^(-1) in the same way. QED.
Lean: `gl_read` (a read of the moved stream, (R A^(-1))(A h) = R h, for a linear equivalence A; the step of TV10 is
the same algebra with A replaced by J, which maps D perp onto K) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`; the induction is
by hand; checked in `model/tv_cancel.py` (check B).
Comment. So, without norms, the class of functions that cuts compute is fixed by D: which way the kept part leans does
not change it. Its certificates are not fixed by D: every claim error of DM11 to DM14 and the bounds of TV2 and TV6 use
orthogonal projections, and they change with the angle. With norms the class itself changes in general: the oblique
cut's norm reads |Pi_K h|, not |Pi h|, the one number through which an angle acts (Fact F14 part 2).

**Lemma TV11 (overlap and crowding) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Let D and E be subspaces of R^d (E the
sum of the areas a cut keeps whole, D the part it drops).
1. For a vector r, there is r' with r' . z = 0 for z in D and r' . z = r . z for z in E (a re-fit read that ignores D
   and reads E exactly as N's read r does) if and only if r . z = 0 for every z in D cap E.
2. Hence such an r' exists for every r if and only if D and E meet only in 0.
Proof. (1) If r' exists and z is in D cap E, then 0 = r' . z = r . z. Conversely, let F be a complement of D cap E in E,
so D + E = D + F with D cap F = {0}. The function f(z_D + z_F) = r . z_F is linear on D + F; for z_E in E write
z_E = z_0 + z_F with z_0 in D cap E, so f(z_E) = r . z_F = r . z_E since r . z_0 = 0. Extend f to R^d (0 on a
complement of D + E) and let r' be its vector. (2) If some z != 0 lies in D cap E, take r = z. QED.
Lean: `crowd_no_read` (part 2) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`; part 1 is the extension of a linear function from
a direct sum (by hand); checked in `model/tv_cancel.py` (check C).
Comment. This is the line between overlap and crowding. A cut can drop D and keep a set of areas whole, for every
reader, exactly when D meets the SUM of the kept areas only in 0, at any angle. Meeting each kept area only in 0 is
not enough: three lines in a plane meet pairwise only in 0, yet dropping one while keeping the other two (which span
the plane) changes some read. Under the laminar areas of Definition DM11 the dropped part and the kept areas of a cut
are orthogonal, so part 2's condition always holds there and the lemma says nothing new; it has content only for areas
at an angle (node S-laminar, card
3-25). Families with more areas than the dimensions hold are outside Part B.V.

**Lemma TV12 (a re-set norm constant is one more direction) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** In the norm
form, let B be a network of Definition DV1 of width d' with first write e', block l with read matrix R'_l, bias b'_l,
writes W'_l and c'_l, logit matrix U', bias c'_y, and norm constants eps_l + c_l with c_l >= 0 (l = 1, ..., L + 1).
Let B^+ have width d' + 1 and stream (z, beta): first write (e'(x), c_1^(1/2)); at block l, read matrix (R'_l, 0), bias
b'_l, writes (W'_l; 0) and (c'_l, c_(l+1)^(1/2) - c_l^(1/2)); logit matrix (U', 0), bias c'_y; and norm constants eps_l.
Then B^+ computes B's logits at every input, and its last coordinate is read by no block and not by the logits.
Proof. By induction, beta before norm l is c_l^(1/2): it starts at c_1^(1/2), and block l adds c_(l+1)^(1/2) -
c_l^(1/2). If B^+'s z before norm l is B's stream h', then |(h', beta)|^2 + eps_l = |h'|^2 + c_l + eps_l, so the read
(R'_l, 0) n_(eps_l)(h', beta) = R'_l h' / (|h'|^2 + eps_l + c_l)^(1/2) is B's read; the inside values agree, and z after
block l is B's stream. The logits follow in the same way. QED.
Lean: `battery_const` ((c^(1/2))^2 = c inside the norm) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`; the induction is by hand;
checked in `model/tv_cancel.py` (check D).
Comment. A build that re-sets each norm's constant to eps_l + c_l (c_l >= 0) is a network of DV1 with N's constants
and one more stream direction that holds a constant and that nothing reads. That direction is written with constants
(its first-write entry and the bias increments), which a projection cut of DV2 does not write; so DV2 allows it by
name (node R-normconst). Write V_N(G) for the infimum of D_P over re-fit area cuts at G that keep N's constants. Then
V_area(G) <= V_N(G), since the class of V_area is larger. The re-set is worth exactly one constant, never-read
direction: TV12 is that equality. It is not worth one more direction of N's stream: a cut that keeps N's constants and
one more kept direction of S has first write Pi e and projected writes, so it cannot hold a constant, and its least
loss can stay above 0 where the re-set cut is exact (referee example in REFEREE-BVO2-2026-10-29.md, finding 11: d = 3,
no blocks, S = span(e_2, e_3) with |P_S x|^2 = 2 on P; dropping S with c = 2 is exact, keeping e_1 and any one vector of
S with N's constant is not). TV12 is about the folded networks of DV1. By Fact F13 part 1 a width-w RMSNorm with
constant eps_0 folds to the constant w eps_0. A build of width w' < d that keeps N's eps_0 has folded constant
w' eps_0 = d eps_0 + c with c = (w' - d) eps_0 < 0, which TV12 (c_l >= 0) does not cover; TV12 covers builds whose
folded constants are at least N's.

**Lemma TV13 (the signed carrying: the logit change is a sum of carried leaks) (under: pure-stream networks; area
cuts; the no-norm form).** In the no-norm form, let B be a re-fit area cut that drops D, with reads r'_(l,i) in D perp, biases b'_(l,i),
logit matrix U' with rows in D perp, bias c'_y, first write Pi e, writes Pi W_l and Pi c_l, and leaks
leak_(l,i)(x) = r'_(l,i) . Pi h_(l-1)(x) + b'_(l,i) - r_(l,i) . h_(l-1)(x) - b_(l,i) as in Theorem TV6. At x in P let
a_(l,i) = r_(l,i) . h_(l-1) + b_(l,i) and a'_(l,i) = r'_(l,i) . ht_(l-1) + b'_(l,i) be the two networks' reads (ht the
cut's stream, as in Lemma TV0), and let the **slope** s_(l,i)(x) = (sigma_l(a') - sigma_l(a)) / (a' - a) when a' != a,
and 0 when a' = a. Let S_l(x) = diag(s_(l,i)(x)), J_l(x) = Pi W_l S_l(x) R'_l, and
Phi_l(x) = (I + J_L(x)) (I + J_(L-1)(x)) ... (I + J_(l+1)(x)) (Phi_L = I). Then at every x in P
   P_perp (y_B(x) - y_N(x)) = omega(x) + sum over l = 1, ..., L of P_perp U' Phi_l(x) Pi W_l S_l(x) leak_l(x),
with omega(x) = P_perp (U' Pi h_L(x) + c'_y - U h_L(x) - c_y) and leak_l the vector of the leak_(l,i). The identity
holds for any function sigma_l applied to each coordinate. If sigma_l is Lipschitz with constant Lip_l, each
|s_(l,i)| <= Lip_l.
Proof. Let delta_l = ht_l - Pi h_l (delta_0 = 0). Then a' - a = r' . ht_(l-1) + b' - a = r' . delta_(l-1) + leak, since
r' . Pi h_(l-1) + b' - a = leak. So sigma(a') - sigma(a) = s (r' . delta_(l-1) + leak) in both cases of the definition
of s, and delta_l = delta_(l-1) + Pi W_l (gt_l - g_l) = (I + J_l) delta_(l-1) + Pi W_l S_l leak_l. By induction,
delta_L = sum over l of Phi_l Pi W_l S_l leak_l. The logits: y_B - y_N = U' ht_L + c'_y - U h_L - c_y =
U' delta_L + (U' Pi h_L + c'_y - U h_L - c_y). Apply P_perp. |s| <= Lip_l since sigma_l is Lip_l-Lipschitz. QED.
Lean: none needed (the slope step is the definition of s; the rest is a linear recursion); checked in
`model/tv_cancel.py` (check G: the identity to rounding error).
Comment (the network's own cancelling). The terms of the sum have signs. When a later block of the cut undoes what an
earlier leak did, the terms cancel in the sum. The identity is true by the definition of s (a difference quotient), so
by itself it says nothing about N; what it does is show where Theorem TV6 loses. Theorem TV6 is this identity
with each entry of P_perp U', Phi_l, Pi W_l and S_l replaced by a size (its norm per area, Lip_l for s), and the sum
over x and over l bounded by Minkowski's inequality; every cancellation is lost there. The slopes S_l and the products
Phi_l are those of the cut, so the terms are not computed from N, P and D alone; Proposition TV14 replaces them by N's.
With
norms, each block's change also has the norm's term of step (a) of TV6, which is not linear in delta; the identity
then needs a second slope for the norm, and is not written here.

**Proposition TV14 (the signed carrying from N's own slopes) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts; sigma with a
Lipschitz derivative; the no-norm form).** In the no-norm form, let each sigma_l be differentiable with |sigma'_l| <= Lip_l and sigma'_l
Lipschitz with constant Lip'_l (for example tanh or GELU; not ReLU). Let B be a re-fit area cut that drops D, as in
Lemma TV13, with leaks leak_l and omega as there. Define from N, P, D and B's reads, biases and logits (with no run of
B), at each x in P:
   S^N_l(x) = diag(sigma'_l(a_(l,i)(x))),   J^N_l(x) = Pi W_l S^N_l(x) R'_l,
   Phi^N_l(x) = (I + J^N_L(x)) ... (I + J^N_(l+1)(x))   (Phi^N_L = I),
   Lambda_N(x) = omega(x) + sum over l of P_perp U' Phi^N_l(x) Pi W_l S^N_l(x) leak_l(x),
   beta_0 = 0,  beta_l(x) = (1 + Lip_l |Pi W_l| |R'_l|) beta_(l-1)(x) + Lip_l |Pi W_l| |leak_l(x)|,
   gamma_0 = 0, gamma_l(x) = |I + J^N_l(x)| gamma_(l-1)(x) + (Lip'_l / 2) |Pi W_l| sum over i of (|r'_(l,i)| beta_(l-1)(x) + |leak_(l,i)(x)|)^2,
   rem(x) = |P_perp U'| gamma_L(x),
with |.| the Euclidean norm of a vector and the operator norm of a matrix. Then at every x in P
   |P_perp (y_B(x) - y_N(x)) - Lambda_N(x)| <= rem(x),   and   D_P(B) <= (1/4) (||Lambda_N|| + ||rem||)^2.
Each term of gamma_L carries the square of a weighted sum of earlier leak norms (beta_l is one), so the formula for rem
is of degree 2 in the leaks: with N, D, R', U' and the slopes S^N fixed, replacing every leak by t times it multiplies
Lambda_N - omega by t and rem by t^2. This is a property of the formula. The leaks of a cut are not free: by Theorem
TV9 part 1 each is at least its least leak, which is small only when N's reads are close to affine functions of the
kept content on P.
Proof. Let delta_l = ht_l - Pi h_l as in Lemma TV13, so delta_l = delta_(l-1) + Pi W_l S_l (R'_l delta_(l-1) + leak_l).
(a) |delta_l| <= beta_l: |S_l v| <= Lip_l |v| and |R'_l delta + leak| <= |R'_l| |delta| + |leak|; induction.
(b) Let delta^N_l = (I + J^N_l) delta^N_(l-1) + Pi W_l S^N_l leak_l, delta^N_0 = 0, so that delta^N_L = sum over l of
Phi^N_l Pi W_l S^N_l leak_l. The difference e_l = delta_l - delta^N_l satisfies
   e_l = (I + J^N_l) e_(l-1) + Pi W_l (S_l - S^N_l)(R'_l delta_(l-1) + leak_l)
(subtract the two recursions and add and subtract Pi W_l S^N_l R'_l delta_(l-1)). Coordinate i of
(S_l - S^N_l)(R'_l delta_(l-1) + leak_l) is (s - sigma'(a))(a' - a) = sigma(a') - sigma(a) - sigma'(a)(a' - a), with
a' - a = r'_(l,i) . delta_(l-1) + leak_(l,i) (proof of Lemma TV13). For a function with an Lip'-Lipschitz derivative,
|sigma(a') - sigma(a) - sigma'(a)(a' - a)| <= (Lip' / 2)(a' - a)^2 (integrate sigma'(a + u (a' - a)) - sigma'(a) over
u in [0, 1]). So that coordinate is at most (Lip'_l / 2)(|r'_(l,i)| beta_(l-1) + |leak_(l,i)|)^2 by (a), and the
Euclidean norm of the vector is at most the sum of its coordinates' sizes. Induction gives |e_l| <= gamma_l.
(c) By Lemma TV13, P_perp (y_B - y_N) = omega + P_perp U' delta_L = Lambda_N + P_perp U' e_L, and |P_perp U' e_L| <=
|P_perp U'| gamma_L = rem. (d) |P_perp (y_B - y_N)(x)| <= |Lambda_N(x)| + rem(x) at every x; Minkowski's inequality for
||.|| and Fact F11. Degree: beta is linear in the leaks, so gamma and rem are quadratic. QED.
Lean: none in this session (the Taylor bound |f(b) - f(a) - f'(a)(b - a)| <= (L / 2)(b - a)^2 for f with an
L-Lipschitz derivative is standard and provable in Mathlib; it is an open Lean item; the rest is the linear recursion
of Lemma TV13 and the triangle inequality); checked in `model/tv_cancel.py` (check H: the pointwise inequality, the
bound, and a family N_t whose leaks shrink with t).
Comment. Lambda_N is the cut's own recursion linearised at N's pre-activations (the chain rule). The expansion keeps
signs, so terms that cancel in the true change also cancel in Lambda_N; TV14 does not say that N cancels anything.
Only the remainder is taken by sizes. Along a family of cuts whose leaks tend to 0 while R' and U' stay bounded, the
bound tends to (1/4) ||Lambda_N||^2, which is (1/4) ||P_perp (y_B - y_N)||^2 to first order: the only loss left is that
of Fact F11. Theorem TV6 takes sizes already at first order. Lambda_N depends on B's reads; as a claim error,
||Lambda_N||^2 names a build unless the reads are fixed from N, P and D, as the projection reads of Theorem TV6 part 3
or the reads r* of Theorem TV9 are. With norms each block's change also has the norm's term (step (a) of TV6), which
needs its own slope; that case is Conjecture DV3.

**Definition DM15 (an area map complete for a zoom) (added 2026-10-29, Part B.V.3).** Let N be as in Definition DV1
(with every eps_l > 0 in the norm form) and M an area map (DM11) with its **members** (DM14: the own parts of its areas
and the part of R^d outside every area). A **zoom of areas** is G_0, ..., G_m with each group S a sum of areas of M whose
sum is direct, with a target size k_S < dim S, the groups of one level with a direct sum (pairwise orthogonal in the
laminar case; at an angle "pairwise" is not enough, Lemma TV11), and each group of G_(j+1) a
sum of groups of G_j. (A group need not be an area: under laminar areas an area that is a sum of two or more groups
would have own part 0.) The members split each group. M is **complete** for the zoom when, for every level j, M holds
carried leak claims (D_j, members, l) of DM14 for l = 1, ..., L + 1, for some D_j that is a sum of members inside the
groups of G_j with dim S - dim(S cap D_j) <= k_S for every group S of G_j. Then V_S = the sum of the members inside S that are not inside D_j (S minus (S cap D_j) in the laminar case). Whether M
is complete for a zoom is decided by scanning M's carried leak claims and rational linear algebra: time polynomial in
their size. Like Definition DM6, it is a relation between a map and a zoom, not a claim.

**Corollary TV6.2 (the stream branch in T5's form, for complete area maps) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts;
carried leak claims).** Let N be as in Definition DV1 with Lipschitz sigma_l and every eps_l > 0 in the norm form, and M an area map
complete for a zoom of areas G_0, ..., G_m (Definition DM15). The rule: for each level j, B_j = the projection cut that
drops D_j (reads Pi_j r, N's biases, constants eps_l + c_l(D_j), logit matrix U Pi_j). Then:
1. B_j replaces each group S of G_j by the directions V_S inside S, at most k_S of them, and keeps every direction
   outside the groups; it is a re-fit area cut at G_j with constants re-set (node R-normconst), that is, by Lemma TV12,
   with N's constants and one more constant, never-read direction.
2. D_P(B_j) <= (1/4) (sum over l = 1, ..., L + 1 of eps_cl(D_j, l)^(1/2))^2: a function of the list of the claims'
   errors alone, and 0 when they are 0. This bounds the loss of B_j, hence the least loss at level j; it says nothing
   about the least-loss build itself when some error is above 0 (as for Theorem TY2).
3. If every claim of M has error 0, D_P(B_j) = 0, so B_j has the least loss among all such networks, and its weights
   are a closed form in N's weights, P and M.
4. The one-time computation is the m + 1 cuts (each a projection of N's matrices and m + 1 sets of constants
   c_l(D_j)); after it, switching to level j selects stored weights.
Proof. (1) Pi_j keeps D_j perp, which is the sum of the V_S and of everything outside the groups. (2) Corollary TV6.1 for
D = D_j; its claims are in M by completeness. (3) Part 2 and D_P >= 0. (4) B_j depends only on N, P and D_j. QED.
Lean: none needed.
Comment. This is the first result of Part B.V in the form of both of T5's promises, on the side branch of node
S-laminar (laminar areas) and under node R-normconst. It holds by construction: a complete map holds, per level, the
claims whose errors are TV6's terms for that level's cut, so which part D_j the map certifies carries the zoom.
A route to a map complete for every zoom at once (no-norm form, projection reads, orthogonal members): the leak and
omega of D are sums over the members inside D, and dropping members only lowers T_l and u entry by entry, so
eps_cl(D, l)^(1/2) is at most a sum over the members B inside D of one claim per member, carried along N's own area
graph. Not proved here. Its graded bound carries N's gains inside the claims' errors
(DM14), so it is loose wherever Theorem TV6 is; with the reads of Theorem TV9 in place of the projection reads, or the
signed carrying of Proposition TV14 in place of TV6, the same construction gives other claim types; which of them stays
small on trained networks is open.

### B.V.4 The signed carrying with norms, for every Lipschitz activation (added 2026-10-29, round 3)

Proposition TV14 has two premises that leave networks out: no norm before any read (node S-nonorm), and an activation
with a Lipschitz derivative (node S-smoothact, which leaves out ReLU). This section removes both. What it does:
1. Definition DV4: the remainder modulus of an activation at a point. It is the one quantity that the second-order
   step of TV14 needs, and it is defined for every Lipschitz activation.
2. Lemma TV15.1: the modulus for smooth activations (the old quadratic term), for differentiable points of any
   Lipschitz activation (it is small compared with the window), and for ReLU-type activations (it is 0 inside the
   distance to the nearest kink: a margin).
3. Lemma TV15.2: the norm's slope and its remainder. The constant of the second derivative is 2 / 3^(1/2).
4. Lemma TV13.1: the exact identity of Lemma TV13 with norms (a second slope: the norm's secant matrix).
5. Theorem TV15: Proposition TV14 with norms and any Lipschitz activation. This proves Conjecture DV3 (D.15) and more.
6. Corollary TV15.3: the order of the remainder. For ReLU without norms the signed sum with N's own on/off pattern is
   the exact logit change when every read window of the cut stays inside N's margin.

**Definition DV4 (the remainder modulus of an activation) (added 2026-10-29, Part B.V.4).** Let sigma: R -> R be
Lipschitz with constant Lip, a a point, and s a number with |s| <= Lip (the **chosen slope** at a: sigma'(a) where
sigma has a derivative at a, and any such number where it has none). The **remainder modulus** of sigma at (a, s) is
   psi_(sigma, a, s)(t) = sup over |u| <= t of |sigma(a + u) - sigma(a) - s u|,   t >= 0.
It is nondecreasing in t (the sup runs over a growing set), psi(0) = 0, and psi(t) <= 2 Lip t (each of the two
terms sigma(a + u) - sigma(a) and s u is at most Lip |u|). For N's neuron i of block l at an input x, a = a_(l,i)(x)
is N's pre-activation and the chosen slope is s_(l,i)(x); write psi_(l,i,x). Any upper bound on the modulus that is
nondecreasing in t (for example 2 Lip t, or the closed forms of Lemma TV15.1) may replace it in Theorem TV15, with
the same proof; for a general sigma the supremum itself need not be computable exactly.

**Lemma TV15.1 (the remainder modulus in three cases) (under: pure-stream networks).** Let sigma, a, s and omega be as
in Definition DV4.
1. (Smooth.) If sigma has a derivative everywhere, sigma' is Lipschitz with constant Lip', and s = sigma'(a), then
   psi(t) <= (Lip' / 2) t^2.
2. (Any Lipschitz sigma, at a differentiable point.) If sigma has a derivative at a and s = sigma'(a), then
   psi(t) / t -> 0 as t -> 0.
3. (Kinks.) Let sigma be continuous and affine on each interval between the points of a finite set K (the kinks), and
   let a not lie in K, with s the slope of the piece that holds a. Then psi(t) = 0 for t <= dist(a, K). For the
   leaky ReLU sigma(v) = max(v, alpha v) with 0 <= alpha <= 1 (alpha = 0 is ReLU) and a != 0,
      psi(t) = (1 - alpha) max(t - |a|, 0).
Proof. (1) sigma(a + u) - sigma(a) - sigma'(a) u = integral over v in [0, 1] of (sigma'(a + v u) - sigma'(a)) u dv, and
|sigma'(a + v u) - sigma'(a)| <= Lip' v |u|; the integral of v over [0, 1] is 1/2. (2) This is the definition of the
derivative: for every e > 0 there is t_0 with |sigma(a + u) - sigma(a) - sigma'(a) u| <= e |u| for |u| <= t_0, so
psi(t) <= e t for t <= t_0. (3) On [a - t, a + t] with t <= dist(a, K) there is no kink in the open interval, so
sigma is affine there with slope s, by continuity also at the ends, and every term of the sup is 0. Leaky ReLU, a > 0,
s = 1: sigma(a + u) - (a + u) = max(0, (alpha - 1)(a + u)) = (1 - alpha) max(0, -(a + u)), which is at most
(1 - alpha) max(0, t - a) for |u| <= t, with equality at u = -t. For a < 0, s = alpha: sigma(a + u) - alpha (a + u) =
max(0, (1 - alpha)(a + u)) <= (1 - alpha) max(0, t - |a|), with equality at u = t. QED.
Lean: `relu_rem_pos` and `relu_rem_neg` (part 3 for ReLU, the inequality for every |u| <= t) in
`lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`; parts 1 and 2 are the integral form of the remainder and the definition of the
derivative (standard; not formalised here); checked in `model/tv_norm.py` (check A: the modulus on a grid, for tanh,
GELU, ReLU and leaky ReLU, against the three formulas).
Comment. At a = 0, ReLU with chosen slope s in [0, 1] has psi(t) = max(s, 1 - s) t: first order. That is the only
case in which a ReLU neuron adds a first-order term, and it needs N's pre-activation to be exactly 0 at a point of P.

**Lemma TV15.2 (the norm's slope and its remainder) (under: pure-stream networks).** Let eps >= 0,
nu(z) = (|z|^2 + eps)^(1/2) and n(z) = z / nu(z) on the set where nu(z) > 0. There:
1. n is smooth, Dn(z) = (I - n(z) n(z)^T) / nu(z), and |Dn(z)| <= 1 / nu(z) (operator norm).
2. For every vector v, |D^2 n(z)[v, v]| <= (2 / 3^(1/2)) |v|^2 / nu(z)^2, and the constant 2 / 3^(1/2) is the least
   one that holds for every eps and z.
3. For z, delta in R^d let m(z, delta) = (max(|z| - |delta|, 0)^2 + eps)^(1/2). If m(z, delta) > 0, then
      |n(z + delta) - n(z)| <= |delta| / m(z, delta),
      |n(z + delta) - n(z) - Dn(z) delta| <= |delta|^2 / (3^(1/2) m(z, delta)^2).
   m(z, delta) depends on delta only through |delta| and does not grow with it, so both bounds hold with any
   beta >= |delta| in place of |delta| (both inside m and in the numerators), provided m(z, beta) > 0.
Proof. (1) The derivative of z / nu(z) in the direction v is v / nu - z (z . v) / nu^3 = (I - n n^T) v / nu. The
matrix I - n n^T is symmetric with eigenvalues 1 (on n perp) and 1 - |n|^2 in [0, 1] (on n), so its operator norm is
at most 1. (2) Differentiate once more along v: D^2 n(z)[v, v] = (-2 (z . v) v - |v|^2 z) / nu^3 + 3 (z . v)^2 z / nu^5.
For |v| = 1 put p = z / nu, c = p . v and q = |p|^2 = |z|^2 / (|z|^2 + eps), so 0 <= q <= 1 and c^2 <= q. Then
nu^2 D^2 n[v, v] = -2 c v + (3 c^2 - 1) p, and
   |-2 c v + (3 c^2 - 1) p|^2 = 4 c^2 + (3 c^2 - 1)^2 q - 4 c^2 (3 c^2 - 1) = 4/3 - (4 - 3 q)(3 c^2 - 1)^2 / 3,
an identity in c and q (expand both sides). Since q <= 1 < 4/3, the right side is at most 4/3. The general v follows
by homogeneity. Equality holds exactly when 3 c^2 = 1, possible when q >= 1/3; for example q = 1/3 and v = p / |p|
(eps = 2 |z|^2). (3) On the segment z + u delta,
u in [0, 1], |z + u delta| >= max(|z| - |delta|, 0), so nu(z + u delta) >= m(z, delta) > 0 and the segment lies in
the set where n is smooth. The first bound is the integral of Dn(z + u delta) delta over u with part 1. The second is
Taylor's formula with integral remainder, n(z + delta) - n(z) - Dn(z) delta = integral over u in [0, 1] of
(1 - u) D^2 n(z + u delta)[delta, delta] du, with part 2 and the integral of (1 - u), which is 1/2. Monotone: |delta|
enters m only through max(|z| - |delta|, 0), which does not grow with |delta|. QED.
Lean: `norm_hess_identity` (the identity of part 2, by `ring`), `norm_hess_le` (the bound 4/3 for q <= 4/3)
and `norm_hess_vec` (the vector step: the squared size of -2 c v + (3 c^2 - 1) p) in
`lean/coarse/Coarse/Stream.lean`; the derivatives and Taylor's formula are standard calculus (not formalised here);
checked in `model/tv_norm.py` (check B: the second derivative by sympy against the formula, the supremum 2 / 3^(1/2) on
a grid, and part 3 at random z, delta, eps).

**Lemma TV13.1 (the signed carrying with norms: an exact identity) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Let N be
as in Definition DV1 in either form, and B a re-fit area cut that drops D as in Lemma TV13, with norm constants
eps'_l >= 0 in the norm form, leaks leak_(l,i) as in Theorem TV6 (with N's norm n and the cut's norm n'), slopes
s_(l,i) as in Lemma TV13, delta_l = ht_l - Pi h_l, and z_l = Pi h_(l-1) (l = 1, ..., L + 1). At an input x where the
segment from z_l to z_l + delta_(l-1) avoids nu' = 0 for every l (always when every eps'_l > 0), let
   M_l(x) = integral over u in [0, 1] of Dn'_l(z_l + u delta_(l-1)) du   (the norm's **secant matrix**; M_l = I in the
   no-norm form),
J_l = Pi W_l S_l R'_l M_l and Phi_l = (I + J_L) ... (I + J_(l+1)) (Phi_L = I). Then
   P_perp (y_B(x) - y_N(x)) = omega(x) + sum over l = 1, ..., L of P_perp U' M_(L+1) Phi_l Pi W_l S_l leak_l,
with omega(x) = P_perp (U' n'_(L+1)(z_(L+1)) + c'_y - U n_(L+1)(h_L) - c_y). In the no-norm form this is Lemma TV13.
Proof. ht_(l-1) = z_l + delta_(l-1), so n'_l(ht_(l-1)) - n'_l(z_l) = M_l delta_(l-1) (the fundamental theorem of
calculus along the segment, on which n'_l is smooth). The cut's read minus N's read is
a' - a = r'_(l,i) . (n'(ht_(l-1)) - n'(z_l)) + leak_(l,i) = r'_(l,i) . M_l delta_(l-1) + leak_(l,i), by the definition
of leak. Then sigma(a') - sigma(a) = s (a' - a) and delta_l = delta_(l-1) + Pi W_l (gt_l - g_l) =
(I + J_l) delta_(l-1) + Pi W_l S_l leak_l, as in Lemma TV13. At the logits, y_B - y_N = U' (n'(ht_L) - n'(z_(L+1))) +
(U' n'(z_(L+1)) + c'_y - U n(h_L) - c_y) = U' M_(L+1) delta_L + (that term); apply P_perp. QED.
Lean: none needed (the fundamental theorem of calculus along a segment, then the linear recursion of Lemma TV13);
checked in `model/tv_norm.py` (check C: the identity to rounding error, with M_l by quadrature).

**Theorem TV15 (the signed carrying from N's own slopes, with norms, for every Lipschitz activation) (under:
pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Let N be as in Definition DV1, in either form, with each sigma_l Lipschitz with
constant Lip_l. Let B be a re-fit area cut that drops D (Definition DV2, except that each eps'_l >= 0
is arbitrary) with first write Pi e, writes Pi W_l and
Pi c_l, block read vectors r'_(l,i) in D perp and biases b'_(l,i), norm constants eps'_l >= 0 (norm form), a logit
matrix U' whose rows lie in D perp, and a logit bias c'_y. Let leak_(l,i) be as in Theorem TV6 and omega as in Lemma
TV13.1. Define from N, P, D and B's reads, biases, logits and norm constants eps'_l
(with no run of B), at each x in P, with z_l = Pi h_(l-1)(x)
(l = 1, ..., L + 1) and N's pre-activations a_(l,i)(x):
   H_l = Dn'_l(z_l) = (I - n'_l(z_l) n'_l(z_l)^T) / nu'_l(z_l)   (H_l = I in the no-norm form),
   s_(l,i) = a chosen slope of sigma_l at a_(l,i) (Definition DV4),   S^N_l = diag(s_(l,i)),
   J^N_l = Pi W_l S^N_l R'_l H_l,   Phi^N_l = (I + J^N_L) ... (I + J^N_(l+1))   (Phi^N_L = I),
   Lambda_N = omega + sum over l = 1, ..., L of P_perp U' H_(L+1) Phi^N_l Pi W_l S^N_l leak_l,
and the bounds, with beta_0 = 0 and, for l = 1, ..., L + 1 (norm form; in the no-norm form kappa_l = 1, theta_l = 0):
   m_l = (max(|z_l| - beta_(l-1), 0)^2 + eps'_l)^(1/2),   kappa_l = 1 / m_l,   theta_l = beta_(l-1)^2 / (3^(1/2) m_l^2),
and, for l = 1, ..., L:
   t_(l,i) = |r'_(l,i)| kappa_l beta_(l-1) + |leak_(l,i)|,
   beta_l = beta_(l-1) + Lip_l |Pi W_l| (|R'_l| kappa_l beta_(l-1) + |leak_l|),
   gamma_0 = 0,  gamma_l = |I + J^N_l| gamma_(l-1) + |Pi W_l S^N_l R'_l| theta_l + |Pi W_l| |w_l|,
with w_l the vector of the psi_(l,i,x)(t_(l,i)) (Definition DV4, at N's a_(l,i) and the chosen s_(l,i)), and
   rem = |P_perp U' H_(L+1)| gamma_L + |P_perp U'| theta_(L+1),
with |.| the Euclidean norm of a vector and the operator norm of a matrix. At an x where every m_l > 0 (always when
every eps'_l > 0, and always in the no-norm form):
   |P_perp (y_B(x) - y_N(x)) - Lambda_N(x)| <= rem(x).
If every m_l > 0 at every x in P, D_P(B) <= (1/4) (||Lambda_N|| + ||rem||)^2.
Part 2 (a sharper drift). The same holds with beta_l replaced, at each l = 1, ..., L and at each x, by
   beta^t_l = min(beta_l, |delta^N_l(x)| + gamma_l(x)),
with delta^N_l the linear recursion of step (b) of the proof (computed from the same data as Lambda_N), and with
beta^t in place of beta in every later m, kappa, theta, t and in the next step of the recursion for beta.
Proof. Let delta_l = ht_l - Pi h_l (delta_0 = 0), Delta_(l,i) = a'_(l,i) - a_(l,i) (the cut's read minus N's), and
for l = 1, ..., L + 1 let rho^n_l = n'_l(z_l + delta_(l-1)) - n'_l(z_l) - H_l delta_(l-1) (0 in the no-norm form).
(a) |delta_l| <= beta_l. Suppose |delta_(l-1)| <= beta_(l-1). By Lemma TV15.2 part 3 with beta_(l-1) in place of
|delta_(l-1)|, |n'_l(ht_(l-1)) - n'_l(z_l)| <= kappa_l beta_(l-1) and |rho^n_l| <= theta_l. As in the proof of Lemma
TV13.1, Delta_(l,i) = r'_(l,i) . (n'_l(ht_(l-1)) - n'_l(z_l)) + leak_(l,i), so |Delta_(l,i)| <= t_(l,i) and the
vector Delta_l has |Delta_l| <= |R'_l| kappa_l beta_(l-1) + |leak_l|. Since delta_l = delta_(l-1) +
Pi W_l (sigma_l(a'_l) - sigma_l(a_l)) and sigma_l is Lip_l-Lipschitz, |delta_l| <= beta_l.
(b) Write sigma_l(a'_(l,i)) - sigma_l(a_(l,i)) = s_(l,i) Delta_(l,i) + rho^s_(l,i). By Definition DV4 and (a),
|rho^s_(l,i)| <= psi_(l,i,x)(|Delta_(l,i)|) <= psi_(l,i,x)(t_(l,i)), since the modulus is nondecreasing; so the
vector rho^s_l has |rho^s_l| <= |w_l|. With Delta_l = R'_l (H_l delta_(l-1) + rho^n_l) + leak_l,
   delta_l = (I + J^N_l) delta_(l-1) + Pi W_l S^N_l leak_l + Pi W_l (S^N_l R'_l rho^n_l + rho^s_l).
Let delta^N_l = (I + J^N_l) delta^N_(l-1) + Pi W_l S^N_l leak_l, delta^N_0 = 0, so delta^N_L = sum over l of
Phi^N_l Pi W_l S^N_l leak_l. Then e_l = delta_l - delta^N_l satisfies e_l = (I + J^N_l) e_(l-1) +
Pi W_l S^N_l R'_l rho^n_l + Pi W_l rho^s_l, and by induction |e_l| <= gamma_l.
(c) The logits: y_B - y_N = U' (n'_(L+1)(z_(L+1) + delta_L) - n'_(L+1)(z_(L+1))) + (U' n'_(L+1)(z_(L+1)) + c'_y -
U n_(L+1)(h_L) - c_y) = U' H_(L+1) (delta^N_L + e_L) + U' rho^n_(L+1) + (that term). Apply P_perp:
P_perp (y_B - y_N) = Lambda_N + P_perp U' H_(L+1) e_L + P_perp U' rho^n_(L+1), and the last two terms are at most
|P_perp U' H_(L+1)| gamma_L + |P_perp U'| theta_(L+1) = rem by (b) and Lemma TV15.2 part 3.
(d) So |P_perp (y_B - y_N)(x)| <= |Lambda_N(x)| + rem(x) at every x. Fact F11 gives D_P(B) <= (1/4)
||P_perp (y_B - y_N)||^2, and Minkowski's inequality for ||.|| gives the bound.
(e) Part 2. Steps (a) and (b) use the bound on |delta_(l-1)| only through some number that is at least |delta_(l-1)|.
By induction on l, beta^t_(l-1) is such a number; then gamma_l, computed with it, bounds |e_l|, so |delta_l| <=
|delta^N_l| + |e_l| <= |delta^N_l| + gamma_l, and step (a) gives |delta_l| <= beta_l as well; so |delta_l| <= beta^t_l.
Every later step goes through with beta^t. QED.
Lean: the finite steps are `norm_hess_identity`, `norm_hess_le`, `relu_rem_pos` and `relu_rem_neg` (Lemmas TV15.1 and
TV15.2); the rest is the linear recursion of Lemma TV13 with the triangle inequality, as in Proposition TV14; checked
in `model/tv_norm.py` (check D: the pointwise inequality and the bound, both forms, tanh, GELU, ReLU; check D2:
part 2, never looser than part 1; check E: the family with shrinking leaks).
Comment (part 2). Step (a) carries the drift by sizes, so beta grows by an operator norm at every block. Part 2
uses the signed linear drift delta^N, in which N's own cancellations are kept, plus the remainder already bounded.
Comment. Lambda_N is the cut's recursion linearised at N's own point: the activation's slope at N's pre-activation
and the norm's slope at N's stream with D removed. Both come from N, P and D (and the cut's reads), with no run of
the cut. For ReLU, S^N_l is N's on/off pattern. The no-norm form is the case H_l = I and theta_l = 0; with a smooth
sigma_l, Lemma TV15.1 part 1 gives |w_l| <= (Lip'_l / 2) |(t_(l,i)^2)_i| <= (Lip'_l / 2) sum over i of t_(l,i)^2, so
Proposition TV14 is a special case. The tag lists neither node S-nonorm nor node S-smoothact: Theorem TV15 holds for
both forms of Definition DV1 and for every Lipschitz activation. Conjecture DV3 (D.15) is part of it (the norm form
with a smooth sigma; the remainder is of second order by Corollary TV15.3). As in TV14, Lambda_N depends on B's reads,
so as a claim error it names a build unless the reads are fixed from N, P and D (the projection reads, or the reads
r* of Theorem TV9). A cheaper premise form: if one checks beta_(l-1) <= eta |z_l| with eta < 1, then
m_l >= (1 - eta) nu'_l(z_l) >= (1 - eta) rho_l (rho_l as in Theorem TV6), which gives the factor 1 / ((1 - eta) rho_l) of route (i) in D.15 (Proposition TV8 uses a
different premise and coupling).

**Corollary TV15.3 (the order of the remainder) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Fix N, P, D and B's reads,
biases, logit matrix and chosen slopes, and evaluate the formulas of Theorem TV15 with every leak_(l,i)(x) and omega(x)
replaced by t times it, t in [0, 1] (a property of the formulas, as in Proposition TV14). Write Lambda_N(t) and
rem(t), and suppose every m_l > 0 at t = 1 at every x in P. Then Lambda_N(t) = t Lambda_N(1), and:
1. there are numbers b_l, from the data, with beta_l(t) <= t b_l, so the norm terms theta_l(t) are at most a constant
   times t^2;
2. if every sigma_l has a Lip'_l-Lipschitz derivative, rem(t) <= c t^2 for a constant c from the data;
3. if every sigma_l is affine between the points of a finite kink set K_l, and no pre-activation a_(l,i)(x) of N on P
   lies in K_l (chosen slope: that of its piece), let mu* = min over l, i, x of dist(a_(l,i)(x), K_l) > 0. Then there
   is t_1 > 0, from the data, such that every w_l(t) = 0 for t <= t_1: rem(t) is the norm terms alone, at most c t^2.
   In the no-norm form rem(t) = 0 for t <= t_1 (a property of the formulas). For the cut itself (t = 1): in the
   no-norm form, if t_(l,i)(x) <= dist(a_(l,i)(x), K_l) for every l, i and every x in P (for example when t_1 >= 1),
   then P_perp (y_B - y_N) = Lambda_N at every point of P;
4. if every sigma_l has a derivative at every a_(l,i)(x) and s_(l,i) is that derivative, rem(t) / t -> 0 as t -> 0.
Proof. Lambda_N is linear in (omega, leak). (1) Each step of the recursion for beta is nondecreasing in beta_(l-1)
(kappa_l grows with it) and in t, so by induction beta_(l-1)(t) <= beta_(l-1)(1) for t in [0, 1]; hence
m_l(t) >= m_l(1) > 0 and kappa_l(t) <= k_l := kappa_l(1). Let b_0 = 0 and b_l = b_(l-1) (1 + Lip_l |Pi W_l| |R'_l| k_l)
+ Lip_l |Pi W_l| |leak_l(x)| (the leaks at t = 1). Induction gives beta_l(t) <= t b_l, so theta_l(t) <=
t^2 b_(l-1)^2 / (3^(1/2) m_l(1)^2), and t_(l,i)(t) <= t tau_(l,i) with tau_(l,i) = |r'_(l,i)| k_l b_(l-1) +
|leak_(l,i)|. (2) By Lemma TV15.1 part 1, each entry of w_l(t) is at most
(Lip'_l / 2) t^2 tau_(l,i)^2. gamma_L is a sum of the theta and w terms with coefficients that do not depend on t
(J^N_l does not), so it is at most a constant times t^2, and so is rem. (3) With tau* = max over l, i, x of
tau_(l,i)(x) (finite: P is a finite list), take t_1 = mu* / tau* (t_1 = 1 if tau* = 0). For t <= t_1 every
t_(l,i)(t) <= mu* <= dist(a_(l,i), K_l), so every psi_(l,i,x)(t_(l,i)) = 0 by Lemma TV15.1 part 3. In the no-norm form theta = 0 as well, so gamma_L = 0 and rem = 0. At t = 1 under the pointwise premise, every
psi term is 0 by Lemma TV15.1 part 3 and theta = 0, so rem = 0 and Theorem TV15 gives equality. (4) Each entry psi_(l,i,x)(t tau_(l,i)) / t -> 0 by Lemma TV15.1 part
2 (and is 0 when tau_(l,i) = 0); the theta terms are O(t^2); a finite sum. QED.
Lean: none needed (bookkeeping on the recursions of Theorem TV15); checked in `model/tv_norm.py` (check E: rem(t) / t^2
bounded for GELU and tanh with norms; rem(t) = 0 below t_1 for ReLU without norms; for the family N_t of networks whose leaks shrink, the true change
equals Lambda_N to rounding error once every window is inside the margin).
Comment. Part 3 says what a kink costs: nothing, while the leaks are too small to switch any of N's neurons on P on
or off. The margin mu* is a property of N and P alone. Part 3's exactness in the no-norm form is the plain fact that
a ReLU network is affine on the region where no neuron switches; the corollary gives the computable radius. The
radius t_1 can be small on trained networks (a pre-activation close to 0 at some point of P); then part 4 still holds
and Theorem TV15 still bounds the remainder at every t. The leaks are not free (Theorem TV9 part 1): the scaling is a
property of the formulas.

### B.V.5 Areas at an angle (node S-laminar, decided by delegation 2026-10-29; added 2026-10-29, round 3)

Definitions DM11, DV2 and DM15 now allow areas at an angle: any two areas nested or meeting only in 0, children with a
direct sum, and own parts that the map chooses. A cut drops a part D (any complement of what it keeps in each area) and may keep the rest in any coordinates (DV2;
node R-cutclass):
the orthogonal projection cut, or the oblique cut that keeps a chosen complement K of D exactly. What it does:
1. Lemma TV16: every cut that drops D is the orthogonal cut in other stream coordinates. Without norms the angle
   changes nothing (the class of functions and V_area are the same). With norms the two kinds differ by Fact F14's one
   scalar per norm. Lemmas TV13, TV13.1, Proposition TV14 and Theorem TV15 hold for the oblique cut, and Theorem TV6's
   parts 1 and 2 hold for any direct decomposition, with oblique projections in place of orthogonal ones.
2. Proposition TV17: what an angle changes with norms. The oblique cut's energy is signed. Energies per area do not add: two examples, one with every per-area oblique energy constant and
   one with every per-area orthogonal energy (DM13) constant, in which every readout claim holds at error 0 and no cut
   is exact.
   So, at an angle and with norms, an energy claim is made on the whole dropped part D (Definition DM13 already allows
   any subspace), not area by area.
Not done here: Theorem TV2 part 3, Corollary TV3.1 and Proposition TV4 use one energy claim per dropped area; at an
angle they need restating with one energy claim on the whole dropped part. Definitions DM13 to DM15 and Corollaries TV6.1 and TV6.2 are unchanged for the orthogonal cut (with the substitution of
Lemma TV16 part 5 in DM14) (they take any subspace D and, by Lemma TV16 part 5, any direct
decomposition).

**Lemma TV16 (cuts and bounds at an angle) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** Let N be as in Definition DV1
in either form, D a subspace of R^d, Pi = P_(D perp) with B_perp an orthonormal basis of D perp (d' = d - dim D), K a
complement of D with projection Q onto K along D and an orthonormal basis B_K, and A_1, ..., A_m a direct decomposition
of R^d with projections Q_A (sum over A of Q_A = I, Q_A Q_F = 0 for A != F, Q_A^2 = Q_A).
1. Every d' x d matrix C with kernel D is C = Y B_perp^T Pi for one invertible d' x d' matrix Y. For the oblique cut,
   C = B_K^T Q and Y = B_K^T Q B_perp.
2. (No norm.) In the no-norm form, the cut with C, reads R'_l, logits U' (on R^(d')), computes at every input the same
   logits as the orthogonal cut with reads R'_l Y and logits U' Y and the same biases. So the re-fit cuts of either
   kind compute the same functions, and V_area(G) is the same over either kind.
3. (Norm.) In the norm form, with the same correspondence, the read of block l of the cut with C at x is s_l(x) times
   the orthogonal cut's read, s_l(x) = ((|z|^2 + eps'_l) / (|Y z|^2 + eps'_l))^(1/2) at that cut's stream z, as long as
   the two streams correspond (Fact F14 part 2). For the oblique cut, |Y B_perp^T Pi h| = |Q h|.
4. (The signed carrying.) Lemmas TV13 and TV13.1, Proposition TV14 and Theorem TV15 hold for the oblique cut, read in
   R^d coordinates, with Pi replaced by Q everywhere (the first write Q e, the writes Q W_l and Q c_l, z_l = Q h_(l-1),
   the leaks r'_(l,i) . n'(Q h_(l-1)) + b'_(l,i) - r_(l,i) . n(h_(l-1)) - b_(l,i), and the norms |Q W_l|), with read
   vectors and logit rows in K.
5. (Theorem TV6 with a direct decomposition.) Parts 1 and 2 of Theorem TV6 hold for any direct decomposition when, in
   lambda_l, T_l and u, |P_A Pi w_(l,i)| is replaced by |Q_A Pi w_(l,i)|, |P_F r'_(l,i)| by |Q_F^T r'_(l,i)|, and
   |P_perp U' P_A| by |P_perp U' Q_A|; and for the oblique cut with Pi replaced by Q as well (a read enters TV6 only through its action on K and its
   size, so any vector with that action may stand, for example Q^T r). The read condition of an
   edge is the same (Q_F^T r' = 0 exactly when r' is orthogonal to F); the write condition uses Q_A Pi w != 0.
Proof. (1) C P_D = 0, so C = C Pi = (C B_perp) B_perp^T Pi, since Pi = B_perp B_perp^T. C has rank d - dim D = d' (its kernel is D), and
B_perp^T Pi maps onto R^(d'), so the d' x d' matrix Y = C B_perp has rank d'. For C = B_K^T Q: Y = B_K^T Q B_perp.
(2) The cut with C has stream z_C = Y z with z the orthogonal cut's stream (first write C e = Y B_perp^T Pi e, writes
C W_l = Y B_perp^T Pi W_l): this is Fact F14 part 1 applied to the orthogonal cut, a network of DV1 of width d', with the
invertible matrix Y. Its reads R'_l z_C = (R'_l Y) z and logits U' z_C = (U' Y) z. Since Y is invertible, every pair
(R'_l, U') corresponds to one pair (R'_l Y, U' Y) and back, so the two classes compute the same functions.
(3) Fact F14 part 2 with A = Y. B_K^T Q h has size |Q h| (Q h lies in K), and B_K^T Q h = Y B_perp^T Pi h by part 1.
(4) In R^d coordinates the oblique cut's stream is ht_l = B_K z_C,l, which lies in K; Lemma TV0's proof goes through
with B_K in place of B_perp (B_K^T B_K = I, B_K B_K^T ht = ht for ht in K, and |B_K^T ht| = |ht|) and Q in place of Pi
(B_K^T Q = B_K^T Q Q). The proofs of TV13, TV13.1, TV14 and TV15 use only that Pi is linear, that the cut's stream and
Pi h_l lie in the range of Pi, and Lemma TV0; each holds with Q. (5) The steps of TV6's proof that use the
decomposition are (b), (c) and (d), with e[F] = |P_B delta|. With e[F] = |Q_F delta|: delta = sum over F of Q_F delta,
so |delta| <= sum of e[F]; r'_i . delta = sum over F of r'_i . Q_F Q_F delta = sum over F of (Q_F^T r'_i) . (Q_F delta),
so |r'_i . delta| <= sum over F of |Q_F^T r'_i| e[F]; Q_A delta_l = Q_A delta_(l-1) + Q_A Pi W_l (gt_l - g_l) gives
e_l[A] <= e_(l-1)[A] + Lip_l sum over i of |Q_A Pi w_i| |Delta_i|; and |P_perp U' delta| <= sum over F of
|P_perp U' Q_F| e[F]. Steps (a) and (e) do not use the decomposition. Edges: Q_F^T r' = 0 iff r' . Q_F v = 0 for every
v iff r' is orthogonal to the range of Q_F, which is F. Part 3 of TV6 is about D and the orthogonal Pi and does not use the decomposition, so for the orthogonal
cut it holds with any direct decomposition; for the oblique cut Proposition TV17 part 1 replaces it. QED.
Lean: `gl_read` (the read step of part 2); the rest is linear algebra and the bookkeeping of TV0, TV6 and TV13 (none
needed); checked in `model/tv_norm.py` (check F: part 1 on random C; part 2 to rounding error; part 3's scalar; part 4,
Theorem TV15 for the oblique cut, pointwise; part 5, the bound of TV6 with a random oblique decomposition and both kinds
of cut).

**Proposition TV17 (what an angle changes with norms: the energy) (under: pure-stream networks; area cuts).** In the
norm form:
1. (The oblique cut's energy.) Let K, Q be as in Lemma TV16 and e_Q(h) = |h|^2 - |Q h|^2. For the orthogonal cut
   (Q = Pi) e_Q(h) = |P_D h|^2 >= 0; for an oblique Q it can be negative. If no reader reads D (R_l P_D = 0 for every l
   and U P_D = 0) and e_Q(h_(l-1)(x)) = c^en_l at every x in P for l = 1, ..., L + 1, with eps_l + c^en_l > 0, then the oblique
   cut with N's reads (R_l B_K, U B_K), biases and norm constants eps_l + c^en_l computes N's logits at every point of P.
2. (Energies per area do not add.) There are N, P and a direct decomposition into three areas S_1, S_2, S_3 (two of
   them at an angle) such that dropping D = S_1 + S_2: every per-area energy |Q_(S_i) h|^2 (i = 1, 2) is constant on P,
   the logits read only S_3 (every readout claim of DM12 that names S_1 or S_2 with V = 0 has error 0), and yet every
   re-fit cut of either kind that drops D has D_P > 0. The same holds with the orthogonal per-area energies |P_(S_i) h|^2 of Definition DM13 constant on P (a
   second example). In the laminar case this cannot happen: |P_D h|^2 is the sum of the per-area energies
   (Pythagoras), so per-area energy claims at error 0 give the claim on D at error 0.
Proof. (1) (I - Q) h lies in D, so R_l h = R_l Q h and U h = U Q h. By
induction the cut's stream (in R^d coordinates) is Q h_l: if it is Q h_(l-1) before block l, its read is
R_l Q h_(l-1) / (|Q h_(l-1)|^2 + eps_l + c^en_l)^(1/2) = R_l h_(l-1) / (|h_(l-1)|^2 + eps_l)^(1/2), N's read, since
|Q h|^2 + c^en_l = |h|^2 at the points of P; so the inside values are N's and the next stream is Q h_(l-1) +
Q (W_l g_l + c_l) = Q h_l. The logits follow in the same way. For Q = Pi, |h|^2 - |Pi h|^2 = |P_D h|^2. For an oblique Q:
d = 2, K = span(e_1), D = span(e_1 + e_2), h = e_1 - e_2 = 2 e_1 - (e_1 + e_2), so Q h = 2 e_1 and e_Q(h) = 2 - 4 = -2.
(2) d = 3, L = 0 (no blocks), two logits, U with rows e_3^T and 0, logit norm constant eps = 1. Areas S_1 = span(e_1),
S_2 = span(u) with u = (cos t, sin t, 0) and 0 < t < pi / 2, S_3 = span(e_3); their sum is direct. P: the four points
h(x) = a e_1 + b u + e_3, (a, b) in {1, -1}^2, equally weighted. Then Q_(S_1) h = a e_1 and Q_(S_2) h = b u, so the
per-area energies are a^2 = 1 and b^2 = 1, constant; U Q_(S_1) = U Q_(S_2) = 0. But |h|^2 = 3 + 2 a b cos t takes two
values, so N's centred logits P_perp (1 / (|h|^2 + 1)^(1/2), 0) take two values on P. Every cut that drops D has
first write C h(x) = C e_3 (C kills D), the same at every point of P, so its logits are the same at every point of P,
and its D_P is at least the least D_P of a constant logit vector against two distinct distributions of positive
weight, which is > 0. Second example: the same N and areas, and P the four points h(x) = x e_1 + y e_2 + e_3 with
x in {1, -1}, s in {1, -1} and y = (s - x cos t) / sin t, so that h . e_1 = x and h . u = s. Then |P_(S_1) h|^2 = 1
and |P_(S_2) h|^2 = 1 at every point (|u| = 1), while |P_D h|^2 = 1 + (s - x cos t)^2 / sin^2 t takes the two values
1 + (1 - cos t)^2 / sin^2 t and 1 + (1 + cos t)^2 / sin^2 t, which differ since cos t > 0. The rest is as in the
