Gaussian fourth moments are classical; the variance formula is checked in `model/t17_sympy.py`.
Comment: in words, the best single unit is the network's switch read pulled by the resolvent (mu I - Q)^{-1} toward the
strong directions of the value map P_perp M (the eigenspaces of Q). One number mu sets how far, and mu is a root of one
explicit polynomial. At the one end the unit copies the switch read (the choice of Theorem T11 at k = r = 1); at the
others it lies in one eigenspace of Q. Under the assumption of part 2 with n >= 2 the optimum is at neither end. The
eigenspaces of Q are not the principal directions of the logits (the covariance of P_perp y adds a rank-one term
alpha^2 (B stilde)(B stilde)^T to a multiple of B B^T), so the kept direction of Theorem T9 is not one of these ends in
general. The unit's gate reads that same unit. The data enter only through Sigma.

**Proposition T17.3 (larger widths: the best kept space solves a self-consistent eigenproblem) (under: H-selfgate,
H-gauss with m_a = 0 and Sigma positive definite; depth 1, one read column, phi(t) = alpha t + beta; 1 <= k < d).**
Notation as in Theorem T17.2. For an orthogonal projection Pi of rank k on R^d put S = stilde stilde^T and
f(Pi) = alpha^2 [(stilde^T Pi stilde) tr(Pi Q) + stilde^T Pi Q Pi stilde] + beta^2 tr(Pi Q).
1. For the kernel K' = Sigma^{-1/2} U, with U (d x k) orthonormal and Pi = U U^T, the build of Theorem T17 is optimal
   among the builds whose first-layer kernel has column space in col(K'), with D2_P = (rho_2 / 2) (f(I) - f(Pi)). So the
   best width-k build is the build of Theorem T17 at a maximiser of f over the rank-k projections, which exists.
2. Every maximiser Pi commutes with the symmetric matrix
   G(Pi) = alpha^2 [tr(Pi Q) S + (stilde^T Pi stilde) Q + Q Pi S + S Pi Q] + beta^2 Q.
   So the range of Pi is spanned by k eigenvectors of G(Pi).
3. G(Pi) = gamma Q + alpha^2 [tr(Pi Q) S + v stilde^T + stilde v^T], with gamma = beta^2 + alpha^2 stilde^T Pi stilde and
   v = Q Pi stilde: a multiple of Q plus a symmetric matrix of rank at most 2. If gamma > 0, every eigenvector x of G(Pi),
   with eigenvalue theta such that theta / gamma is not an eigenvalue of Q, lies in the span of
   (theta / gamma I - Q)^{-1} stilde and (theta / gamma I - Q)^{-1} v.
4. (Reduction to one vector.) Put p = Pi stilde. Then |p|^2 = p^T stilde, and if p != 0 the range of Pi is
   span(p) + W' with W' (dimension k - 1) orthogonal to p and to stilde, and
   f(Pi) = (alpha^2 |p|^2 + beta^2) tr(Pi_{W'} Q) + 2 alpha^2 p^T Q p + beta^2 p^T Q p / |p|^2.
   The complement of {stilde, p} has dimension at least d - 2 >= k - 1 (d - 1 if p = stilde, the only multiple of
   stilde on the sphere besides 0), so such W' exist. Conversely every p != 0 with |p|^2 = p^T stilde and every such W'
   give a rank-k projection with Pi stilde = p. So the maximum of f over rank-k projections is the larger of (a) the
   supremum over p != 0 with |p|^2 = p^T stilde of
   h(p) = (alpha^2 |p|^2 + beta^2) kappa_{k-1}(p) + 2 alpha^2 p^T Q p + beta^2 p^T Q p / |p|^2, with kappa_{k-1}(p) the sum
   of the k - 1 largest eigenvalues of Q compressed to the orthogonal complement of {stilde, p}, and (b) the value
   beta^2 kappa'_k at p = 0, with kappa'_k the sum of the k largest eigenvalues of Q compressed to the orthogonal
   complement of stilde. In words: in case (a) the best kept space is one read-carrying direction p plus the k - 1 top
   directions of Q compressed to the complement of stilde and p; in case (b) it holds no read-carrying direction.
Proof. (1) As in Theorem T17.2 part 1. Here K'^T Sigma K' = U^T U = I, so the kept features w are standard normal in R^k, Gamma = Sigma K', s^T Gamma w = b^T w with b = U^T stilde, and
P_perp M Gamma w = C w with C = B U. At one position the trace of the covariance of P_perp m_V = (alpha b^T w + beta) C w is
alpha^2 (|b|^2 |C|_F^2 + 2 |C b|^2 - |C b|^2) + beta^2 |C|_F^2 (Isserlis; the odd moments vanish), and |b|^2 =
stilde^T Pi stilde, |C|_F^2 = tr(Pi Q), |C b|^2 = stilde^T Pi Q Pi stilde. So it is f(Pi), and f(I) is the trace for y
(the kernel I sees everything). The rest is as in Theorem T17.2 part 1. A kernel of rank less than k is never better
than a rank-k kernel whose column space contains it (Lemma T17a: F(V) <= F(V'') for V'' in V; padding needs k <= d).
Every rank-k V is Sigma^{-1/2} col(U) for an orthonormal U, and F depends on V only. The rank-k projections form a compact set.
(2) f extends to a polynomial on symmetric matrices whose gradient at Pi, in the trace inner product, is G(Pi) (the
derivative of (stilde^T Pi stilde) tr(Pi Q) is tr(Pi Q) S + (stilde^T Pi stilde) Q, that of tr(Pi Q Pi S) is
Q Pi S + S Pi Q, and that of tr(Pi Q) is Q). For an antisymmetric X, Pi(t) = e^{t X} Pi e^{-t X} is a rank-k projection with
derivative X Pi - Pi X at t = 0. At a maximiser, 0 = tr(G (X Pi - Pi X)) = tr(X (Pi G - G Pi)). The matrix
Y = Pi G - G Pi is antisymmetric, so taking X = Y gives tr(Y Y) = 0, hence Y = 0 (`antisymm_zero_of_trace`). Commuting
symmetric matrices have a common orthonormal eigenbasis, and the range of Pi is spanned by k of its vectors.
(3) Expand G. If G x = theta x, then (theta I - gamma Q) x = alpha^2 [tr(Pi Q) (stilde^T x) stilde + (stilde^T x) v
+ (v^T x) stilde], which lies in span(stilde, v); divide by gamma and apply (theta / gamma I - Q)^{-1}.
(4) p^T stilde = stilde^T Pi stilde = |Pi stilde|^2. If p != 0, let W' be the orthogonal complement of p inside range(Pi);
for x in W', stilde^T x = stilde^T Pi x = p^T x = 0. Then Pi = p p^T / |p|^2 + Pi_{W'}, so stilde^T Pi stilde = |p|^2,
tr(Pi Q) = p^T Q p / |p|^2 + tr(Pi_{W'} Q) and stilde^T Pi Q Pi stilde = p^T Q p; substituting gives the formula. Conversely,
for such p and W', Pi stilde = p (p^T stilde) / |p|^2 + Pi_{W'} stilde = p. For fixed p the coefficient
alpha^2 |p|^2 + beta^2 is non-negative, so the best W' maximises tr(Pi_{W'} Q) over (k - 1)-dimensional subspaces of the
complement of {stilde, p}, which is kappa_{k-1}(p) by Ky Fan's maximum principle (`kyfan_coord`, as in Theorem T12). If
p = 0, the range of Pi is orthogonal to stilde, f(Pi) = beta^2 tr(Pi Q), and Ky Fan gives (b). QED.
Lean: `antisymm_zero_of_trace` (an antisymmetric matrix with tr(Y Y) = 0 is zero), through `antisymm_trace_sq`; part 4
uses `kyfan_coord` for the coordinate step of Ky Fan.
Comment: so at k >= 2 the best kept space is a fixed point: it is spanned by k eigenvectors of a matrix that depends on
it, and each such eigenvector (with gamma > 0 and theta / gamma outside the spectrum of Q) lies in the span of two
resolvent vectors at its own theta, which generalises the curve of Theorem T17.2. Parts 2 and 3 hold at every critical
point; they are necessary, not sufficient, and do not say which k eigenvectors. Part 4 is the sharper statement: the
width-k problem is a search over one vector p on the sphere |p|^2 = p^T stilde (centre stilde / 2; it passes through
p = 0, which is case (b)), with an eigenvalue problem inside. A fast exact method is Conjecture
D8. The kept spaces at different widths are not claimed to nest, and the reads change with the width: the builds of this
section are not claimed to be prefixes of one stored build (unlike T6, T11 part 4 and T13 part 3).

**Proposition T18 (the subset fold: closed-form builds that are never worse than the copy) (under: H-selfgate; the
premises of Theorem T16 part 5; any law).** Use the notation of Part B.5 and Theorem T16. Let c_1, ..., c_q be the
columns of all the network's effective reads R*_l (they span K R, of dimension r <= k), and fix a positive definite
d x d matrix Omega (for example the pooled second moment E sum_p rho(p) a a^T, the metric of Theorem T17 part 2). For a
subset T of {1, ..., q}:
1. Let Rf_T in R^{N_1} be the span of the member-space reads of T, r_T = dim Rf_T <= k, R_{0,T} a basis matrix of it,
   f_T = R_{0,T}^T uhat, C_{f_T} = Cov(f_T) (positive definite, as a compression of C_f), C_{y f_T} = P_perp A Chat R_{0,T},
   e_T the residual of the centred logits after linear regression on f_T, and U'_T its top k - r_T principal directions,
   all computed with the network's own gated features. Put
   Lambda_T = [R_{0,T}^T ; U'_T^T (P_perp A - C_{y f_T} C_{f_T}^{-1} R_{0,T}^T)] and V_T = col(K Lambda_T^T).
2. Replace every column c_i by its Omega-orthogonal projection onto V_T. Call the result Rhat_T. The columns in T are
   unchanged, because K Rf_T lies in V_T.
3. The value of T is J_k(Rhat_T) (Theorem T16 part 3), attained by the build of Theorem T16 part 4.
Then the minimum over T of J_k(Rhat_T) <= J_k(R*) = the value of Theorem T11, because T = {1, ..., q} gives R*, and
every J_k(Rhat_T) >= 1/2 sum_{j > k} mu_j (Theorem T12). The minimum is over at most 2^q values J_k(Rhat_T), each in the
closed form of Theorem T16 part 3 when Sigma_{Rhat_T} is positive definite (the form still contains expectations of
gated features under P).
Proof. Every column of Rhat_T lies in V_T, of dimension at most k, so r'(Rhat_T) <= k and J_k(Rhat_T) is defined. For
T = {1, ..., q}, Rf_T is the whole forced read space R, the first rows of Lambda_T are R_0^T, so V_T contains K R and every
c_i, and Rhat_T = R*. Then J_k(R*) is the value of Theorem T11 by Theorem T16 part 5. The lower bound is Theorem T16 part 5 (through
Theorem T12). QED.
Lean: none, the proof only combines Theorems T11, T12 and T16.
Comment: this is the projected read of Theorem T17 used without H-gauss. Keep some reads exactly, and let the others read
their best guess inside the kept space. It is a formula with a guarantee, not an optimum. T = the empty set uses the kept
space of Theorem T9 (the top principal directions, through the network's gates) and projects every read into it. The
subset fold searches the kept space only among the spaces V_T (one per subset). Under the hypotheses of Theorem T17.2
with n >= 2, part 4 there shows that the copy end (T = everything, at k = r = 1) is not optimal; it does not decide the
other end. So for the subset fold the choice of the kept space, not of the read, is what remains open.

Comment (where hardness can still sit). Under the premises of Theorem T17.2 (m_a = 0, Sigma positive definite, Q != 0,
every r_j > 0, depth 1, one read column, affine gate, k = 1), width 1 reduces to one eigendecomposition and the real roots
of one polynomial of degree at most 3n - 2. Its coefficients are rational in the input when Sigma, M, s, alpha and beta
are rational: A = s^T Sigma (mu I - N Sigma)^{-1} s, D = -dA/dmu and B = mu D - A are rational functions of mu with
rational coefficients, and prod_j (mu - lambda_j) is the minimal polynomial of N Sigma (similar to Q, hence
diagonalisable), which has rational coefficients. So real algebraic root isolation applies. A complexity statement would
need this written out in a bit model, and it is not claimed here. If it is written out, a hardness result for affine
gates must use a case outside those premises, for example a law that is not Gaussian, a constant entry (m_a != 0 and
Sigma singular), some r_j = 0, several read columns, k >= 2, or depth >= 2. On a finite law with an affine gate at width 1 and one position, a build is
y_B = H'' (alpha q' (kappa^T a)^2 + beta kappa^T a) + c' (H'' the head as a vector). For a fixed read q' (or when
beta = 0, or n_y = 2), the value after fitting the head and the bias is a ratio of polynomials in kappa built from the
law's moments up to order four; with q' free, beta != 0 and n_y >= 3 it is the largest root of a quadratic with
polynomial coefficients. Conjecture D9 states a decision problem for beta = 0.

## B.H One recursion over a tree of areas: zoom and depth as one step (side branch under nodes R-tree and R-branch, added 2026-10-29)

Shonu (2026-10-29): a clean network works by gating, "the earlier ones are coarser and then they get finer and finer";
"instead of thinking like, how are we thinking of this whole network at once, I want to think of this recursively";
and "i see zoom recursion and depth recursion as the same thing ... we should treat this as one unified idea we want
to prove is optimal". This Part makes the idea one object: a tree of areas (Definition DH1). A group of a zoom is a
set of subtrees (Definition DH3), and both a step of the zoom and a step back to an earlier layer move a group up
this tree.
1. Lemma TH0: inside a node's area, everything later in the network is a function of that node's units, and removing
   a group changes no kept unit (with branch claims, Definition DH2).
2. Theorem TH1: at every grouping of subtrees, at any mix of depths, the least loss is the sum over the groups of a
   least loss on the group's own areas. It is the "local terms" of the idea, at every depth at once; for groups made
   of whole nodes in the last hidden layer it is a case of TM1.
3. Proposition TH2: two kinds of zoom step. Along steps that merge sibling subtrees the least loss can only grow, and
   if the coarsest level is exact, every level is exact and is built from the level below (part 1). A step that lifts a group to an earlier layer
   does not: a coarser level can be exact while a finer level is not (part 2).
4. Proposition TH3: at a lossy sibling merge with three logits, the step-by-step build is strictly worse than the least
   build, for the objective D2_P. Conjecture TH4 (Part D.16): a pass of summaries up the tree, not of units.
Status: every item uses nodes R-tree, R-branch and S-plainff (PENDING, card 3-24), so this Part is a side branch.
Setting (node S-plainff): N is a plain feed-forward network: each hidden layer is dense and reads only the layer
before, with no positions and no skips. Layer l (l = 1, ..., L) has units h_i = relu(z_i) with
z_i(x) = sum over units j of layer l - 1 of W_ij h_j(x) + b_i, layer 0 is the input x, and y_N(x) = W_out h^(L)(x) + c_N.
Claims are those of Part A.7.

**Definition DH1 (tree map, nodes, subtrees).** A map M of N on P is a **tree map** when:
1. its districts cover every hidden layer (a unit that is off on all of P may be a district with region empty); and
2. for l = 1, ..., L - 1, every non-empty region of layer l + 1 lies inside a region of layer l.
A **node** is a pair v = (l, R) with R a non-empty region of layer l. Its **units** U(v) are the units of the
districts of layer l with region R, and its **area** is R. The **root** is the formal node (0, P), whose units are the
input coordinates. The **children** of v are the nodes (l + 1, R') with R' inside R (for the root: every node of
layer 1). The **subtree** sub(v) is the set of units of v and of every node below v along the child relation.
Comment. The non-empty regions of one layer are pairwise disjoint (Definition DM2), so a node of layer l + 1 has
exactly one parent. Two nodes have areas that are nested when one lies below the other and disjoint otherwise: if
v' is not below v and l(v') >= l(v), the ancestor of v' in layer l(v) is a node other than v, whose region is
disjoint from v's, and the area of v' lies inside it. Item 2 is strong: once a layer splits P into areas, no unit of
a later layer may be on in two of them. That is the "earlier coarser, later finer" of the idea, as a property of N.

**Definition DH2 (branch claim; judgment in any layer).**
1. For a set B of hidden units of N, a **branch claim** (B) says that no hidden unit outside B reads B on P. For a
   hidden unit k not in B, let r_k(x) be the sum over the units u of B in the layer below k of W_ku h_u(x) (what k
   receives from B), and
      e_k = (sum over x in P of p_x r_k(x)^2) / (sum over x in P of p_x (r_k(x)^2 + (z_k(x) - r_k(x))^2))
   (no term when the denominator is 0, which happens only when r_k is 0 on P). The error eps_branch(B) is the
   largest e_k (0 if there is none). It is 0 exactly when every hidden unit outside B receives 0 from B at every point
   of P. It is rational, computable in polynomial time, and unchanged by the rescaling of Fact F1 (a rescaled k
   multiplies the numerator and the denominator by c^2; a rescaled u in B leaves each W_ku h_u(x) unchanged) and by a
   copy of a unit of layer L as in Definition DN1 (a copy of k has k's term; no hidden unit reads layer L; a branch
   claim that holds u is read as holding every copy of u). The logits are not units: they may read B.
2. A **judgment claim** (R, K, a) of Definition DM4 may name a region R of any hidden layer l and a set K of units of
   districts of layer l with region R; the error is that of DM4. A map holds at most one judgment claim per node
   (l, R) (a region may repeat from layer to layer).
Source: the essay, "The dogs go on to their own area, which doesn't have to worry about cars" (part 1), and its
"reusable judgment" (part 2). Node R-branch.

**Definition DH3 (subtree groups, boxes, and builds at a tree grouping) (node R-tree).** Let M be a tree map.
1. A **subtree group** S is given by a node u (its **parent**), a non-empty set W_S of children of u, and for each
   w in W_S a set J_w of units of U(w) (w's **kept judgment units**, possibly empty) such that sub(w) minus J_w is not
   empty: S is the union over w in W_S of sub(w) minus J_w. Its **top** T(S) is the union of the U(w) minus J_w (units
   of layer l(u) + 1), z_T(x) is the vector of their pre-activations, and its **areas** are the areas of the w in W_S.
2. A **tree grouping** G is a set of subtree groups, each with a target size k_S >= 0, such that the sets W_S are
   pairwise disjoint and no node of their union lies in the subtree of another node of it (the subtrees are pairwise
   disjoint). Then the groups are disjoint and
   the areas of different groups are disjoint (Comment of DH1). The units in no group are **kept**.
3. A **box** of S of size k is a list of k units relu(m^T z_T(x) + beta), m and beta real, placed in layer l(u) + 1,
   where z_T(x) is formed from layer l(u) of the build with N's weights and biases of the units of T(S) (so each box
   unit is a unit of N's kind in layer l(u) + 1, reading layer l(u)).
4. A **class (b) build at G** is N with the units of every group removed, a box for every group, and every unit of a
   box and of a set J_w that lies below layer L carried to layer L by **copy units** (a copy of a unit of value h >= 0 in
   layer l is a unit of layer l + 1 that reads only it, with weight 1 and bias 0, so its value is relu(h) = h). Its
   logits are free: any weights on every unit of the build's layer L and any bias. Copy units do not count toward
   k_S. Wiring: a kept unit keeps N's weights from the kept units of the layer below and has no weight from box or
   copy units; a box unit reads only units of layer l(u), through N's rows of T(S) (removed units of layer l(u) are
   absent, so they enter with weight 0). V_b(G) is the infimum of D_P over these builds; V2_b(G) the infimum of D2_P.
5. A **zoom of tree groupings** G_0, ..., G_m is a zoom in the sense of Definition D50 part 2 (every group of G_(j+1)
   is a union of groups and kept units of G_j). A changed group S' of G_(j+1) is a **sibling merge** when every group
   of G_j inside S' has the parent of S' and the kept judgment units of S' (its other children are kept units). The
   case with no group of G_j inside S' (S' is made of kept units only) is a **creation**. A changed group is a
   **lift** when it contains a group of G_j whose parent is not the parent of S'. An **(r) sequence** along the zoom is defined as in Definition
   D50 part 5: B_0 is a least class (b) build at G_0, and a step to G_(j+1) copies B_j's boxes of the unchanged groups
   and its kept units, and gives each changed group S' k_(S') new units relu(mu^T p_(S')(x) + beta), where p_(S')
   lists the pre-activations, at x, of B_j's units in the children of S' (a kept child contributes its z); a step is
   allowed when these new units equal, at every point of P, a box of S' (part 3). B_(j+1) is a least build of the step.
Comment. For a parent u in layer L - 1 every group lies in layer L, a box reads the pre-activations of its group's
units, and no copy units are needed: these are the class (b) builds of Definition D50' at a grouping whose groups
are unions of whole nodes minus kept judgment units. For such groupings TH1 below is a case of Theorem TM1 (TM1
needs districts only in layer L, while TH1 asks for a tree map). A box reads the pre-activations of its group's top units, as class (b) reads its group's; whether a
box may also read the kept gates above it is option (b) of card 3-24 (it would make lifts nest, and would let a box
vary on its siblings' areas).

**Lemma TH0 (inside an area, the network is local; removing a group changes no kept unit) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).**
1. Let M be a tree map whose district claims have eps = 0, and let v be a node of layer l. At every point x of the
   area of v, every unit of layer l outside U(v) is off, and every unit of a layer after l outside sub(v) is off. So
   the values at x of the units of sub(v) in later layers, and y_N(x) - c_N when l < L, are functions of h_U(v)(x)
   alone (computed by the units of sub(v)); for l = L, y_N(x) - c_N is W_out applied to the units of U(v).
2. Let G be a tree grouping such that, for every group S and every w in W_S, M holds the branch claim
   (sub(w) minus J_w) with eps = 0. Then in every class (b) build at G, every kept unit takes at every point of P its
   value in N, and every box reads N's z_T(x).
Proof. (1) A unit of a layer l' >= l that is on at x lies in a district whose region R' contains x, since its district
claim has eps = 0. The node (l', R') has an ancestor in layer l (Definition DH1 item 2 applied l' - l times), whose
region contains x. The non-empty regions of layer l are disjoint and the area of v contains x, so that ancestor is v,
and the unit lies in sub(v) (in U(v) when l' = l). Hence at x the units of layer l + 1 of sub(v) read only units of
U(v) that can be on, the units of layer l + 2 of sub(v) read only units of sub(v) of layer l + 1, and so on: each is a
function of h_U(v)(x). The logits read layer L, whose on units at x lie in sub(v).
(2) By induction over the layers. A kept unit k of layer l' reads layer l' - 1 of the build. There, the kept units
have N's values (induction), the removed units are absent, and box and copy units are read only by copy units and
the logits. So k's pre-activation in the build is N's minus what k receives in N from the removed units of layer
l' - 1. Each removed unit lies in sub(w) minus J_w for one w in some W_S, and k is not in that set (k is kept). By the
branch claim, k receives 0 from sub(w) minus J_w at every point of P. Summing over the groups and the w, k receives 0
from all removed units, so its value is N's. For a box of S, the units of T(S) read layer l(u) in N. A removed unit of
layer l(u) lies in a set sub(w') minus J_(w') of another group, and the units of T(S) are not in it: if one were, w
would lie in sub(w'), against Definition DH3 item 2. So the units of T(S) receive 0 from removed units (branch claim),
and the box reads N's z_T(x). QED.
Lean: none, by hand (bookkeeping of which units are on where, by induction over the layers).

**Theorem TH1 (the split down the tree) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, every claim it uses has
eps = 0).** Let M be a tree map and G a tree grouping, and suppose:
1. every district claim of M has eps = 0;
2. for every group S and every w in W_S: every district that holds a unit of T(S) has a shelter claim (Definition
   DM3) with eps = 0; for every w in W_S
   whose area is not all of P, M holds a judgment claim (area of w, J_w, a_w) in layer l(w) (Definition DH2 part 2)
   with eps = 0; and M holds the branch claim (sub(w) minus J_w) with eps = 0.
For a group S let
   L_S = inf of sum over w in W_S of sum over x in the area of w of p_x KL(softmax(y_N(x)) || softmax(V C(x) + U_w h_(J_w)(x) + t_w)),
the infimum over boxes C of S of size k_S, logit weights V on C, U_w on J_w, and vectors t_w in R^{n_y}; let L2_S be
the same with (1/2) |P_perp (V C(x) + U_w h_(J_w)(x) + t_w - y_N(x))|^2 in place of the KL term. Then:
1. V_b(G) = sum over the groups S of G of L_S, and V2_b(G) = sum over S of L2_S.
2. For every set G' of groups of G (with their sizes), V_b(G') = sum over S in G' of L_S, and likewise for V2_b.
3. If every L_S (L2_S) is attained, a least build at G is assembled from attaining choices for each group, and in it a
   group enters only through its box, its logit weights on the box and on (the copies of) its J_w, and one term of the
   bias. So across the levels of a zoom of tree groupings that all meet premises 1 and 2, changing one group changes
   only these.
4. L_S depends only on the points of S's areas, their weights, and the values there of z_T, of h_(J_w) and of y_N; by
   Lemma TH0 part 1, y_N on the area of w is a function of h_U(w).
The parents of the groups may lie in any layers, in one grouping. With every parent in layer L - 1, parts 1 to 3 are
a case of Theorem TM1 (groups made of whole nodes minus their judgment units, under a tree map, which TM1 does not
need).
Proof. Take any class (b) build B at G, with bias c_B. By Lemma TH0 part 2 (premise 2 gives its branch claims), every
kept unit has its value in N at every point of P and every box reads N's z_T.
Facts at a point. (i) Let x be outside the areas of S. Every unit of T(S) lies in a district whose region is the area
of some w in W_S and which has a shelter claim with eps = 0, so z_T(x) is one fixed vector, every unit of S's box takes one value, and the box writes
one vector v_S to the logits (through its copies); if S's areas cover P, v_S is any fixed vector (then G = {S}, and
the proof does not use it). The units of every J_w are off at x (district claims). (ii) Let x be in the area of w,
w in W_S. The areas of different groups are disjoint (DH3 item 2), so every other group S' writes v_(S') at x, and
the J_(w'') of every other w'' (in W_S or in another group) are off. By Lemma TH0 part 1, every unit of layer L that is on at x
lies in sub(w); the units of sub(w) are in S except those of J_w, which lie in layer l(w). So the kept units of layer
L that are on at x are those of J_w when l(w) = L and no others when l(w) < L, where J_w reaches layer L through its
copies. Hence
   y_B(x) = V_S C_S(x) + U_w h_(J_w)(x) + (sum over the groups S' other than S of v_(S')) + c_B,
with V_S, U_w the build's logit weights on S's box and on J_w (or their copies). (iii) Let x be in no area of any
group. Every unit of a group is off at x (its district's region lies inside an area of its group), so
y_N(x) = c_N + (sum over the kept units f of layer L of W_out[., f] h_f(x)), and y_B(x) = (sum over the kept units f
of layer L of the build's weight on f times h_f(x)) + (sum over all groups of v_S) + c_B.
Lower bound. By (ii), the terms of D_P(B) at the points of the areas of S form a sum of the kind in L_S, with t_w the
same vector (sum over S' other than S of v_(S')) + c_B for every w; the infimum in L_S lets each t_w vary on its own,
so these terms add to at least L_S. The areas of different groups are disjoint and the other terms are >= 0, so
D_P(B) >= sum over S of L_S. Lean: `split_lower` (as in TM1).
Upper bound. Let e > 0 and pick for each S a choice (C_S, V_S, (U_w), (t_w)) whose sum is within e / |G| of L_S. Build
B: each group gets the box C_S with weights V_S; every kept unit of layer L that is in no J_w keeps N's weight; the
bias is c_B = c_N - sum over S of v_S (Lean: `constants_cancel`). If the area of some w is all of P, then w is the only node of
its layer and every node of a later layer lies below w, so G has the one group S and W_S = {w}; take c_B = t_w - v_S, and every point
is as in (ii). Otherwise give the units J_w (or their copies) the weights U_w + s_w a_w^T with
s_w = t_w - c_N + v_S. The units J_w are off outside the area of w and a_w^T h_(J_w) = 1 on it, so this adds s_w at the
points of that area and nothing elsewhere (Lean: `judgment_shift`). At x in the area of w, by (ii),
y_B(x) = V_S C_S(x) + U_w h_(J_w)(x) + s_w + (c_N - v_S) = V_S C_S(x) + U_w h_(J_w)(x) + t_w, so these terms are those of
the chosen sum. At x in no area, by (iii), y_B(x) = y_N(x). So D_P(B) <= sum over S of L_S + e, and part 1 follows. The
same argument with the squared term gives the statement for V2_b.
(2) G' meets premises 1 and 2, with more kept units; a group's J_w are the same in G' and in G. Apply part 1. (3) The
upper bound with e = 0 and attaining choices (Lean: `split_least`). (4) Read off the formula of L_S. QED.
Lean: `judgment_shift`, `split_lower`, `constants_cancel`, `split_least` in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Map.lean` (the four
one-line steps of TM1); the rest by hand.
Comment. This is the recursion of the idea in its local form: at every level of every zoom the least build is put
together from one problem per group, and each problem sees only its own areas. With every parent in layer L - 1 it is
a case of TM1; with the parents in earlier layers it is the deep form that Conjecture CM3 asked for, with the branch claim in
place of CM3's premise that no unit descends from two groups (a dense network never meets that premise, while a branch
claim is a statement about the values on P). TH1 says nothing about how hard each L_S is: for one group in one layer
it is the problem of Proposition T57.

**Proposition TH2 (sibling merges nest; lifts do not) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups,
branch claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).**
1. Let G_0, ..., G_m be a zoom of tree groupings in which every changed group is a sibling merge (creations included),
   G_m meets premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1, and k_S >= k_(S') whenever a group S of G_j lies in a group S' of
   G_(j+1). Then every level meets premises 1 and 2, and:
   (a) V_b(G_j) <= V_b(G_(j+1)) for every j (the least loss can only grow along the zoom), and likewise for V2_b;
   (b) if some class (b) build B\* at G_m has D_P(B\*) = 0, then there is an (r) sequence with D_P(B_j) = 0 = V_b(G_j)
       at every level j. The same holds for D2_P.
2. There are a network N with two logits, a mix P, a tree map M with every claim eps = 0, and a zoom G_0, G_1, G_2, G_3
   of tree groupings whose first step is a creation and whose other changed groups are lifts, with every target size
   1 and every level meeting premises 1 and 2 of TH1, such that V_b(G_0) = V_b(G_3) = 0 while V_b(G_1) > 0 and
   V_b(G_2) > 0. So (a) and (b) fail for lifts: a least build at a coarser level can be exact while no build at a
   finer level is.
Proof. (1) Premises. A group of G_j lies in a group S of G_m (groups never dissolve, Definition D50 part 2). By
induction down the zoom, a sibling merge keeps the parent and the kept judgment units, so every group of G_j inside S
has S's parent and S's J_w, and its set W is part of W_S. So its top is part of T(S), its claims are among S's, and
the sets W of different groups of G_j are disjoint parts of the sets W of G_m's groups: G_j is a tree grouping that
meets premises 1 and 2.
Restriction. Let S' be a group of some G_i, with box units relu(m_t^T z_(T(S'))(x) + beta_t), t = 1, ..., k_(S'), and
let S_c be a group of a level j < i inside S'. Write m_t = (m_(t,c), m'_t) for the parts on T(S_c) and on T(S')
minus T(S_c). The units of T(S') minus T(S_c) lie in districts whose regions are areas of S' other than those of S_c,
with shelter claims at eps = 0, so on S_c's areas their pre-activations take one fixed value zeta_c. The
**restriction** of unit t to S_c is relu(m_(t,c)^T z_(T(S_c))(x) + beta_t + m'_t^T zeta_c). On S_c's areas it equals
unit t. Pad it with units relu(-1) (value 0) up to k_(S_c) >= k_(S').
(a) Let B be any class (b) build at G_(j+1). By fact (ii) in the proof of TH1, B's terms on the areas of a group S'
of G_(j+1) are those of a choice for L_(S') (with t_w read off from B). For a group S_c of G_j inside S', the
restriction of S''s box with the same V, U_w and t_w is a choice for L_(S_c) whose terms on S_c's areas are B's terms
there. An area of S' that lies in no group of G_j is the area of a node whose units, except J_w, are kept at G_j; on
it the build of TH1's upper bound keeps N's units, and its terms are 0. A group of G_j that is a group of G_(j+1) has
the same least loss at both levels. So the sum over the groups of G_j of their least losses is at most D_P(B), and by
TH1 part 1 V_b(G_j) <= D_P(B) for every such B. Hence V_b(G_j) <= V_b(G_(j+1)). The same holds for D2_P.
(b) Let B_j be the class (b) build at G_j whose box for each group S_c is the restriction of B\*'s box of its group of
G_m, with B\*'s logit weights on the box and on J_w and, as in the upper bound of TH1, t_w read off from B\*. B\*'s
terms on the areas of S_c are 0 (D_P(B\*) = 0), so the choice attains L_(S_c) = 0, and on the areas of kept units of
G_j the build keeps N's units. By TH1 part 1 and its upper bound, D_P(B_j) = 0 = V_b(G_j); in particular B_0 is a
least build at G_0. A step from B_j reaches B_(j+1): let S' be a changed group of G_(j+1), in the group S of G_m, with
children in G_j the groups S_1, ..., S_q and a set K' of kept units. The pre-activation of the restriction of unit t
to S_c is p_(t,c) = m_(t,c)^T z_(T(S_c)) + beta_t + m'_(t,c)^T zeta_c, and T(S') is the union of the T(S_c) and of
the units of K' that lie in T(S'). So
   sum over c of p_(t,c)(x) + sum over i in K' of (m_t)_i z_i(x) = m_t|_(T(S'))^T z_(T(S'))(x) + (a constant),
with (m_t)_i = 0 for a unit i of K' outside T(S'). (This is the identity of Lemma T60 part 1, proved here directly;
T60 itself is stated for one hidden layer.) Hence the restriction of unit t to S' is relu of the left side plus a
constant: a new unit of the step, and a box unit of S'. Unchanged groups are copied, and a step that reaches D_P = 0
is a least step. The same proof holds for D2_P.
(2) Let x be in R^2 and P the four points (1, 0), (2, 1), (3, 0), (4, 1), each of weight 1/4. Layer 1 has the units
a_1 = relu(x_1), a_2 = relu(x_2); layer 2 the unit g = relu(a_1); layer 3 the units f_i = relu(g - i) for i = 1, 2, 3;
the logits are y_N = (f_1 - 2 f_2 + 2 f_3, 0). On P, g = 1, 2, 3, 4, and N's gap Delta_N = f_1 - 2 f_2 + 2 f_3 is
0, 1, 0, 1. The map M has the districts {a_1, a_2}, {g} and {f_1, f_2, f_3}, each with region P, their shelter claims,
and the branch claims of the three subtrees; every error is 0 (no point lies outside P; no hidden unit outside a
subtree reads it, since each subtree holds every later layer). M is a tree map with one node per layer, v_l = (l, P).
No judgment claim is needed (every area is P). The zoom: G_0 has no groups; G_1 = {sub(v_3)}, parent v_2, top {f_1,
f_2, f_3}; G_2 = {sub(v_2)}, parent v_1, top {g}; G_3 = {sub(v_1)}, parent the root, top {a_1, a_2}; each target size
is 1; the first step creates the group from kept units and the next two add the kept units of one layer each to
it (lifts). V_b(G_0) = 0 (N itself). At G_3 the box
relu(x_2) takes the values 0, 1, 0, 1 on P, and with gap weight 1 it gives Delta_N, so V_b(G_3) = 0. At G_1 a box unit
is relu(m^T (g - 1, g - 2, g - 3) + beta) = relu(mu g + nu), and at G_2 it is relu(mu x_1 + nu) with x_1 = g on P; no
kept unit of layer 3 remains, so in both cases the gap of a build is a relu(mu g + nu) + gamma on P. That function of
g is monotone (non-decreasing if a mu >= 0, non-increasing otherwise), and 0, 1, 0, 1 is not, so its gap differs from
Delta_N at some point of P, and for two logits D_P = 0 forces equal gaps (as in T20): no build at G_1 or G_2 is exact.
For the infimum: the gap vectors of these builds lie in the closed set Mon of monotone vectors of R^4; D_P is a
continuous function D(d) of the gap vector d that grows without bound as an entry of d goes to plus or minus infinity
(N's class probabilities lie strictly between 0 and 1), so D has a least value on Mon, and it is positive because
Delta_N is not in Mon and D(d) = 0 only at d = Delta_N. Hence V_b(G_i) >= min over d in Mon of D(d) > 0 for i = 1, 2.
QED.
Lean: `no_zigzag` (a relu(mu g + nu) + gamma takes no values 0, 1, 0, 1 at g = 1, 2, 3, 4: no build at G_1 or G_2 is
exact) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Recur.lean`; the positive minimum over Mon, and part 1, by hand. Check:
`model/th_tree.py` (part 1, exact fractions), `model/th_lift.py` (part 2).
Comment. Part 1 is the essay's "a smaller network is a coarser version of the larger one" as a theorem for sibling
merges: the coarse unit, seen on one child's areas, is a unit of that child's least build, and the recursion runs
from the finest level up. It is the mechanism of Corollary T60.1, now for any network with a tree map at error 0 and
not only for T43's instances. Proposition T61 does not contradict it: T61's instance has no tree map that meets
TH1's premises for its grouping. From the table in the proof of T61, z_A = tau_1 - 39/40 takes the value 1/40 at A,
-39/40 at C, D and mid CD, and the distinct values -7/40, -3/40, -19/40, -23/40 at B, mid AB, mid AC, mid BD. Each
of z_B = s_1 - 39/40, z_C = tau_2 - 39/40 and z_D = s_2 - 39/40 likewise takes one value at exactly three points and
distinct values at the other five. A region R of A's district with district error 0 contains A, and shelter error 0
needs z_A constant outside R, so the complement of R holds at most three points and R at least five. The same holds
for B, C and D. Two sets of at least five of the eight points meet, so the areas of {A, C} and of {B, D} cannot be
disjoint (DH3 item 2). (`model/th_t61.py` lists every such region.) Part 2 says why depth and zoom differ as steps, though TH1 treats them alike: a lift
changes what a box reads. A box above the bottleneck g in part 2 sees x_2, which the finer boxes below g cannot see.
On this instance, whenever least builds at G_1 and G_2 exist (an argument like T54 part 1 should give them; it is not
written here), every (r) sequence reaches 0 at G_3, because the kept units a_1, a_2 join the group there and a new
unit may read z_(a_2) = x_2. What fails is the order of the levels, not the step.

**Proposition TH3 (at a lossy sibling merge, step by step is strictly worse) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a
tree map, subtree groups,
branch claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** For D2_P there are a network N with one hidden layer and three
logits, a mix P, a tree map M with every claim eps = 0, and a zoom G_0, G_1, G_2 in which the one step G_1 -> G_2 is a
sibling merge of two groups of target size 1 into one group of target size 1, every level meets premises 1 and 2 of
TH1, V2_b(G_1) = 3/2 and V2_b(G_2) = 2, and every (r) sequence has D2_P(B_2) >= 3.
Proof. The input is x = (j_1, j_2, x_a, x_b, x_c) in R^5 and the hidden units are J_1 = relu(j_1), J_2 = relu(j_2),
u_a = relu(x_a), u_b = relu(x_b), u_c = relu(x_c) (weights the identity, biases 0). The mix has two areas. Omega_1:
the four points with (j_1, j_2) = (1, 0), x_c = -1 and (x_a, x_b) = (3 + s_a, 3 + s_b) for (s_a, s_b) in
{(2, 1), (2, -1), (-2, 1), (-2, -1)}, each of weight 1/8. Omega_2: the two points with (j_1, j_2) = (0, 1),
x_a = x_b = -1 and x_c = 3 + s_c for s_c in {1, -1}, each of weight 1/4. The logits are y_N = e_a u_a + e_b u_b + e_b u_c
with e_a = (1, -1, 0) and e_b = (1, 1, -2), which are orthogonal, sum to 0 (so P_perp e = e) and have |e_a|^2 = 2,
|e_b|^2 = 6.
The map. Districts {J_1}, {u_a, u_b} with region Omega_1 and {J_2}, {u_c} with region Omega_2; each unit is off
outside its region (there its pre-activation is 0 or -1), and the pre-activations of {u_a, u_b} and of {u_c} are
constant outside their regions (equal to -1), so the district and shelter claims have eps = 0. The judgment claims
(Omega_i, {J_i}, 1) have eps = 0. There is one hidden layer, so every branch claim has eps = 0. This is a tree map with
the nodes w_1 = (1, Omega_1) and w_2 = (1, Omega_2), children of the root. G_0 has no groups; G_1 has S_1 = {u_a, u_b}
(J_(w_1) = {J_1}) and S_2 = {u_c} (J_(w_2) = {J_2}), each of size 1; G_2 has S' = {u_a, u_b, u_c}, size 1. The step
G_0 -> G_1 creates S_1 and S_2 under the root, and G_1 -> G_2 is a sibling merge.
Centred signals. On Omega_1, y_N(x) is a constant plus Y(x) = s_a e_a + s_b e_b, and on Omega_2 a constant plus
Y(x) = s_c e_b. On each area the build may add any constant vector (through J_i), and a box of size 1 writes
v phi(x) for one vector v and its unit's values phi. Without loss of generality v lies in the image of P_perp (its
part along (1, 1, 1) changes no term of D2_P). For a fixed unit vector vhat in that image, the least over all functions phi
and constants of the sum over an area of p_x (1/2) |Y - v phi - const|^2 is (1/2) (sum of p_x |Y|^2 minus
vhat^T Sigma vhat), with Sigma the sum over the area of p_x Y Y^T (the area's Y has mean 0). Here
Sigma_1 = 2 e_a e_a^T + (1/2) e_b e_b^T and Sigma_2 = (1/2) e_b e_b^T; the sums of p_x |Y|^2 are 7 and 3; with the unit
vectors ehat_a, ehat_b, Sigma_1 has the eigenvalues 4 (on ehat_a) and 3 (on ehat_b), and Sigma_2 has 3 on ehat_b.
G_1. By TH1 part 1 (for D2), V2_b(G_1) = L2_(S_1) + L2_(S_2). The bound gives L2_(S_1) >= (1/2)(7 - 4) = 3/2, reached by
the box relu(x_a) (x_a >= 1 on Omega_1, so phi = 3 + s_a there) with v = e_a. And L2_(S_2) = 0 with relu(x_c) and
v = e_b. So V2_b(G_1) = 3/2.
G_2. One box unit writes v phi on both areas, with one v. The bound summed over the two areas is
(1/2)(10 - vhat^T (Sigma_1 + Sigma_2) vhat) >= (1/2)(10 - 6) = 2, since Sigma_1 + Sigma_2 has the eigenvalues 4 and 6. The
box relu(x_b + x_c) reaches it with v = e_b: it is s_b + 2 >= 1 on Omega_1 and s_c + 2 >= 1 on Omega_2. So V2_b(G_2) = 2.
Every least B_1 reads only s_a on Omega_1. Its box for S_1 is one unit relu(q(x)) with q = m_a x_a + m_b x_b + beta
(its top is {u_a, u_b}). Its term 3/2 forces vhat = +-ehat_a (the eigenvalue 4 is simple) and phi = kappa s_a + const on
Omega_1 with kappa not 0 (the least phi for that vhat). phi takes two values, each at the two points with one s_a, and
one of the values is positive. At the two points of that value relu(q) > 0, so q is equal there; these points differ
only in x_b, by 2, so m_b = 0. Hence p_1, the pre-activation of B_1's unit for S_1, is a function of s_a on Omega_1;
and p_2, that of S_2's unit, is constant on Omega_1 (it reads x_c only, by the same top rule). So every new unit of the
step to G_2 is, on Omega_1, a function of s_a, and on Omega_2 a function of s_c.
The (r) step. With such a unit and vhat = cos(theta) ehat_a + sin(theta) ehat_b + (a part orthogonal to both), the
largest captured amount on Omega_1 is the sum of p_x (vhat^T Y)^2 projected onto functions of s_a, which is
4 cos(theta)^2 (since s_b has mean 0 at each value of s_a), and on Omega_2 at most 3 sin(theta)^2. So D2_P(B_2) >=
(1/2)(10 - max over theta of (4 cos(theta)^2 + 3 sin(theta)^2)) = (1/2)(10 - 4) = 3 > 2. QED.
Lean: `capture_le` (4 c^2 + 3 s^2 <= 4 when c^2 + s^2 <= 1) and `relu_pos_eq` (equal positive ReLU values force equal
pre-activations) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Recur.lean`; the eigenvalues by sympy in `model/th_break.py`. Check:
`model/th_break.py` (exact fractions, and a search over (r) steps).
Comment. The least unit of the merged group uses e_b on both children, while the least unit of child 1 keeps only
e_a: child 1 drops a direction its parent needs, and by Lemma T60 part 3 a dropped direction never comes back. This
is the same kind of failure as Proposition T61, now inside the clean setting of TH1 (every claim at error 0, a tree
map), so being clean in the sense of TH1 does not make step by step optimal at a lossy step. The instance has one
hidden layer, so its branch claims say nothing and it lies in the setting of TM1; depth plays no part in it. It uses
two output directions; with two logits, in the case of Route (1) of Conjecture TH4 (least boxes on at every point of
their areas), a sibling merge of size 1 loses nothing beyond its children (Part D.16). What the parent needs from child 1
is the whole matrix Sigma_1, not child 1's least unit; Conjecture TH4 states the recursion that passes it up, and
Theorem TP2 (Part B.P) proves it for sibling merges and D2_P when the nodes hold linear-read claims: the least
loss is pinned by the summaries, with a gap of half the linear-read errors.
DM6 gives no complete map for three logits, so TH3 is not about T5's exactness promise; it is about which rule can be
least at a lossy level.

## B.P Passing summaries up the tree: the recursion that Proposition TH3 broke (side branch under nodes R-tree, R-branch, S-plainff and R-linread, added 2026-10-29)

Shonu (2026-10-29), after Proposition TH3: "we've shown that recursion in the naive sense is not optimal ... I'd like
to try to prove a very similar thing, but now passing up the summary", with summaries cheap to make and to use, and
instant switching kept. Proposition TH3 shows what a child must pass up: not its least unit but what its area can
give in every output direction. This Part makes that object exact for the objective D2_P (node R-obj).
1. Definition DP1: a linear-read claim on a node says that inside the node's area, after the terms the build gets
   for free (a constant and the kept judgment units), N's centred logits are a linear function of the pre-activations
   of the node's top units. Its error is the energy that no linear function captures. It is a claim about N alone.
2. Definition DP2: the summary of a node is one number and one n_y x n_y matrix, read from N on the node's area; its
   build record holds what a build needs besides the summary.
3. Theorem TP1: for one group, (1/2) tail <= L2_S <= (1/2) tail + (1/2)(sum of the linear-read errors), where tail is
   the sum of the eigenvalues of the summed matrices below the k_S largest. A box of units that are on at every point
   of P reaches the upper value. At error 0 the least loss is a closed form. Corollary TP1.1: among boxes whose units
   are on at every point of the group's areas the upper value is least for any error (Route (1) of Conjecture TH4).
4. Theorem TP2: along a zoom, a sibling merge adds the children's matrices, the least loss of every level is pinned by
   summaries alone, in any order, and a rule that passes up a compressed summary loses at most half of the trace it
   drops. In the instance of Proposition TH3 the (r) step is such a rule. Corollary TP2.1: two logits.
5. Proposition TP3: the one-time cost is one pass of N over P and one least-squares solve per node; the value and box
   directions of a level cost a number of operations set by n_y alone; the build costs operations linear in the width
   of the group's top and judgment units; a switch selects stored weights.
What B.P does not do: at a lift (a step to an earlier layer) the lifted group's summary is computed again from N in
the one-time pass, not from its children's summaries (TP2 part 5). So B.P carries the zoom recursion of sibling
merges, not the depth recursion.
Status: every item uses nodes R-tree, R-branch, S-plainff (card 3-24) and R-linread (card 3-26), all PENDING, and
R-obj, so this Part is a side branch. Setting and notation are those of Part B.H. Arithmetic: exact real arithmetic
with exact eigenvectors (the eigenvalues of a rational matrix are algebraic, in general not rational); the summaries
themselves are rational.

**Definition DP1 (linear-read claim) (node R-linread).** Let M be a tree map, w = (l, R) a node and J any set of units
of U(w) (for example the units of a judgment claim (R, J, a) of M). Write T_w = U(w) minus J; when T_w is empty,
z_(T_w) has no coordinates, B_w = 0, Sigma_w = 0 and eps_lin(w) = E_w. On the area R put the inner product <f, g>_w = sum over x in R of p_x f(x) g(x) of real functions (p_x > 0), let
F_w be the span of the constant 1 and of the functions h_j (j in J) on R, and let Pi_w be the orthogonal projection
onto the complement of F_w, applied to each coordinate of a vector-valued function. Let
   Y(x) = P_perp y_N(x),   Ytil = Pi_w Y,   ztil = Pi_w z_(T_w)
(z_(T_w)(x) is the vector of pre-activations of the units of T_w). Let B_w = C_yz C_zz^+ with
C_yz = sum p_x Ytil ztil^T and C_zz = sum p_x ztil ztil^T (^+ the Moore-Penrose inverse), the least-norm solution of
min over B of sum over x in R of p_x |Ytil(x) - B ztil(x)|^2, and let r_w = Ytil - B_w ztil. The **linear-read claim**
(R, J) says r_w = 0 at every point of R. Its error is
   eps_lin(w) = sum over x in R of p_x |r_w(x)|^2.
It is rational (least squares over the rationals), computable in time polynomial in the size of N, P and the claim,
and 0 exactly when the claim holds (every p_x > 0). It is unchanged by the rescaling of Fact F1 (a rescaled unit of
T_w scales one coordinate of ztil, and least squares does not see the scale; a rescaled unit of J leaves F_w
unchanged) and by a copy of a unit of layer L as in Definition DN1 (a copy repeats a coordinate of ztil, and the fit
and its residual do not change). It names an area and a set of units and refers to no build, size or zoom.
Source: the essay's "reusable judgment" (the build gets the judgment units for free) and its linear reads; the
claim asks that every bend of N's logits inside R come from the judgment units and not from units below the node.

**Definition DP2 (summary and build record of a node).** With the notation of DP1, the **summary** of w is the pair
   s_w = (E_w, Sigma_w),   E_w = sum over x in R of p_x |Ytil(x)|^2,   Sigma_w = B_w C_zz B_w^T,
a number and a rational symmetric positive semidefinite n_y x n_y matrix whose image lies in the image of P_perp. Its
**build record** is: B_w (n_y x |T_w|); the coefficients A_w, G_w of Y - Ytil and of B_w (z_(T_w) - ztil) in the basis
(1, h_j : j in J) of F_w (the parts the free terms must carry); the vector b_w = B_w zeta_w, where zeta_w is the
constant value of z_(T_w) outside R (it exists when the districts of T_w have shelter claims at eps = 0); and the
number rho_w = max over x in P of |B_w z_(T_w)(x)|. For a set W of nodes put E_W = sum over w in W of E_w and
Sigma_W = sum over w in W of Sigma_w. For a symmetric positive semidefinite matrix A and k >= 0, top_k(A) is the sum of
its k largest eigenvalues (all of them when k exceeds n_y) and tail_k(A) = tr A - top_k(A). For a subtree group S with
nodes W_S and target size k_S put
   Lin_S = (1/2) (E_(W_S) - top_(k_S)(Sigma_(W_S))),   eps_lin(S) = sum over w in W_S of eps_lin(w).
Comment. The normal equations hold with the Moore-Penrose inverse: if C_zz v = 0 then v^T ztil(x) = 0 at every x in R
(as every p_x > 0), so C_yz v = 0, and hence C_yz C_zz^+ C_zz = C_yz. So every coordinate of r_w is orthogonal to every
coordinate of ztil, E_w = tr Sigma_w + eps_lin(w), and Lin_S = (1/2) tail_(k_S)(Sigma_(W_S)) + (1/2) eps_lin(S).
Sigma_w has rank at most min(n_y - 1, |T_w|). In the instance of Proposition TH3, Sigma_1 and Sigma_2 of its proof are
the summaries of w_1 and w_2 (there Ytil is the centred signal and is linear in ztil).

**Theorem TP1 (one group: the summary pins the least loss) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree
groups, branch claims, every claim other than the linear-read claims has eps = 0, linear-read claims, the objective
D2_P).** Let M be a tree map and G a tree grouping that meet premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1, and let S be a group of
G. For each w in W_S let M hold the linear-read claim (area of w, J_w), with any error. Then:
1. (Lower bound.) L2_S >= Lin_S - (1/2) eps_lin(S) = (1/2) tail_(k_S)(Sigma_(W_S)).
2. (Upper bound, reached.) There is a box of S of size k_S whose units are on at every point of P, with logit weights
   V, U_w and vectors t_w, whose terms in L2_S sum to exactly Lin_S. With q_1, ..., q_(k_S) orthonormal eigenvectors of
   Sigma_(W_S) for its k_S largest eigenvalues, taken in the image of P_perp (when k_S > n_y - 1 the units after the
   first n_y - 1 get q_t = 0 and write nothing), unit t is relu(m_t^T z_(T(S))(x) + beta_t), where m_t has the part
   B_w^T q_t on T_w for each w in W_S, beta_t = 1 + sum over w in W_S of rho_w, and V = (q_1, ..., q_(k_S)).
3. So (1/2) tail_(k_S)(Sigma_(W_S)) <= L2_S <= Lin_S, and L2_S = Lin_S when every eps_lin(w) = 0. The lower bound is 0
   when k_S >= rank Sigma_(W_S), and then the statement says only L2_S <= Lin_S = (1/2) eps_lin(S). If every group of G
   meets the premise on S, then by Theorem TH1 part 1 V2_b(G) lies between the sums over the groups of the two sides,
   and the build assembled from the boxes of part 2 (TH1's upper bound) has D2_P = sum over S of Lin_S. Its gap to the
   least is at most (1/2) times the sum of the linear-read errors used: a bound graded in these errors alone, with
   every other claim at eps = 0, for D2_P.
Proof. Fix S and write W = W_S, k = k_S.
(1) This part uses only the definitions of L2_S and DP1. Take any choice in L2_S: a box C of size k, V, U_w, t_w. Let
g(x) = P_perp V C(x). Its values lie in the image Wim of P_perp V, of dimension d <= k; let Q be an n_y x d matrix with
orthonormal columns spanning Wim. Fix w in W. The term of L2_S on the area of w is (1/2) sum p_x |g + f - Y|^2 with
f = P_perp (U_w h_(J_w) + t_w), whose coordinates lie in F_w. For any functions f with coordinates in F_w,
sum p_x |Y - g - f|^2 >= sum p_x |Pi_w (Y - g)|^2 (Pi_w is the orthogonal projection onto the complement of F_w,
coordinate by coordinate). Pi_w (Y - g) = Ytil - Pi_w g, and Pi_w g = Q Pi_w (Q^T g) takes values in Wim. At each
point, |Ytil - Q b|^2 >= |(I - Q Q^T) Ytil|^2 for every b. So the term is at least (1/2) (E_w - tr(Q^T K_w Q)) with
K_w = sum p_x Ytil Ytil^T. Write Ytil = B_w ztil + r_w. By the Comment of DP2, K_w = Sigma_w + R_w with
R_w = sum p_x r_w r_w^T positive semidefinite and tr R_w = eps_lin(w). Summing over w,
   L2-terms >= (1/2) (E_W - tr(Q^T Sigma_W Q) - tr(Q^T R_W Q)).
By Ky Fan's maximum principle (literature table), tr(Q^T Sigma_W Q) <= top_d(Sigma_W) <= top_k(Sigma_W) (eigenvalues
>= 0). Since Q Q^T is a projection and R_W >= 0, tr(Q^T R_W Q) <= tr R_W = eps_lin(S). The choice was arbitrary, so
L2_S >= Lin_S - (1/2) eps_lin(S), which equals (1/2) tail_k(Sigma_W) by the Comment of DP2.
(2) Sigma_W is symmetric, positive semidefinite, with image inside the image of P_perp, so its eigenvectors for
positive eigenvalues lie there, and the others can be chosen there. For a unit vector q, |q^T B_w z_(T_w)(x)| <= rho_w,
so m_t^T z_(T(S))(x) + beta_t >= 1 at every x in P (for q_t = 0 the unit is the constant beta_t and writes nothing);
each box unit then equals m_t^T z_(T(S))(x) + beta_t on P. Fix w in W and x in the area of w. The units of T_(w') for
w' in W other than w lie in districts with region the area of w', disjoint from that of w, with shelter claims at
eps = 0, so z_(T_(w')) = zeta_(w') on the area of w. Also z_(T_w) - ztil has coordinates in F_w. Hence on the area of w,
   V C(x) = Q Q^T B_w ztil(x) + phi_w(x),
with phi_w a function whose coordinates lie in F_w and whose values lie in the image of P_perp. Y - Ytil has
coordinates in F_w, so Y - Ytil - phi_w = U_w h_(J_w) + t_w on the area of w for some U_w and t_w (F_w is spanned by 1
and the h_j, j in J_w); take them, and apply P_perp, which changes nothing since Y, Ytil, phi_w and V C lie in its
image. The term on the area of w is then (1/2) sum p_x |Q Q^T B_w ztil - Ytil|^2. Write
Ytil - Q Q^T B_w ztil = r_w + (I - Q Q^T) B_w ztil; the second part is linear in ztil and r_w is orthogonal to ztil,
so the sum is eps_lin(w) + tr Sigma_w - tr(Q^T Sigma_w Q). Summing over w,
   sum = (1/2) (eps_lin(S) + tr Sigma_W - top_k(Sigma_W)) = (1/2) (E_W - top_k(Sigma_W)) = Lin_S,
using tr(Q^T Sigma_W Q) = top_k(Sigma_W) for the eigenvectors (zero columns add nothing).
(3) Parts 1 and 2 give the sandwich; rank Sigma_W <= k gives tail_k = 0. TH1 part 1 for D2_P gives
V2_b(G) = sum over S of L2_S, and TH1's upper bound with the choices of part 2 (they attain their terms exactly) is a
class (b) build with D2_P = sum over S of Lin_S. QED.
Lean: `energy_split` (the orthogonal split of a weighted residual energy, used in parts 1 and 2) and `trace_bound`
(the inequality step of part 1) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Recur.lean`, scalar forms; Ky Fan's principle is classical
(Mathlib has no eigenvalue sums in this form). Check: `model/tp_summary.py`.
Comment. Part 1 holds for every box, of any shape. At eps_lin = 0, TP1 is reduced-rank regression (Izenman 1975, in
the literature table) with one output space shared by the areas and free regressors per area; its hypothesis of a
nonsingular covariance is not needed here (the pseudo-inverse). TP1 gives no rule for a group with large eps_lin,
where a least box may switch inside its areas; that is where the hardness of Proposition T57 can sit (the linear-read
error of T57's instances is not computed here). The gap eps_lin(S) / 2 is the most a box that switches can take from
the residuals r_w (Corollary TP1.1).

**Corollary TP1.1 (boxes on throughout their areas; Route (1) of Conjecture TH4) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, every claim other than the linear-read claims has eps = 0,
linear-read claims, the objective D2_P).** In the setting of Theorem TP1, the least of the terms of L2_S over the boxes
of S whose units are on at every point of S's areas is Lin_S, for any values of eps_lin. In particular, if L2_S is
attained by such a box, then L2_S = Lin_S.
Proof. The box of TP1 part 2 is such a box and reaches Lin_S. Conversely, let C be such a box, with any V, U_w, t_w.
On the area of w each unit equals m_t^T z_(T(S)) + beta_t, and the parts on T_(w') (w' other than w) are constant there,
so g = P_perp V C is P_perp V M_w z_(T_w) + const, and Pi_w g = P_perp V M_w ztil, whose coordinates are linear in
ztil. As in TP1 part 1 the term on the area of w is at least (1/2) sum p_x |Ytil - Pi_w g|^2 =
(1/2)(eps_lin(w) + sum p_x |B_w ztil - Pi_w g|^2), since r_w is orthogonal to every linear function of ztil, and
sum p_x |B_w ztil - Q b(x)|^2 >= tr Sigma_w - tr(Q^T Sigma_w Q) with Q spanning the image of P_perp V. Summing over w and
using Ky Fan as in TP1 part 1: the terms are at least (1/2)(eps_lin(S) + tr Sigma_W - top_k(Sigma_W)) = Lin_S. QED.
Lean: `energy_split` and `trace_bound`, as in TP1.

**Theorem TP2 (summaries pass up the tree) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch
claims, every claim other than the linear-read claims has eps = 0, linear-read claims, the objective D2_P).** Let
G_0, ..., G_m be a zoom of tree groupings, every level meeting premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1, and let M hold the
linear-read claim (area of w, J_w) of every node w in W_S of every group S of every level. Then:
1. (Sums.) A summary depends only on the node w and on J_w. If a changed group S' of G_(j+1) is a sibling merge with
   groups S_1, ..., S_q of G_j inside it and nodes W' of its own (children of its parent whose units were kept at
   G_j), then Sigma_(W_(S')) = Sigma_(W_(S_1)) + ... + Sigma_(W_(S_q)) + Sigma_(W'), and the same for E.
2. (Every level from summaries.) For every level j, Lin(G_j) := sum over the groups S of G_j of Lin_S, and the box
   directions q_t of TP1 part 2, are computed from the summaries of the nodes in the groups of G_j alone, and
   (1/2) sum over S of tail_(k_S)(Sigma_(W_S)) <= V2_b(G_j) <= Lin(G_j). The build of TP1 part 3 has D2_P = Lin(G_j);
   its weights are computed from the q_t and the build records of these nodes. No level uses the build of another
   level. When every eps_lin is 0, every level is least.
3. (Compressed summaries.) Let a rule replace each Sigma_w by a symmetric matrix Sigma'_w with
   0 <= Sigma'_w <= Sigma_w (in the order of positive semidefinite matrices), let tau_w = tr(Sigma_w - Sigma'_w),
   and build each group as in TP1 part 2 with orthonormal eigenvectors Q' of Sigma'_(W_S) in place of Q. Then that
   group's terms are (1/2)(E_(W_S) - tr(Q'^T Sigma_(W_S) Q')) <= Lin_S + (1/2) sum over w in W_S of tau_w.
4. (The instance of Proposition TH3.) There, the least D2_P over (r) steps from a least B_1 is 3, and it equals the
   value (1/2)(E - top_1(Sigma'_1 + Sigma_2)) of the rule of part 3 with Sigma'_1 = 4 ehat_a ehat_a^T (tau_(w_1) = 3).
   The summary rule gives Lin = 2 = V2_b(G_2), and part 3 bounds the compressed rule by 2 + 3/2.
5. (Lifts.) Part 1 is stated for sibling merges only. At a lift the nodes of S' are not the nodes of the groups
   inside it, and part 2 holds with the lifted group's own nodes, whose summaries are made in the same one-time pass
   from N. In the instance of Proposition TH2 part 2: Lin(G_1) = Lin(G_2) = 1/20 with eps_lin = 1/10 at each level
   (the top pre-activations are affine in g, and the gap 0, 1, 0, 1 is not), and Lin(G_3) = 0 with eps_lin = 0 (the
   top reads x_2, and the gap equals x_2 on P). There the lower bound of part 2 is 0 at G_1 and G_2 (Sigma has rank 1
   and k = 1), so TP2 does not see the positive least loss that TH2 part 2 proves.
Proof. (1) DP1 and DP2 read only N, P, the area of w and J_w. A sibling merge keeps the parent and the kept judgment
units (Definition DH3 item 5), so W_(S') is the disjoint union of the W_(S_c) and W', and Sigma and E add over
disjoint sets of nodes by their definition. (2) TP1 part 3 at each level; Lin_S reads only E_w and Sigma_w for w in
W_S, q_t reads only Sigma_(W_S), and the weights of TP1 part 2 and of TH1's assembly read q_t and the build records
(m_t from B_w, beta_t from rho_w, U_w and t_w from A_w, G_w and the q_t, the constant outputs from b_w and beta_t).
(3) The computation of TP1 part 2 holds for any n_y x k matrix Q with orthonormal columns in the image of P_perp and
gives the terms (1/2)(E_W - tr(Q^T Sigma_W Q)). The eigenvectors Q' of Sigma'_W for positive eigenvalues lie in the
image of P_perp, because 0 <= Sigma'_w <= Sigma_w puts the kernel of Sigma_w inside that of Sigma'_w; the others can be
chosen there. tr(Q'^T Sigma_W Q') >= tr(Q'^T Sigma'_W Q') = top_k(Sigma'_W) (Sigma_W - Sigma'_W >= 0), and
top_k(Sigma_W) <= top_k(Sigma'_W) + top_k(Sigma_W - Sigma'_W) <= top_k(Sigma'_W) + sum of tau_w (subadditivity of top_k
follows from Ky Fan's principle; top_k of a positive semidefinite matrix is at most its trace). So the terms are at
most (1/2)(E_W - top_k(Sigma_W)) + (1/2) sum tau_w. (4) TH3's proof shows every (r) step has D2_P(B_2) >= 3: every new
unit of the step is, on Omega_1, a function of s_a, and the capture on Omega_1 is at most vhat^T (4 ehat_a ehat_a^T) vhat
(s_b has mean 0 at each value of s_a). The value 3 is reached: the unit relu(p_1 + c), with p_1 the pre-activation of
B_1's unit for S_1 (on Omega_1 it is kappa s_a + const, kappa not 0) and c large enough that the unit is on at every
point of P, with logit weight a multiple of e_a, is an allowed new unit, and with the free terms it captures 4 on
Omega_1 and 0 on Omega_2, so D2_P = (1/2)(10 - 4) = 3. Sigma'_1 + Sigma_2 has the eigenvalues 4 (on ehat_a) and 3 (on
ehat_b), so the compressed rule's value is (1/2)(10 - 4) = 3, and its box (Q' = ehat_a) is this unit up to the free
terms. Sigma_1 - Sigma'_1 = 3 ehat_b ehat_b^T >= 0 with trace 3. The values 2 and 3/2 are TH3's and TP1's with
eps_lin = 0. (5) In TH2 part 2 there are two logits, y_N = (Delta_N, 0), so Ytil = (Delta_N - 1/2, 1/2 - Delta_N) / 2
after centring on P (the mean of Delta_N is 1/2), J is empty and the area is P. E = 2 (1/4) sum (Delta_N - 1/2)^2 / 4
= 1/8. At G_1 the top pre-activations are g - i, affine in g, so Sigma is the regression of Ytil on g: g = 1, 2, 3, 4
has variance 5/4, the covariance of Delta_N with g is 1/4, so tr Sigma = 1/8 x (1/4)^2 / ((5/4)(1/4)) = 1/40,
eps_lin = 1/10, and with k = 1 (Sigma has rank 1) Lin = (1/2)(1/8 - 1/40) = 1/20 and tail_1 = 0. G_2 has the top {g}:
the same numbers. At G_3 the top pre-activations are x_1 and x_2, and Delta_N = x_2 on P, so eps_lin = 0,
tr Sigma = E and Lin = 0. QED.
Lean: `topk_trunc` (the scalar form of part 3) and `th3_summary` (the numbers 3/2, 2, 3 of part 4) in
`lean/coarse/Coarse/Recur.lean`; the eigenvalue steps by sympy in `model/tp_summary.py`.
Comment. Part 2 is the statement Proposition TH2 part 1 gave for exact levels, now for lossy levels too, within the
sandwich of TP1. Part 4 says what went wrong in TH3, in its instance: child 1's least unit keeps only the e_a part of
Sigma_1, and a dropped direction is lost to every later level (Lemma T60 part 3). In general an (r) step sees a child
through all functions of its units' pre-activations, which is not of the form Sigma'_w <= Sigma_w when eps_lin > 0, so
part 3 is not a statement about every (r) step. Part 3 gives a budget: a rule may compress summaries to save memory
and loses at most half the trace it drops.

**Corollary TP2.1 (two logits) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, every
claim other than the linear-read claims has eps = 0, linear-read claims, the objective D2_P, two logits).** With
n_y = 2 and k_S >= 1, Lin_S = (1/2) eps_lin(S). So L2_S <= (1/2) eps_lin(S); if L2_S is attained by a box whose units
are on at every point of S's areas, then L2_S = (1/2) eps_lin(S); and for a sibling merge S' of groups S_1, ..., S_q and
nodes W', with every size at least 1 and each least box of this kind, L2_(S') = L2_(S_1) + ... + L2_(S_q) +
(1/2) eps_lin(W').
Proof. The image of P_perp is one line, so every Sigma_w, and Sigma_(W_S), has rank at most 1, and top_1 = tr. By the
Comment of DP2, Lin_S = (1/2)(E - tr Sigma) = (1/2) eps_lin(S). TP1 part 3 and Corollary TP1.1 give the rest, and
eps_lin adds over disjoint sets of nodes. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (a reading of TP1 and TP1.1).
Comment. This is Route (2) of Conjecture TH4 under Route (1)'s premise: with two logits a sibling merge of size 1
loses nothing beyond its children and the nodes it takes from kept units.

**Proposition TP3 (the cost of summaries, and switching) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree
groups, branch claims, every claim other than the linear-read claims has eps = 0, linear-read claims, the objective
D2_P).** In the setting of Theorem TP2, in exact real arithmetic with exact eigenvectors, write n_w = |T_w| + |J_w| and
|R_w| for the number of points in the area of w.
1. (One-time cost.) Given the values z and y_N of N at every point of P (one pass of N over P), the summary s_w, the
   build record and eps_lin(w) take O(|R_w| (n_w + n_y)^2 + n_w^3 + n_y^2 |T_w|) arithmetic operations for each node w.
2. (Value and directions of a level.) For a group S, Lin_S and q_1, ..., q_(k_S) are computed from the summaries of
   its nodes alone, with no access to N or P: one sum of |W_S| matrices of size n_y x n_y and one eigen-decomposition,
   O(|W_S| n_y^2 + n_y^3) operations. This does not depend on the width or depth of N, or on P.
3. (The build of a level.) From the q_t and the build records, the weights of S's box, the logit weights on its box
   and on its judgment units (or their copies) and its part of the bias take
   O(k_S sum over w in W_S of n_y (|T_w| + |J_w| + 1)) operations: linear in the width of the group's top and judgment
   units, and free of P and of N's depth.
4. (Nesting in the size.) For one group and k < k', the box of TP1 part 2 for k may be taken as the first k units of
   the box for k', with the same logit weights on them (beta_t does not depend on q_t). The logit weights on the kept
   judgment units (or their copies) and the bias of the assembled build are a stored base value plus one stored term
   for each box unit.
5. (Switching.) After a one-time computation of the builds of every group of every level (parts 1 to 3), a switch to
   level j selects stored weights and does no arithmetic on N, P or the summaries. Copying the selected weights costs
   O(sum over the changed groups S of k_S (|T(S)| + n_y) + n_y sum over their nodes of |J_w|) numbers.
Proof. (1) From the values at the points of R_w: project the columns of z_(T_w) and of Y onto the complement of F_w
(a least-squares fit on at most n_w + 1 columns), form C_zz and C_yz, take C_zz^+ (O(|T_w|^3)), and form B_w, Sigma_w,
E_w, eps_lin(w) = E_w - tr Sigma_w, the coefficients A_w, G_w (read off the projection), b_w and rho_w (one pass over
P). (2) Sigma_(W_S) is the sum; its top k_S eigenvalues and eigenvectors come from one eigen-decomposition of an
n_y x n_y symmetric matrix. (3) m_t has the part B_w^T q_t on each T_w; U_w and t_w are A_w and G_w combined with the q_t
(TP1 part 2); the bias of TH1's assembly is a sum of these and of the constant outputs, computed from b_w and beta_t.
(4) Order an orthonormal eigenbasis of Sigma_(W_S) in the image of P_perp by decreasing eigenvalue; for every k its
first k vectors are top eigenvectors, so the box for k is the first k units of the box for k'; beta_t is the same for
every unit vector; V's columns are the q_t. In TP1 part 2, phi_w is a sum over the box units t of q_t times a function
in F_w, so U_w and t_w are N's projection term minus a sum of one term per unit; the bias and judgment weights of TH1's
assembly are linear in the t_w and in the box's constant outputs, which are sums over units. (5) Store the build of
every group of every level, the per-unit terms of part 4 and the base values; a build at level j is the union of the
stored builds of the groups of G_j and the kept units. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (operation counts and a reading of TP1's construction).
Comment. The trunk asks that a switch cost time that does not grow with N. Part 5 meets it in the reading of
Proposition TY3 part 1: a switch selects stored weights. If the selected weights must be copied, the copy grows with
the width of the changed groups, as any build of N's kind must. Part 2 says more: the least D2 value of a level the
developer did not give up front, and its box directions, need no access to N; the box weights then need the build
records (part 3). DM6 (complete maps) is not extended here to linear-read claims, so TP1's closed form at eps_lin = 0
is not yet T5's exactness clause; card 3-26 asks whether it should be.

**Remark (KL).** Theorems TP1 and TP2 are for D2_P (node R-obj, DROPPED by Shonu on 2026-10-31: label OPT-D2). By Fact
F11, KL(softmax(y) || softmax(y + delta)) <= (1/4) |P_perp delta|^2 at every point, so the build of TP1 part 3 has
D_P <= (1/2) Lin(G) (label ONE-BUILD). Part B.I turns this into statements about the least KL: when k_S >= rank
Sigma_(W_S) the least is within eps_lin(S) / 4 of 0 (Theorem TI2); when k_S = 0 it is the information table
(Theorem TI1); for 0 < k_S < rank Sigma_(W_S) the D2 summaries do not fix it (Proposition TI5), and it is open
(Theorems TI3, TI4, Conjecture DI1).

## B.L The broken cases read as networks: reuse at a merge, linear areas at a lift (side branch under nodes R-tree, R-branch, S-plainff, R-linread and R-oninside, added 2026-10-29)

Shonu (2026-10-29): a smaller network that is a coarser version of a larger one exists and is understood ("this is
literally existing in the network ... an interpretable object which we understand how it was formed"), so the failures
of Propositions TH3 and TH2 part 2 should have "a more interpretable understanding of why that doesn't work based not
just on the mathematics but on the network itself, which can point us to a different solution". This Part reads the
two instances as networks and turns each reading into a theorem.
1. Remark B.L.1: what N does in each instance. In TH3 two units in two areas write the same output direction (reuse),
   and the child that drops it cannot see the reuse. In TH2 part 2 the finer levels see only N's bottleneck unit, and
   the lift lets the box read an input that N's later layers never use.
2. Theorem TL1 (sibling merges): from a build whose boxes are of the kind TP1 builds, a merge step made only from the
   children's box units reaches Lin of the next level whenever every output direction the merge keeps is, inside each
   child's areas, a direction that child's box already writes (condition (K)). At linear-read error 0 the step is
   least; otherwise it is within half the linear-read errors of least. (K) holds when every child lost nothing, and
   when the children write orthogonal output directions and the merge is no larger than any child. It is a sufficient
   condition. TH3 is a case where it fails.
3. Definition DL1 (on-inside claim) and Theorem TL2 (lifts): when the units a lift passes through are on at every point
   of their area and the area's judgment units are flat there, every unit of the finer level is a unit of the coarser
   box one layer down. So a lift whose box has room for all of them never raises the least loss, for D_P and D2_P alike.
   Corollary TL2.1: TH2 part 2 is this case.
Status: every item uses nodes R-tree, R-branch, S-plainff (card 3-24); TL1 also R-linread (card 3-26) and R-obj; TL2
the new node R-oninside (card 3-27), all PENDING, so this Part is a side branch. Setting and notation are those of Parts
B.H and B.P.

**Remark B.L.1 (the two instances as networks).** Each point is marked: essay, or my reading.
1. Proposition TH3. Area 1 has u_a writing e_a and u_b writing e_b; area 2 has u_c writing e_b. Inside area 1 the
   e_a signal is the louder one (the eigenvalue 4 of Sigma_1 against 3), so child 1's least unit keeps e_a. Over both
   areas e_b is the louder one (3 + 3 = 6 against 4), because two units in two areas write it. The direction is
   reused, and the reuse is visible only through the readers: N's logit weights on u_b and u_c are equal. A child
   that decides from its own area alone cannot see it (my reading). The essay's learning story says the reused route
   is the one that wins ("circuits race to capture the remaining error, and the ones that reuse what's already there,
   and can be reused in turn, outcompete the rest"; essay). Theorem TL1 gives a sufficient condition for a merge step
   to be least. When the merge is no larger than any child, it can fail only when the children's output directions
   are not orthogonal (part 2(b)), which is reuse in this sense. TH3 shows that the failure can be strict. A merge
   that is larger than one of its children can fail with no reuse (Comment of TL1).
2. Proposition TH2 part 2. N computes its gap 0, 1, 0, 1 from the one unit g through three units f_i that fold g like
   a lookup on four points (by TP2 part 5 its linear-read error is 1/10 out of an energy of 1/8). The finer levels G_1
   and G_2 see the network only through g. The coarsest level G_3 reads x_1 and x_2, and x_2 equals the gap on P,
   though no unit of N reads a_2 = relu(x_2) (my reading: the box at G_3 uses a route that N never uses). Every unit
   that a lift of this zoom passes through (g at the first lift; a_1 and a_2 at the second) has a pre-activation >= 0
   at every point of P. Theorem TL2 shows that in this case a lift whose box has room for every finer unit can only
   lower the least loss: on P, the finer class is contained in the coarser one, one layer down. So TH2 part 2 is not a
   failure of the step; it says that a lift by itself is not a coarsening, only a smaller size is.
3. The essay's picture of a coarse neuron is a union of a branch of N's own units ("one 'curves & loops' neuron
   instead of ten curve detectors"; essay), and its picture of depth is a gate in front of an area ("the dogs go on to
   their own area, which doesn't have to worry about cars"; essay). In the language of B.H: a merge joins units that
   share readers, and inside an area, behind its gate, the value path is linear (my reading, compatible with the gated
   pathways of Saxe, Sodhani and Lewallen 2022 in the literature table). TL1 is about the first, TL2 about the second.

**Theorem TL1 (a merge step reaches Lin when no child dropped a direction the merge keeps) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, linear-read claims, every claim other than the linear-read claims
has eps = 0, the objective D2_P).** Let G_j and G_(j+1) be consecutive levels of a zoom of tree groupings, both
meeting premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1, and let M hold the linear-read claim (area of w, J_w), with any error, for
every node w of every group of both levels. Let every changed group of the step be a sibling merge (Definition DH3
item 5; a creation is the case with no group inside). For such a group S', of the groups S_1, ..., S_q of G_j and the
nodes W', write Sigma_c = Sigma_(W_(S_c)), Sigma' = Sigma_(W_(S')), k_c = k_(S_c), k' = k_(S') and r = n_y - 1 (the
dimension of the image of P_perp). A list of directions of size k is a list q_1, ..., q_k whose first min(k, r)
entries are orthonormal vectors in the image of P_perp and whose other entries are 0. Call a box of a group S **of
TP1 type with directions q_1, ..., q_k** when its units are on at every point of P and, for each unit t, there is a
number c_t > 0 such that for each node w in W_S the part m_t|T_w of the unit's read on T_w satisfies
(m_t|T_w)^T ztil(x) = c_t q_t^T B_w ztil(x) at every x in the area of w. Let B_j be a build at G_j, assembled as in TH1's
upper bound, whose box for each group S is of TP1 type with a list of directions of eigenvectors of Sigma_(W_S) for its
k_S largest eigenvalues (the build of TP1 part 3 is one), and let K_c be the span of the directions of S_c's box.
**Condition (K)** at S' (relative to these directions): there is a list of directions q'_1, ..., q'_(k') of
eigenvectors of Sigma' for its k' largest eigenvalues such that q'_t lies in K_c + ker Sigma_c for every t and every c.
Then:
1. If (K) holds at every changed group, there is an allowed (r) step from B_j whose build B_(j+1) has
   D2_P(B_(j+1)) = Lin(G_(j+1)), and whose boxes are of TP1 type with directions of the same kind (for S', the q'_t).
   So D2_P(B_(j+1)) - V2_b(G_(j+1)) <= (1/2) eps_lin(G_(j+1)) (the sum of the linear-read errors of the level), and
   B_(j+1) is least when these errors are 0. Starting from the build of TP1 part 3 at G_0: if the directions can be
   chosen at every level so that (K) holds at every changed group of every step for the children's chosen directions,
   there is an (r) sequence with D2_P(B_j) = Lin(G_j) at every level.
2. (K) holds at S' in each of these cases, for any directions of B_j of the kind above: (a) rank Sigma_c <= k_c for
   every c (every child lost nothing); (b) the images of Sigma_1, ..., Sigma_q and Sigma_(W') are pairwise orthogonal
   and k' <= k_c for every c.
3. (K) is decided from the summaries, the sizes and the children's chosen directions, with no access to N or P. When
   for every group the k_S-th and (k_S + 1)-th largest eigenvalues of its summed matrix differ (or k_S >= r), K_c is the
   span of the eigenvectors for the k_c largest eigenvalues whatever the choice, and (K) is decided from the summaries
   and the sizes alone.
4. In the instance of Proposition TH3, (K) fails at the merge G_1 -> G_2.
Proof. (1) Fix a changed group S' and a list q'_t as in (K), and write q'_t = q^(c)_t + n_(c,t) with q^(c)_t in K_c and
n_(c,t) in ker Sigma_c. Kernel step: Sigma_c is the sum over w in W_(S_c) of Sigma_w, and
n^T Sigma_w n = sum over x in the area of w of p_x (n^T B_w ztil(x))^2 >= 0. If Sigma_c n = 0, the sum over w of the
n^T Sigma_w n is 0, so each is 0 (Lemma `psd_parts_zero`), and with p_x > 0 each n^T B_w ztil(x) is 0 (Lemma
`weighted_sq_zero`). Hence, at every x in the area of every w in W_(S_c),
   (q^(c)_t)^T B_w ztil(x) = (q'_t)^T B_w ztil(x).                                                        (*)
Write q^(c)_t = sum over s of alpha_(c,t,s) q_(c,s), with q_(c,s) the directions of S_c's box, c_(c,s) > 0 their numbers
and p_(c,s)(x) = m_(c,s)^T z_(T(S_c))(x) + beta_(c,s) the pre-activations of its units (zero directions get alpha = 0).
Give S' the new units
   relu(sum over c, s of (alpha_(c,t,s) / c_(c,s)) (p_(c,s)(x) - beta_(c,s)) + sum over w in W' of (B_w^T q'_t)^T z_(T_w)(x) + beta'_t),
t = 1, ..., k', with beta'_t = 1 + max over x in P of the absolute value of the rest (P is finite). Each is
