relu(m''_t^T z_(T(S'))(x) + beta'_t) with m''_t a linear combination of reads on the top units, so it is a unit of a box
of S' (Definition DH3 item 3); it reads only the pre-activations of B_j's units in the children of S' and the z of the
kept children: the step is allowed (DH3 item 5). By the choice of beta'_t each unit is on at every point of P. On the
area of w in W_(S_c), (m''_t|T_w)^T ztil = (q^(c)_t)^T B_w ztil = (q'_t)^T B_w ztil by the TP1 type of S_c's box and
(*); on the area of w in W' this holds by construction. So the box is of TP1 type with directions q'_t and all
c_t = 1. The computation of TP1 part 2 uses only this property, the shelter claims, the free terms and V = (q'_t), an
n_y x k' matrix whose nonzero columns are orthonormal in the image of P_perp; it gives the terms of S' as
(1/2)(E_(W_(S')) - top_(k')(Sigma')) = Lin_(S') (the sum of the k' largest eigenvalues, zero columns adding nothing). A
sibling merge keeps each J_w (DH3 item 5), so the free terms and Pi_w are those of the children. Treat every changed
group the same way, copy B_j's boxes of the unchanged groups (with logit weights V = (q_t / c_t), their terms are
Lin_S by the same computation), and assemble with TH1's upper bound. Then D2_P(B_(j+1)) = sum over the groups of
G_(j+1) of Lin_S = Lin(G_(j+1)). By TP1 part 3, V2_b(G_(j+1)) >= Lin(G_(j+1)) - (1/2) eps_lin(G_(j+1)), which gives the
gap, and equality when the errors are 0. The build is of TP1 type with directions of the kind required, so induction
over the steps gives the last sentence; at G_0 the build of TP1 part 3 is of this type (with no groups it is N).
(2)(a) The positive eigenvalues of Sigma_c number rank Sigma_c <= min(k_c, r), and they are strictly larger than the
others, so every list of eigenvectors for the k_c largest eigenvalues contains a basis of the image of Sigma_c. Then
K_c + ker Sigma_c is the whole space, and any list of directions for Sigma' meets (K). (b) If the images are pairwise
orthogonal, an eigenvector v of Sigma_c for a positive eigenvalue lambda satisfies Sigma_(c'') v = 0 for c'' other than
c and Sigma_(W') v = 0 (v lies in the image of Sigma_c, orthogonal to the image of each other symmetric matrix of the
sum), so Sigma' v = lambda v; the same holds for Sigma_(W'). So the positive eigenvalues of Sigma', with their
multiplicities, are the union of those of the Sigma_c and of Sigma_(W'), with eigenvectors inside one image each, and
the eigenvectors for 0 may be taken in ker Sigma' (the intersection of the ker Sigma_c and of ker Sigma_(W'), each
matrix being positive semidefinite) and in the image of P_perp. Choose the positive part of the list for Sigma' from
these blocks: from block c it takes n_c values, which may be taken to be the n_c largest of Sigma_c (as a multiset),
with n_c <= k' <= k_c. K_c is invariant under Sigma_c and spanned by eigenvectors for the k_c largest eigenvalues of
Sigma_c, so for each value lambda it contains an eigenspace part of dimension equal to the number of times lambda occurs
among them, which is at least the number of times it occurs among the n_c largest. So the vectors from block c can be
chosen orthonormal inside K_c. A vector from block c lies in ker Sigma_(c'') for every other c''; a vector from
Sigma_(W') or from ker Sigma' lies in every ker Sigma_c; zero entries lie everywhere. So (K) holds. (3) K_c is the span
of the children's chosen directions; (K) asks whether an eigenvector list of the n_y x n_y matrix Sigma' can be chosen
in the subspaces K_c + ker Sigma_c: linear algebra on n_y x n_y matrices. With a gap at each cut, K_c is the sum of the
eigenspaces of the k_c largest eigenvalues (or the whole image when k_c >= r), independent of the choice. (4) Sigma_1 =
2 e_a e_a^T + (1/2) e_b e_b^T has the simple eigenvalue 4 on ehat_a, so K_1 is the line of ehat_a for every choice, and
ker Sigma_1 is the line of (1, 1, 1). Sigma' = Sigma_1 + Sigma_2 has the simple eigenvalue 6 on ehat_b, which is
orthogonal to both lines, so it is not in K_1 + ker Sigma_1. QED.
Lean: `psd_parts_zero` and `weighted_sq_zero` in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Netread.lean`, scalar forms of the kernel step;
the transfer of the TP1 type, the eigenvector choices and the assembly are by hand. Check: `model/tl_netread.py`
(part A).
Comment. TL1 is a sufficient condition. An (r) step reads its children through every function of their units'
pre-activations, so it may capture more than K_c when (K) fails (Comment of TP2), and TL1 does not say that (K) is
needed. TH3 shows that the failure of (K) can be strict. (K) can also fail with no reuse: one child, no W', and
k' > k_1 with rank Sigma_1 > k_1 (TH3's area 1 alone, with k_1 = 1 and k' = 2), a merge that grows the size. Part 2(a)
is the essay's crush read on a tree: as long as every child loses nothing, the first lossy merge is reached by the step.
Part 2(b) is "no reuse across siblings". When (K) fails, the summary rule of TP2 part 2 still gives Lin, so a rule may
test (K) per merge and pass up the full summary only where it fails.

**Definition DL1 (on-inside claim) (node R-oninside).** Let v = (l, R) be a node of a tree map, D a set of units of
U(v) and K a set of units of U(v) disjoint from D. The **on-inside claim** (R, D, K) says: every unit of D has a
pre-activation >= 0 at every point of R, and every unit of K has the same value at every point of R. Its error is
   eps_on(R, D, K) = max of the terms e_i,   e_i = (sum over x in R of p_x min(z_i(x), 0)^2) / (sum over x in R of p_x z_i(x)^2)
for i in D (no term when the denominator is 0, that is when z_i = 0 on R), and
   e_k = (sum over x, x' in R of p_x p_x' (h_k(x) - h_k(x'))^2) / (sum over x, x' in P of p_x p_x' (h_k(x) - h_k(x'))^2)
for k in K (no term when h_k is constant on P). It is rational, computable in time polynomial in the size of N, P
and the claim, and 0 exactly when the claim holds (every p_x > 0). It is unchanged by the rescaling of Fact F1 (a
rescaled unit multiplies its numerator and denominator by c^2) and by copies as in Definition DN1 (a copy has the
same term, and the error is a largest term). It names an area and two sets of units and refers to no build, size or
zoom. Source: the essay's gate ("a neuron in front of them acts as a gate ... its negative side keeps the dogs out")
supports the K part: the gate is flat on the area it opens. The D part (behind the gate, inside the area, the area's
units do not switch) is my reading.
Comment. With D = U(v) minus K and K the units of a judgment claim of v, the claim says that inside R the layer is a
linear map of its inputs and the gate sends a constant. Hypothesis H-flatgate (node R-flatgate) asks the K part for a
gate in front of a family; DL1 asks it as a claim with an error, for any node.

**Theorem TL2 (a lift through units that are on re-expresses every finer unit) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a
tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** Let G_j and G_(j+1) be
consecutive levels of a zoom of tree groupings, both meeting premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1, such that G_(j+1)
changes one group S', with parent u' and nodes W_(S') with kept judgment units J'_w. Suppose:
1. (one layer) every group of G_j inside S' has its parent in {u'} or in W_(S');
2. (no loose units) every unit of S' in a layer after l(u') + 1 lies, at G_j, in a group of G_j or in a set J_w of
   such a group;
3. (on inside) for every u in W_(S') that is the parent of a group of G_j, M holds the on-inside claim
   (area of u, U(u) minus J'_u, J'_u) with eps = 0;
4. (size) k_(S') >= n_j(S'), where n_j(S') counts the box units of the groups of G_j inside S', the units of their sets
   J_w that are not in a set J'_w of S', and, when l(u') + 1 = L, the kept units of G_j that lie in S'.
Then for every class (b) build B at G_j there is a class (b) build B' at G_(j+1) with y_(B')(x) = y_B(x) at every
point of P. Hence V_b(G_(j+1)) <= V_b(G_j) and V2_b(G_(j+1)) <= V2_b(G_j), and by TH1 part 2,
L_(S') <= sum over the groups S of G_j inside S' of L_S (and the same for L2).
Proof. By Lemma TH0 part 2 at both levels (branch claims at eps = 0), every kept unit of B and of B' takes its value
in N at every point of P, and every box reads N's pre-activations of its top. For u in W_(S') whose area R_u is not P,
premise 2 of TH1 at G_(j+1) gives the judgment claim (R_u, J'_u, a_u) with eps = 0: the sum over k in J'_u of
(a_u)_k h_k is 1 on R_u, and these units are 0 outside R_u (district claims), so this sum is the indicator of R_u on P.
B' is B with the units of S' and the copy units of S''s replaced units removed, a box of S' of size k_(S') carried to
layer L by copy units, and the copies of the units of J'_w (DH3 item 4). The units of B that S' replaces are listed by
kind; by premises 1 and 2 these are all of them.
(A) A box unit of a group S of G_j with parent u'. It is relu(m^T z_(T(S)) + beta) with T(S) inside T(S'), so it is a
unit of a box of S' (zero read on the rest of T(S')), and it has the same values. A unit i of a set J_w of such a group
that is not in J'_w lies in U(w) minus J'_w, inside T(S'), and is relu(e_i^T z_(T(S'))): also a unit of a box of S'.
(B) A box unit f = relu(m^T z_(T(S)) + beta) of a group S of G_j with parent u in W_(S'), placed in layer l(u') + 2.
At a point x of R_u, the units of layer l(u) = l(u') + 1 outside U(u) are off (Lemma TH0 part 1), so
z_(T(S))(x) = W_D h_D(x) + W_K h_K(x) + b, with D = U(u) minus J'_u, K = J'_u, and W, b N's rows of T(S). The
on-inside claim gives h_D = relu(z_D) = z_D on R_u and h_K = kappa, a constant vector, on R_u. So on R_u,
   f(x) = relu(mhat^T z_D(x) + betahat),   mhat = W_D^T m,   betahat = beta + m^T (W_K kappa + b)          (**)
(the scalar form is Lemma `relu_push_down`). Let g(x) = relu(mhat^T z_D(x) + betahat) at every x in P. Since D lies in
T(S'), g is a unit of a box of S', placed in layer l(u') + 1. Off R_u: the units of T(S) lie in districts with regions
inside R_u, so their shelter claims (TH1 premise 2 at G_j) make z_(T(S)) constant off R_u and f is a constant c_0
there; the units of D lie in districts with region R_u, so their shelter claims (TH1 premise 2 at G_(j+1)) make z_D
constant off R_u and g is a constant c_1 there. If R_u = P, f = g on P. Otherwise f = g + (c_0 - c_1)(1 - sum over k in
J'_u of (a_u)_k h_k) on P (Lemma `lift_compensate`).
(C) A unit k of a set J_w of such a group S, not in a set J'_w of S', placed in layer l(u') + 2: it is relu(N's row of
k applied to layer l(u) plus its bias), the same form as (B) with m a unit vector, so the same argument gives a box unit
g_k of S' with h_k = g_k + (c_0 - c_1)(1 - sum (a_u)_k h_k) on P, here c_0 = 0 (k is off outside R_u by its district
claim).
(D) When l(u') + 1 = L, a kept unit i of G_j in S': it is relu(e_i^T z_(T(S'))), a box unit of S'. When
l(u') + 1 < L, a kept unit of layer l(u') + 1 in S' (in U(u) minus J'_u for some u in W_(S')) is read in N only by
units of sub(u) minus J'_u (the branch claim (sub(u) minus J'_u) of S' at G_(j+1)), all of which are of kind (B) or (C)
at G_j by premise 2, so B reads it only through those units, and B' needs no unit for it.
In B, the units of kinds (B) and (C) are read only by their copy units (DH3 item 4: kept units have no weight from box
or copy units), and the kept units of kind (A) in sets J_w are read by no hidden unit outside sub(w) minus J'_w (branch
claim of S' at G_(j+1)), whose units are all replaced. So in B every replaced unit reaches the logits only through its
copies. By premise 4 the replacements fit in a box of S' of size k_(S'); give any further units logit weight 0.
Logits of B': for each replaced unit, the logit weight B gives its copy goes to the copy of its replacement; the terms
(c_0 - c_1) of (B) and (C) are carried by the copies of the units of J'_u and by the bias. The units of B outside S' and
their readers are unchanged. So y_(B') = y_B on P. Taking B near the infimum gives the inequalities for V_b and V2_b.
The group inequality follows from TH1 part 2 applied to the set {S'} at G_(j+1) and the set of groups inside S' at
G_j: the kept units of G_j in S' add no term to V_b of a set of groups at G_j, since by TH0 they match N. QED.
Lean: `relu_push_down` (a one-row scalar form of (**)) and `lift_compensate` (the constant off the area) in
`lean/coarse/Coarse/Netread.lean`; the matrix form of (**) and the bookkeeping of kinds (A) to (D) by hand. Check:
`model/tl_netread.py` (part B).
Comment. Under its premises (one-layer lift, no loose units, on-inside claims, and k_(S') >= n_j(S')), TL2 says a lift
does not raise the least loss: on P the finer class is contained in the coarser class. So "lifts do not nest"
(TH2 part 2) is what a lift does when the size has room. The content is a rewriting: relu(z) = z where z >= 0, and a
function constant off an area is fixed by the area's indicator. It also shows that the box class of Definition DH3
grows when a lift moves the box to an earlier layer, so a coarser level can use a route that N never uses (x_2 in
TH2 part 2); that is a property of the box definition, not of N (card 3-24, option (b), and node R-deep are where that
definition is decided). The depth step of the one recursion (zoom and depth as one idea) is then "move each unit one
layer down", exact where the layer it passes is linear in its area. What a lift costs comes only from k_(S') <
n_j(S'): the lifted box must choose, and inside the area of u it must also make the switching between the children's
areas that the children's judgment units did. That is where the one-node problem of Proposition T57 can sit; TL2 says
nothing about it.

**Corollary TL2.1 (the instance of Proposition TH2 part 2) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree
groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** In the instance of TH2 part 2, with the
on-inside claims (P, {g}, empty set) and (P, {a_1, a_2}, empty set) added to its map, the steps G_1 -> G_2 and
G_2 -> G_3 meet the premises of TL2, so V_b(G_3) <= V_b(G_2) <= V_b(G_1). TH2 part 2 proves V_b(G_3) = 0 and
V_b(G_1), V_b(G_2) > 0; the inequality V_b(G_2) <= V_b(G_1) is new.
Proof. Every area is P, so no judgment claim is needed. Step G_1 -> G_2: S' = sub(v_2) with parent v_1 and node v_2,
top {g}; the group of G_1 (sub(v_3), parent v_2) has its parent in W_(S'); the units of S' after layer 2 are f_1, f_2,
f_3, all in that group; the units passed are U(v_2) = {g}, whose pre-activation a_1 = x_1 takes the values 1, 2, 3, 4
on P, so the on-inside claim (P, {g}, empty set) has eps = 0; n_1(S') = 1 = k. Step G_2 -> G_3: S' = sub(v_1), parent
the root, top {a_1, a_2}; the group of G_2 (sub(v_2), parent v_1) has its parent in W_(S'); the units of S' after
layer 1 are g, f_1, f_2, f_3, all in that group; the units passed are a_1, a_2, with pre-activations x_1 in
{1, 2, 3, 4} and x_2 in {0, 1}, both >= 0; n_2(S') = 1 = k. TL2 gives the inequalities. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (a reading of TL2 on the instance). Check: `model/tl_netread.py` (part B).
Comment. In fact V_b(G_1) = V_b(G_2): in both classes the gap of a build is a relu(mu g + nu) + gamma on P (proof of
TH2 part 2), so the two infima are the same.

### B.L.2 Deep layers: a clean subtree is affine in its top, the least of every level is a closed form, and a bound with errors (added 2026-10-29, later)

Shonu (2026-10-29): "continue until you can find the theorem which finds the optimal small network for deep layer
cases". Theorem TL2 left one case open: a lift with fewer box units than the finer level, where the box must also make
the switching between the children's areas. This section shows when a box has no switching to make, and what it costs
when it nearly has none. Inside its area a unit that is on acts as the identity, and a gate that is flat on its area
and sheltered off it has a vote that is an affine function of the layer above. So a subtree whose claims hold is affine
in its top pre-activations, and Theorems TP1 and TP2 give the least of every level in closed form, at any depth.
1. Theorem TL3: under district, shelter, on-inside and judgment claims at eps = 0 in a subtree, the logits on the
   subtree's area are affine in its top pre-activations, and so is the indicator of every area below. Corollary TL3.1:
   the linear-read error is 0. Corollary TL3.2: what this forces: every split below the top is a flat 0/1 direction of
   the top layer, so the top layer must already carry the area code of every finer gate; for points in general
   position no split is possible once the area has more than twice as many points as the top has units.
2. Proposition TL4: at a lift, the parent's table is the sum of its children's tables plus one between table, made
   from the children's masses and mean outputs (the votes of the gates the lift swallows).
3. Corollary TL5: for every grouping of a zoom of tree groupings whose nodes meet TL3's premises (merges and lifts, any
   depth), the least D2 is (1/2)(E - top_k(Sigma)) per group, reached by units that are on everywhere; the tables come
   from the deepest nodes' tables and means, the nodes' masses and c_N by two rules (merge: add; lift: add and a
   between table). Its scope is TL3's: subtrees with no switching below the top except along flat 0/1 directions of
   the top layer; for points in general position, linear subtrees (TL3.2).
4. Theorem TL6: with errors, the linear-read error of a subtree is at most a constant times the square of a sum of
   absolute defects, built layer by layer from N's weights, the shelter values and the gates' margins. When the claims
   that TP1 needs are at eps = 0 and only on-inside claims and the shelter claims below the groups' tops have errors,
   this bounds the gap of the closed form (with summaries computed from N) to the least. The table recursion of TL4
   has no error bound yet.
Status: every item uses nodes R-tree, R-branch (judgment claims in hidden layers, Definition DH2 part 2), S-plainff
(card 3-24) and R-oninside (card 3-27); TL3.1, TL5 and TL6 also R-linread (card 3-26); TL5 also R-obj; all PENDING: a
side branch.

**Theorem TL3 (inside its area, a clean subtree is affine in its top) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map,
on-inside claims, judgment claims in hidden layers, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** Let M be a tree map and w = (l, R_w) a node. For a node v write
J_v for the set of units of v's judgment claim (Definition DH2 part 2) when M holds one, and J_v = empty set otherwise,
and T_w = U(w) minus J_w. Suppose M holds, with eps = 0:
1. every district claim;
2. a shelter claim for every district of layers l + 1 to L whose units lie in sub(w);
3. for every node v at or below w, the on-inside claim (R_v, U(v) minus J_v, J_v);
4. for every node v below w whose area is not the area of its parent, a judgment claim (R_v, J_v, a_v).
Then at every point of R_w: (i) the indicator of the area of every node at or below w, and the value of every unit of
every such node, are affine functions of z_(T_w); (ii) y_N is an affine function of z_(T_w).
Proof. By Lemma TH0 part 1 (district claims), at a point of R_w every unit of layer l outside U(w) is off, and every
unit of a later layer outside sub(w) is off. So on R_w the units that can be on lie in nodes at or below w, and it is
enough to prove (i) for them, layer by layer.
Layer l. The only node of layer l at or below w is w. Its area's indicator is 1 on R_w. Its units in T_w have
pre-activation >= 0 on R_w (on-inside claim), so their values equal z_(T_w). Its units in J_w are constant on R_w
(on-inside claim, K part).
Step from layer l' to layer l' + 1 (l <= l' < L). Assume (i) for the nodes of layer l' at or below w. Let v be a node of
layer l' + 1 below w, with parent v' (a node of layer l' at or below w), and let i be a unit of U(v). On R_w the units of
layer l' that are on lie in nodes at or below w, so the pre-activation z_i = sum over j of W_ij h_j + b_i is affine
in z_(T_w) on R_w. The indicator of R_v: if R_v = R_(v'), it is the indicator of R_(v'), affine by assumption.
Otherwise premise 4 gives the judgment claim (R_v, J_v, a_v): sum over k in J_v of (a_v)_k h_k = 1 on R_v. By the
on-inside claim each h_k is a constant kappa_k on R_v, so sum (a_v)_k kappa_k = 1 and some kappa_k is not 0, hence > 0.
For that unit, relu(z_k) = kappa_k > 0 on R_v gives z_k = kappa_k on R_v; off R_v (at points of P, a non-empty set since
R_v lies strictly inside R_(v')) h_k = 0 by its district claim (region R_v), so z_k <= 0, and z_k is a constant zeta_k
there by its shelter claim. So, on P, the indicator of R_v is (z_k - zeta_k) / (kappa_k - zeta_k) (Lemma
`gate_indicator`), affine in z_(T_w) on R_w. Values: a unit i of U(v) minus J_v has z_i >= 0 on R_v (on-inside claim)
and, off R_v, h_i = 0 (district claim) and z_i = zeta_i <= 0 (shelter claim), so h_i = z_i - zeta_i (1 - indicator of
R_v) at every point of P (Lemma `relu_sheltered`), affine on R_w. A unit k of J_v is kappa_k on R_v and 0 off it, so
h_k = kappa_k times the indicator of R_v. This is (i) for layer l' + 1.
(ii) y_N = W_out h_L + c_N, and on R_w the units of layer L that can be on lie in nodes at or below w (for l = L, in
U(w)), so y_N is affine in z_(T_w) on R_w by (i). QED.
Lean: `gate_indicator` and `relu_sheltered` (the two scalar steps) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Netread.lean`; the induction
over layers by hand. Check: `model/tl_deep.py` (part A).

**Corollary TL3.1 (the linear-read error of a clean subtree is 0) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map,
on-inside claims, judgment claims in hidden layers, linear-read claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** In the setting of TL3, the linear-read claim
(R_w, J_w) of Definition DP1 has eps_lin(w) = 0.
Proof. Ytil = Pi_w P_perp y_N, and F_w contains the constants and the h_j, j in J_w. By TL3 (ii), y_N = G z_(T_w) + g on
R_w, so Ytil = P_perp G ztil (Pi_w acts coordinate by coordinate and is linear). So B = P_perp G fits with residual 0,
the least-squares residual r_w is 0, and eps_lin(w) = 0. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (one line of least squares).

**Corollary TL3.2 (what TL3's premises force) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, on-inside claims,
judgment claims in hidden layers, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** In the setting of TL3:
1. for every node v below w with R_v not R_w, the indicator of R_v is an affine function of z_(T_w) on R_w that takes
   only the values 0 and 1, so the points z_(T_w)(x), x in R_w, lie on two parallel hyperplanes, one for R_v and one
   for the rest; every unit of every node below w is constant on P minus its area;
2. if for no d + 1 distinct points x of R_w do the z_(T_w)(x) lie on one hyperplane of R^d (d = |T_w|), and
   |R_w| > 2d, then every node below w has area R_w, every unit below w outside the sets J_v has h = z on R_w, every
   unit of a set J_v below w is constant on R_w, and sub(w) acts on R_w as a stack of affine maps.
Proof. (1) TL3 (i) for the indicator; the units by their shelter and district claims. (2) A split below w gives, by (1),
an affine function that is 0 on a non-empty part of R_w and 1 on the rest; each of the two level sets is a hyperplane
and holds the images of at most d distinct points of R_w, so |R_w| <= 2d. If no node below w splits, every area below
w is R_w (an area that is a proper part of R_w has an ancestor that splits), and the on-inside claims give h = z for
the units outside the J_v and constant values for the units of the J_v. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (counting points on two hyperplanes).
Comment. TL3 covers subtrees in which every switching below the top is already decided by flat directions of the top
layer: each finer gate reads an area code that the top layer carries with one value inside the area and another
outside. That is the essay's "earlier gates coarse" taken literally (a coarse layer holds the decisions that later
layers use). In `model/tl_deep.py` the top layer carries such codes (carrier units, one per finer area). For points
in general position, part 2 says the premises leave no split below the top: then all switching sits at or above the
group's top, and TL5 is reduced-rank regression of a linear subtree (Izenman 1975, literature table). My reading: in
trained networks gates read features that vary inside the area (a question for Part C); for such gates the claims
have errors and Theorem TL6 applies. The instances that are
hard or lossy break a premise: in the zigzag of TH2 part 2 the units f_i switch inside the one area P, and no tree map
with district claims at eps = 0 gives them areas on which they stay on (f_1 is on at g = 2, 3, 4, so its region contains
these points; f_3 has a negative pre-activation at g = 2, so a region on which it stays on lies inside g = 3, 4 and
contains g = 4; the two regions are neither equal nor disjoint). In T43 (one hidden layer, where TL3's premise 2 is
empty) what fails is TH1's shelter premise on the group's top, which TL5 needs: the detectors' pre-activations vary off
their single-point regions.

**Proposition TL4 (summaries pass through a lift) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, on-inside claims,
judgment claims in hidden layers, linear-read claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** Let u be a node of layer l < L whose premises in Theorem TL3
hold, and let w_1, ..., w_q be its children (the nodes of layer l + 1 with area inside R_u). Each child meets TL3's
premises (they are among u's). For every node v, Sigma_v and E_v are those of Definition DP2 with the set J_v of TL3.
Let R_0 be the set of points of R_u in no child's area. For c = 1, ..., q (and c = 0 when R_0 is not empty) let
P_c = sum over x in R_(w_c) (in R_0) of p_x, ybar_c = (1/P_c) sum of p_x P_perp y_N(x) over that set, and ybar_u the
same mean over R_u. Then y_N = c_N on R_0, and
   Sigma_u = Sigma_(w_1) + ... + Sigma_(w_q) + Gamma_u,   E_u = E_(w_1) + ... + E_(w_q) + tr Gamma_u,
   Gamma_u = sum over c (from 0 when R_0 is not empty, else from 1) of P_c (ybar_c - ybar_u)(ybar_c - ybar_u)^T.
Proof. By Corollary TL3.1, eps_lin is 0 at u and at every child. By the Comment of DP2, K_v = Sigma_v + Rres_v with
Rres_v = sum p_x r_v r_v^T positive semidefinite and tr Rres_v = eps_lin(v) = 0, so Rres_v = 0 and Sigma_v = K_v =
sum over x in R_v of p_x Ytil_v Ytil_v^T, with E_v = tr Sigma_v. The units of J_v are constant on R_v (on-inside
claim), so F_v is the constants on R_v and Ytil_v = P_perp y_N - ybar_v there (for v = u and for each child). The
children's areas are pairwise disjoint (regions of one layer) and inside R_u, and every region of layer l + 1 lies
inside one region of layer l (Definition DH1 item 2), so R_u is the disjoint union of the children's areas and R_0. On
R_0 every unit of a layer after l is off: units outside sub(u) by Lemma TH0 part 1, and units inside sub(u) by their
district claims (their regions lie inside children's areas). So y_N = c_N on R_0, and its part on R_0 adds only the
c = 0 term. For each vector e, applying Lemma `within_between` to the numbers e^T P_perp y_N(x) on each of these sets,
with the point e^T ybar_u, and summing over the sets gives e^T K_u e = sum over c of e^T K_(w_c) e + e^T Gamma_u e (on
R_0 the within part is 0). Two symmetric matrices with the same quadratic form are equal. Traces give E_u. QED.
Lean: `within_between` (the scalar split for one set) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Netread.lean`; the sum over the sets and
polarisation by hand. Check: `model/tl_deep.py` (part B).
Comment. TL4 is the law of total variance (literature table) applied to the children's areas. Gamma_u is the table of
the children's votes: how far the mean output of each child's area is from the parent's mean. Below the lift those
votes were free (each child's judgment units carried them); after the lift the box carries them, with units that are
on everywhere, since by TL3 the children's indicators are affine in the parent's top pre-activations. The recursion's
input is: the tables (E_v, Sigma_v) and the means ybar_v (vectors in the image of P_perp) of the nodes of layer L, the
mass P_v of every node, and c_N. A node of a layer
below L with no children has Sigma_v = 0, E_v = 0 and ybar_v = P_perp c_N. Each ybar_u is then
(sum over c of P_c ybar_c + P_0 P_perp c_N) / P_u with P_0 = P_u - sum of the P_c.

**Corollary TL5 (the least small network at every grouping of a deep zoom) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a
tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0, the
objective D2_P).** Let G be a tree grouping that meets premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1, with each kept judgment set J_w
equal to the set of w's judgment claim (empty when there is none), and such that every node w in W_S of every group S
meets the premises of Theorem TL3. Then:
1. (The least, in closed form.) V2_b(G) = sum over the groups S of G of (1/2)(E_(W_S) - top_(k_S)(Sigma_(W_S))), and the
   build of TP1 part 3 attains it: for each group, k_S units on at every point of P with reads (B_w^T q_t on T_w, for w
   in W_S) on the group's top pre-activations, and logit weights q_t, the orthonormal eigenvectors of Sigma_(W_S) for
   its k_S largest eigenvalues (zero after n_y - 1). No class (b) build at G, of any shape, does better.
2. (One recursion.) For a zoom of tree groupings each of whose levels meets these premises, the tables Sigma_(W_S),
   E_(W_S) of every level come from the input of the Comment of TL4 (the tables and means of the nodes of layer L, the
   masses of the nodes, and c_N) by two rules: a sibling merge adds the tables of its nodes (TP2 part 1); a node's own table is
   given by TL4 from its children's, applied at every node of layers L - 1 down to the layer of the group's nodes. So
   the value and the box directions of every level need no access to N or P once this input is known (TP3 part 2); the
   box weights read the build records B_w of the nodes in W_S, made in the one-time pass from N.
3. (Nesting and switching.) For one group, the box for size k is the first k units of the box for any larger size, and
   a switch to a level selects stored weights (TP3 parts 4 and 5).
4. (KL.) The build of part 1 has D_P <= (1/2) V2_b(G) (Fact F11, as in the Remark (KL) of B.P).
Proof. (1) Corollary TL3.1 gives eps_lin = 0 for every node w in W_S; Theorem TP1 part 3 gives L2_S = Lin_S; TP1 part 1
(any box, of any shape: its outputs lie in a subspace of dimension at most k_S) and TH1 part 1 give the least. (2) TP2
part 1 for sibling merges; TL4 and the Comment of TL4 for the tables of single nodes, by induction from layer L. TP2
part 2 and TP3 part 2 for the cost. (3) TP3 parts 4 and 5. (4) F11 at every point, and V2_b(G) = D2_P of the build of
part 1. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (a composition of TL3.1, TL4, TP1, TP2, TP3 and TH1). Check: `model/tl_deep.py` (parts C and D).
Comment. Part 1 is the last sentence of TP2 part 2 with TL3 supplying its premise; the new content is part 2, the
table rule for lifts. What the network says about the optimum (my reading): a coarse neuron of any level is one unit
that stays on over its group's whole area, reads the group's top neurons along one linear read, and writes one output
direction (the union of a branch, as in the essay's "curves & loops" neuron). The finer gates it swallows are not
lost: their votes enter Gamma, and the coarse neuron carries them linearly. TL5 covers subtrees that are affine in
their top on their area (Corollary TL3.2); with errors, Theorem TL6.

**Theorem TL6 (the linear-read error of a subtree, with errors in its claims) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a
tree map, linear-read claims).** Let M be a tree map and w = (l, R_w) a node. For every node v at or below w let J_v be
a set of units of U(v) (for example the set of v's judgment claim), and T_w = U(w) minus J_w. For every node v below w
whose area is not its parent's, let k_v be a unit of J_v with kappahat_(k_v) > 0 and kappahat_(k_v) > zetahat_(k_v)
(defined below). For a function f on R_w (real or vector valued) write ||f|| = (sum over x in R_w of p_x |f(x)|^2)^(1/2).
For each unit define its constants and absolute defects (all sums over points of R_w):
1. a unit i of a node v at or below w, not in J_v: zetahat_i = the p-mean of z_i over R_w minus R_v (0 if that set is
   empty); d_i = ||min(z_i, 0) on R_v|| + ||h_i on R_w minus R_v|| + ||(z_i - zetahat_i) on R_w minus R_v||;
2. a unit k of J_v for a node v below w: kappahat_k = the p-mean of h_k over R_v, zetahat_k as in item 1;
   d_k = ||(h_k - kappahat_k) on R_v|| + ||h_k on R_w minus R_v||; a unit of J_w has d = 0;
3. a unit j of a layer >= l in no node at or below w: d_j = ||h_j||.
For each such node v put alpha_v = 1 / (kappahat_(k_v) - zetahat_(k_v)) (the inverse of the gate's margin) and
g_v = ||(kappahat - h) on R_v|| + ||min(z, 0) on R_v|| + ||(z - zetahat) on R_w minus R_v||, all for the unit k_v. Let
c_v be the vector of the numbers |zetahat_i| (i in U(v) minus J_v) and kappahat_k (k in J_v). Let ||W_(l'+1)|| be the
operator norm of N's weight matrix from layer l' to layer l' + 1, and Delta_(l') the Euclidean norm of the vector of the
d's of the units of layer l'. Define, for l' = l, ..., L - 1,
   eps_l = Delta_l,   eps_(l'+1) = Delta_(l'+1) + ||W_(l'+1)|| eps_(l') + sum over nodes v of layer l' + 1 below w of |c_v| eta_v,
   eta_v = eta_(v') if R_v is the area of v's parent v' (eta_w = 0), and eta_v = alpha_v (g_v + ||W_(l'+1)|| eps_(l')) otherwise.
Then eps_lin(w) <= |P_perp W_out|^2 eps_L^2 (operator norm), for every choice of the units k_v, so the least over the
choices bounds it too. When the premises of Theorem TL3 hold at eps = 0 with these sets J_v, a unit k_v as required
exists (by the proof of TL3, some unit of J_v has kappa_k > 0 >= zeta_k), and for it, and for every unit, every d and
every g is 0, so eps_L = 0, in agreement with Corollary TL3.1.
Proof. Build an affine stand-in hhat, layer by layer, on R_w. Layer l: hhat_i = z_i for i in T_w, hhat_k = h_k for k in
J_w, and hhat_j = 0 for the other units of layer l. Layer l' + 1: zhat = W_(l'+1) hhat_(l') + b; for a node v below w,
iotahat_v = iotahat_(v') when R_v = R_(v') (iotahat_w = 1), and otherwise iotahat_v = (zhat_(k_v) - zetahat_(k_v))
alpha_v; hhat_i = zhat_i - zetahat_i (1 - iotahat_v) for i in U(v) minus J_v, hhat_k = kappahat_k iotahat_v for k in J_v,
and hhat_j = 0 for units in no node at or below w. Each step is a linear map plus a constant, or a constant times an
affine function, so every hhat is an affine function of (z_(T_w), h_(J_w)) on R_w. Let e_(l') = h_(l') - hhat_(l') on R_w,
and write iota_v for the indicator of R_v (equal to 1 on R_w for v = w). Layer l: e_i = -min(z_i, 0) for i in T_w, 0 for
k in J_w, h_j for the others, so ||e_l|| <= Delta_l = eps_l. Step: z - zhat = W_(l'+1) e_(l') pointwise, so
||z - zhat|| <= ||W_(l'+1)|| ||e_(l')||. For a gate (Lemma `gate_err_identity`), (kappahat - zetahat)(iota_v - iotahat_v)
= ((kappahat - zetahat) iota_v - z_(k_v) + zetahat) + (z_(k_v) - zhat_(k_v)); the first bracket is kappahat - z =
(kappahat - h) - min(z, 0) on R_v and zetahat - z on R_w minus R_v (not empty, since R_v lies strictly inside its
parent's area, which lies inside R_w), so ||iota_v - iotahat_v|| <= alpha_v (g_v + ||W_(l'+1)|| ||e_(l')||), and when
R_v = R_(v') the error function is the parent's. For a unit i of U(v) minus J_v (Lemma `unit_err_identity`),
h_i - hhat_i = (h_i - z_i + zetahat_i (1 - iota_v)) + (z_i - zhat_i) + zetahat_i (iota_v - iotahat_v); the first bracket
is -min(z_i, 0) on R_v and h_i - (z_i - zetahat_i) off it, of norm at most d_i. For k in J_v, h_k - hhat_k =
(h_k - kappahat_k iota_v) + kappahat_k (iota_v - iotahat_v), whose first part has norm at most d_k. Units in no node at
or below w have error h_j. Collecting the units of layer l' + 1 by the triangle inequality, ||e_(l'+1)|| <=
Delta_(l'+1) + ||W_(l'+1)|| ||e_(l')|| + sum over v of |c_v| ||iota_v - iotahat_v||, so ||e_(l')|| <= eps_(l') and
||iota_v - iotahat_v|| <= eta_v by induction. Finally y_N = W_out h_L + c_N, and Yhat = P_perp (W_out hhat_L + c_N) is
affine in (z_(T_w), h_(J_w)) on R_w; F_w contains the constants and the h_j, j in J_w, so Pi_w Yhat is linear in ztil.
Least squares is at most any linear fit, and Pi_w does not increase the energy, so eps_lin(w) <= sum over R_w of
p_x |Ytil - Pi_w Yhat|^2 = ||Pi_w (P_perp y_N - Yhat)||^2 <= ||P_perp W_out e_L||^2 <= |P_perp W_out|^2 eps_L^2. QED.
Lean: `gate_err_identity` and `unit_err_identity` (the two error identities) in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Netread.lean`; the
triangle inequalities and the induction by hand. Check: `model/tl_deep.py` (part E).
Comment. TL6 bounds the linear-read error of one node, computed from N; it uses no claim and holds for every N, tree
map and choice of sets. It bounds the gap to the least only where Theorem TP1 applies: when the district claims, the
branch claims, the shelter claims of the groups' tops and the groups' own judgment claims are at eps = 0, and only
on-inside claims and shelter claims of districts below the tops have errors (then TL6's district defects vanish), TP1
part 3 with the summaries of DP2 computed from N puts the closed-form build within (1/2) sum over the groups and their
nodes of |P_perp W_out|^2 eps_L(w)^2 of the least. The table recursion of TL4 is proved at eps = 0 only and has no error
bound yet. The bound reads as the network: an error enters at a unit and is carried up by the weight norms, and a gate
with a small margin kappahat - zetahat multiplies the errors that reach it by alpha_v (a weak gate amplifies, as in
Proposition TM4). The defects are absolute, not the normalised errors of Definitions DM2, DM3 and DL1: with normalised
errors alone no bound holds (with L = 1, units relu(x) and relu(x + 1), logits (h_1 - h_2, 0) and the three points -1,
1, K with weights p, (1 - p)/2, (1 - p)/2, the only normalised error tends to 0 as K grows while eps_lin / E_w tends to
1/(1 + p); referee report REFEREE-BL2-2026-10-29.md). So the bound depends on N and P through the weight norms, the
shelter values and the margins; it is not T5's graded clause, which asks for a bound in the claims' errors alone.

## B.I The least KL loss: the information table, the exact cases, and the open case (added 2026-10-31)

Shonu (2026-10-31), on card 3-30: "refit everything, but specifically to find the optimal KL ... for everything,
including deep networks". Node R-obj is DROPPED: the trunk's objective D_P is the only target, and every result
reached through D2_P stays as a record, labelled OPT-D2. Theorem TH1 (and TY4 for networks with skips) already
splits the least KL loss V_b(G) into one local problem L_S per group, exactly (label EQ). This Part works on L_S
itself, for KL.
1. Definition DI1: the information table of a node: its mass, its mean softmax, and its information I_w (the
   weighted KL from N's softmax to the area's mean softmax).
2. Lemma TI0 and Theorem TI1 (label OPT-KL): a group replaced by nothing has KL least = the sum of its nodes'
   information, at any depth, in closed form. The table passes up the tree: a sibling merge adds, and a lift adds
   the children's information plus one KL term per child (the chain rule of KL). It needs no linear-read claim.
3. Theorem TI2 and Corollary TI2.1 (label OPT-KL): a group with at least as many units as the rank of its D2 table
   has KL least at most a quarter of its linear-read error, and TP1's box comes within that of it. So a level whose
   groups are each dropped or fully kept (node S-keepdrop) is least in closed form, with every claim other than the
   linear-read claims at eps = 0 and a gap of at most a quarter of the linear-read errors, exact when they are 0,
   even where the least is > 0. Only the linear-read errors are graded (TH1 has no graded form).
4. Theorem TI3: every KL least matches N's mean softmax on every area. Among boxes on throughout their areas, the
   least is a least over k-dimensional output spans of convex problems, and it is attained.
5. Theorem TI4: when the variation inside the areas is small (scale a), the KL least is a^2 times the D2 problem
   in each area's Fisher metric, plus O(a^3). With one mean softmax it is the eigenvalue tail of the Fisher-whitened
   table. D2's directions are KL's to this order when that mean softmax is uniform, and need not be otherwise
   (Proposition TI5 part 2).
6. Proposition TI5: the D2 summaries (E, Sigma), even with the area means, do not fix the KL least.
7. Conjectures DI1 and DI2 (Part D.17): for 0 < k_S < rank Sigma the KL least of a clean group is NP-hard, and a
   least box may have to switch inside its area (a computed candidate), unlike D2.
What B.I does not do, said plainly: for a group with 0 < k_S < rank Sigma_(W_S) units it gives no closed form of
the KL least. TP1's eigenvector closed form is the least of D2 there, not of KL (TY5, TI5), and no KL closed form
is known (TI3 reduces it to a non-convex least over output spans). That case holds most real coarsening (many
units into few). It is open: Conjecture DI1 and card 3-31 (2026-11-02: Theorem TQ23 proves DI1, so no polynomial closed form exists in general unless P = NP). TH1 has no graded form, so TI1 is exact only.
Status: every item uses nodes R-tree, R-branch, S-plainff (card 3-24); TI1, TI2.1, TI3's Remark, TI4, TI5, DI1 and
DI2 also R-oninside (card 3-27); TI2, TI2.1, TI3's Remark, TI4, TI5, DI1 and DI2 also R-linread (card 3-26); TI2.1 also
S-keepdrop (card 3-31); all PENDING: a side branch. For networks with skips and channel units (S-skipff), Lemma TI0
and Theorem TI1 parts 2 to 4 carry over through TY4 (its part 1 gives y_N = c_N on R_0 there too); the items that use
the claims of DL1 and DP1 have no statement there yet, since those claims are not defined for channel units with
positions.

**Definition DI1 (information table).** Write s_x = softmax(y_N(x)). For a set R of points of P with mass
m_R = sum over x in R of p_x > 0 let
   sbar_R = (1 / m_R) sum over x in R of p_x s_x,   I(R) = sum over x in R of p_x KL(s_x || sbar_R).
The **information table** of a node w of a tree map is (m_w, sbar_w, I_w) with R the area of w. sbar_R has full
support (each s_x has). I(R) >= 0, with equality exactly when s is constant on R (Gibbs). The table reads only N's
outputs on P: it is unchanged by the rescaling of Fact F1 and by copies (Definition DN1), and it refers to no build,
size or zoom. It is not a claim (it has no error): it is a summary, as in Definition DP2. It takes O(|R| n_y)
operations and n_y logarithms per point. Unlike DP2's summaries it is not rational in general.
Comment. I(R) / m_R is the mutual information between the point (drawn from p / m_R on R) and the class (drawn
from s_x): the information about the class that the position inside R carries; I(R) is m_R times it. It plays the
role of E_w in DP2: (1/2) E_w is the D2 least at k = 0 for any J_w, while I_w is the KL least at k = 0 only when the
kept judgment units are flat on the area (TI1 part 1).

**Lemma TI0 (the chain rule of KL over a partition) (under: none).** Let R be a set of points with m_R > 0.
1. For every probability vector q of full support,
   sum over x in R of p_x KL(s_x || q) = I(R) + m_R KL(sbar_R || q).
2. If R is the disjoint union of sets R_1, ..., R_q, each of mass m_c > 0, with means sbar_c, then
   I(R) = sum over c of I(R_c) + sum over c of m_c KL(sbar_c || sbar_R),   sbar_R = (1 / m_R) sum over c of m_c sbar_c.
Proof. (1) sum over x of p_x sum over i of s_(x,i) log(s_(x,i) / q_i) = sum over x of p_x sum over i of s_(x,i)
log(s_(x,i) / sbar_(R,i)) + sum over i of (sum over x of p_x s_(x,i)) log(sbar_(R,i) / q_i), and the inner sum of the
last term is m_R sbar_(R,i). (2) Apply (1) on each R_c with q = sbar_R, and add over c. The mean of the means
follows from the definition. QED.
Lean: `kl_split` (part 1 as a finite sum, with the column sums in place of m_R sbar_R) and `kl_chain` (the algebraic
core of part 2: the identity summed over the fibres of a map from the points to the parts, for any lb and lq) in
`lean/coarse/Coarse/Merge.lean`. The choices lq = log sbar_R and lb_c = log sbar_c, the column sums m_c sbar_c, and the
mean of the means are by hand. This is the "compensation identity" of information theory (literature table).

**Theorem TI1 (a group replaced by nothing: the information table passes up the tree) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** Let M be
a tree map and G a tree grouping that meet premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1.
1. (The least, closed form; label OPT-KL.) Let S be a group of G with k_S = 0 such that, for every w in W_S, M holds
   the on-inside claim (area of w, empty set, J_w) of Definition DL1 with eps = 0 (void when J_w is empty). Then
   L_S = sum over w in W_S of I_w,
   attained when the logits on the area of w are log sbar_w (up to a multiple of the all-ones vector).
2. (Sibling merge.) Let S' be a sibling merge of groups S_1, ..., S_q (Definition DH3 item 5), with own nodes W'
   (children of its parent whose units were kept). Let S' and every S_i have size 0, let S' and the S_i meet TH1's
   premises at their levels, and let every node of every W_(S_i) and of W' carry the on-inside claim
   (area of w, empty set, J_w) with eps = 0. Then
   L_(S') = L_(S_1) + ... + L_(S_q) + sum over w in W' of I_w.
3. (Lift.) Let u be a node of layer l < L, w_1, ..., w_q its children (the nodes of layer l + 1 with area inside the
   area R_u of u), and R_0 the set of points of R_u in no child's area, with mass m_0. Then y_N = c_N on R_0, and
   I_u = sum over c of (I_(w_c) + m_(w_c) KL(sbar_(w_c) || sbar_u)) + m_0 KL(softmax(c_N) || sbar_u),
   sbar_u = (sum over c of m_(w_c) sbar_(w_c) + m_0 softmax(c_N)) / m_u,
   with the last terms absent when R_0 is empty. A node of a layer below L with no children has I = 0 and
   sbar = softmax(c_N).
4. (A zoom of drop groups.) Let G_0, ..., G_m be a zoom of tree groupings, each meeting premises 1 and 2 of TH1,
   whose groups all have size 0 and meet the premise of part 1. Then for every level j,
   V_b(G_j) = sum over the groups S of G_j of sum over w in W_S of I_w,
   and a least build at G_j has the logits log sbar_w on the area of each node w of each group. Every table comes
   from the tables of the nodes of layer L, the masses of the nodes and c_N, by part 3 applied from layer L - 1
   down; a switch to a level selects stored vectors. Along the zoom V_b does not fall: a merge adds the information
   of the nodes it takes in, and a lift adds the between terms of part 3, each >= 0.
Proof. (1) With k_S = 0 there is no box, and by the formula of L_S in Theorem TH1 the logits of a choice on the area
of w are U_w h_(J_w)(x) + t_w. The on-inside claim with eps = 0 makes h_(J_w) one vector on that area, so these
logits are one vector v_w, and v_w ranges over all of R^(n_y) as t_w does. By Lemma TI0 part 1 the term of w is
I_w + m_w KL(sbar_w || softmax(v_w)) >= I_w, with equality exactly when softmax(v_w) = sbar_w (Gibbs), which a
v_w = log sbar_w reaches. The terms of different w have separate variables. (2) W_(S') is the disjoint union of the
W_(S_i) and W' (DH3 item 5), and the J_w are the same; apply part 1 to S' and to each S_i. (3) On R_0 every unit of
a layer after l is off: a unit outside sub(u) by Lemma TH0 part 1, and a unit of sub(u) in a layer after l lies in
a node whose ancestor in layer l + 1 is a child of u (Definition DH1 item 2), so its region lies inside a child's
area and its district claim (eps = 0, premise 1 of TH1) makes it 0 on R_0. Since l < L, every unit of layer L is off
on R_0 and y_N = c_N there, so s = softmax(c_N) on R_0 and I(R_0) = 0. R_u is the disjoint union of the children's
areas and R_0 (the regions of layer l + 1 are disjoint and each lies inside one region of layer l). Lemma TI0 part 2
gives the formula. A node below L with no children has R_0 = R_u. (4) TH1 part 1 for D_P and part 1 for each group
give V_b(G_j); TH1 part 3 assembles a least build from the attaining choices of part 1. The tables: induction from
layer L by part 3. Monotonicity: by part 2 and by part 3 with KL >= 0. QED.
Lean: `kl_split`, `kl_chain` in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Merge.lean`; the rest by hand (the bookkeeping of TH0 and TL4).
Check: `model/ti_info.py` (parts A and B).
Comment. TI1 is the KL twin of Proposition TL4 and Theorem TP2 part 1 at k = 0: I_w in place of E_w, and
m_c KL(sbar_c || sbar_u) in place of the between table Gamma_u. It needs neither the linear-read claim nor TL3's
premises below the node: only TH1's premises (district, shelter, judgment and branch claims) and flat kept judgment
units; part 3 alone needs only the district claims. What it says about the network
(my reading): a capability that is removed is replaced, on its area, by the average of what N says there, taken in
probabilities, not in logits (TY5 part 2 prices the logit average). The loss of removing it is the information that
the position inside the area carries about the class.

**Theorem TI2 (enough units: the KL least is within a quarter of the linear-read error) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, every claim other than the linear-read claims has eps = 0,
linear-read claims).** In the setting of Theorem TP1 (the premises of TH1, and the linear-read claims
(area of w, J_w) for every w in W_S, with any error):
1. For every k_S, the choice of TP1 part 2 has KL terms (the terms of L_S) at most (1/2) Lin_S
   = (1/4) tail_(k_S)(Sigma_(W_S)) + (1/4) eps_lin(S). So 0 <= L_S <= (1/2) Lin_S.
2. (Label OPT-KL, graded in the linear-read errors only.) If k_S >= rank Sigma_(W_S), then 0 <= L_S <= (1/4) eps_lin(S), and the choice of TP1 part 2 is
   within (1/4) eps_lin(S) of L_S. When every eps_lin(w) = 0, L_S = 0 and that choice attains it.
Proof. (1) At each point, Fact F11 gives KL(softmax(y_N) || softmax(y_N + delta)) <= (1/4) |P_perp delta|^2, which is
half of the D2 term (1/2) |P_perp delta|^2. The D2 terms of TP1 part 2's choice add to Lin_S (TP1 part 2), so its
KL terms add to at most (1/2) Lin_S. By the Comment of DP2, Lin_S = (1/2) tail_k(Sigma_(W_S)) + (1/2) eps_lin(S).
L_S is an infimum of sums of KL terms, so it is >= 0 and at most the KL terms of that choice. (2) Sigma_(W_S) is
positive semidefinite, so when k_S >= its rank every eigenvalue below the k_S largest is 0 and tail = 0; then part 1.
QED.
Lean: `softmax_var_le` (Fact F11's lemma, `Coarse/Fold.lean`); the rest by hand.
Check: `model/ti_info.py` (part C).
Comment. The condition k_S >= rank Sigma_(W_S) is a condition between map and zoom (Sigma is read from N, P and the
group's nodes, and its rank is computed exactly, in polynomial time, as for a rational matrix). Under it the gap is
in the claims' errors alone and is 0 when they are 0: the form of T5's graded clause, for these groups, with only the
linear-read claims graded. A rank above n_y - 1 is impossible, so a group with k_S >= n_y - 1 always meets it.

**Corollary TI2.1 (keep-or-drop groupings: every level least for KL) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree
map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, every claim other than the linear-read claims has eps = 0,
linear-read claims, keep-or-drop zooms).** Let G be a tree grouping that meets premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1, in
which every group S is a **drop group** (k_S = 0, and the on-inside claims of TI1 part 1 hold with eps = 0) or a
**keep group** (k_S >= rank Sigma_(W_S), with linear-read claims (area of w, J_w) for its nodes, any error). Let B be
the build of TH1's upper bound with the vectors log sbar_w for the drop groups and the choices of TP1 part 2 for the
keep groups. Then (label OPT-KL):
   V_b(G) = sum over drop groups of sum over w in W_S of I_w + sum over keep groups of L_S,
   V_b(G) <= D_P(B) <= V_b(G) + (1/4) sum over keep groups of eps_lin(S),
and the keep groups' sum of L_S lies in [0, (1/4) sum of eps_lin(S)]. When every eps_lin is 0, D_P(B) = V_b(G) =
the drop groups' information: an exact closed form, also where it is > 0. Along a zoom whose levels are all such
groupings, every level comes from the information tables (TI1 part 3) and from the summaries Sigma_(W_S) and build
records of the keep groups' nodes, made from N in one pass (TP3 part 1); a switch selects stored weights. (Label
OPT-KL, graded in the linear-read errors only: every other claim is at eps = 0.)
Proof. TH1 part 1 for D_P gives V_b(G) = sum over S of L_S. TI1 part 1 gives L_S for the drop groups and TI2 part 2
bounds it for the keep groups. TH1's upper bound (with e = 0 and the chosen choices) is a class (b) build whose D_P
is the sum of the chosen terms: the drop groups' terms equal their L_S, and each keep group's terms are at most its
L_S + (1/4) eps_lin(S) by TI2 part 2. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (a composition of TH1, TI1 and TI2).
Comment. Node S-keepdrop (card 3-31) narrows the developer's zoom: a level may not coarsen a capability to fewer units
than the rank of its table. Under it, with every claim other than the linear-read claims at eps = 0, the least KL is a
closed form with a gap of at most (1/4) sum of eps_lin. This is T5's exactness clause once Definition DM6
(completeness) covers the claims of DP1 and DL1 (card 3-26); T5's graded clause is met in the linear-read errors only.
Without S-keepdrop, the groups with 0 < k_S < rank Sigma_(W_S) are the open case of Theorems TI3 and TI4.

**Theorem TI3 (what every KL least does, and the open case as a least over output spans) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** Let M and G meet premises 1
and 2 of Theorem TH1, and let S be a group of G.
1. (The means match.) Let a choice (C, V, U_w, t_w) attain L_S, and on the area A_w of w let
   q_x = softmax(V C(x) + U_w h_(J_w)(x) + t_w). Then for every w in W_S
   sum over x in A_w of p_x q_x = m_w sbar_w,   sum over x in A_w of p_x (q_x - s_x) h_j(x) = 0 for every j in J_w,
   and sum over w in W_S of sum over x in A_w of p_x (q_x - s_x) C(x)^T = 0. Every least class (b) build at G
   restricts on S's areas to such a choice, so its mean softmax on each area of each group equals N's.
2. (Boxes on throughout their areas; label EQ.) Let L_S^on be the infimum of the terms of L_S over the boxes of S of
   size k_S whose units are on at every point of S's areas, and k = min(k_S, n_y - 1). For a k-dimensional subspace
   Q of the image of P_perp let
   F(Q) = sum over w in W_S of f_w(Q),   f_w(Q) = inf of sum over x in A_w of p_x KL(s_x || softmax(C_w z_(T_w)(x) + U_w h_(J_w)(x) + t_w)),
   the infimum over linear maps C_w from R^(T_w) into Q, matrices U_w and vectors t_w. Then L_S^on = min over Q of
   F(Q). The minimum is attained, and a box on at every point of P with output span Q and reads C_w attains L_S^on.
   For each Q, f_w(Q) is the infimum of a convex function of (C_w, U_w, t_w): a multinomial logistic regression with
   soft labels s_x on the features z_(T_w), h_(J_w) and 1, with the output of the z-part confined to Q.
Proof. (1) The variables t_w, U_w and V range over whole vector spaces, and the terms are differentiable in them. The
derivative of KL(s || softmax(l)) in the logits l is softmax(l) - s. So the derivative of the terms in t_w is
sum over x in A_w of p_x (q_x - s_x), in U_w it is sum over A_w of p_x (q_x - s_x) h_(J_w)(x)^T, and in V it is the sum
over all of S's areas of p_x (q_x - s_x) C(x)^T. At a least point each is 0. Least builds: the lower bound in the proof
of TH1 writes the terms of D_P(B) on S's areas as a choice of the kind in L_S (with every t_w the same vector) and
the other terms as >= 0, so D_P(B) = V_b(G) = sum over S of L_S forces each group's terms to equal L_S; that choice
attains L_S, and the first equation is the statement on the means.
(2) Upper bound: given Q with an orthonormal basis Qm (an n_y x k matrix) and C_w = Qm A_w, take k box units, unit t
with the read (A_w)_t on T_w for each w and the bias beta_t = 1 + sum over w of max over x in P of |(A_w)_t z_(T_w)(x)|
(finite, P is finite), as in TP1 part 2; these units are on at every point of P, and V = Qm. On the area of w the
units of T_(w') (w' other than w) take their shelter values zeta_(w'), so V C(x) = Qm A_w z_(T_w)(x) + a constant, which
t_w absorbs. So every value of f_w(Q) is reached, and L_S^on <= F(Q). Lower bound: for a box on throughout S's areas,
on the area of w each unit is m_t^T z_(T(S)) + beta_t and the parts on the other T_(w') are constant, so
V C(x) = V M_w z_(T_w)(x) + a constant (as in the proof of Corollary TP1.1). Adding a multiple of the all-ones vector to
the logits changes no softmax, so V may be replaced by P_perp V, whose image has dimension at most k; let Q be a
k-dimensional subspace of the image of P_perp that contains it. Then the terms are at least F(Q). So L_S^on = inf
over Q of F(Q). Convexity: l -> KL(s || softmax(l)) = logsumexp(l) - s^T l + sum s log s is convex, and the logits are
linear in (C_w, U_w, t_w). Attainment: let Lin_w be the linear space of the functions x -> A ztil_w(x) on A_w (A any
n_y x |T_w| matrix, ztil_w = Pi_w z_(T_w) as in DP1, with F_w spanned by 1 and the h_j, j in J_w). A tuple g = (g_w) of
functions g_w from A_w to the image of P_perp is realised by a choice with output span Q exactly when, for each w,
Pi_w g_w lies in Lin_w and takes values in Q (the part of g_w with coordinates in F_w is reached by U_w and t_w, any
part in Lin_w by C_w, and Pi_w of the logits is C_w ztil_w). Let Z be the union over Q of these tuples. Z is closed:
if g^n in Z tends to g, with subspaces Q^n, a subsequence of the Q^n tends to some Q (the set of k-dimensional
subspaces is compact) with the orthogonal projections P_(Q^n) tending to P_Q; then Pi_w g^n_w = P_(Q^n) Pi_w g^n_w tends
to P_Q Pi_w g_w, which is therefore Pi_w g_w, and Pi_w g_w lies in Lin_w, a closed (finite-dimensional) space. So g
is in Z with Q. The terms, as a function of the centred logits g, are continuous and tend to infinity when |g| does:
KL(s || q) >= -H(s) - (min over i of s_i) log(min over i of q_i), every s_x has full support, and the least entry of
softmax(l) tends to 0 when |P_perp l| does. So the infimum over the closed set Z is attained at some g in Z, with some
Q; that Q attains the least of F (F(Q) <= the terms at g, and F >= L_S^on everywhere), and the upper-bound box with it
attains L_S^on. When k_S > k, the remaining box units are relu(0 . z + 1) with logit weight 0. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (first-order conditions, convexity of log-sum-exp, compactness of the set of subspaces).
Check: `model/ti_open.py` (part A: the means match at the computed least of the instances of TI5 part 2).
Remark (the ends of part 2). With k_S = 0 there is no Q, and under the on-inside premise of TI1, L_S^on = L_S = sum of
I_w (TI1 part 1). With linear-read claims at eps = 0 and k_S >= rank Sigma_(W_S), L_S^on = L_S = 0 (TI2 part 2; TP1's
box is on throughout). These use the premises of TI1 and TI2, not only TI3's.
Comment. Part 1 is the KL form of the D2 fact that a least build's mean logits match N's: here what matches is the
mean probability on each area (calibration on each area). A D2-least build breaks it in general (TY5 part 3: its mean
softmax on P is (3/4, 1/4), N's is (7/10, 3/10)). Part 2 is not a closed form. For a fixed span Q it is an exact
convex program in N's numbers (exact optimisation with a guarantee, which counts as "not training" in the reading of
Theorem T21); the choice of Q is a point of a manifold of dimension k (n_y - 1 - k), and F is not convex in it. For D2,
Ky Fan's principle solves that choice in closed form (TP1). Whether a box that switches inside its areas can beat
L_S^on for KL is open (for D2 it cannot: TP1 part 1); Theorem TI4 shows it gains nothing to second order. Conjecture
DI2 (Part D.17) says it can beyond second order. If it holds, the picture of Corollary TL5, a coarse unit that stays on
over its whole area, is a property of D2, not of the KL least.

**Theorem TI4 (small variation inside the areas: the D2 problem in the Fisher metric) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, every claim it uses has
eps = 0).** Let M, G and S meet premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1, and for every w in W_S let M hold, with eps = 0, the
on-inside claim (area of w, empty set, J_w) and the linear-read claim (area of w, J_w). Then F_w (Definition DP1) is
the constants on A_w, and on A_w, P_perp y_N(x) = ybar_w + Y_w(x) with ybar_w the mean and Y_w = Ytil = B_w ztil_w
linear in ztil_w; K_w := sum over A_w of p_x Y_w Y_w^T = Sigma_w. Let sigma_w = softmax(ybar_w) and
H_w = diag(sigma_w) - sigma_w sigma_w^T, positive definite on the image of P_perp. For a >= 0 let L_S(a) be L_S with
softmax(y_N(x)) replaced by softmax(ybar_w + a Y_w(x)) on each A_w (the same boxes and features), and L_S^on(a) the
same over boxes on throughout. Let k = min(k_S, n_y - 1). For a k-dimensional subspace Q of the image of P_perp with
an orthonormal basis Qm let
   psi_w(Q) = tr(H_w Sigma_w) - tr((Qm^T H_w Qm)^(-1) Qm^T H_w Sigma_w H_w Qm),   Phi = (1/2) min over Q of sum over w in W_S of psi_w(Q).
1. (Second order.) L_S(a) = a^2 Phi + O(a^3) and L_S^on(a) = a^2 Phi + O(a^3) as a -> 0. So boxes that switch
   inside their areas gain only O(a^3).
2. (One mean softmax.) If sigma_w = sigma for every w in W_S (for example when S has one node), with H its matrix and
   H^(1/2) the square root of H on the image of P_perp, then
   Phi = (1/2) tail_k(H^(1/2) Sigma_(W_S) H^(1/2)),
   and Q = H^(-1/2) times the span of the top k eigenvectors of H^(1/2) Sigma_(W_S) H^(1/2) attains it (H^(-1/2) the
   inverse of H^(1/2) on the image of P_perp).
3. (Uniform mean.) If moreover sigma is uniform, then H = (1/n_y) P_perp and Phi = (1/n_y) (1/2) tail_k(Sigma_(W_S)) =
   (1/n_y) L2_S (TP1 at eps_lin = 0, a = 1): to second order the KL least directions are D2's. When sigma is not
   uniform they need not be (Proposition TI5 part 2).
Proof. Notation: on A_w, write the logits of a choice as ybar_w + a beta_x (beta_x is defined up to a multiple of the
all-ones vector; take it in the image of P_perp, which changes no softmax). The term at x is
KL(softmax(y) || softmax(y + delta)) with y = ybar_w + a Y_w(x) and delta = a (beta_x - Y_w(x)).
Taylor step. With A the log-sum-exp function, KL(softmax(y) || softmax(y + delta)) = A(y + delta) - A(y) -
softmax(y)^T delta = (1/2) delta^T H(y) delta + r with |r| <= (4/3) |delta|^3 for every y: the third derivative of A
in a direction delta is the third central moment of delta_Y with Y drawn from softmax(y + t delta), at most
(2 max |delta_i|)^3 in absolute value, and the integral remainder carries the factor 1/6. In the same way the
derivative of H in a direction e is the bilinear form (v, u) -> E[(e_Y - E e_Y)(v_Y - E v_Y)(u_Y - E u_Y)], and
|E[...]| <= 2 |e|_inf (v^T H v)^(1/2) (u^T H u)^(1/2) <= |e| |v| |u| (Cauchy-Schwarz and v^T H v <= |v|^2 / 2, Fact
F11), so its operator norm is at most |e|, uniformly in y and n_y, and the operator norm of
H(ybar_w + a Y_w(x)) - H_w is at most a max over x of |Y_w(x)|.
Upper bound. Let Q attain Phi with basis Qm, and let beta_x = Pihat_w Y_w(x) with Pihat_w = Qm (Qm^T H_w Qm)^(-1)
Qm^T H_w, the projection onto Q that is orthogonal in the inner product of H_w. beta is linear in ztil_w with values
in Q, so (TI3 part 2, scaled by a) a box on throughout reaches these logits up to constants that t_w absorbs. With
delta = a (Pihat_w - I) Y_w(x), bounded by a c_2, the terms are (a^2 / 2) sum over w and x of p_x
((I - Pihat_w) Y_w)^T H_w ((I - Pihat_w) Y_w) + O(a^3). Expanding, sum over x of p_x |(I - Pihat_w) Y_w|_(H_w)^2 =
tr(H_w Sigma_w) - tr(H_w Pihat_w Sigma_w) = psi_w(Q) (Pihat_w is H_w-self-adjoint and idempotent, and K_w = Sigma_w).
So L_S^on(a) <= a^2 Phi + O(a^3), and L_S(a) <= L_S^on(a).
Lower bound. Take any choice (any box, on throughout or not) with terms at most L_S(a) + a^3 <= C a^2 for a <= 1
(the upper bound). At each point the term is at most C a^2 / p_min, so by Pinsker's inequality the softmaxes q_x and
s_x = softmax(ybar_w + a Y_w(x)) are within sqrt(2 C / p_min) a in l1 distance, and s_x is within c a of sigma_w
(softmax is Lipschitz). For a small enough every entry of q_x is at least (min sigma_w) / 2, and P_perp log q_x =
P_perp (ybar_w + a beta_x) is within a constant times a of P_perp log sigma_w = ybar_w (the logarithm is Lipschitz
on [(min sigma_w)/2, 1]). So |beta_x| <= c_3, uniformly in the choice, and |delta| <= a (c_3 + max |Y_w|). The Taylor
step gives terms >= (a^2 / 2) sum over w and x of p_x (beta_x - Y_w)^T H_w (beta_x - Y_w) - c_4 a^3. Now
P_perp V C(x) takes values in a subspace Q' of the image of P_perp of dimension at most k (any box), and the other part
of a beta_x, P_perp (U_w h_(J_w) + t_w) - ybar_w, is one vector a tau_w on A_w (J_w flat). So beta_x = g_x + tau_w with
g_x in Q'. For fixed Q' and tau_w the least over g_x at each point is |(I - Pihat) (Y_w(x) - tau_w)|_(H_w)^2 (Pihat for
Q'), and summing over x, since sum over x of p_x Y_w(x) = 0 (Y_w is centred on A_w), the sum is
sum p_x |(I - Pihat) Y_w|^2 + m_w |(I - Pihat) tau_w|^2 >= psi_w(Q'). Enlarging Q' to dimension k does not raise
psi_w (a larger subspace leaves a smaller H_w-residual). So the terms are >= a^2 Phi - c_4 a^3, and L_S(a) >= a^2 Phi
- O(a^3).
(2) H is positive definite on the image of P_perp (v^T H v is the variance of v_Y under sigma, which has full
support; it is 0 only for constant v). With all H_w = H, sum over w of psi_w(Q) = tr(H Sigma_W) - tr((Qm^T H Qm)^(-1)
Qm^T H Sigma_W H Qm). Put U = H^(1/2) Qm and Wm = U (U^T U)^(-1/2), an orthonormal basis of H^(1/2) Q; then the second
trace is tr(Wm^T M Wm) with M = H^(1/2) Sigma_W H^(1/2), and tr(H Sigma_W) = tr M. As Q ranges over the k-dimensional
subspaces of the image of P_perp, so does H^(1/2) Q. By Ky Fan's maximum principle the largest tr(Wm^T M Wm) is
top_k(M), reached by the top k eigenvectors. So the least of the sum is tail_k(M). (3) For sigma uniform,
H = (1/n_y) I - (1/n_y^2) 1 1^T = (1/n_y) P_perp, M = (1/n_y) Sigma_W (Sigma_W has image in that of P_perp), the
eigenvectors are Sigma_W's, and tail_k(M) = (1/n_y) tail_k(Sigma_W); by TP1 part 3 at eps_lin = 0,
L2_S = (1/2) tail_k(Sigma_W). QED.
Lean: none, by hand (Taylor's theorem with remainder, Pinsker's inequality and Ky Fan's principle).
Check: `model/ti_open.py` (part B).
Comment. The family softmax(ybar_w + a Y_w) is a network: in a network with one hidden layer and one area it is N
with its logit weights multiplied by a and its logit bias moved so that the mean stays ybar_w; with several areas the
logit weights of the judgment units move too, so that each area keeps its mean. TI4 says what KL does that D2 does
not: it measures each output direction in the Fisher metric H of the area's mean prediction. A direction that moves
probability between likely classes counts more than one that moves it between unlikely classes. With n_y = 1000
and a confident area, H is far from uniform. TI4 is a description of V(G) to second order, not a rule that reaches it:
the O(a^3) term is not bounded by the claims' errors, so TI4 does not meet the bar; it locates the open case. With
different mean softmaxes on the areas of S, Phi is a least over Q of a sum of terms in different metrics, which has no
eigenvalue solution in general (Conjecture DI1).

**Proposition TI5 (the D2 table does not fix the KL least) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree
groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** In each pair below, N has one hidden
layer, the map has one district holding every hidden unit with region P, G = {S} with S the hidden units, W_S = {w}
with area P and J_w empty; every claim that TH1 uses, the on-inside claim (P, the hidden units, empty set) and the
linear-read claim (P, empty set) have eps = 0; and the two networks of a pair have the same summary (E_w, Sigma_w)
and the same B_w.
1. (k_S = 0, two logits.) (a) One unit u, two points with weights 1/2, h_u(x_1) = 2 log 3, h_u(x_2) = 0; N has logits
   (h_u, 0) and N' has logits (h_u - log 3, 0). Then L_S(N) = (1/2)(KL((9/10, 1/10) || (7/10, 3/10)) +
   KL((1/2, 1/2) || (7/10, 3/10))) and L_S(N') = (3/4) log 3 - log 2, and these differ. (b) The pair also differs
   with the same area means: N with logit gaps h_u in {c - 1, c + 1} (two points, weights 1/2) and N' with gaps in
   {c - sqrt 2, c, c + sqrt 2} (weights 1/4, 1/2, 1/4), c = 2, logits (h_u - c, 0), h_u = relu(c + x) at the points
   x = -1, 1 and x = -sqrt 2, 0, sqrt 2: in both the centred gaps have mean 0 and variance 1, so E_w = 1/2 and the
   same Sigma_w, and L_S(N) = log 2 - h2(sigmoid(1)), L_S(N') = (1/2)(log 2 - h2(sigmoid(sqrt 2))), with
   h2(r) = -r log r - (1 - r) log(1 - r); these differ. (In 1(b), N and N' are one network on two mixes P and P'.)
2. (k_S = 1, three logits.) For a > 0, two units h_i = relu(x_i + 2) on the four points (+-1, 0), (0, +-1) of R^2 with
   weights 1/4, f_1 = (1, -1, 0) / sqrt 2, f_2 = (1, 1, -2) / sqrt 6, and logits y = a (f_1 (h_1 - 2) + f_2 (h_2 - 2))
   + y_0, with y_0 = 0 for N_a and y_0 = (log (1/2), log (1/4), log (1/4)) for N'_a. Both have Sigma_w =
   (a^2 / 2) P_perp (so every direction ties for D2) and E_w = a^2. Then
   L_S(N_a) = a^2 / 12 + O(a^3),   L_S(N'_a) = a^2 / 16 + O(a^3),
   so they differ for small a. In N'_a every choice whose terms are within a^3 of L_S(N'_a) has an output line
   that tends to the span of (2, -1, -1) (the class of mass 1/2 against the others) as a -> 0, and a D2-least build whose box writes along (0, 1, -1) has KL = (3/32) a^2 + O(a^3),
   a factor 3/2 above the least to second order.
So no rule that reads only the summaries of DP2, or those with the area means ybar_w, returns the KL least.
Proof. The claims: the units are on at every point (in 1(a) take u = relu(t) at the inputs t = 2 log 3 and t = 0,
pre-activation >= 0; in 1(b) the pre-activations c + x are >= 2 - sqrt 2 > 0; in 2 they are x_i + 2 >= 1), the region is P (no shelter or judgment claim is needed, as
in TY5 part 3), and the logits are affine in the pre-activations (eps_lin = 0). Ytil, and hence E_w, Sigma_w and B_w,
is the centred part of P_perp y, which the logit biases do not change.
(1a) s for N: (9/10, 1/10) and (1/2, 1/2), mean (7/10, 3/10); for N': (3/4, 1/4) and (1/4, 3/4), mean (1/2, 1/2), so
L_S(N') = KL((3/4, 1/4) || (1/2, 1/2)) = (3/4) log 3 - log 2 (TI1 part 1). Expanding the logarithms,
L_S(N) = (3/5) log 3 + (1/2) log 5 - (7/10) log 7. So 20 (L_S(N') - L_S(N)) = log(3^3 7^14) - log(2^20 5^10), which is
not 0: the two integers differ (only the first has the prime factor 7), and 3^3 7^14 > 2^20 5^10, so
L_S(N') > L_S(N). (1b) With
gaps symmetric about 0 the mean softmax is (1/2, 1/2) and KL(Bern(sigmoid(t)) || Bern(1/2)) = log 2 - h2(sigmoid(t)),
even in t. The centred gaps have the same mean 0 and variance 1, so the same E_w and Sigma_w (both mixes' B_w read
the gap with weight 1/2 per logit). With phi(t) = log 2 - h2(sigmoid(t)) = log 2 + t sigmoid(t) - log(1 + e^t), phi'(t) =
t sigmoid(t)(1 - sigmoid(t)). Put psi(r) = phi(sqrt r) for r >= 0: psi'(r) = sigmoid(sqrt r)(1 - sigmoid(sqrt r)) / 2,
strictly decreasing, so psi is strictly concave and psi(1) > (psi(0) + psi(2)) / 2 = psi(2) / 2 (psi(0) = 0). That is
L_S(N) > L_S(N'): the two laws of the gaps have the same mean and variance, and KL is not quadratic in the gap. (2) F F^T = P_perp for F = (f_1, f_2), and the mean of (x_1, x_2)(x_1, x_2)^T over the points is (1/2) I,
so Sigma_w = (a^2 / 2) P_perp and E_w = a^2. ybar_w = P_perp y_0 (the points have mean 0). This is the family of TI4
with Y_w(x) = a-free part F x and Sigma_w(a = 1) = (1/2) P_perp; TI4 part 2 applies (one node). For N_a, sigma is
uniform: H = (1/3) P_perp, M = (1/6) P_perp, eigenvalues 1/6, 1/6, tail_1 = 1/6, Phi = 1/12. For N'_a, sigma =
(1/2, 1/4, 1/4): H (0, 1, -1) = (1/4)(0, 1, -1) and H (2, -1, -1) = (3/8)(2, -1, -1) (direct computation), so on the
image of P_perp H has eigenvalues 1/4 and 3/8 with these eigenvectors; M = (1/2) H has eigenvalues 1/8, 3/16;
tail_1 = 1/8, Phi = 1/16, attained by Q = span of H^(-1/2)(2, -1, -1), which is (2, -1, -1). For the D2 build with
q = (0, 1, -1) / sqrt 2 (an eigenvector of H, so its Euclidean and H-projections agree), the second-order loss is
(1/2) (1/2) (tr H - q^T H q) = (1/4)(5/8 - 1/4) = 3/32, by the upper-bound computation of TI4 with that Q (its terms
are a^2 / 2 psi + O(a^3)). The output lines: TI4's lower bound, applied to a choice whose output span lies in a
line Q', gives terms >= (a^2 / 2) psi(Q') - c a^3 with c not depending on Q' (the constants come from Pinsker's
inequality and the Taylor step only). With the upper bound, a choice within a^3 of L_S has psi(Q') <= 2 Phi + O(a)
(an output span {0} is padded by any line; it has psi = tr(H Sigma) > 2 Phi, so it is excluded for small a). psi is
continuous on the compact set of lines of the plane, with the unique minimiser span(2, -1, -1) (3/16 > 1/8 on the
other eigenvector, and psi between), so Q' tends to that line. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (exact rational eigenvalues and integer comparisons; `model/ti_open.py` part C re-checks the
closed forms with sympy).
Comment. Part 1 is the reason in its simplest form: D2 sees the logits after removing their mean, and KL sees the
probabilities. The tables of TP2 forget exactly what KL needs: where the area's mean output sits (part 1a, part 2) and
the shape of the law of the outputs beyond its second moments (part 1b). So the KL recursion cannot be a recursion of
D2 tables. At k = 0 it is the recursion of information tables (TI1); for k >= 1 no finite table of this kind is known.

## B.Q Squeezing a capability: packing (added 2026-10-31, ROADMAP.md session 1; revised after REFEREE-BQ-2026-10-31.md)

Shonu (2026-10-31), on card 3-31: "you can only keep them or drop them. That's the same as pruning ... we need to
completely fix this third row". Row 3 is a group S with 0 < k_S < rank Sigma_(W_S) (Part B.I). This Part finds its
form and bounds one build of that form. It does not yet give the least itself.
1. The deciding test. The plan's first guess was "no unit of a box serves two separated nodes, so a squeeze picks
   which nodes keep their detail" (a tree knapsack). It is false (Proposition TQ2 part 3): a unit that serves two
   nodes whose areas favour disjoint class sets beats every unit that serves one, for confident enough areas. Read as
   a network: on each area the free offset t_w pushes the other node's classes down, and then one output direction
   moves each node's own classes on its own area. The price is the probability each area still gives to the other
   node's classes.
2. Definition DQ1: the active-class summary (A, K) and its value eps_act, computed from N's logits on A. It is a
   summary of N (like Definition DI1), not a claim: it has no statement that holds at eps_act = 0.
3. Theorem TQ1: the least of a squeezed group is at least the sum of its nodes' own leasts (part 1). When every node
   moves its own classes in at most k_S directions and the class sets are disjoint, a packed box with max_w r^K_w
   units has terms at most the sum of eps_act (part 2; label ONE-BUILD: its lower side is 0 there, and eps_act = 0
   only when the loss is 0).
4. Proposition TQ2: eps_act is 0 only for a node without variation (part 1, a property of DQ1, not of row 3); the
   least of every row-3 group is > 0 (part 2); the tree knapsack is not the form (part 3).
5. Theorem TQ3 (two-sided, in the limit of confident areas): the least of a squeezed group tends to the sum of its
   areas' own-block leasts, with explicit factors on both sides.
6. Lemma TQ4: the closed-form alignment of two areas that share k units (reverse pairing: each area's strongest
   direction with the other's weakest).
7. Conjectures DQ2 (TQ4 is the cost of sharing, to second order) and DQ3 (TQ3 recurses down the tree), Part D.18.
8. Conjecture DQ1 (Part D.18): for nodes of comparable confidence, the least is within a fixed factor of the packed
   bound (first-order tightness).
What B.Q does not do, said plainly: it gives no exact form of the row-3 least and no bound that reaches it. Whether
some claim type gives row 3 an exact closed form is OPEN; nothing here shows it impossible (the earlier sentence
"row 3 is never exact, a fact of softmax" was wrong and is withdrawn: TI1 is exact with a least > 0). The packed
build of TQ1 is the canonical one; how to line up its shared directions is the next object (Lemma TQ4, Conjecture
DQ2; Part C, H-active, measures it).

correct; its findings fixed, not re-refereed).
