Setting of B.Q. M and G meet premises 1 and 2 of Theorem TH1; S is a group of G with k_S >= 1; for every w in W_S, M
holds with eps = 0 the on-inside claim (area of w, empty set, J_w). Where a statement says so, M also holds with
eps = 0 the linear-read claim (area of w, J_w); then, as in Theorem TI4, on the area A_w of w,
P_perp y_N(x) = ybar_w + Y_w(x) with ybar_w the p-weighted mean on A_w and Y_w = B_w ztil_w linear in the centred top
pre-activations, and r_w = rank Sigma_w is the dimension of the span of the Y_w(x). A choice of L_S has, on A_w, the
logits V C(x) + t_w, with t_w one vector (the free terms U_w h_(J_w) + t_w of TH1, constant on A_w by the on-inside
claim); V C(x) lies in the image of V, of dimension at most k_S, for every box (units may switch).

**Definition DQ1 (active-class summary).** An active-class summary is computed from a pair (A, K) of the area A of a
node and a set K of classes with 0 < |K| < n_y. Write s_x = softmax(y_N(x)), ybar_A for the p-weighted mean of
P_perp y_N on A, Y(x) = P_perp y_N(x) - ybar_A, Pi^K the diagonal 0/1 matrix of K, rho_K(x) = |Pi^K Y(x)|_2 (the
size of the area's movement on the classes K), phi(t) = e^t - 1 - t, and for x in A and a class i not in K
   g_(x,i)(beta) = max(phi(-Y(x)_i - beta + rho_K(x)), phi(-Y(x)_i - beta - rho_K(x))).
Its value is
   eps_act(A, K) = sum over i not in K of min over real beta of sum over x in A of p_x s_(x,i) g_(x,i)(beta),
mu(A, K) = sum over x in A of p_x s_x(classes not in K) is its outside mass, and r^K(A) = the dimension of the span
of the Pi^K Y(x), x in A, is its own-class rank.
Properties. (1) It reads only N's logits on A, the weights p and K: no build, size or zoom. The rescaling of Fact F1
and copies (Definition DN1) leave the logits unchanged, so they leave eps_act unchanged. (2) For each class i the
function of beta is convex (phi is convex, a maximum of convex functions is convex, sums keep it); it is positive
and tends to infinity with |beta| (A is not empty and s_(x,i) > 0), so its minimum is attained; eps_act is
n_y - |K| one-dimensional convex problems, each computed to any precision by bisection on its slope, in time
polynomial in |A| n_y and the number of bits. (3) A closed upper form: with beta_i = max over x of
(-Y(x)_i + rho_K(x)), every argument of phi lies in [-2 D_A, 0], D_A = max over x and i not in K of
(|Y(x)_i| + rho_K(x)), and phi(t) <= -t for t <= 0 (Lean `phi_le_neg`), so eps_act(A, K) <= 2 D_A mu(A, K).
(4) eps_act(A, K) = 0 exactly when Y = 0 on A (Proposition TQ2 part 1).
Comment. eps_act is a summary, as I_w is in DI1: it has no statement that holds when it is 0 (it is 0 only when N's
output does not vary on A, whatever K is). So a bound in eps_act is a bound in quantities computed from N, not the
graded clause of the trunk, whose bounds are in claims' errors. It weighs the probability outside K by how far the
packed box of TQ1 moves those classes' logits: the box drops the area's own movement -Y(x)_i on that class (known in
sign), and another node's direction adds at most rho_K(x) there. The first form (2026-10-31) put a wider envelope,
|Y(x)|_2, on every outside class with one shift for all classes; the proof of TQ1 needs only the form above (Part C,
H-active, compares the two). Node R-active (card 3-32).

**Theorem TQ1 (packing: a lower bound for every squeezed group, and one packed build) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, active-class summaries,
squeeze-complete groups, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** In the setting of B.Q:
1. (The least is at least the sum of the nodes' own leasts; any k_S; needs neither linear-read claims, summaries nor
   completeness.) For w in W_S let L_w(k) be the infimum, over boxes of size k (units may switch) and vectors t, of
   sum over x in A_w of p_x KL(s_x || softmax(V C(x) + t)), the box reading the units of T(S). Then
   L_S >= sum over w in W_S of L_w(k_S).
2. (Packing; label ONE-BUILD, bounded by summaries of N.) Let the linear-read claims hold with eps = 0, let
   K_w (w in W_S) be pairwise disjoint class sets, and let r^K_w := r^K(A_w) <= k_S for every w (node
   S-squeezecomplete). For each w let U_w be an n_y x k_S matrix whose first r^K_w columns are an orthonormal basis of
   the span of the Pi^K_w Y_w(x) (Pi^K_w = Pi^(K_w)) and whose other columns are 0, and beta^w the vector, 0 on K_w, of
   the minimisers of Definition DQ1 for (A_w, K_w). The **packed choice** has V = sum over w of Pi^K_w U_w, box values
   c_w(x) = U_w^T Pi^K_w Y_w(x) on A_w (a box on throughout, reading U_w^T Pi^K_w B_w on ztil_w, as in TP1 part 2), and
   t_w = ybar_w - beta^w plus the constant that absorbs the box's shelter and bias terms on A_w. Its terms are at most
   sum over w of eps_act(A_w, K_w), so
   sum over w of L_w(k_S) <= L_S <= terms of the packed choice <= sum over w in W_S of eps_act(A_w, K_w).
   When moreover k_S >= r_w for every w, every L_w(k_S) = 0 (TI2 part 2 for the one node w), and the lower side is 0.
3. (Units.) The packed choice uses max over w of r^K_w <= max over w of r_w units. TI2's sufficient condition uses
   rank Sigma_(W_S) units, which is at least max over w of r_w (Sigma_(W_S) is the sum of the positive semidefinite
   Sigma_w).
4. (A level.) Let G be a tree grouping meeting premises 1 and 2 of TH1 whose groups are drop groups (TI1 part 1), keep
   groups (k_S >= rank Sigma_(W_S), linear-read claims at eps = 0: TI2 part 2) or packed groups (the premises of
   part 2). The build with log sbar_w on the drop groups' areas, TP1 part 2's choice on the keep groups and the packed
   choice on the packed groups has
   V_b(G) <= D_P(B) <= V_b(G) + sum over packed groups of sum over W_S of eps_act(A_w, K_w).
   The packed choice of a group is fixed by per-node arrays (U_w, K_w, beta^w, ybar_w), made from N once; a level
   selects stored per-node arrays and adds the n_y x k_S matrices Pi^K_w U_w of its packed groups.
Proof. (1) By the formula of L_S in Theorem TH1, a choice of L_S is a box of size k_S and vectors t_w, with the terms
of w equal to sum over A_w of p_x KL(s_x || softmax(V C(x) + t_w)). The same box and t_w are admissible in L_w(k_S),
so the terms of w are >= L_w(k_S). Adding over w gives the bound for every choice, hence for the infimum.
(2) The box: c_w(x) = U_w^T Pi^K_w B_w ztil_w(x) is linear in ztil_w; a box unit per column, on throughout with a
large bias as in TP1 part 2, gives on A_w the values c_w(x) plus a vector constant on A_w (the units of the other
nodes' tops sit at their shelter values, premise 1 of TH1), and V times that constant goes into t_w. On A_w,
Pi^K_w U_w c_w(x) = Pi^K_w U_w U_w^T Pi^K_w Y_w(x) = Pi^K_w Y_w(x), since Pi^K_w Y_w(x) lies in the span of the first
r^K_w columns of U_w. So the logits are
   ybar_w + Y_w(x) + d_x,   d_x = - beta^w - (I - Pi^K_w) Y_w(x) + sum over w' != w of Pi^K_(w') U_(w') c_w(x).
d_(x,i) = 0 for i in K_w. For i not in K_w, at most one w' has i in K_(w') (the K are disjoint), and
|(U_(w') c)_i| <= |U_(w') c|_2 <= |c|_2 (U_(w') has orthonormal or zero columns) with |c_w(x)|_2 =
|Pi^K_w Y_w(x)|_2 = rho_(K_w)(x); so d_(x,i) = -Y_w(x)_i - beta^w_i + sigma_(x,i) with |sigma_(x,i)| <= rho_(K_w)(x).
(On A_w, Y_w(x) = P_perp y_N(x) - ybar_w is the Y of Definition DQ1 for A = A_w.) Since ybar_w + Y_w(x) =
P_perp y_N(x), its softmax is s_x, and for any d,
   KL(s || softmax(log s + d)) = log(sum over i of s_i e^(d_i)) - sum over i of s_i d_i <= sum over i of s_i (e^(d_i) - 1 - d_i)
by log z <= z - 1 (Lean `pack_step`). The classes of K_w give 0. For i not in K_w, phi(-Y_w(x)_i - beta_i + sigma)
with |sigma| <= rho_(K_w)(x) is at most g_(x,i)(beta_i): phi is convex, so on an interval it is largest at an end.
Summing with the weights p_x and the minimisers beta^w_i gives the terms of w <= eps_act(A_w, K_w). The lower side is
part 1, and L_w(k_S) = 0 when k_S >= r_w by TI2 part 2.
(3) V has k_S columns of which only the first max r^K_w are nonzero; the units for the zero columns have logit
weight 0. r^K_w <= r_w because Pi^K_w maps the span of the Y_w(x) onto the span of the Pi^K_w Y_w(x).
rank Sigma_(W_S) >= r_w for each w because the image of a sum of positive semidefinite matrices contains each image.
(4) TH1 part 1 for D_P gives V_b(G) = sum of L_S; TH1's upper bound assembles the three kinds of choices; the drop
groups' terms equal their L_S (TI1 part 1), the keep groups' terms are 0 = L_S (TI2 part 2 with eps_lin = 0), and the
packed groups' terms are at most L_S + sum of eps_act (part 2, as L_S >= 0). The stored arrays are per node and do not
depend on the level. QED.
Lean: `pack_step`, `phi_nonneg`, `phi_le_neg` in `lean/coarse/Coarse/Pack.lean`; the convexity step and the
bookkeeping by hand.
Check: `model/ts_tree.py` (parts A, B and D).
Comment. What it says about the network (my reading): a capability whose sub-capabilities each live on their own
inputs and favour their own classes can be squeezed to as many coarse units as its largest sub-capability moves its
own classes in. One coarse unit then means "the breed" on dog photos and "the make" on car photos. Under Hypothesis
H-active that price is small; Part C measures it on ResNet-18 and finds the canonical packed build too weak there.
This is the picture of a unit carrying mutually exclusive features (literature table), here derived from the KL
least, not assumed.

**Proposition TQ2 (the active-class summary, the positive least of row 3, and the failure of the tree knapsack) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, active-class summaries, squeeze-complete groups, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** Each part states the smaller set it uses.
1. (Under: none.) For every active-class summary, eps_act(A, K) = 0 exactly when Y = 0 on A.
2. (Under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, every claim it
   uses has eps = 0.) In the setting of B.Q, if k_S < rank Sigma_(W_S) (row 3), then L_S > 0.
3. (Under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read
   claims, active-class summaries, squeeze-complete groups, every claim it uses has eps = 0.) Let a > 0 and m >= 0.
   N has inputs (sigma, c_+, c_-), the 8 inputs (+1, c, 0) and (-1, 0, c) for c in {-3/2, -1/2, 1/2, 3/2}, each of
   weight 1/8, hidden units g_1 = relu(sigma), g_2 = relu(-sigma), u_1 = relu(c_+ + 2 + 10 (sigma - 1)),
   u_2 = relu(c_- + 2 - 10 (sigma + 1)), and 5 logits
   y = m (e_1 + e_2) g_1 + m (e_3 + e_4) g_2 + a (u_1 - 2 g_1)(e_1 - e_2) / sqrt 2 + a (u_2 - 2 g_2)(e_3 - e_4) / sqrt 2.
   The map has the districts {u_1, g_1} with region A_1 = {sigma = +1} and {u_2, g_2} with region A_2 = {sigma = -1};
   the group S is {u_1, u_2} with k_S = 1, nodes w_1, w_2 with T_(w_i) = {u_i}, J_(w_i) = {g_i}; K_1 = {1, 2},
   K_2 = {3, 4}. Then every claim of the setting holds with eps = 0, r^K_w = r_w = 1 <= k_S, and for every m large
   enough the least over boxes whose output direction lies on the line of Y_(w_1) or of Y_(w_2) is above L_S: one unit
   serving both nodes does better than every unit serving one.
Proof. (1) If Y = 0 on A, every argument of phi is -beta, and beta = 0 gives 0. Suppose Y(x) != 0 for some x.
(a) If rho_K(x) > 0 at some x, then for every i not in K the two arguments -Y(x)_i - beta +- rho_K(x) differ, so they
are not both 0, and g_(x,i)(beta) > 0 for every beta (phi >= 0 vanishes only at 0: Lean `phi_nonneg`,
`phi_eq_zero`); with s_(x,i) > 0 every class term is positive for every beta, and its minimum (attained, property
(2)) is positive. (b) If rho_K = 0 on A, then Y has its nonzero entries outside K; as Y is centred on A
(sum p_x Y(x) = 0) and not 0, some i not in K has Y(.)_i not constant on A, so -Y(x)_i - beta is not 0 at every x,
and the class term of i is positive for every beta. Either way eps_act > 0.
(2) Let k = k_S. Every choice has, on A_w, logits t_w + V C(x) with V C(x) in a subspace Q of dimension <= k of the
image of P_perp (after removing multiples of the all-ones vector, which change no softmax), and the infimum can only
fall when the box values are replaced by free values in Q at each point (free values include every box's values). So L_S >= min over k-dimensional subspaces Q of
F(Q) = sum over w of f_w(Q), f_w(Q) = inf over t in the image of P_perp and g_x in Q of
sum over A_w of p_x KL(s_x || softmax(t + g_x)). KL(s || softmax(l)) tends to infinity with |P_perp l|, uniformly over
the finitely many s_x (proof of TI3 part 2), so there is R, depending on the s_x only, with |t + g_x| <= R at every
point for every (t, g) whose terms are at most sum over w of I_w (the value at g = 0, t = log sbar_w, by Lemma TI0
and Gibbs). Shifting the mean of g into t (both lie in the image of P_perp, and Q is a subspace), take
sum over A_w of p_x g_x = 0; then |g_x| <= 2R and |t| <= R'. So, writing g_x = P_Q h_x with |h_x| <= 2R, f_w(Q) is a
minimum over a compact set of (t, h) that does not depend on Q of a function continuous in (Q, t, h) (Q through its orthogonal projection, on the compact Grassmannian of
k-dimensional subspaces of the image of P_perp): f_w is continuous and attained. If F(Q) = 0, each f_w(Q) = 0 is
attained, softmax(t_w + g_x) = s_x on A_w, so P_perp(y_N(x) - y_N(x')) = g_x - g_(x') lies in Q for x, x' in A_w,
hence every Y_w(x) lies in Q (Y_w(x) = P_perp y_N(x) - ybar_w; no linear-read claim is needed: under the on-inside
claim the centred part Ytil of DP1 is a linear combination of the Y_w(x'), so the image of Sigma_w lies in the span of
the Y_w(x)), the image of every Sigma_w lies in Q, and so does the image of
Sigma_(W_S) = sum of the Sigma_w (positive semidefinite): rank Sigma_(W_S) <= k, a contradiction. So F > 0 on the
compact Grassmannian, its minimum is > 0, and L_S >= that minimum.
(3) The claims: on A_1 (points (+1, c, 0)), g_1 = 1, g_2 = 0, the pre-activation of u_2 is 0 + 2 - 20 = -18 (so u_2 = 0),
u_1 = c + 2 >= 1/2 > 0; on A_2 (points (-1, 0, c)) the same with the indices swapped. So the district of w_i is 0 off
its region (district claims), its pre-activations are the constant -18 (u_i) and -1 (g_i) off its region (shelter
claims; with one input coordinate c for both areas this fails, REFEREE-BQ2 finding E1), u_i is on throughout A_i and
g_i is one value there (on-inside claims), no unit outside a district reads it (branch claims; one hidden layer, so the tree has one level and the judgment units J_(w_i) = {g_i} are kept), and
on A_i the logits are m(e's) + a (u_i - 2)(e's) / sqrt 2, affine in u_i (linear-read claims). Y_(w_1)(x) = a c (e_1 -
e_2) / sqrt 2 on A_1 (c has mean 0), so r^K_(w_1) = r_(w_1) = 1, and likewise for w_2; K_1 and K_2 are disjoint; so
the premises of TQ1 part 2 hold. Take the line of Y_(w_1), v = (e_1 - e_2) / sqrt 2 (the other line is the same with
the nodes swapped). On A_2 the logits of such a choice are t_2 + alpha_x v, which do not move the classes 3 and 4
against each other. By the chain rule of KL over a partition of the classes (for probability vectors s, q of full
support and a set K of classes, KL(s || q) = KL((s(K), 1 - s(K)) || (q(K), 1 - q(K))) + s(K) KL(s|K || q|K) +
(1 - s(K)) KL(s|not K || q|not K), where s|K is s restricted to K and renormalised; expand log(s_i / q_i) =
log(s(K) / q(K)) + log((s_i / s(K)) / (q_i / q(K))) for i in K and the same outside K; every term is >= 0),
KL(s || q) >= s(K_2) KL(s|K_2 || q|K_2) at each point. On A_2, s|K_2 = softmax(a c (1, -1) / sqrt 2) does not depend
on m, and q|K_2 is one vector on A_2 (v is 0 on K_2). So the terms on A_2 are at least (min over x in A_2 of
s_x(K_2)) J_2, with J_2 = min over q of sum over A_2 of p_x KL(s|K_2 || q) > 0 (s|K_2 varies with c) and
min over x of s_x(K_2) >= 1 - mu(A_2, K_2) / p_min = 1 - 8 mu(A_2, K_2). As m grows, mu(A_2, K_2) tends to 0 (the
other classes fall by m against K_2), so the pure least is at least J_2 / 2 for m large. On the other side, Y_w and
hence D_A do not depend on m, and every outside mass tends to 0, so eps_act(A_w, K_w) <= 2 D_(A_w) mu(A_w, K_w) tends
to 0 (Definition DQ1, property (3)). By TQ1 part 2, L_S <= eps_act(A_1, K_1) + eps_act(A_2, K_2) < J_2 / 2 for m
large. QED.
Lean: `phi_nonneg`, `phi_eq_zero` (part 1); parts 2 and 3 by hand (compactness; the chain rule over classes, proved
inline).
Check: `model/ts_sep.py` (part 3 at m in {0, 1, 3, 6}, Part C), `model/ts_tree.py` (part C: the minimum of F over
directions is > 0 for k = 1).
Comment. Part 2 covers all of row 3: a squeezed group always loses something. That is not a statement that row 3 has
no exact form (TI1's drop groups lose I_w > 0 and have one). Part 3 is why the plan's tree knapsack was the wrong
form: it carried the D2 picture (Ky Fan on a block-diagonal table) over to KL. KL measures each area's output in that
area's own Fisher metric (TI4), and in a confident area the other classes weigh almost nothing, so one direction can
carry different meanings on different areas. Part 3 proves it for m large; Part C (TQ2 part 3) reports smaller m.

**Theorem TQ3 (the clean-limit sandwich: a squeezed group is the sum of its areas' own problems) (under: plain
feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, active-class summaries, every
claim it uses has eps = 0).** In the setting of B.Q, let K_w (w in W_S) be pairwise disjoint class sets, mu_w =
mu(A_w, K_w), p_w = the least weight of a point of A_w, and for a probability vector s and a class set K let s|K be s
restricted to K and renormalised. For w in W_S and k >= 0 let
   L^c_w(k) = inf of sum over x in A_w of p_x KL(s_x|K_w || softmax((V C(x) + t)|K_w)),
the infimum over boxes of size k (reading T(S); units may switch) and vectors t: the **own-block problem** of w, a
|K_w|-class problem on A_w alone with N's conditional targets. Let L^(c,on)_w(k) be the same over boxes on at every
point of A_w, and L^on_S the least of the terms of L_S over boxes of S on at every point of S's areas (TI3 part 2).
1. (Lower side; any boxes.) L_S >= sum over w of (1 - mu_w / p_w)_+ L^c_w(k_S), and
   L^on_S >= sum over w of (1 - mu_w / p_w)_+ L^(c,on)_w(k_S).
2. (Upper side; the glued build.) For each w fix a choice of L^(c,on)_w(k_S) with block logits
   l_w(x) = tau_w + V_w c_w(x) on K_w (V_w a |K_w| x k_S matrix, c_w linear in ztil_w plus a constant), let Q_w be a
   |K_w| x k_S matrix of orthonormal or zero columns whose span contains that of V_w, chat_w(x) := Q_w^T V_w c_w(x)
   (so Q_w chat_w = V_w c_w), and rhat_w(x) = |l_w(x) - lbar_w|_2 = |chat_w(x) - mean|_2 (the size of the fit's own
   movement, lbar_w the p-mean of l_w on A_w), lambda_w(x) = lse_K(y_N(x)) - lse_K(l_w(x))
   (lse_K the log-sum-exp over the classes of K_w), and
   E_w = sum over i not in K_w of min over real beta of sum over x in A_w of p_x s_(x,i)
         max(phi(-y_N(x)_i + lambda_w(x) - beta + rhat_w(x)), phi(-y_N(x)_i + lambda_w(x) - beta - rhat_w(x))).
   Then L_S <= L^on_S <= sum over w of (the choice's terms for w) + sum over w of E_w. E_w is a summary of the kind
   of Definition DQ1 (with the fit's movement in place of N's): when the choice's block logits equal
   (P_perp y_N(x))|K_w plus one constant vector, E_w = eps_act(A_w, K_w). Closed upper form: E_w <= 2 D_w mu_w, D_w = max over x and i not in K_w of
   (|y_N(x)_i - mean over x of y_N(.)_i| + |lambda_w(x) - mean of lambda_w| + rhat_w(x)).
3. (The limit.) Let N_m be a family of networks with these premises in which P, the weights p and the top
   pre-activations z_(T(S)) on S's areas do not depend on m, and on each area the logits on K_w (up to one constant per
   point) and the variation of every logit (the y_N(x) minus their p-mean on A_w) do not depend on m, while the
   outside masses mu_w tend to 0 (at any rates; for example only the logit weights of the judgment units change). Then
   L^on_S(N_m) - sum over w of L^(c,on)_w(k_S) -> 0, and when the sum is > 0 the ratio tends to 1.
   The same holds for L_S and the L^c_w when the always-on and the switching leasts of every own-block problem agree
   (Conjecture DI2 asks whether they can differ).
Proof. (1) Take any choice of L_S; on A_w its logits are l(x) = V C(x) + t_w. The chain rule of KL over the classes
(proof of TQ2 part 3) gives KL(s_x || softmax(l)) >= s_x(K_w) KL(s_x|K_w || softmax(l)|K_w), and softmax(l)|K_w =
softmax(l|K_w) with l|K_w = V|K_w C(x) + t_w|K_w, so the box with the logit rows V|K_w and the vector t_w|K_w is a choice
of the own-block problem of w. s_x(K_w) = 1 - s_x(not K_w) >= 1 - mu_w / p_w at every point of A_w (mu_w is a
p-weighted sum of nonnegative terms, each at most mu_w / p_w after dividing by its weight). So the terms of w are at
least (1 - mu_w / p_w)_+ L^c_w(k_S); the box is shared, but each bound is a bound on one area's terms, and they add.
For boxes on throughout S's areas the restriction to A_w is on at every point of A_w, which gives the second line.
(2) The build: one box of k_S units, on throughout, whose unit j reads on the top of each w the j-th row of the read
of chat_w (the reads of different w sit on disjoint coordinates T_w; on A_w the other tops sit at their shelter
values, premise 1 of TH1, which add a constant per area), with logit weights V = sum over w of Pi^(K_w) Q_w (the rows
of K_w are Q_w; rows outside every K are 0), and t_w chosen below. On A_w its logits on K_w are tau_w + Q_w chat_w(x) +
a constant = l_w(x) + a constant, and on a class i not in K_w they are a constant plus leak_(x,i), with leak_(x,i) =
(Q_(w') chat_w(x))_i when i lies in K_(w') (one w' at most, the K are disjoint) and 0 otherwise; centring chat_w (the
mean goes into t_w), |leak_(x,i)| <= |Q_(w') (chat_w(x) - mean)|_2 <= rhat_w(x). Compare with the reference q° on A_w:
q°|K_w = softmax(l_w(x)), q°(K_w) = s_x(K_w), and q° = s_x outside K_w. By the chain rule,
KL(s_x || q°) = s_x(K_w) KL(s_x|K_w || softmax(l_w(x))) <= KL(s_x|K_w || softmax(l_w(x))). The build's logits are
log q° + d_x with d constant on K_w, equal to lse_K(l_w) - lse_K(y_N) + lse(y_N); subtracting that constant from all
of d (it changes no softmax), d becomes 0 on K_w and, for i not in K_w, d_(x,i) = (t_w)_i + leak_(x,i) - y_N(x)_i +
lambda_w(x) + (a constant per class), so with (t_w)_i set to -beta_i plus the constants, d_(x,i) = -y_N(x)_i +
lambda_w(x) - beta_i + leak_(x,i) up to the class means that beta absorbs. For any full-support q° and d,
KL(s || softmax(log q° + d)) = KL(s || q°) + log(sum over i of q°_i e^(d_i)) - sum over i of s_i d_i
                            <= KL(s || q°) + sum over i of (q°_i e^(d_i) - q°_i - s_i d_i)
by log z <= z - 1 and sum q° = 1. The classes of K_w give q°_i e^0 - q°_i - 0 = 0; for i not in K_w, q°_i = s_(x,i),
so the term is s_(x,i) phi(d_(x,i)), and with |leak| <= rhat_w(x) and phi convex it is at most the max in E_w. Summing
with p_x and the minimising beta gives the terms of w <= (the choice's terms for w) + E_w. The closed form: beta_i at
the top of its range makes every argument of phi lie in [-2 D_w, 0], where phi(t) <= -t (property (3) of DQ1).
(3) In N_m the conditional targets s_x|K_w (the softmax of the logits on K_w), the weights and the box's inputs
z_(T(S)) are fixed, so each own-block problem, and L^(c,on)_w(k_S), does not depend on m. For e > 0 fix, for each w,
one choice within e of L^(c,on)_w(k_S), the same for every m; its lambda_w and rhat_w are then fixed, and so is D_w
(the variation of y_N is fixed by premise). Hence
sum over w of (1 - mu_w / p_w)_+ L^(c,on)_w(k_S) <= L^on_S(N_m) <= sum over w of L^(c,on)_w(k_S) + sum over w of 2 D_w mu_w + |W_S| e.
Both sides tend to the sum (up to |W_S| e, for every e > 0) as every mu_w tends to 0.
The last sentence: the same squeeze with L^c_w in place of
L^(c,on)_w on the lower side and L_S <= L^on_S on the upper side. QED.
Lean: `pack_step2`, `phi_le_neg` (`Coarse/Pack.lean`); the chain rule over classes by hand (proved in TQ2 part 3).
Check: `model/ts_tq3.py`.
Note: the K_w are the analyst's choice, not a property of N, so the disjointness premise narrows no network.
Label: not one of the bar's four labels; a two-sided limit (LIMIT). It does not meet the bar as stated, since the
gap is in summaries of N and closes only in the limit. What TQ3 adds beyond TQ1: when every own-class rank is <= k_S
and the linear-read claims hold, every own-block least is 0 and TQ3 says no more than TQ1 part 2. Its content is the
case where an area is squeezed below its own rank. What it does meet, said precisely: when some area's own-block least is > 0 (an area squeezed below the
rank of its own movement), the gap over the least tends to 0 while the least stays positive: the bar's "reaches V(G)
even where V(G) > 0", in the limit of clean (confident) areas, and for boxes on throughout.
Remark (the recursion is open). An own-block problem with its rank above k_S is again a squeeze, of one area. Only
the lower side (part 1) carries over to a split of A_w into sub-areas with disjoint sub-blocks: the box of w reads the
top of w, one affine map of z_(T_w) on all of A_w, so the gluing of part 2 (different reads on disjoint coordinates) is
not available below the top (REFEREE-BQ2 finding E3). The recursion is Conjecture DQ3 (Part D.18).

**Lemma TQ4 (lining up two areas: reverse pairing) (under: none).** Let P and Q be k x k positive definite matrices
with eigenvalues p_1 >= ... >= p_k and q_1 <= ... <= q_k (P's in descending, Q's in ascending order), and c > 0. Then
   min over invertible k x k T of tr(T P T^T) + c tr(T^(-1) Q T^(-T)) = 2 sqrt(c) (sqrt(p_1 q_1) + ... + sqrt(p_k q_k)),
attained by T = W diag(t_1, ..., t_k) U^T with U the eigenvectors of P in the order of the p_i, W those of Q in the
order of the q_i, and t_i^2 = sqrt(c q_i / p_i). So the strongest direction of P is lined up with the weakest of Q.
Proof. Write T = W' D U' (singular value decomposition, D = diag(d_i) > 0, d_1 <= ... <= d_k). Then tr(T P T^T) =
tr(D^2 U'^T P U') and tr(T^(-1) Q T^(-T)) = tr(D^(-2) W'^T Q W'). By the lower trace inequality of von Neumann (for
symmetric A and B, tr(AB) >= sum over i of a_i^(down) b_i^(up), the eigenvalues paired largest with smallest),
tr(D^2 U'^T P U') >= sum over i of p_i d_i^2 (the d_i^2 ascending against the p_i descending), and
tr(D^(-2) W'^T Q W') >= sum over i of q_i / d_i^2 (the 1 / d_i^2 descending against the q_i ascending). So the sum is
at least sum over i of (p_i d_i^2 + c q_i / d_i^2) >= sum over i of 2 sqrt(c p_i q_i) (the arithmetic-geometric mean
inequality, with equality at d_i^2 = sqrt(c q_i / p_i)). These d_i^2 are ascending (q_i ascending, p_i descending),
so with U' = U, W' = W in the stated orders both trace inequalities hold with equality and the bound is reached. QED.
Lean: none (von Neumann's trace inequality is not in Mathlib in this form); `model/ts_tq4.py` checks it on random
matrices against a direct minimisation.
Comment. In the second-order regime of TI4 with small outside masses, this is the cost of sharing k units between two
areas that each fill all k: P and Q are each area's movement in its box coordinates, weighted by the other area's
second-moment metric of the leaked classes (Conjecture DQ2). It says how to line up the shared directions in closed
form, and that the best alignment is not a balancing (the Hankel singular values of control theory solve a different
problem, with one covariance and one metric): each area's strongest direction should share a unit with the other's
weakest.

**Definition DQ5 (the leak problem of a squeezed group) (added 2026-11-01).** In the setting of B.Q, let the
linear-read claims hold with eps = 0 and let K_w (w in W_S) be pairwise disjoint class sets with 0 < |K_w| < n_y. For x in A_w and a
class i not in K_w let
   rho_(x,i) = exp(y_N(x)_i) / (sum over j in K_w of exp(y_N(x)_j)),
the odds of class i against the block K_w at x. Let Z_w be the span of the ztil_w(x), x in A_w. A **leak point** is a
tuple (L_w, g_w, beta_w), w in W_S, of a linear map L_w from Z_w into the image of P_perp, a linear functional g_w on
Z_w and a vector beta_w in R^(n_y), such that
   (a) the sum over w of the images of the L_w has dimension at most k_S; and
   (b) on its own block each L_w moves as N does: Pi^(K_w) L_w ztil_w(x) = Pi^(K_w) Y_w(x) + (g_w ztil_w(x)) 1_(K_w)
       for every x in A_w.
Its value is
   Lambda(L, g, beta) = sum over w of sum over x in A_w of p_x sum over i not in K_w of rho_(x,i) phi(d_(x,i)),
   d_(x,i) = (L_w ztil_w(x))_i - Y_w(x)_i - g_w ztil_w(x) - beta_(w,i),
and the **leak least** Lambda_S is the infimum of the values over all leak points (+infinity if there is none).
Properties. (1) Lambda_S reads only N's logits on S's areas, the features ztil_w, the weights p, the K_w and k_S.
(2) With k = min(k_S, n_y - 1), for a fixed subspace Q of dimension k of the image of P_perp, the leak points with every image inside Q form a
convex set (conditions (a) and (b) become linear), and Lambda is convex on it (phi is convex and each d_(x,i) is
affine in (L, g, beta)). So, as in Theorem TI3 part 2, the only non-convex choice is Q. (3) When every own-class rank
r^K(A_w) <= k_S, leak points exist: with U_w and V = sum over w of Pi^(K_w) U_w as in Theorem TQ1 part 2, the maps
L_w = P_perp V U_w^T Pi^(K_w) B_w meet (a) (images in P_perp of the image of V) and (b) (Pi^(K_w) V U_w^T Pi^(K_w) Y_w =
Pi^(K_w) Y_w, and P_perp subtracts one multiple of the all-ones vector per point, linear in ztil_w).
Comment. Condition (b) says that the coarse units reproduce each area's own movement exactly, up to one shift of its
block per point. What is left to choose is how each area's movement spills onto the other areas' blocks and onto the
classes in no block (the d_(x,i)); Lambda weighs each spill by its odds rho. In the family of Theorem TQ5, e^m times
N_m's probability of class i at x tends to rho_(x,i).

**Theorem TQ5 (the confident limit to first order: along N_m, the always-on least of a complete squeeze is the leak least) (under: plain
feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, active-class
summaries, squeeze-complete groups, every claim it uses has eps = 0).** In the setting of B.Q, let the linear-read
claims hold with eps = 0, let the K_w be pairwise disjoint, and let r^K(A_w) <= k_S for every w in W_S. For m >= 0 let
N_m be N with the logits of every class outside K_w lowered by m on A_w, for every w in W_S (for example by adding
-m (1 - 1_(K_w)) to the logit weights of w's judgment units, which are on throughout A_w with a_w^T h_(J_w) = 1, or,
when W_S has one node whose area is all of P, to the logit bias); every area is lowered by the same m; P,
the weights, the top pre-activations, the movements Y_w and the claims are those of N. Let L^on_S(m) be the least of
the terms of L_S for N_m over boxes on throughout S's areas (Theorem TI3 part 2). Then:
1. Lambda_S is finite and attained.
2. (Upper side, every m.) Every leak point gives an always-on box whose terms for N_m are at most
   e^(-m) Lambda(L, g, beta). So L^on_S(m) <= e^(-m) Lambda_S for every m >= 0.
3. (Lower side.) L^on_S(m) >= e^(-m) Lambda_S - o(e^(-m)) as m -> infinity. So e^m L^on_S(m) -> Lambda_S, and the box
   of part 2 at a minimiser of Lambda has terms within o(e^(-m)) of the least, a relative gap that tends to 0 when
   Lambda_S > 0.
Proof. One point. Fix w, x in A_w, and write s = softmax(y_(N_m)(x)), q = softmax(l) for logits l, u = sum over i not
in K_w of s_i / s(K_w) and v = sum over i not in K_w of q_i / q(K_w). Define delta_i for i not in K_w by
q_i / q(K_w) = (s_i / s(K_w)) e^(delta_i). By the construction of N_m, s_i / s(K_w) = e^(-m) rho_(x,i) exactly, so
u = e^(-m) R_x with R_x = sum over i not in K_w of rho_(x,i), v = e^(-m) sum of rho_(x,i) e^(delta_i), s(K_w) = 1/(1+u),
q(K_w) = 1/(1+v). Splitting the sum of KL(s || q) into the classes of K_w and the others, and writing
log(s_i / q_i) = log(s_i / s(K)) - log(q_i / q(K)) + log(s(K) / q(K)) for i outside K = K_w,
   KL(s || q) = s(K) KL(s|K || q|K) + E,   E = log((1 + v)/(1 + u)) - sum over i not in K of s_i delta_i     (exact).
With s_i = e^(-m) rho_(x,i) / (1 + u) and e^(-m) sum of rho_i delta_i = (v - u) - e^(-m) sum of rho_i phi(delta_i),
and w := (v - u)/(1 + u) > -1,
   E = log(1 + w) - w + e^(-m) (sum over i not in K of rho_(x,i) phi(delta_i)) / (1 + u).      (*)
(2) Let (L, g, beta) be a leak point. Write the stacked map [L_w] as V Phi with V an n_y x k_S matrix and Phi_w maps
from Z_w to R^(k_S) (condition (a)), and extend Phi_w to all of R^(T_w) by 0 on a complement of Z_w. Take the box of
k_S units, unit j reading the j-th row of Phi_w on the coordinates T_w for every w (the T_w are disjoint) with the bias
of TP1 part 2, so that it is on at every point of P, and logit weights V. On A_w the other tops sit at their shelter
values (premise 2 of TH1), and ztil_w = z_(T_w) minus its p-mean on A_w (F_w is the constants, as in TI4), so the box
writes V Phi_w ztil_w(x) = L_w ztil_w(x) plus a vector constant on A_w, which t_w absorbs: the logits on A_w are
l(x) = L_w ztil_w(x) + t_w. Choose Pi^(K) t_w = Pi^(K) ybar_w and, for i not in K, (t_w)_i = (ybar_w)_i - m - beta_(w,i).
N_m's logits on A_w are ybar_w - m (1 - 1_K) + Y_w(x) plus a multiple of the all-ones vector per point. By (b), on K
the two differ by one multiple of 1_K per point, (g_w ztil_w(x) + c_x) 1_K, so q|K = s|K, and delta_i = l_i - y_(N_m)(x)_i
minus that multiple, which is d_(x,i). In (*), log(1 + w) - w <= 0, so KL(s || q) = E <= e^(-m) sum of rho_(x,i)
phi(d_(x,i)). Weighting by p_x and adding over x and w gives the terms <= e^(-m) Lambda(L, g, beta).
(1) and (3) by compactness. Lower bound on one point: by Lean `log_one_add_ge`, log(1 + w) - w >= -w^2 / (1 + w), so
(*) gives KL(s || q) >= s(K) KL(s|K || q|K) - w^2/(1 + w) + e^(-m) (sum of rho_i phi(delta_i)) / (1 + u).    (**)
Let R be the largest R_x and p_min the least weight on S's areas. Take m with e^(-m) R <= 1, so u <= 1 and
w >= -1/2. For any always-on choice with terms T_m <= e^(-m)(Lambda_S + 1) (there are such, by part 2 with
Lambda_S < infinity by property (3) of DQ5): at each point, KL(s || q) <= T_m / p_min.
Step A (v is of order e^(-m)). phi(t) >= e^t / 2 - 2 for every real t (e^t / 2 + 1 - t > 0), so
sum of rho_i phi(delta_i) >= e^m v / 2 - 2 R, and, as 1 <= 1 + u <= 2, the last term of (**) is at least
v/4 - 2 e^(-m) R. Also w = (v - u)/(1 + u) lies in [-u, v], so w^2 <= v^2 + u^2 and, with 1 + w >= 1/2,
w^2/(1 + w) <= 2 v^2 + 2 e^(-2m) R^2. Case v <= 1/16: 2 v^2 <= v/8, and (**) gives
T_m / p_min >= v/8 - 2 e^(-m) R - 2 e^(-2m) R^2, so v <= 8 (T_m / p_min + 2 e^(-m) R + 2 e^(-2m) R^2), of order
e^(-m). Case v > 1/16: from the exact form of E, since s_i <= e^(-m) rho_i, log(1 + u) <= u and
delta_i <= m + log v - log rho_i (because e^(-m) rho_i e^(delta_i) <= v),
E >= log(1 + v) - e^(-m) R - e^(-m) R (m + c_0 + log^+ v), with c_0 the largest -log rho_(x,i) (finitely many) and
log^+ v = max(log v, 0) <= log(1 + v). Take m so large that e^(-m) R <= 1/4 and e^(-m) R (1 + m + c_0) <=
(1/4) log(17/16). Then for every v > 1/16 the subtracted terms are at most (1/4) log(1 + v) + (1/4) log(1 + v), and
KL(s || q) >= E >= (1/2) log(1 + v) >= (1/2) log(17/16), which is above T_m / p_min once m is large. So for m large
v <= 1/16, v and |w| are at most a constant times e^(-m), and w^2/(1 + w) is at most a constant times e^(-2m).
Step B (the spills). With Step A, (**) gives, after weighting and adding, sum over w and x of p_x sum of
rho_(x,i) phi(delta_(x,i)) <= (1 + e^(-m) R) (e^m T_m + c e^(-m)), and, as s(K) >= 1/2 and KL(s || q) >= s(K) KL(s|K || q|K) - w^2/(1 + w), sum of p_x KL(s|K || q|K) <=
2 (T_m + c e^(-2m)), which tends to 0.
Suppose e^m L^on_S(m) <= Lambda_S - e along a sequence of m tending to infinity, for some e > 0, and take choices with
e^m T_m <= Lambda_S - e/2 there. Then the spill sums are at most Lambda_S - e/4 for m large. On A_w, the choice's
logits are V C(x) + t_w with V C(x) = V M_w ztil_w(x) plus a constant (TI3 part 2, lower bound), and the stacked map
[V M_w] has rank <= k_S; put L^m_w = P_perp V M_w (adding a multiple of the all-ones vector changes no softmax), which
meets (a). Since s|K does not depend on m and has full support, KL(s|K || q|K) -> 0 at each of the finitely many points
forces the logits of q on K, centred over K, to converge to those of s: with P^K the centring over K,
P^K (L^m_w ztil_w(x) + t^m_w - ybar_w - Y_w(x)) -> 0 at every x of A_w; averaging over A_w with the weights p (ztil_w
and Y_w are centred on A_w) gives P^K (t^m_w - ybar_w) -> 0, and then P^K (L^m_w ztil_w(x) - Y_w(x)) -> 0; so
Pi^K L^m_w ztil_w(x) = Pi^K Y_w(x) +
(g^m_w ztil_w(x)) 1_K + e^m_w(x) with g^m_w the K-mean of (L^m_w - B_w) (a linear functional) and e^m_w(x) -> 0, and
delta^m_(x,i) = d_(x,i)(L^m, g^m, beta^m) + o(1) for suitable vectors beta^m (the shift of the K-log-sum-exp is the
K-mean plus a term that tends to 0). Boundedness: the spill sums bound every delta^m (phi is coercive and every
p_x rho_(x,i) > 0); as ztil_w is centred on A_w (sum of p_x ztil_w(x) = 0), a bound on f(x) - beta for a linear f at
every point of A_w bounds beta and f; so on every row the values L^m_w ztil_w(x) - (g^m_w ztil_w(x)) 1 are bounded (outside
K by the spills, on K by the convergence), and since L^m_w is P_perp-valued, L^m_w ztil_w(x) is their image under
P_perp, hence bounded; then g^m_w ztil_w(x) and beta^m are bounded. The values at the finitely many points fix the maps
on Z_w, so a subsequence converges to (L*, g*, beta*). The limit meets (a) (the matrices of rank <= k_S form a closed
set) and (b) (e^m_w -> 0), and by continuity Lambda(L*, g*, beta*) <= Lambda_S - e/4 < Lambda_S, against the definition
of Lambda_S. So liminf of e^m L^on_S(m) >= Lambda_S, which with part 2 is part 3. Part 1: a minimising sequence of
leak points has bounded d (coercivity of phi), hence bounded (L, g, beta) by the same argument, and a limit point is a
leak point with value Lambda_S. QED.
Lean: `log_one_add_ge` (`Coarse/Pack.lean`); the splitting of KL and the compactness by hand.
Check: `model/tq_leak.py`.
Label: LIMIT-1 (exact first-order coefficient, two-sided; not one of the bar's four labels). What it adds to TQ3: in
the complete case TQ3's lower side is 0 and its upper side a bound; TQ5 gives the exact leading term on both sides,
and a build that reaches it. In words: when the areas are confident, the least of a squeeze is the odds-weighted spill
of the best way to share the units, and nothing else. What it does not do, said plainly: it gives Lambda_S as a least
over output spans of convex problems (property (2) of DQ5), not in closed form, and it is a statement about the limit
m -> infinity, not at the network's own confidence. Its scope, said precisely: the lower side is about boxes on throughout (L^on_S; whether switching boxes go lower is
Conjecture DI2's question); the family lowers every area by the same m; and part 3 gives no rate for the o(e^(-m)).
REFEREE-BQ3-2026-11-01.md: correct after the repairs of Step A and Step B (findings E1, G1 to G3).

**Lemma TQ6 (equal spills: the least off-diagonal energy of a rank-k matrix with unit diagonal) (under: none).** Let
n >= k >= 1 be integers. For every real n x n matrix X of rank at most k with X_ii = 1 for every i,
   sum over i != j of X_ij^2 >= n^2 / k - n.
Equality holds exactly when X = (n/k) P with P a symmetric orthogonal projection of rank k whose diagonal entries all
equal k/n. Such P exist for every n >= k.
Proof. Let sigma_1, ..., sigma_k be the k largest singular values of X (the others are 0) and X = U Sigma W^T a
singular value decomposition. Then n = tr X = tr(Sigma W^T U) = sum over i <= k of sigma_i (W^T U)_ii <= sum over
i <= k of sigma_i, since the entries of the orthogonal matrix W^T U are at most 1 in absolute value. By the
Cauchy-Schwarz step (Lean `sq_sum_le_card_fin`), (sum over i <= k of sigma_i)^2 <= k sum of sigma_i^2 = k |X|_F^2. So
|X|_F^2 >= n^2 / k, and subtracting the n diagonal entries gives the bound. Equality forces equality in both steps:
all sigma_i (i <= k) equal, hence equal to n/k, and (W^T U)_ii = 1 for i <= k, so the first k columns of U and W
agree and X = (n/k) U_k U_k^T = (n/k) P with P the projection onto the span of those columns; X_ii = 1 gives
P_ii = k/n. Conversely such an X has rank k, unit diagonal, |X|_F^2 = (n/k)^2 k = n^2/k. Existence: for n = k take
P = I. For n > k, let F be the k x n matrix with rows sqrt(2/n) cos(2 pi l j / n) and sqrt(2/n) sin(2 pi l j / n),
j = 1, ..., n, for l = 1, ..., floor(k/2), and, when k is odd, one more row with every entry 1/sqrt(n). The
frequencies l are below n/2, so the rows are orthonormal (sums of cos^2 and sin^2 over a full period give n/2, the
cross sums vanish), and every column has squared norm (2/n) floor(k/2) + (k - 2 floor(k/2))/n = k/n. Then P = F^T F is
a symmetric projection of rank k with diagonal k/n. QED.
Lean: `sq_sum_le_card_fin` (`Coarse/Pack.lean`); the singular value steps by hand.

Comment. Where it may enter (route only, Conjecture DQ4; not derived here, REFEREE-BQ3 finding G5): when every area
of a squeezed group moves its own block in one direction, the small-movement form of the leak problem should reduce to
numbers X_(w'w) (the spill of area w's coarse code onto block w', relative to w''s own read), forming a matrix of
rank at most k_S with unit diagonal. The spills are vectors on each block, so the reduction needs the own directions
centred on their blocks (else the rank bound becomes k_S + 1) and is exact only when the odds are equal within each
block; otherwise two weighted problems of this shape bound the leak least from both sides. Under that reduction, with
equal strengths and equal odds, the least spill is n^2/k - n times one constant, reached when the coarse units hold
the areas' directions as an equal-norm tight frame (frame theory, literature table).

**Proposition TQ7 (one metric for the group: the shared span, to second order, within the spread of the areas'
metrics) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read
claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0) (added 2026-11-01).** Let M, G and S meet the premises of Theorem TI4, with its
notation (Sigma_w, H_w, psi_w, Phi, L_S(a), L^on_S(a), k = min(k_S, n_y - 1)). Let Hb be positive definite on the image
of P_perp, and let eta in [0, 1) satisfy (1 - eta) Hb <= H_w <= (1 + eta) Hb (Loewner order, on the image of P_perp)
for every w in W_S. Let M_b = Hb^(1/2) Sigma_(W_S) Hb^(1/2) and Q_b = Hb^(-1/2) times the span of the top k
eigenvectors of M_b (the **shared span** in the metric Hb; it is computed from N alone, by one eigenvector problem).
1. (1 - eta) (1/2) tail_k(M_b) <= Phi <= (1 + eta) (1/2) tail_k(M_b).
2. (1/2) sum over w of psi_w(Q_b) <= ((1 + eta)/(1 - eta)) Phi.
3. The always-on box of TI4's upper bound built at Q_b has terms at most a^2 ((1 + eta)/(1 - eta)) Phi + O(a^3), while
   L_S(a) >= a^2 Phi - O(a^3). So, to second order, the shared span is within the factor (1 + eta)/(1 - eta) of the
   least, and the factor tends to 1 as eta does. With eta = 0 this is Theorem TI4 part 2.
Proof. For y in the image of P_perp and a subspace Q of it, write r_H(y, Q) = min over b in Q of |y - b|_H^2 (|v|_H^2 =
v^T H v). As shown in the proof of TI4 (upper bound), psi_w(Q) = sum over x in A_w of p_x r_(H_w)(Y_w(x), Q): the
H_w-orthogonal projection onto Q leaves exactly that residual. If (1 - eta) Hb <= H <= (1 + eta) Hb, then for every b,
(1 - eta) |y - b|_Hb^2 <= |y - b|_H^2 <= (1 + eta) |y - b|_Hb^2, and taking the minimum over b in Q on each side,
(1 - eta) r_Hb(y, Q) <= r_H(y, Q) <= (1 + eta) r_Hb(y, Q). Summing over x and w with the weights p,
   (1 - eta) Psi(Q) <= sum over w of psi_w(Q) <= (1 + eta) Psi(Q),   Psi(Q) = sum over w and x in A_w of p_x r_Hb(Y_w(x), Q).
Psi is the one-metric objective of TI4 part 2 with H = Hb: by that proof (Ky Fan's principle), min over Q of Psi(Q) =
tail_k(M_b), attained at Q_b. (1) Phi = (1/2) min over Q of sum psi_w lies between (1/2)(1 - eta) min Psi and
(1/2)(1 + eta) min Psi. (2) sum psi_w(Q_b) <= (1 + eta) Psi(Q_b) = (1 + eta) min Psi <= ((1 + eta)/(1 - eta)) min over Q
of sum psi_w = ((1 + eta)/(1 - eta)) 2 Phi. (3) The upper-bound computation in the proof of TI4 holds for any
k-dimensional Q, not only a minimiser: the box at Q has terms (a^2/2) sum over w of psi_w(Q) + O(a^3). Use (2), and
TI4 part 1 for the lower bound. QED.
