Comment (read as a network). This is a clean case in which relatives share a pole at several levels of one zoom, and it is the structured counterpart of Theorem TQ17, whose tails are level. Part 5 says plainly how narrow it is: fine distinctions below 1/K in probability. So it is not yet "coarser, never fractured" at a network's own confidence. Exact symmetry enters here only as a clean case to check against, not as a principle of clean. Label: certificate of the table least, the value a convex program of m numbers.

**Corollary TQ18.1 (the test on a network: when one read is exactly the least) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-01; widened after REFEREE-BQ10).** Let S be a group, T the other units of the last hidden layer, and Y the span of 1 and h_T on P. Let (A, V, c) be a stationary triple for free codes on P (Z = R^n), with g <= rho and g <= rho sigma / 2, and let the columns of c lie in the span of Y and z_S on P. Then V_b(k) = L_on(k) = L_free(k) = D(A, V, c), and no network with k new top units that keeps T's values has a lower loss on P.
Proof. Theorem TQ18 part 1 gives L_free(k) = D(A, V, c). The triple's codes are, on P, affine in z_S plus a part in the span of h_T, and A takes that part, so L_on(k) <= D(A, V, c). Proposition TQ11 parts 1 and 2 close the chain. QED.

Comment. This holds at any k, for codes in the span of Y and z_S, with no claim on the map: the rule's one-time computation finds a triple and runs the test. The same holds on a region table through Theorem TQ14 part 4, where the test is easier, since with n photos against K regions g <= rho worsens by about the square root of n / K. Label: OPT-KL, exact case only. Parts 3 and 5 of Theorem TQ18 give its graded form in the test and in the defects, not in N's cleanliness. Part C measures how far real networks are from the test.

**Lemma TQ19 (lumping the tail) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Let s be a positive distribution on C classes, H a set of classes, zeta the mass of s outside H, w the tail of s normalised, s# = (s on H, zeta), and for a logit vector l let l# = (l on H, <w, l> + H(w)), with H(w) the entropy of w.
1. KL(s || softmax(l)) >= KL(s# || softmax(l#)).
2. So if the rows share one H and one w (s_x on the tail equals zeta_x w), the lumped rows are a case of Definition DQ14 with C' = |H| + 1, and the rank of the logit part does not rise. Then L_Z(k) >= L#_Z(k), and Theorem TQ18 on a lumped triple gives a lower bound on L_Z(k). Theorem TQ18 there needs C' >= k + 2. For free codes, |H| >= k + 1 is needed in any case, since otherwise the lumped least is 0 (Proposition TQ11 part 4). If the tail is empty, there is no lump and the statement is trivial.
Proof. (1) With A the log-sum-exp, KL(s || softmax(l)) = A(l) - <s, l> - H(s). By Jensen, the log of the sum of exp(l_i) over the tail is at least <w, l> + H(w). So A(l) >= A(l#). And <s, l> = <s on H, l on H> + zeta <w, l>, and H(s) = H(s#) + zeta H(w), so that -<s, l> - H(s) = -<s#, l#> - H(s#), since the last entry of l# carries zeta H(w). (2) l# is linear in l on the common H and w, with an added constant, so a rank-limited logit stays rank-limited. QED.
Lean: none, by hand (Jensen, one line).

### B.Q.10 Results of the fan-out rounds (added 2026-11-01; statements and proofs by round agents, checked by hostile referees; files `rounds/round1_full.jsonl`, `rounds/round2_full.jsonl`)

The round names (D3, E6, C10 and so on) are kept in brackets, because the proofs cite them. Each item carries the referee's correction where there was one. No result here meets the bar: none is OPT-KL on a table with real structure, and real networks miss the premise of each certificate (Part C). Numbers in the agents' proofs moved to Part C and to the round files.

**Theorem TZ1 (the patchwork certificate: one local projector per patch; round name D3) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Theorem D3 (the patchwork certificate: a dual point with one local projector per patch). Let rows x carry p_x, s_x, and let l_x = t + V c_x be a rank-k build, q_x = softmax(l_x), G = D_p(S - Q). A patch b is a set of rows R_b, a set of classes H_b with |H_b| >= k + 2, and matrices G_b on R_b x H_b with sum over b of G_b = G. Let L_b be the block of l, doubly centred, assumed of rank exactly k. Assume G_b 1 = 0, 1^T G_b = 0, G_b L_b^T = 0, L_b^T G_b = 0. Choose shares w_b >= 0 on R_b x H_b, with sum over b of w_b[x, i] <= p_x q_x[i]. For a competitor, let Pi_b be a projector of rank |H_b| - 1 - k on R^(H_b), with Pi_b killing 1 and V' restricted to H_b. Let Phi_b(Pi_b) be matrices on R_b x H_b with Phi_b 1 = 0, 1^T Phi_b = 0, and (G_b + Phi_b) killing 1 and V' on H_b. If for every Pi_b: Val_b = <Phi_b, l> - sum over x, i of w_b[x, i] phi(-Phi_b[x, i] / w_b[x, i]) >= 0, with all arguments >= -1, then L_free(k) = D(build) = the sum of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)). Test Q gives Val_b >= 0. Take a positive vector eta on H_b, summing to 1. Whiten: Gt = G_b D_eta^(-1/2). Let Ut be an orthonormal basis of the k-dimensional whitened span, Pi0 the projector onto the complement of D_eta^(1/2) 1 and Ut, Pi_eta the same for the competitor. Let r_x = min over i of w_b[x, i] / eta_i, rt_x = min over i of w_b[x, i] / sqrt(eta_i), and ct the row codes in Ut. Let B be any matrix with 1^T B = 0 and ct^T B = I. Test Q: some w >= 0 has |Gt_x|^2 + w^2 |B_x|^2 <= rt_x^2 for every x, and 2 |D_r^(-1/2) (Gt Gt^T + w^2 B B^T) D_r^(-1/2)|_op <= w. Test F is Theorem D4 below, applied inside the patch.
Proof. Let G° = sum over b of (G_b + Phi_b) and q°_x = s_x - G°_x / p_x = q_x - (sum over b of Phi_b[x]) / p_x. Row sums are 1. On each patch G_b + Phi_b kills 1 and V', and its columns sum to 0 (1^T G_b = 0, 1^T Phi_b = 0), so the sum over x of p_x <q°_x - s_x, t' + V' c'_x> = 0. Weak duality (part 1 of TQ13) gives D(competitor) >= the sum of p_x (H(q°_x) - H(s_x)). By (E) of TQ17, the sum of p_x (H(q°_x) - H(q_x)) = the sum over b of <Phi_b, l> - the sum over x, i of p_x q_x[i] phi(d / q_x[i]), with d = -(sum over b of Phi_b[x, i]) / p_x, since rows of Phi_b sum to 0. The map (w, y) -> w phi(y / w) is the perspective of a convex function, so it is jointly convex and homogeneous, hence subadditive: p q phi(d / q) <= the sum over b of w_b phi(-Phi_b / w_b), and the leftover share carries y = 0 and costs 0. The same subadditivity gives q + d >= 0 from the arguments >= -1. So D(competitor) >= the sum of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)) + the sum over b of Val_b. Finally D(build) = the sum of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)) - <G, l>, and <G_b, l> = <G_b, L_b> = 0, because G_b has zero row and column sums and is orthogonal to L_b. Test Q: let Ett = Pi_eta - Pi0, Rt = Gt + w B Ut^T, Phi_b = (Rt Ett) D_eta^(1/2). Then Rt Pi0 = Gt, since Gt Pi0 = Gt and Ut^T Pi0 = 0, so G_b + Phi_b = Rt Pi_eta D_eta^(1/2), which kills 1 and V'. 1^T Rt = 0. Linear term: rows of Phi_b sum to 0 (Ett kills D_eta^(1/2) 1) and columns sum to 0. So <Phi_b, l> = <Rt Ett, Lt>, with Lt the row-centred, eta-centred, whitened block = ct Ut^T. The left space of Lt is the left space of L_b, so ct^T Gt = 0, and <Phi_b, l> = w tr(Ut^T Pi_eta Ut) =: w X. Also |Ett|_F^2 = 2 X, by equal ranks, as in (F) of TQ18, and |Ett|_op <= 1. Positivity: |Phi_b[x, i]| <= |Rt_x| sqrt(eta_i) <= rt_x sqrt(eta_i) <= w_b[x, i], where |Rt_x|^2 = |Gt_x|^2 + w^2 |B_x|^2, since Gt Ut = 0. Remainder: phi(y) <= y^2 for y >= -1, so the cost is at most the sum of (Rt Ett)[x, i]^2 eta_i / w_b[x, i] <= |D_r^(-1/2) Rt Ett|_F^2 <= |D_r^(-1/2) Rt|_op^2 2 X. Rt Rt^T = Gt Gt^T + w^2 B B^T. So Val_b >= X (w - 2 |...|_op) >= 0. QED. Cases: TQ18 part 6 is one patch with uniform eta at Z = R^n. TQ22 plus TQ18 is disjoint patches on rows' class sets (masses preserved). TQ17 is one patch with Test F. New: patches may overlap, and a residual may move mass between families, which disjoint minors cannot see. Head form: for each row pick a set H_x, let D_H(l) = the sum of p_x s_x(H_x) KL(s_x | H_x || softmax(l_x) | H_x). By the chain rule D_H <= D. The same proof, on rows restricted to H_x, gives: if D_H's residual decomposes into patches inside the heads and passes, then D_H(build) <= L_free(k) <= D(build). The gap is the build's misfit of head mass and of the tail. No tiny entry outside the heads enters the test. QED.
Referee: correction: D3 as stated, with w_b > 0 on the patch in Test Q. It contains TQ18 part 6 at Z = R^n, and TQ17 and D4 through Test F. It is a certificate of L_free, not a slot result.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ2 (the reflection certificate; round name D4) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Theorem D4 (the reflection certificate: TQ17's row identity holds for every build). Let V^T V = I, V^T 1 = 0, Pi0 = J - V V^T of rank m = C - 1 - k >= 1, u_i = V^T e_i, Refl = 2 Pi0 - J. Let * map rows to classes, with kappa_x > 0, such that: (a) the sum of kappa_x over rows with partner i is the same number kappabar for every class i; (b) the sum over x of kappa_x c_x e_(*x)^T Pi0 = 0; (c) Xi = - the sum over x of kappa_x c_x u_(*x)^T has symmetric part with least eigenvalue lam > 0. Let tau_e = lam / (2 kappabar), mu_x = kappa_x / p_x, q'_x = q_x[*x], m_x = the least of q_x[i] over i != *x, and s_x = q_x + mu_x Pi0 e_(*x). If m_x >= mu_x / 2 and g_x(T) = (mu_x tau_e - gamma_x) T + gamma_x T^2 - q'_x phi(mu_x T / q'_x) >= 0 on [0, 1 - 1/C], with gamma_x = 4 m_x phi(-mu_x / (2 m_x)), then L_free(k) = the sum of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)). The condition holds whenever mu_x <= 2 m_x and mu_x / m_x + log(1 + mu_x / q'_x) < tau_e. Part 2: with one row per class, a bijection * and equal kappa, (a) and (b) hold exactly when c_x = -A u_(*x) + c_0 for a k x k matrix A, and then lam = kappa lambda_min(sym A). Any class points and any permutation are allowed, with no k = C/2.
Proof. For a competitor take Pi as in TQ18, E = Pi - Pi0, e_x = J e_(*x). Three identities hold for all projectors of equal rank, with E 1 = 0: Refl E + E Refl = -2 E^2 (expand both sides), E^2 commutes with Pi0 (Pi0 E^2 = Pi0 - Pi0 Pi Pi0 is symmetric), and Refl^2 = J. Let f_x = E Refl e_x. Then f_x[*x] = e_x^T E Refl e_x = -e_x^T E^2 e_x = -T_x, and |f_x|^2 = e_x^T Refl E^2 Refl e_x = e_x^T E^2 e_x = T_x. So the sum over i != * of f_i^2 = T - T^2, so |f_i| <= 1/2 for i != *. T_x <= 1 - 1/C since |E|_op <= 1. Let q°_x = q_x - mu_x f_x = s_x - mu_x Pi Refl e_x. It is a distribution by m_x >= mu_x / 2 and by f_* = -T <= 0. Feasibility: rows kill 1 and V'. The rows sum to 0, since by (a) the sum of kappa_x e_x = kappabar J 1 = 0. Linear term: the sum of kappa_x <f_x, t + V c_x>. The t part vanishes by (a). With Refl e_x = Pi0 e_* - V u_*, E V = Pi V, and (b), what is left is tr(M Xi), M = V^T Pi V positive semidefinite. So it is at least lam tr M. And the sum of kappa_x T_x = kappabar tr(E^2) = 2 kappabar tr M by (a) and (F). So the linear term is at least the sum of p_x mu_x tau_e T_x. Cost: as in TQ17, on i != * the monotone ratio gives q phi(-mu f / q) <= gamma_x f^2, and at the partner q' phi(mu T / q'). The row's total is at least p_x g_x(T_x) >= 0. D(build) = the entropy sum, since 1^T G = 0 by (a) and G V = 0. The small-mu condition: phi(y) <= y^2 on [-1, 0] gives gamma <= mu^2 / m, phi(y) <= y log(1 + y) for y >= 0 gives the partner term, and T <= 1. Part 2: (b) says that for each class the code of its row lies in the span of 1 and V's rows, as a function of u_i. Then Xi = -kappa sum (A u_i + c_0) u_i^T with the signs of the statement gives kappa A, using the sum of u_i u_i^T = I and the sum of u_i = 0. QED. TQ17 is the case of pairs: * = partner, kappa = mu, Xi = 2 mu tau I, tau_e = tau. QED.
Referee: correction: D4 as stated. It covers free codes and the table.

**Theorem TZ3 (moment certificate for an always-on read; round name E6) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** rho is replaced by an average Fisher number). This uses no training premise. Setting: rows with p_x > 0, positive s_x. Z has a p-orthonormal basis zeta_x in R^D (sum p zeta zeta^T = I), first coordinates spanning Y, with 1 in Y; zeta has full column rank. Competitors: l'_x = B' zeta_x with B' = [A', V' M'] and V' of rank at most k. L_Z(k) is the least. Triple: q_x = softmax(B_0 zeta_x), B_0 = [A_0, V M_0], V^T V = I, V^T 1 = 0, M_0 of rank k, sigma its least singular value, C >= k + 2, k* = min(k, C-1-k). Stationary: Gamma_0 = sum p (s - q) zeta^T has zero Y part, and its other part Gamma satisfies V^T Gamma = 0, Gamma M_0^T = 0. g = |Gamma|_op. Psi(B) = sum p Cov(q_x) B zeta_x zeta_x^T on {B: 1^T B = 0}, self-adjoint, eta its least eigenvalue, zeta_max = largest |zeta_x|. Then eta > 0, and: (1) If g <= eta sigma / 2 and 2 sqrt(k*) g zeta_max <= eta, the triple is a global least: L_Z(k) = sum p (H(q) - H(s)). (2) If only 2 sqrt(k*) g zeta_max <= eta: D(triple) - L_Z(k) <= k* g (2 g / eta - sigma)_+. (3) The test reads s only through Gamma_0. So adding to s any delta with sum p delta zeta^T = 0 that keeps it positive changes neither the test nor the triple's status; what the read cannot compute costs nothing here, however large it is, and s may have tiny entries. Scope, plainly: at Z = R^n, eta is a per-row minimum, about the least probability, and TQ18 returns, so it gives nothing new for free codes. It covers the always-on read and region tables with K >> dim Z, not the gated box: V_b <= L_on, so it does not give V(G) by itself. Labelled proved matching lower bound for L_on only.
Proof. (a) eta > 0: if Var over q_x of B zeta_x is 0 at every row, then B zeta_x is in R 1, since q_x > 0; with 1^T B = 0 this gives B zeta_x = 0 at all rows, so B = 0. (b) Fix a competitor. Pi is the projector onto the complement of 1 and V' (extend if needed), rank m = C - 1 - k; Pi_0 likewise for V; E = Pi - Pi_0; X = tr(V^T Pi V) <= k*; |E|_F^2 = 2 X, as in TQ18. Let Btil = M_0^T (M_0 M_0^T)^-1, w = g sigma, R = Gamma + w V Btil^T. Then Pi_0 R = Gamma, and |R|_op = g: left spaces are orthogonal by V^T Gamma = 0, right spaces by Gamma M_0^T = 0. (c) Let B_E = Psi^-1 of the matrix with zero Y part and other part -E R (it lies in the domain since 1^T E = 0). f_x = B_E zeta_x, g_x = f_x - <q_x, f_x> 1, q°_x = q_x (1 + g_x) = q_x + Cov(q_x) f_x. Row entries sum to 1. |B_E|_F <= |E R|_F / eta <= g sqrt(2 X) / eta, and osc(f_x) <= sqrt 2 |f_x|_2 <= 2 sqrt(k*) g |zeta_x| / eta <= 1, so q° >= 0. (d) Feasibility: sum p (q° - s) zeta^T = (sum p (q° - q) zeta^T) - Gamma_0, with Y part 0 and other part -E R - Gamma = -Pi R, since Pi_0 R = Gamma. So V'^T annihilates it, and <its matrix, B'> = 0. TQ13 part 1 at each row gives D(l') >= sum p (H(q°) - H(s)). (e) H(q°) - H(q) = -<log q, q° - q> - KL(q° || q). log q_x = B_0 zeta_x - (log Z_x) 1 and q° - q is orthogonal to 1. So the linear term is <B_0, the other part E R> = tr(M_0^T V^T E Gamma) + w tr(M_0^T V^T E V Btil^T) = 0 + w tr(V^T E V) = w X, using Gamma M_0^T = 0, V^T Pi_0 = 0, Btil^T M_0^T = I. (f) (1 + y) log(1 + y) <= y + y^2 for y >= -1, with E_q g = 0, gives sum p KL <= sum p Var_q(f) = <B_E, Psi B_E> = <E R, Psi^-1 E R> <= 2 X g^2 / eta. (g) So D(l') >= sum p (H(q) - H(s)) + X g (sigma - 2 g / eta). At stationarity sum p <q - s, log q> = 0, so D(triple) = sum p (H(q) - H(s)). (1), (2) follow with X <= k*. (3): delta changes neither Gamma_0 nor q°, and H(s) cancels on both sides. Same-form note: Z = R^n has zeta_x = e_x / sqrt(p_x), and Psi is a block per row, with the test of TQ18 in the first condition. QED.
Referee: correction: Referee: a false step in the first form: The bound is proved only for r <= 2 k*. The use on ResNet-18 has r about 499 and 2 k* = 28, outside that range. The author marks it 'expected'. Referee: a false step in the first form: eta carries tiny probabilities whenever one read direction can sit on rows where a class is tiny. This is a property of the read, not of the theorem. As stated, for L_on and region tables only, not free codes, not the gated box. For every class i and unit w in R^D: eta <= (C/(C-1)) sum p_x q_x[i](1 - q_x[i])(w . zeta_x)^2 <= (C/(C-1)) max of q_x[i] over rows with w . zeta_x != 0. So rho is replaced by the least read-weighted mean of a class's probability. This helps only on a read that cannot steer onto rows where a class is tiny. Proved: under the test with r <= 2 k*, L_Z(k) - L_Z(C-1) <= <Gamma, Psi^-1 Gamma> <= r g^2 / eta. Beyond that range it stays a conjecture.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ4 (packing dual; round name C10) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Theorem C10 (packing dual). Rows x, weights p_x, s_x > 0 on C classes; kept part of dimension y (y = 1 if none); r = y + k. A block S is a list of n pairs (x_j, i_j), rows distinct, classes distinct. Premise: no pair (x, i) is a diagonal pair of one block and an off-diagonal pair of another. Block numbers: Y_jl = log s_(x_j)[i_l]; for any vectors a, g, Ybar = Y - a 1^T - 1 g^T; m_S = min_j Ybar_jj; A_S = the off-diagonal part of Ybar, symmetrised; |A|_(r) = (sum over j <= r of sigma_j(A)^2)^(1/2). Parameters b in (0,1], x0 > 0, kappa_b = phi(-b)/b^2, k'' = r + n x0, m' = m_S - 1 - kappa_b b. G_S(k) = m'(n^2/k'' - n) - (n/sqrt k'')|A_S|_(r). Let xi_S >= 0, with xi_S = 0 where G_S <= 0 or n <= k'', such that for each off-diagonal pair (x,i) the sum of xi_S over blocks holding it is at most b p_x s_x[i], and for each diagonal pair at most x0 p_x s_x[i]. Then L_Z(k) >= L_free(k) >= the sum over S of xi_S G_S(k).
Proof. Fix a competitor. Let U_S be a basis of the span of Y and the codes restricted to the rows of S. 1 is in its range, and its rank is at most r. C8 gives x, T, R^S with xi = xi_S. Let R be the sum of the R^S on (row, class) pairs. Domain: off-diagonal |R| <= sum xi_S <= b p s, and on the diagonal 0 <= R <= sum xi_S/x0 <= p s. Row sums of R are 0 by (d). So q°_x = s_x - R_x/p_x is a distribution. Each column of R^S is orthogonal to the restricted logit column of its class by (d), so sum over x of <R_x, l_x> = 0. TQ13 part 1 gives D >= sum p_x (H(q°_x) - H(s_x)), and (E) of TQ17 makes this <log s, R> - sum p s phi(-R/(p s)). Diagonal cost: with y = R/(ps) in [0,1], ps phi(-y) <= ps y^2 <= R. Off-diagonal cost: ps phi(-R/ps) <= kappa_b R^2/(ps), since phi(y)/y^2 is decreasing and y >= -b. R^2 <= (sum xi_S)(sum xi_S (T^S)^2), and sum xi_S <= b ps. So the cost is at most kappa_b b sum xi_S (T^S_jl)^2, and by (f) its block total is at most kappa_b b tr R^S. Gain: R^S has zero row and column sums, so <log s, R^S> = <Ybar, R^S> >= m_S tr R^S - xi_S <A_S, T>, since the diagonal of R^S is >= 0 and off it R^S = -xi_S T. T has rank <= r, so <A_S,T> <= |A_S|_(r)|T|_F <= |A_S|_(r) sqrt(Sigma), Sigma = sum 1/x_l, by von Neumann and (f). Net of a block: xi_S[m'(Sigma - sum T_ll) - sqrt(Sigma)|A_S|_(r)] >= xi_S h(Sigma), with h(Sigma) = m'(Sigma - n) - sqrt(Sigma)|A_S|_(r). By Cauchy-Schwarz and (a), Sigma >= n^2/k''. h is quadratic in sqrt Sigma with vertex |A|/(2m'). G_S > 0 forces m' > 0 and n/sqrt k'' > |A|/m'. So h is increasing past n^2/k'', and h >= G_S there. If the span has lower rank, each term only improves. QED. It uses no stationary triple, no pinned span, no test such as g <= rho, and no projector fixed in advance: the dual point changes with the competitor and stays a distribution by the two entry limits. A tiny entry excludes only the blocks that hold it. QED.
Referee: correction: As stated, with the two Y renamed. Complement, proved by me, same premises and same block list. For n > r let G'_S = (n - r)(m_S - 3) - sqrt(r) |A_S|_(r). Let xi_S >= 0, with xi_S = 0 where G'_S <= 0, the sum of xi_S on each off-diagonal pair at most 2 p s, and on each diagonal pair at most p s. Then L_free(k) >= the sum of xi_S G'_S. Proof: R^S = xi_S Pi_S, Pi_S the projector onto the complement of a dimension-r subspace of R^n that holds 1 and the restricted logit span. Pi_jl <= 1/2 off the diagonal, 0 <= Pi_jj <= 1, phi(u) <= u^2 on u >= -1, the sum of Pi^2 is n - r, and <A, Pi> = -<A, P> since A has zero diagonal. Tested: 1255 tables, 0 chain failures. It beat C10 on 521 tables, mostly where r > n/2.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Corollary TZ5 (level tail, any k; round name C11) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Corollary C11 (level tail, any k). Let K = C, p = 1/K, a on the diagonal, beta off it, e = (K-1) beta, m = log(a/beta). If k'' = k + 1 + K b beta/a < K and m > 1 + kappa_b b, then L_table(k) >= (b beta/K)(m - 1 - kappa_b b)(K^2/k'' - K). At b = 1 this is beta (m - 2)(K - k'')/k'', about e (m - 2)/(k + 1) for k much below K.
Proof. C10 with one block, x_j = i_j = j, x0 = b beta/a, xi = b beta/K, a_c = log beta, g = 0, so A = 0. Both entry limits hold with equality. QED.
Referee: correction: With r = k + 1 <= K, K >= 3 and 2 beta (K-1)/(K-2) <= a, also: L_free(k) >= (2 beta (K - r)/(K - 2)) (m - 2K/(K - 2)). Proof: fix a competitor. Let Pi be the projector onto the complement of a dimension-r subspace holding 1 and V, and R = xi Pi, xi = 2 beta/(K-2). Then Pi_ci <= 1/2 - 1/K gives R_ci <= beta/K, the premise gives R_cc <= a/K, <log s, R> = xi (K-r) m, and phi(u) <= u^2 gives cost at most (K/beta) xi^2 (K-r). Use the larger of this and C11; this one wins when k + 1 > K/2 - 1. At K = 2k it matches TQ17 at first order in m: exact is beta m + O(beta) and the bound is beta (m - 2K/(K-2)). C11's own limit there is only (K-2)/(K+2). Tested against fits at K = 6 to 24, all k, m = 3, 5, 8: 0 violations. Fitted slope against this slope at K = 16: k = 8: 1.000, 1.000; k = 7: 2.625, 1.143. So tightness is expected only for k >= K/2, and not proved beyond K = 2k.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ6 (the gap is convex in the table; round name I1) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Fix rows, weights p and any set B of logit tables: rank-k free codes, a read, kept units, or the real class (b) logits of V_b. Let psi(s) = inf over l in B of the sum of p_x [A(l_x) - <s_x, l_x>], with A = log-sum-exp, and L_B(s) = psi(s) - sum p_x H(s_x). For l in B define gap(l, s) = D(s, l) - L_B(s). Then: (1) s -> gap(l, s) is convex and >= 0 on the product of closed simplices. (2) S(l) = {s : l attains L_B(s)} is a convex set, and it holds softmax(l). (3) (Split rule.) If s_inf is in S(l), theta is in (0, 1], and w = (s~ - (1 - theta) s_inf) / theta is a table (entries >= 0), then gap(l, s~) <= theta gap(l, w) <= theta sum p_x KL(w_x || softmax(l_x)). (4) So mixes of certified tables with one build are certified, whichever certificate each used.
Proof. gap(l, s) = sum p_x [A(l_x) - <s_x, l_x>] - psi(s). The first part is affine in s. psi is an infimum of affine functions, so it is concave (F1). This gives (1), and gap >= 0 because l is in B. S(l) is the zero set of a convex function >= 0, so it is convex. D(softmax(l), l) = 0 gives softmax(l) in S(l). (3) Convexity at s~ = (1 - theta) s_inf + theta w, with gap(l, s_inf) = 0. Then L_B(w) >= 0 gives the second inequality. (4) is (2). QED. Lean: none, by hand. Label: a lemma on KL. QED.
Referee: correction: I1 as stated.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ7 (graded in the largest log-ratio, first order; round name I2) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Let l* attain L_B(s), q* = softmax(l*). Let s~ be a positive table, delta = s~ - s, lambda = the least over x, i of s~_x[i] / s_x[i], with lambda < 1, and r = (s~ - lambda s) / (1 - lambda). (1) One-sided exact form: D(s~, l*) - L_B(s~) <= (1 - lambda) sum p_x KL(r_x || q*_x). Call this B1d. (2) Let d = the largest over x, i of |log(s~_x[i] / s_x[i])|, L = L_B(s), TV = sum p_x TV(s_x, q*_x), e_x = 1 - max_i s_x[i], ebar = sum p_x e_x / (1 - e_x). Then D(s~, l*) - L_B(s~) <= B1(d) := (1 - e^-d) [ (1 + e^d)(L + TV) + e^(2d) ebar ]. (3) Sandwich for the value: D(s, l*) + sum p_x <delta_x, log(s_x / q*_x)> + sum p_x KL(s~_x || s_x) - B1(d) <= L_B(s~) <= the same expression without -B1(d). No C, K, k or smallest probability enters, and no premise on delta. It replaces TQ17 part 6: the term e log(1/e) and the premise |delta|_inf <= m_c - mu_c / 2 are gone. The price is that the error is a log-ratio, as F5 requires.
Proof. (1) s~ >= lambda s entrywise, so r is a table, and s~ = lambda s + (1 - lambda) r. Apply I1(3) with s_inf = s, theta = 1 - lambda. (2) lambda >= e^-d, and the slope is monotone by the perspective form, so we may use theta = 1 - e^-d with r re-defined at that theta. Entrywise r_i <= s_i (e^d - e^-d) / (1 - e^-d) = (1 + e^d) s_i, and |r_i - s_i| <= s_i (e^d - 1) / (1 - e^-d) = e^d s_i. KL(r || q*) = KL(r || s) + <r, log(s / q*)>. First term: KL(r || s) <= chi2(r, s). Let c be the top class. On i != c the sum of (r_i - s_i)^2 / s_i is at most e^(2d) e_x. At c, |r_c - s_c| <= e^d e_x, since rows sum to 1, so that term is at most e^(2d) e_x^2 / (1 - e_x). The total is e^(2d) e_x / (1 - e_x). Second term: <r, log(s / q*)> <= (1 + e^d) E_s (log(s / q*))_+, and E_s X_+ = KL(s || q*) + E_s X_-, with E_s X_- = E_s (log(q* / s))_+ <= E_s (q* / s - 1)_+ = TV(s, q*). Sum with weights p_x. (3) F2(a) gives D(s~, l*). Then L_B(s~) <= D(s~, l*) and (2). QED. Lean: none, by hand. Label: OPT-KL, graded clause: the build l* has loss L_B(s~) + gap, with the gap bounded by d and 0 at d = 0. QED.
Referee: correction: Referee: a false step in the first form: Parts (a), (b) and the inequality in (c) are correct. These sentences in (c) are false: 'This constant has no tiny probability in the sense of 1 / rho when s / q* is bounded, and Xbar and Y both scale with the tail mass.' Y sees only the span of V, so it can sit on a class of size rho. At pole tables Xbar does not scale with the tail, because the partner term s^2 / q* has order 1. I2 parts (1), (2), (3) as stated. Replace the sentence with this: B1d is at or below part 6 on the tested tables, and B1 is not. I did not prove an order between them. B1 is first-order tight only at tables with a second minimiser. (a) as stated, with W > 0. (b) as stated, with Var > 0. (c): limsup as d goes to 0 of [eta^2 Xbar / theta0] / G(d) <= 2 R'^2 Xbar / (theta0 Y), for each fixed table with Y > 0. This constant can hold 1 / (mass on the span). At pole tables Xbar has order 1 and Y has the order of the tail, so the constant has order 1 / tail.

**Theorem TZ8 (graded, second order, at a table with margin; round name I3) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Let l* attain L_B(s) and let s_alpha = q* + alpha (s - q*), alpha > 1, be a table that l* also attains. Put theta0 = 1 - 1/alpha. If delta = s~ - s has delta >= -theta0 q* entrywise, then D(s~, l*) - L_B(s~) <= B2 := theta0 sum p_x KL(q*_x + delta_x / theta0 || q*_x) <= (1 / theta0) sum p_x sum_i delta_x[i]^2 / q*_x[i]. In the error alone: let eta = e^d - 1, R_inf = max s / q*, Xbar = sum p_x [ sum over i != c(x) of s_x[i]^2 / q*_x[i] + e_x^2 / q*_x[c(x)] ]. If eta <= theta0 / R_inf, the gap is at most eta^2 Xbar / theta0. Margins: (a) TQ17 or D2: alpha is any factor with (pi, t, tau, alpha mu) in the pole family, per family, the least over families. (b) TQ18 part 1: alpha = rho min(1, sigma/2) / g, since rho and sigma depend only on the build. (c) D3 Test Q: any scale of the residual that still passes.
Proof. s = (1/alpha) s_alpha + (1 - 1/alpha) q*. So s~ = (1 - theta0) s_alpha + theta0 (q* + delta / theta0). Apply I1(3) with s_inf = s_alpha, w = q* + delta / theta0, which sums to 1 per row and is >= 0 by the premise. KL <= chi2 gives the next bound. In the error: |delta_i| <= eta s_i and |delta_c| <= eta e_x since rows sum to 0, and eta <= theta0 / R_inf gives feasibility. (a) In D2, s - q* on H_j is (mu_j / p_c) Pi* e_c, so scaling moves mu_j to alpha mu_j, and the block form and the masses stay. (b) G scales by alpha, and the test's other numbers do not move. QED. Lean: none, by hand. Label: OPT-KL, graded clause. The constants Xbar, R_inf and theta0 are read from the named table and build. The only number of N in the bound is d. QED.

Y sees only the span of V, so it can sit on a class of size rho. At pole tables Xbar does not scale with the tail, because the partner term s^2 / q* has order 1. The number g sees only P_Z G. The part (I - P_Z) G also scales, and no test bounds it. If P_Z G = 0 the formula gives alpha = infinity. So the premise of I3 fails at that alpha. I3 general part, (a), (c) as stated. Then I1(3) gives gap <= theta0 sum p KL(q* + delta/theta0 || q*), with delta >= -theta0 q*. Added lemma: margin alpha > 1 forces softmax(l*) to be the only minimiser's softmax. At pole tables Xbar has order 1 and Y has the order of the tail, so the constant has order 1 / tail.

**Theorem TZ9 (sharp moment certificate; round name J1) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Setting of E6: rows p_x > 0, s_x > 0; zeta_x in R^D p-orthonormal, first y coordinates span Y, 1 in Y; competitors l'_x = B' zeta_x, B' = [A' | V' M'], rank V' <= k. Triple B_0 = [A_0 | V M_0], V^T V = I, V^T 1 = 0, M_0 of rank k, least singular value sigma, C >= k + 2, q = softmax(B_0 zeta). Gamma_0 = sum p (s - q) zeta^T = [0 | Gamma], V^T Gamma = 0, Gamma M_0^T = 0. D_0 = D(triple). Psi(B) = sum p Cov(q_x) B zeta_x zeta_x^T on {1^T B = 0}, eta its least eigenvalue. <<X>> = <[0|X], Psi^-1 [0|X]>. For a rank m = C-1-k projector Pi with Pi 1 = 0, V'^T Pi = 0: Pi_0 = J - V V^T, E = Pi - Pi_0, S = V^T Pi V, X = tr S. For any (D-y) x k matrix W, which may depend on Pi: R_W = Gamma + V W^T, Omega = W^T M_0^T. Then: (1) If q° are row distributions with sum p (q° - q) zeta^T = [0 | -E R_W], then D(l') >= D_0 + tr(S Omega) - sum p KL(q° || q). (2) Fisher point: F = Psi^-1 [0 | -E R_W], f_x = F zeta_x, g_x = f_x - <q_x, f_x>, q° = q(1 + g). If g_x >= -a with a in (0,1] on all rows, the cost is at most c(a) <<E R_W>>, with c(a) = phi(-a)/a^2 = integral over t in [0,1] of (1-t)/(1-t a), c(0+) = 1/2, c(1) = 1. (3) So if for every Pi: g >= -a and c(a) <<E R_W>> <= tr(S Omega), then L_Z(k) = D_0. Without the second condition: D_0 - L_Z(k) <= sup over Pi of (c(a) <<E R_W>> - tr(S Omega))_+. (4) With W = w Btil, Btil = M_0^T (M_0 M_0^T)^-1: Omega = w I. The true ratio is tau(w) = sup over Pi of <<E R_w>> / X, and the test is c(a) tau(w) <= w. Pi by Pi, with A_1 = <<E Gamma>>, A_2 = <<E V Btil^T>>, A_12 their Psi^-1 inner product, a w >= 0 exists exactly when X - 2 c A_12 >= 2 c sqrt(A_1 A_2). (5) Chain: tau(w) <= 2 lambda_max(A_w) <= 2 max(g^2, w^2/sigma^2) / eta, where A_w is the form E -> <<E R_w>> on symmetric E with E 1 = 0, tr E = 0. At w = g sigma, c = 1 this is E6's first condition. E6's second condition implies a <= 1. Also a can be taken as sqrt(2 k*) times the largest over x, i of the Frobenius norm of the symmetric matrix that represents the linear map E -> g_x[i].
Proof. Fenchel: A(l') >= <q°, l'> + H(q°) for a distribution q°, with A the log-sum-exp. So D(l') >= sum p (H(q°) - H(s)) + sum p <q° - s, l'>. Moment of q° - s: [0 | -E R - Gamma] = [0 | -Pi R], since Pi_0 R = Gamma (V^T Gamma = 0, 1^T Gamma = 0, Pi_0 V = 0). Against B' = [A' | V' M'] this is -tr(R^T Pi V' M') = 0. So D(l') >= sum p (H(q°) - H(s)). H(q°) - H(q) = -<log q, q° - q> - KL(q°||q). log q_x = B_0 zeta_x - (log Z_x) 1, and q° - q is orthogonal to 1. So the linear sum is <V M_0, E R> = tr(M_0^T V^T E Gamma) + tr(M_0^T V^T E V W^T) = tr(V^T E Gamma M_0^T) + tr(S W^T M_0^T) = tr(S Omega), using Gamma M_0^T = 0 and V^T Pi_0 = 0. D_0 = sum p (H(q) - H(s)) - <Gamma_0, B_0> and <Gamma_0, B_0> = 0. This gives (1). (2): Cov(q_x) f_x = q_x g_x entrywise, so the moment is Psi(F) = [0 | -E R]. KL(q°||q) = E_q phi(g). phi(y) = y^2 times the integral of (1-t)/(1+t y), which decreases in y, so phi(y) <= c(a) y^2 for y >= -a. E_q g^2 = Var_q(f), and sum p Var_q(f_x) = <F, Psi F> = <<E R>>. (3), (4): direct. Minimising c(A_1 + 2 w A_12 + w^2 A_2) - w X over w gives w* = (X - 2 c A_12)/(2 c A_2), and the value is <= 0 exactly when the stated inequality holds, given w* >= 0. (5): |E|_F^2 = 2 X, so <<E R>> <= lambda_max |E|_F^2. Also <<Y>> <= |Y|_F^2 / eta and |E R|_F <= |E|_F |R|_op, with |R_w|_op = max(g, w/sigma) by the orthogonality on both sides. g_x[i] is linear in E, so its size is at most |E|_F times that Frobenius norm, and X <= k*. QED.

**Theorem TZ10 (what z cannot compute: an exact split; round name J3.1) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** exact split). Let Z be any code space with basis zeta. The full-rank read least L_Z^inf = min over all B of D(B) is attained at B*, q* = softmax(B* zeta), because s > 0 makes D coercive. For every B': D(B') = L_Z^inf + sum p KL(q* || softmax(B' zeta)). So L_Z(k) = L_Z^inf + R_k(q*), R_k the rank-k read least of the table q*, and L_Z(k) >= L_Z^inf + L_free(k; q*). (Converse of TQ14 part 6.) With T empty, L_on(k) = L_free(k) exactly when some free-code least of s has logits in the read, because both infima are attained. (Fixed span.) If (t, V, c) is free-stationary with G V = 0, then for a read at the same span V: D - D(free) = sum p KL(q || softmax(t' + V M z)), exactly. L_Z^inf is a convex program, 0 exactly when log s_x is affine in zeta_x modulo 1, and it names no build, size or zoom.
Proof. TQ20 with sum p (s - q*) zeta^T = 0 gives the identity: the linear term vanishes for all B'. R_k >= L_free(k; q*) since reads are free codes. Attainment: the set of rank <= k matrices is closed and D is coercive modulo constants, for rows of free logits and for B alike. A read least with value L_free is then a free least in the read. Fixed span: TQ20, and sum p <s - q, V (c' - c)> = 0 by G V = 0 row by row. QED.

**Theorem TZ11 (exact read cost at a binding rank; round name J3.3) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** K = C = 2k >= 4, pi_c = 1/K, sbar_c = a on class c and b on each other class, a > b > 0, r = a - b. Each region A_c has rows x with z_x = y_x e_c in R^K and y_x >= 0. The p-law of y on A_c is the same for all c, E y = 1, y not a.s. 0 (normalisation), and Z = the span of 1 and the K coordinates of z. So z has within-class variation, and D may be K + 1 > k. Let tau be the unique root of E[ y (u^y - u^-y) / (u^y + u^-y + K - 2) ] = r, with u = e^tau. Then L_on(k) = L_Z(k) = E log(2 cosh(tau y) + K - 2) - r tau - H(sbar). The pole read attains it: l_x = tau y_x (e_c - e_c'), for any pairing. L_free(k) = L_table(k) is the same formula at y = 1 (TQ17 part 4). So L_on(k) > L_free(k) unless y is a.s. constant, and the cost is exact.
Proof. Upper side. q_x has u_x/Z_x on c, 1/(u_x Z_x) on c', 1/Z_x elsewhere, with u_x = e^(tau y_x). Write qq, q', q'' for these. D = E[H(q_x)] - H(sbar) + sum p <q_x - s_x, log q_x>, and with kappa_x = r - (qq - q'), s_c - q_x = a_x Pi* e_c + (kappa_x/2)(e_c - e_c'), a_x = K (q'' - b). Pi* kills e_c - e_c', so the last sum is -tau E[kappa y] = 0 at the root. E[H(q_x)] = E log Z - tau E[y (qq - q')] = E log Z - tau r. Lower side. Fix a competitor l'_x = t' + y_x B'_c with B'_c = V' M' e_c. Let Pi be a rank k - 1 projector with Pi 1 = 0, V'^T Pi = 0, E = Pi - Pi*, and alpha_x = 2 (q'' - q') >= 0. Define q°_x = q_x - alpha_x E e_c. Key identity: E[alpha y] = E[a_x y]. Proof: with A = E[qq y], A' = E[q' y], A'' = E[q'' y], we have A - A' = r and A + A' + (K-2) A'' = 1, so 2 (A'' - A') = K A'' - (1 - r) = K (A'' - b). Positivity as in TQ17: on diagonal and tails, E_ci <= 1/2 and alpha/2 <= q'' - q', so the entry is >= q' > 0; at the partner the entry is q' + alpha T. Feasibility: q° - s = (alpha_x - a_x) Pi* e_c - alpha_x Pi e_c - (kappa_x/2)(e_c - e_c'). Against t': each part sums to 0 over c, since the law of y is common. Against y B'_c: E[(alpha - a) y] = 0, Pi B'_c = 0, E[kappa y] = 0. So D(l') >= sum p (H(q°) - H(sbar)). Expand by (E) of TQ17: row bracket = alpha_x tau y_x (D_c + T_c) - sum q phi(-alpha_x E / q). Sum over c of E[alpha tau y] D_c = 0, since tr Pi = k - 1 = K beta. The row identity (R) and the entry bounds give the bracket >= g_x(T_c) with g_x(T) = (alpha tau_x - gamma_x) T + gamma_x T^2 - q' phi(alpha T / q'), tau_x = tau y_x, gamma_x = 4 q'' phi(-alpha / (2 q'')). This g_x has exactly the form of TQ17 part 4 at u = u_x: g''' > 0, g(0) = g(1/2) = g'(1/2) = 0, so g_x >= 0 on [0,1]. At y_x = 0, alpha = 0 and g_x = 0. So D(l') >= E H(q_x) - H(sbar). Strictness: x -> log(2 cosh x + K - 2) is strictly convex and E y = 1, so E Phi(tau y) > Phi(tau) for each tau != 0 when y is not a.s. constant. The root is unique, by strict convexity of D in tau, with derivative -r at 0 and 1 - r at infinity. QED.

**Proposition TZ12 (hinge form of a gate; the read is generically not V_b; round name J4.1) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-01).** (1) Every gated build is a read plus hinges: l' = l'' + sum over j of v_j (-u_j)_+, with l'' = t' + A h_T + sum v_j u_j, u_j = m_j . z + beta_j. In code form: with c = M z, y = R c in any basis R, the code is max(y, theta) coordinate by coordinate. (2) Let l be any always-on build with codes c_x, r_x = s_x - q_x, x_0 a row with unique code at a vertex of conv{c_x}, a in the open normal cone with gap gamma = the next least of a . c_x above a . c_(x_0), and a . b = 1. For delta in (0, gamma]: the build l + V b (a . c_(x_0) + delta - a . c)_+ has k units, and D falls by p_(x_0) [KL(s_(x_0)||q_(x_0)) - KL(s_(x_0)||softmax(l_(x_0) + delta V b))], with first-order slope p_(x_0) <r_(x_0), V b>. (3) So if L_on(k) = V_b(k) with a least triple: at k >= 2, V^T r_x = 0 at each such vertex row (for rows that share a vertex code, the p-weighted sum is 0). At k = 1 with unit vector v of V: <r, v> <= 0 at the lowest row of the code and >= 0 at the highest row. With stationarity sum p <r,v> = 0 and sum p <r,v> c = 0, that needs at least 3 sign changes of <r,v> along the code. A saturating target has the wrong pattern. (4) This is a limit result on all L_on-based theorems at k >= 2: a certificate of L_on (E6, J1) gives V(G) only with this vertex condition or the free-code test of TQ18.1. A limit result fills no slot.
Proof. (1) relu(u) = u + (-u)_+. Basis: V M = (V R^-1)(R M), and R can have a as a row with b the matching column of R^-1 exactly when a . b = 1. (2) Only x_0 is below the kink for delta <= gamma. Use the unit with row a, moved down by its bias so that the kink is at a . c_(x_0) + delta. The others stay on by large bias. (3) If V^T r_bar != 0 at k >= 2, the open cone holds an a that is not a negative multiple of V^T r_bar, and then some b has a . b = 1 and <V^T r_bar, b> > 0. So D falls. At k = 1, a and b have one sign: bottom row a > 0, b > 0; top row a < 0, b < 0. The sign count: a function orthogonal to the affine functions of c has at least 2 sign changes; the ends fix an odd number. QED.
Referee: correction: Referee: a false step in the first form: Part 3 at k = 1: "needs at least 3 sign changes". The parity step needs strict signs at both end rows. With <r,v> = 0 at an end row, or r = 0 on v, the count can be 2 or 0. At k = 1, if L_on = V_b then <r,v> <= 0 at the lowest row and >= 0 at the highest row. If both are strict, the number of sign changes is odd and at least 3. If either is 0, 2 sign changes can occur, or r can vanish on v. All other parts as stated. A limit result: no slot.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ13 (a gate can remove all of the read cost; round name J4.2) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-01).** On the family of J3.3 with y_x > 0 on all rows: V_b(k) = L_free(k) = L_table(k) < L_on(k), unless y is a.s. constant. So L_on(k) - V_b(k) is the full closed-form cost of J3.3, and by J3.4 L_on / V_b -> 1 + K (1/y_min - 1) at confidence. The build uses read weights of size 1/y_min. Jump: for every y_min > 0 the value V_b(k) = L_table(k) does not depend on y_min. If instead a mass p_0 of rows per region has y_x = 0, then V_b(k) >= p_0 (log K - H(sbar)). So V_b jumps as y_min -> 0+, while L_on's formula is continuous there. So no bound on V_b in a distance on z can be continuous, in the manner of F8. Random-start fits are not evidence: the gated optimum needs off rows and the fits below can miss it.
Proof. Take H an invertible k x k matrix of +-1, columns h_j (H = 1 1^T - 2 I for k >= 3; [[1,1],[1,-1]] at k = 2), G = H^-1. On regions of pair j let the bit vectors be w = (1 + h_j)/2 at c, w = (1 - h_j)/2 at c'. Then pole code = tau G (2 w - 1): plus or minus tau e_j. So the pole logits equal t' + V' w, with V' = 2 tau V_pole G and t' = -tau V_pole G 1. Unit i: u_i = 1 - L times the sum of z[c] over classes c with w_c[i] = 0, with L >= 1/y_min. On a region with w[i] = 1, u_i = 1, because z[c''] = 0 for the other classes and the coefficient of its own class is 0. On a region with w[i] = 0, u_i = 1 - L y_x <= 0. So relu(u_i) = w_c[i] exactly on every row. Loss = L_table(k) at tau_0. With TQ11 part 1 and TQ14 part 4, V_b(k) = L_free(k) = L_table(k). Jump: rows with y = 0 all have z = 0, so one code and one q_0, and the mean of KL(sbar_c||q_0) over c is at least log K - H(sbar), the Jensen gap at mean uniform. QED.
Referee: correction: V_b(k) = L_free(k) = L_table(k) < L_on(k) for y > 0 on all rows. If a mass p_0 of each region has y = 0: V_b(k) >= p_0 (log K - H(sbar)) + (1 - p_0) L_table(k). This is above L_table(k), because log K - H(sbar) is the loss of the uniform q and L_table(k) is strictly lower. So the jump holds for every p_0 > 0.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ14 (the wall theorem; round name H1) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** an inequality at every confidence, with no tail depth in it). Rows x have weights p_x > 0, sum 1, and a top class tau(x). Fix e with e >= the tail mass of every row, m = log(1/e). Write s_x[i] = e mu_xi for i != tau(x), mu_xi >= 0, and s_x[tau(x)] = 1 - e w_x with w_x = sum_i mu_xi <= 1. h_x = -sum_i mu_xi log mu_xi >= 0. hbar = sum p h, wbar = sum p w, p_min = least p_x. Let l_x = A Y[x] + V c_x be a logit class, with c in a linear code class Z (free codes: Z = R^n; always-on read: Z = span of Y and z). Let M_xi = l_x[tau(x)] - l_x[i]. Define V = V_Z(mu, k) = inf of sum over x, i != tau(x) of p_x mu_xi (M_xi - 1) over the class, subject to M_xi >= 1 for ALL x and i != tau(x) (V = +inf if nothing is feasible). Let Lam = V + wbar. Then (a) Upper, if V < inf: L_Z(k) / e <= (m + 1) V - hbar + Lam log_+((C - 1)/Lam) + e. (b) Lower, for every v0 in [0, V] with e (v0 + wbar) <= p_min, and with Lam0 = v0 + wbar: L_Z(k) / e >= (m + 1) v0 - hbar - Lam0 log_+(Lam0 / p_min) - e Lam0^2 / p_min. (c) (a) holds also for V_b(k) with V^b, the same program over gated units, since it only needs a logit class closed under positive scaling; then V_free <= V^b, and V_b(k) >= L_free(k) gives (b) with V_free. No least tail entry, no eta, no rho, and no block appears. Entries with mu_xi = 0 are allowed. Rows may be photos or regions.
Proof. Upper. Take a near-optimal feasible logit table, and let delta = log_+((C-1)/Lam), m' = m + delta. Scale it by m' (the class is a linear space, or closed under scaling) and gauge the top logit to 0, so d_i = -m' M_i. With a = 1 - e w, Z = 1 + sum exp(d_i), the exact identity is KL(s_x || softmax) = a log a + log Z + sum_i e mu_i (-m + log mu_i + m' M_i). Then log Z <= Z - 1 <= (C-1) e exp(-delta), because M_i >= 1. Also a log a <= -e w + e^2 w^2, since (1-u)log(1-u) = -u + sum_{j>=2} u^j/(j(j-1)) and sum 1/(j(j-1)) = 1. Summing with p and using sum p mu M = V + wbar gives L/e <= m V + delta Lam - hbar - wbar + (C-1) exp(-delta) + e. If Lam < C-1 then (C-1)exp(-delta) = Lam and the right side is (m+1)V + Lam log((C-1)/Lam) - hbar + e. If Lam >= C-1 then delta = 0 and C-1 <= Lam gives the same form with log_+ = 0. Lower. Fix V (the matrix). For fixed V, M is linear in w = (A, c), and LP(V) = min sum p mu (M(w) - 1) s.t. M(w) >= 1 has dual max { sum (y - p mu) : y >= 0 on tail entries, <y - p mu, M(w)> = 0 for all w }. Its value is 0 at y = p mu. If the primal is feasible, strong duality gives value Val_V >= V >= v0. If it is infeasible, the dual is unbounded. In both cases a convex combination (or a point on the ray) gives a dual feasible y with sum (y - p mu) = v0 exactly, so sum y = Lam0. Set R_xi = y_xi - p_x mu_xi on the tail and R_x,tau = -sum_tail R_xi. Then <R, l> = -<y - p mu, M> = 0 for every logit in the class. Let q°_xi = e y_xi / p_x on the tail, q°_tau = 1 - e y_x / p_x with y_x = sum_i y_xi; this is a distribution, since e Lam0 <= p_min. For every l in the class, the Gibbs variational bound log sum e^l >= <q°, l> + H(q°) gives sum p KL(s || softmax l) >= sum p [H(q°_x) - H(s_x)] + e <R, l> = sum p [H(q°_x) - H(s_x)]. Now compute. H(s_x) = -a log a + e m w_x + e h_x. H(q°_x) = -q°_tau log q°_tau + (e/p_x) sum y_xi (m + log(p_x / y_xi)). So the difference summed with p is e m v0 + e sum y log(p/y) - e hbar + sum p [a log a - q°_tau log q°_tau]. Here log mu has cancelled: the cost q° log(q°/s) and the gain q° (log s) meet, which is A's cancellation in general form. Then y_xi <= Lam0 gives sum y log(p/y) >= -Lam0 log_+(Lam0/p_min). Also a log a >= -e w (from log a >= -(1-a)/a), and -q log q >= q(1-q) gives p_x q°_tau (1 - q°_tau) >= e y_x - e^2 y_x^2 / p_x. Summing: sum p [..] >= e (Lam0 - wbar) - e^2 Lam0^2 / p_min = e v0 - e^2 Lam0^2 / p_min. This holds at every V, so it holds at the infimum. QED.
Referee: correction: H1 as stated, plus a stronger lower side. Row form: fix V and a dual y with e y_x <= p_x for each row and sum (y - p mu) = v0. Then every competitor with that V has L/e >= (m+1) v0 - hbar - sum_x y_x log_+(y_x/p_x) - e sum_x y_x^2/p_x. Uniform form: for beta >= 1 with e beta <= 1, let P_beta(V) = min <p mu, M - 1> + beta sum_x p_x xi_x, subject to M_xi + xi_x >= 1, xi >= 0. Let V_beta = inf over V of P_beta(V), so V_beta <= V. For v0 in [0, V_beta] and Lam0 = v0 + wbar: L/e >= (m+1) v0 - hbar - Lam0 log beta - e beta Lam0. Proof: same as H1, with sum_i y_xi log(p_x/y_xi) >= y_x log(p_x/y_x). Author's (b) is the case beta = max(1, Lam0/p_min). V_beta = V is proved only at that beta. Evidence at a fixed V only: K = 8, k = 2, m = 12 gives 13.50 against the author's 9.74, with fit 17.72 and upper 19.66. On the real table the domain is now not empty, but the value is below 0, because 1.37 v0 < hbar = 2.13 for v0 <= 1. So it stays vacuous there.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ15 (the limit of the wall program; round name H2) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Fix rows, p, top classes and a tail shape mu (mu_xi >= 0, w_x = 1). Let the table be s_x[tau] = 1 - e, s_x[i] = e mu_xi, and m = log(1/e). Then lim as e -> 0 of L_Z(k) / (e m) = V_Z(mu, k), with an error at most Lam log_+ max((C-1)/Lam, Lam/p_min) / m + O(1/m), when V_Z is finite. If V_Z = +inf the ratio tends to +inf. Also, H2 is not a limit in a fixed exponent table: if s_x[i] proportional to exp(-m A_xi) with several exponents, then only tail entries of the largest scale keep weight, so mu has zeros, and walls stay at M >= 1 for all entries. If V = 0 on such a mu, then L is o(e m) and the piecewise-linear value says nothing further.
Proof. Direct from H1 with v0 = V, dividing by e m, and with v0 -> inf when V = +inf. In the exponent family put e = the largest tail entry scale times its count; other entries have mu -> 0, and H1 holds at each m. QED.
Referee: correction: H2 as stated. In the exponent family, L/(e m) tends to V at the limit tail mu, by the continuity above.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ16 (structure of the wall program; round name H3) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Let n_ci = p_c mu_ci, and let l_c[i] = t_i + v_i . c_c. (1) M_ci + M_ic = S_ci = <v_c - v_i, c_c - c_i>, with no t in it. (2) M >= 1 is feasible for (V, c) with some t iff for every cycle (i_1, ..., i_l), the sum over j of <c_(i_j), v_(i_j) - v_(i_(j+1))> >= l. This is cyclic monotonicity with a margin: the codes sit in the cells of a power diagram of F(x) = max_i (t_i + v_i . x). (3) If n is balanced (sum_i n_ci = sum_i n_ic for each c), the objective has no t, and it is a sum of cycle sums. Under Fact F8 with label regions and uniform p, n is balanced: Fact F8 says the mean softmax equals the label share, and that is the same statement. (4) In the level case, f := sum_(c != i) (M_ci - 1) = K tr(Vbar^T Cbar) - K(K-1), with Vbar, Cbar centred. (5) Let Abar_ci = (M_ci + M_ic)/2 - 1 >= 0 for c != i, with diagonal 0, and A_ci = M_ci - 1. For x with sum x = 0: x^T Abar x - |x|^2 = -<V^T x, C^T x>. So on W_V = {x perp 1, V^T x = 0}, of dimension >= d := K - 1 - k, x^T Abar x = |x|^2 exactly. (6) So for a projector Pi onto a d-dimensional subspace of W_V: sum_(c != i) Pi_ci Abar_ci = d. (7) The program is linear for fixed V, and bilinear overall. It is classical rank in L and tropical only in the softmax (the top-class max); it is not a tropical rank problem.
Proof. (1) Expand: t and the row constants cancel. (2) t_c - t_i >= 1 - (v_c - v_i) . c_c are difference constraints, and Bellman-Ford feasibility holds iff no cycle is negative. M_ci > 0 for all i is the cell condition. (3) sum n_ci (t_c - t_i) = sum t_c (sum_i n_ci - sum_i n_ic). Flow decomposition gives the cycles. Fact F8: sum_c p_c s_c[i] = p_i gives sum_(c != i) p_c s_c[i] = p_i (1 - s_i[i]) = sum_(j != i) p_i s_i[j]. (4) sum_(c<i) <v_c - v_i, c_c - c_i> = K sum <vbar_c, cbar_c>. (5) sum_(c,i) x_c x_i S_ci = 2 (sum x)(sum x_c <v_c, c_c>) - 2 <V^T x, C^T x> = -2 <V^T x, C^T x>. Also S = 2(11^T - I) + 2 Abar gives sum x_c x_i S_ci = -2 |x|^2 + 2 x^T Abar x. (6) Trace. (7) M is linear in (t, c) at fixed V. QED.
Referee: correction: H3 parts 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 as stated. Part 3 for label regions with p = label share, at a stationary point, on training inputs.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ17 (the wall program at k = 1; round name H4) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** exact, and this is not a linear program over order types). Rows = classes. V(n, 1) = the least over orders of the classes and over gaps u_j > 0 of sum_(c<i) { n_ci [ (i-c-1) + 2 sum_(j=c)^(i-1) (x_j - x_c)/u_j ] + n_ic [ (i-c-1) + 2 sum_(j=c)^(i-1) (x_i - x_(j+1))/u_j ] }, where x_j is the partial sum of the u. For each order this is a geometric program. (a) Level table: u uniform is optimal, M_ci = (c-i)^2, V = c(K, 1) = (K+3)(K-2)/6, that is L_free(1) / (e m) -> (K+3)(K-2)/6. (b) K = 3: V = the least over the middle class b, with ends a, c, of n_ac + n_ca + 4 sqrt(n_ac n_ca). (c) So on a table with rational entries the limit value can be irrational: mu rows (0, .8, .2), (.5, 0, .5), (.6, .4, 0), p = 1/3, gives V = 4/15 + 4/sqrt(75). So the limit is not the value of any finite union of linear programs with rational coefficients indexed by sign patterns or order types.
Proof. With k = 1, M >= 1 forces the codes into the K distinct cells of a convex piecewise-linear F. So all slopes differ, and classes sorted by slope have x_1 < ... < x_K. Let delta_j = v_(j+1) - v_j, b_j the crossing of lines j, j+1. Let alpha_j = M_(j,j+1) = delta_j (b_j - x_j) >= 1, and gamma_j = M_(j+1,j) = delta_j (x_(j+1) - b_j) >= 1, so delta_j u_j = alpha_j + gamma_j. Telescoping lines: for c < i, M_ci = sum_(j=c)^(i-1) delta_j (b_j - x_c) = sum [alpha_j + (alpha_j + gamma_j)(x_j - x_c)/u_j], and M_ic = sum [gamma_j + (alpha_j + gamma_j)(x_i - x_(j+1))/u_j]. Every (u > 0, alpha, gamma >= 1) is realised by some t, v, x, and all M_ci are >= i - c >= 1 then. The objective increases in alpha and gamma, so alpha = gamma = 1. That is the formula. (a) M_ci + M_ic = 2 (sum u_j)(sum 1/u_j) >= 2 (i-c)^2 by Cauchy, with equality at uniform u. Sum: f = K(K-1)(K+3)(K-2)/6, and c = f/(K(K-1)). (b) K = 3: overshoot n_ac (1 + 2 r) + n_ca (1 + 2/r) with r = u_1/u_2, and the neighbours overshoot 0. Minimise over r. The least is at middle class 2, with n_13 = 1/15, n_31 = 1/5. A rational LP has a rational value. QED.
Referee: correction: H4 as stated, with 'exact' meaning a finite min of geometric programs, not a closed form.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ18 (the level constant; round name H5) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** bounds, exact cases, and a correction). Level table: mu_ci = 1/(K-1). Let c(K, k) = lim L_table(k) / (e m) = V, f(K, k) = K (K-1) c(K, k) = the least of sum_(c != i) (M_ci - 1), and d = K - 1 - k. (1) For 1 <= k <= K-2: f(K, k) >= 2 K d / (K - 2) (projector), and f(K, k) >= K d / (k + 1) (the limit of C11; not re-derived). (2) f(K, k-) is nondecreasing as k falls, and c(K, k) is nondecreasing in K. (3) Exact: c(K, K-1) = 0; c(K, K-2) = 2 / ((K-1)(K-2)), that is f = 2K/(K-2), attained by M = 1 except M_12 = M_21 = 2 (K-1)/(K-2); c(2k, k) = 1/(2k - 1), that is f = K, attained by a pairing with M = 2 on partners; c(K, 1) = (K+3)(K-2)/6. (4) CORRECTION to the brief: c(K, k) does not tend to 1 at K = 2k. c(64, 32) = 1/63. (5) Upper bounds that are not closed forms: Petersen gives c(10, 4) <= 1/3, Clebsch gives c(16, 5) <= 1/3 (f = 30 and 80), triangular-lattice patches give f(7, 2) <= 42.
Proof. (1) By H3 (6), with Pi the projector onto W_V, or a d-dimensional part of it: Pi kills 1, so Pi <= J. Then |Pi(e_c + e_i)|^2 <= 2 - 4/K, and Pi_ci = (|Pi(e_c + e_i)|^2 - |Pi(e_c - e_i)|^2)/4 <= 1/2 - 1/K. Since Abar >= 0: d = sum Pi_ci Abar_ci <= (1/2 - 1/K) f. (2) A principal submatrix of M is feasible for the same k. Averaging over subsets of size K - 1, each ordered pair lies in K - 2 of them: (K-2) f(K,k) >= K f(K-1,k). (3) k = K-2: x = (K-2, K-2, -2, ..., -2) has M x = 2 * 1 for the stated M: row j >= 3 gives -x_j = 2; row 1 gives (K-2)(M_12 - 2) = 2. So rank J M J <= K-2, and any zero-diagonal M with that rank is t + V c up to row constants. Then f = 2 (M_12 - 1) = 2K/(K-2), which equals the bound (1). k = K/2: J M J = -J(I - P)J has rank K/2 with P the pairing, f = K, equal to (1) at d = K/2 - 1. k = 1 is H4. (4) From (3). (5) Direct: Petersen adjacency A has eigenvalues 3, 1^5, -2^4, and M = 11^T - I + A has rank J M J = 4, and it is an EDM; Clebsch 5, 1^10, -3^5 likewise. QED.
Referee: correction: H5 as stated.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ19 (the two-table identity; round name F2) (under: none) (added 2026-11-01).** Let Sum p_x = 1. (a) For positive tables s, s~ and any logits l with q = softmax(l): D(s~, l) = D(s, l) + sum of p_x <s~_x - s_x, log(s_x / q_x)> + sum of p_x KL(s~_x || s_x), exactly. (b) Let d = the largest over x, i of |log(s~_x[i] / s_x[i])| and eta = e^d - 1. Then, for every Z and k, L_Z(k)(s~) <= L + eta (L + sqrt(2 L)) + eta^2, with L = L_Z(k)(s). The same holds with s and s~ exchanged, and with d and eta unchanged. No C, K, k or tiny probability enters.
Proof. (a) KL(s~||q) = sum s~ log(s~/s) + sum s~ log(s/q), and sum s log(s/q) = KL(s||q). Subtract. (b) |s~_i - s_i| <= eta s_i, so |<s~ - s, log(s/q)>| <= eta E_s |log(s/q)|. With X = log(s/q): E_s |X| = E_s X + 2 E_s (-X)_+ = KL(s||q) + 2 E_s (log(q/s))_+ <= KL + 2 E_s (q/s - 1)_+ = KL + 2 TV <= KL + sqrt(2 KL), by log y <= y - 1 and Pinsker. KL(s~||s) <= log(1 + chi2(s~, s)) <= chi2 <= eta^2. Sum over x with weights p_x, and use Jensen on the square root. Take l along a minimising sequence for s. Each l of the class stays in the class, since the class does not depend on the table. QED. First-order tightness: I did not prove it. The true first-order change along a direction is the p-weighted mean of <s~ - s, log(s/q*)>. So the bound and the true worst slope are both of order E_s |log(s/q*)|, and E_s |X| <= L + sqrt(2L) is an inequality I have not matched from below in a centred form. QED.
Referee: NOT refereed. Treat as unconfirmed.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ20 (overflow: Sylvester with numbers) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Lemma G1 (overflow: Sylvester's inequality with numbers). Let Lh be a real matrix of rank <= k, with rows and columns split into J blocks; Ah_b are the diagonal blocks and Off = Lh minus those blocks. (a) For theta > 0 let r_b = the number of singular values of Ah_b above theta and o = sum r_b - k. If o >= 1 then sigma_j(Off) > theta for j = 1..o, so the Ky Fan norm |Off|_(o) >= o theta. (b) For J = 2, write Lh = [A B; C D], r_1 = the number of singular values of A above theta_1, r_2 the same for D at theta_2, o = r_1 + r_2 - k >= 1. Then sigma_i(C) sigma_(o+1-i)(B) > theta_1 theta_2 for each i = 1..o, so for any nu, nu' > 0: nu |B|_(o) + nu' |C|_(o) >= 2 o sqrt(nu nu' theta_1 theta_2). (c) At B = 0 this gives rank A + rank D <= k, and this exact form is rank B >= rank A + rank D - k.
Proof. (a) Lh = Diag + Off, with Diag the direct sum of the Ah_b, so Diag has at least k + o singular values above theta. Weyl: sigma_(k+j)(Diag) <= sigma_(k+1)(Lh) + sigma_j(Off) = sigma_j(Off). (b) Let U_A, W_A hold the singular vectors of A above theta_1, and U_D, W_D those of D above theta_2. Compress: M = [S_A Bt; Ct S_D], with S_A, S_D diagonal with entries above theta_1, theta_2, and Bt = U_A^T B W_D, Ct = U_D^T C W_A. rank M <= k. By the Schur complement, rank M = r_1 + rank(S_D - Z), Z = Ct S_A^-1 Bt. So rank(S_D - Z) <= r_2 - o. Weyl gives sigma_(r_2 - o + j)(S_D) <= sigma_j(Z), so sigma_o(Z) >= sigma_(r_2)(S_D) > theta_2. Horn's product inequality: sigma_o(Z) <= sigma_i(Ct) |S_A^-1|_op sigma_(o+1-i)(Bt) < sigma_i(Ct) sigma_(o+1-i)(Bt) / theta_1. Compression does not raise singular values. For the sum: nu sigma_(o+1-i)(B) + nu' sigma_i(C) >= 2 sqrt(nu nu' theta_1 theta_2) by AM-GM; add over i. (c) L = X Y^T: rank(X_1 Y_2^T) >= rank X_1 + rank Y_2 - k (Sylvester). QED. Gauge note: B -> eB, C -> C/e keeps D = C A^+ B, so no bound holds on B alone. The product is the right object. It is first-order sharp: for k = 1 and a 2 x 2 matrix, |b c| = |a d|. QED.
Referee: no separate verdict on this item.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ21 (kept families, one shared budget) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Theorem G4 (kept families, shared budget: exact least at a loss above 0). Classes split into families H_1..H_J with |H_b| = K_b = 2 r_b >= 4, with a fixed-point-free pairing c <-> c' inside each. C = sum K_b, w = C/2 = sum r_b. Rows: regions A_c of P, one per class, with masses pi_c, and s_x = s_c on A_c. R_b = the union of A_c over c in H_b. Y = the span of the indicators of the R_b. L^Y(k) = inf over A' (C x J), V' (C x k), free codes c of sum p_x KL(s_x || softmax(A'[b(x)] + V' c_x)). Numbers: any offsets A_b in R^C, one per family; tau_b > 0, mu_b > 0 with mu_b tau_b = Y0 the same for all b. Write mu_c = mu_b / pi_c for c in H_b, q_c = softmax(A_b + tau_b (e_c - e_c')), q'_c = q_c[c'], m_c = the least of q_c[i] over all i != c' (strangers included), beta_b = 1/2 - 1/K_b, Pi*_b = (1/2)(I + swap) - 1_b 1_b^T / K_b on H_b, Pi* = their direct sum, s_c = q_c + mu_c Pi* e_c, phi(y) = (1+y) log(1+y) - y, gamma_c = 4 m_c phi(-mu_c/(2 m_c)), g_c(T) = (mu_c tau_b - gamma_c) T + gamma_c T^2 - q'_c phi(mu_c T / q'_c). Premises: (1) m_c >= mu_c / 2; (2) g_c >= 0 on [0, 1 - 1/K_b]. Let X = sum pi_c (H(q_c) - H(s_c)). Then: 1. L^Y(w) = X > 0, attained by units e_c - e_c' per pair, codes +-tau_b, offsets A_b. 2. For k <= w: L^Y(k) >= X + Y0 (w - k). 3. L_free(w) >= X >= L_free(w + J - 1), and X <= SHARE(w) with equality when the conditional of A_b on each H_b' does not depend on b. 4. If g_c > 0 on (0, 1 - 1/K_b], then every minimiser at k = w has J_F span(V') equal to the sum of the pole spaces, so family b receives exactly r_b units (J_F = the direct sum of the centrings on H_b). 5. mu_c <= 2 m_c and mu_c / m_c + log(1 + mu_c / q'_c) < tau_b are enough for g_c > 0, so any A_b and tau_b give members at small mu. 6. For J >= 2 the sum of TQ22 minors at k = w is 0, since w >= K_b - 1. 7. If kept units T have span(1, h_T) = Y on P, and each pair function (+1, -1 on the pair's regions, 0 elsewhere) is affine in z_S on P, then V_b(w) with T kept equals X.
Proof. Upper side. KL(s_c || q_c) = H(q_c) - H(s_c) + <q_c - s_c, log q_c>, and <q_c - s_c, log q_c> = -mu_c e_c^T Pi* A_b, since Pi* kills 1 and e_c - e_c'. Multiply by pi_c and add over c in H_b: -mu_b 1_b^T Pi* A_b = 0. So the build's loss is X. X > 0 since s_c != q_c for K_b >= 4. Lower side. Fix a competitor of rank k <= w. Let S0 = J_F col(V'), of dimension at most k. Let Pi be the orthogonal projector onto a subspace of dimension C - J - k of range(J_F) orthogonal to S0. Then Pi 1_b = 0 for each b, and Pi V' = 0, because V' differs from J_F V' by family-constant columns. Put q°_x = s_x - mu_c Pi e_c on A_c. Rows sum to 1. Feasibility: on R_b the sum of p_x mu_c <Pi e_c, A'_b> is mu_b <Pi 1_b, A'_b> = 0, and <Pi e_c, V' c_x> = 0. Weak duality (TQ13 part 1) gives D >= sum pi_c (H(q°_c) - H(s_c)). Write q°_c = q_c - mu_c f_c, f_c = (Pi - Pi*) e_c. By (E) of TQ17, H(q°_c) - H(q_c) = mu_c <log q_c, f_c> - sum over i of q_c[i] phi(-mu_c f_c[i] / q_c[i]). Linear term. log q_c = A_b + tau_b (e_c - e_c') + const. The sum of f_c over c in H_b is (Pi - Pi*) 1_b = 0, so the A_b part vanishes, family by family. What is left is Y0 times the sum of (D_c + T_c), with D_c = Pi_cc - beta_b, T_c = beta_b - Pi_cc'. And sum D_c = tr Pi - sum K_b beta_b = (C - J - k) - (w - J) = w - k. Entries. Pi <= J_F, so Pi_ci <= (1/4) |J_F (e_c + e_i)|^2. In one family this is beta_b; across families it is 1/2 - (1/K_b + 1/K_b')/4. So T_c >= 0. Also f_c[c] <= 1/2, in-family tail f = Pi_ci + 1/K_b <= 1/2, stranger f = Pi_ci <= 1/2, f_c[c'] = -T_c. T_c <= 1 - 1/K_b, since Pi_cc' >= -1/2. Row identity. The sum of f_c[i]^2 is Pi_cc - 2 e_c^T Pi Pi* e_c + beta_b. Pi* e_c = (e_c + e_c')/2 - 1_b / K_b and Pi 1_b = 0, so it equals beta_b - Pi_cc' = T_c. So the sum over i != c' of f^2 is T_c - T_c^2. Domain and cost. For i != c', mu_c f <= mu_c / 2 <= m_c <= q. The partner is only lifted, so a tiny q'_c is allowed. As in TQ17, phi(y)/y^2 decreases and q phi(-w/q) decreases in q, so q phi(-mu_c f / q) <= gamma_c f^2. So D >= X + Y0 (w - k) + sum pi_c g_c(T_c) >= X + Y0 (w - k). This is 1 and 2. 3. Offsets count as a kept part, so L_free(w) >= L^Y(w). For the other side, write A_b = A_1 + (A_b - A_1): J - 1 free columns with family-indicator codes hold all the offsets. SHARE(w) >= X: the same dual has zero sum on each family, so masses are kept and the chain rule gives the SHARE objective; offsets common across rows are a subset. Equality is the build. 4. Equality forces T_c = 0, so f_c = 0 by the row identity, so Pi = Pi*. If dim S0 < w, the complement holds more than one rank-(w - J) projector, and all would have to equal Pi*, which is impossible. So S0 is the sum of the pole spaces. 5. As TQ17 part 3. gamma_c <= mu_c^2 / m_c, q' phi(mu T / q') <= mu T log(1 + mu / q') for T <= 1, drop gamma T^2. 6. Each minor has K_b - 1 <= w, so it fits exactly. 7. Upper: always-on read units relu(m . z + beta) equal the pair function plus a constant on P; the constant goes into kept offsets. Lower: a network of this class has logits A' h_T + V' (unit values), a member of the class of L^Y(w). QED. Comment. D2 reaches this same X with k units per family, because its strangers are copied from a shared build. Here strangers are set by offsets, and at k = w the units are not shared. The budget is one projector across all families: tr Pi = sum (r_b - 1). QED.
Referee: correction: A false step in a first form: 'w >= K_b - 1'. w = r_b + (the sum of the other r), so the inequality fails when r_b > 1 + (the sum of the other r). The agent's tables did not reach the failing case in this check. Stronger form, proved here. Let tau vary per pair (tau_j). Let Y0 be any number at most the least of mu_b tau_j. Replace g_c by g_c(T) = (Y0 / pi_c - gamma_c) T + gamma_c T^2 - q'_c phi(mu_c T / q'_c). Keep premise (1). Then L^Y(w) = X. The only proof change: the linear term is the sum over pairs of mu_b tau_j |Pi (e_c - e_c')|^2. This is a sum of squares, so it is at least Y0 (w - k) + Y0 sum T_c. Check: 4 tables with price ratio up to 2.5, 3000 projectors each, 0 below X, 0 left the simplex, fit / X >= 1 (1.00000 on the table with the largest X). G4 is the case of equal prices. Separately, on tables that meet only the old premise at each family's own price, fit / X = 1.0000 at price ratio 100. So equal prices do not look necessary even outside this proof. That wider case is expected, not proved. For every 0 <= k <= C - J, L^Y(k) >= X + Y0 (w - k). So the line of slope -Y0 supports the rank profile at w on both sides. At k = C - J this gives X <= Y0 (w - J). Check above w: k = w + 1, w + 2 on 5 tables, 0 violations. As stated, with 'for all b, b' including b = b''. Also true: X is the least over the wider class A'[b(x)] + V c_x + a free family constant per row, at V of rank w. As stated, with the meaning of 'receives' written out. As stated. In the stronger form, replace tau_b by Y0 / mu_b on the right side. For the family minors (classes H_b, any rows): if w >= K_b - 1 for each b, the sum at k = w is 0. In general, with X_b the part of X on H_b, the sum is at least the sum over b of (X_b - Y0 (w - r_b))_+. Proof: on H_b, s_c conditioned on H_b is a TQ17 table with weight pi_c q_c(H_b) and residual mu_c / q_c(H_b). Its premises follow from G4's, since a larger m lowers gamma. Then apply the line of part 2 with J = 1. Check at (16,4): line 1.7e-4, minor fit 3.4e-4, X 5.1e-4. As stated, for one group. It is a conditional statement on a claim that names sizes and the build's numbers.
