**Lemma TZ22 (exact information dual) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** K1 (exact information dual; under: none). Rows x with weights p_x, positive table s, sbar = sum p_x s_x, I(s) = sum p_x KL(s_x || sbar). Fix V (C x k). A coupling for V is a list of rows pi_x on the simplex with (i) sum p_x pi_x = sbar and (ii) V^T pi_x = V^T s_x for every x. Then for every t, c, with l_x = t + V c_x, and every coupling pi: sum p_x KL(s_x || softmax(l_x)) >= sum p_x [H(pi_x) - H(s_x)] = I(s) - I(pi). Equality holds when pi_x = softmax(l_x), and at any stationary point in t and c the fit is itself a coupling. So L_free(k) = inf over V of [I(s) - min over couplings of I(pi)]. The same holds on region tables, so for L_table(k).
Proof. With A = log-sum-exp, KL(s||softmax(l)) = A(l) - <s,l> - H(s). Sum over x. By (i), sum p_x <s_x - pi_x, t> = 0. By (ii), sum p_x <s_x - pi_x, V c_x> = 0. So the loss equals sum p_x [A(l_x) - <pi_x, l_x> - H(s_x)]. Gibbs gives A(l) - <pi,l> >= H(pi), with equality at pi = softmax(l). The conditions (i), (ii) are the stationarity conditions in t and c for q = softmax(l), so a stationary q is a coupling and equality holds. Marginal sbar is common, so H(pi|X) - H(s|X) = I(s) - I(pi). Equality of the inf and the max at fixed V: the coupling problem is a concave maximum under linear constraints, and s is an interior feasible point, so Fenchel duality has no gap. Read as a network: for a chosen head V, the dual point is a distribution on classes that depends on V, it handles tiny classes through entropy, and the marginal constraint (i) couples rows of all blocks. These are the three properties the common block asked for. The min over V is not convex, so a lower bound at k must give a coupling for every V. That is what K2 does. QED.
Referee: correction: As stated, with the attainment proof, and with a literature row for the recalled source. A frame, not a bound.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ23 (information floor) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** K2 (information floor; sharper F4; under: none). Let s be a positive table on any finite rows, sbar = sum p_x s_x, and 0 < e <= min over x, i of s_x[i] / sbar[i]. If e = 1 the table is constant and the claim is trivial. Otherwise, for every k >= 0: L_free(k) >= I(s) - k log(1/e). Since every code class and the unit form lie inside free codes, L_table (at T empty), L_on and V_b(k) with T empty obey the same floor. With kept units of rank y, replace k by k + y.
Proof. Let theta = 1 - e, beta = e/theta, so 1 + beta = 1/theta. Write nu = sbar and s_x = e nu + theta r_x, with r_x a distribution and sum p_x r_x = nu. Fix t, V. Write f_c(i) = t'_i + b_i . c, with t' = t - log nu, b_i the row i of V. Shift by row constants so that <nu, t'> = 0 and <nu, b> = 0. Let psi(c) = log <nu, exp f_c>. Restrict to the span of the b_i, of dimension k' <= k. Since all nu_i > 0 and 0 is in the relative interior of conv(b), psi is coercive and strictly convex. Step 1: KL(s_x || softmax(log nu + f_c)) = KL(s_x||nu) - <s_x, f_c> + psi(c) = KL(s_x||nu) - theta <r_x, f_c> + psi(c). So loss >= I(s) - Phi, with Phi = sum p_x sup_c [theta <r_x, f_c> - psi(c)] = sum p_x psi*(eta_x), eta_x = theta <r_x, b>, because sum p_x <r_x, t'> = <nu, t'> = 0. Each eta_x lies in the relative interior of conv(b), so a maximiser c_x exists with grad psi(c_x) = eta_x. Step 2: let G_x(c) = <r_x, f_c> - (1+beta) psi(c). Then sup G_x = Gamma_x = <r_x,t'> + psi*(eta_x)/theta and G_x(c) = Gamma_x - (1/theta) D(c, c_x), with D the Bregman distance D(c, c_x) = psi(c) - psi(c_x) - eta_x . (c - c_x). Jensen gives exp <r_x, f> <= <r_x, exp f>, so sum p_x exp G_x(c) <= <nu, exp f_c> exp(-(1+beta) psi(c)) = exp(-beta psi(c)). Step 3: integrate over c. With Z = integral of exp(-beta psi) and I_x = integral of exp(-(1/theta) D(c, c_x)): sum p_x exp(Gamma_x) I_x <= Z. Jensen gives sum p_x Gamma_x + sum p_x log I_x <= log Z. And sum p_x Gamma_x = Phi / theta. Step 4 (contraction): put c = c_x + e (w - c_x). D is convex in its first slot and 0 at c_x, so D(c, c_x) <= e D(w, c_x), and (1/theta) e = beta. So I_x >= e^(k') V_x, with V_x = integral of exp(-beta D(w, c_x)) dw. Step 5: V_x = Z E_P exp(beta [psi(c_x) + eta_x . (w - c_x)]), with P proportional to exp(-beta psi). Jensen gives log(V_x / Z) >= beta [eta_x . wbar - psi*(eta_x)], wbar the mean of P. Since sum p_x eta_x = theta <nu, b> = 0: -sum p_x log V_x <= -log Z + beta Phi. Step 6: Phi/theta <= k' log(1/e) + beta Phi, and 1/theta - beta = 1. So Phi <= k' log(1/e) <= k log(1/e). QED. Kept units: A h_T + V c has rank at most y + k, so it is a free-code logit of that rank. Read as a network: a tail the row must keep is a penalty on sharp codes, and it limits how many classes k units can tell apart, across all rows at once. The floor is 0 unless k < about I / log(1/e). Mostly I <= log K, so it covers coarse zooms (small k), not k = 14 at K = 1000. QED.
Referee: correction: K2 as stated, with the k' = 0 line, and with the rows named. Add Corollary: the floor is positive only when k < log min(K, C). Label: lower bound. Remove the slot remark 'slot 1 in the letter and slot 2 as a bound'. As stated, with the two lines added. As stated for e <= 1/2. For larger e the bound is still true and is vacuous when the condition fails. Gap >= (1 - e) log m - h(e) - log w - k (log(1/e) + b + log w) - o(1), at most I(s_e). Reaching (1 - 4e)/16 needs much smaller m than through F4. As stated, with the normalisation written out and the limit added.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Proposition TZ24 (ceiling of information floors) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** P-ceil (ceiling of information floors; under: none). Premises: any positive table on C classes, any weights, any k. Let s_x >= e sbar with e in (0,1], and let g be any per-unit charge with g(e) >= 1 - e. Then I(s) - k g(e) <= (1 - e)(H(sbar) - k) <= (1 - e)(log C - k). So a floor of the form I(s') - k g(e'), on the table itself or on any table s' derived from it on at most C classes, is <= 0 once k >= log C, for every admissible e'. This covers: K2 (g = log(1/e)); K2b(a), which gives <= alpha (1 - u)(H(sbar) - k) with u = e/alpha; K2b(d) minors, each term <= w_b (1 - e_b)(log|H_b| - k); TQ19 lumps (C' <= C); and every soft-e or truncated table, since any charge for the moved mass only subtracts more. At C = 1000 such a floor is empty at every k >= 7. Positive needs C > e^k, which is 1.2 million classes at k = 14. At the real e = 2.9e-9, K4's charge is 9.47 nats per unit, above 1 - e, so the conclusion holds on this table.
Proof. Write s_x = e sbar + (1 - e) r_x. r_x >= 0 by the definition of e, it sums to 1, and sum p_x r_x = sbar. Joint convexity of KL gives KL(s_x || sbar) <= (1 - e) KL(r_x || sbar). Average over x: I(s) <= (1 - e) I(r). I(r) = H(sbar) - H(r | x) <= H(sbar) <= log C. So I(s) - k g(e) <= (1 - e) H(sbar) - k (1 - e). For K2 use log(1/e) >= 1 - e. K2b(a): I(s) - (1 - alpha) I(r) - alpha k log(alpha/e) <= (alpha - e) I(r) - alpha k log(1/u) = alpha [(1 - u) I(r) - k log(1/u)] <= alpha (1 - u)(H(sbar) - k). QED. Read as a network: a unit can lose at most about 1 - e of a nat of what it keeps, and N has at most log C nats to lose. QED.
Referee: correction: Keep P-ceil and add this. Any K4-form term obeys I(s') - (k/2) log(1/(e(2 - e))) <= (1 - e) log C' - (k/2) log(1/(e(2 - e))). So at k = 14 even the conjectured K4 is empty on these minors. The same inequality with a weight w_b applies to each minor.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ25 (a certified coupling for every head) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** P-coup (a certified coupling for every head; B3 of round 1, re-proved in K1's frame; under: none; NOT refereed). Rows x, weights p_x, s_x > 0, n_xi = p_x s_x[i], T = log s. Let R, H be rows and classes with |H| >= k + 2, a > 0 on R, b > 0 on H with sum b = 1, and a_x b_i <= n_xi on R x H. Let That be T on R x H with the b-mean of each row subtracted, then the a-weighted mean of each column. r_x^2 = sum_i b_i That_xi^2, beta = max a_x sqrt(b_i) r_x / n_xi, M = D_a^(1/2) That D_b^(1/2), E = sum over j > k of sigma_j^2(M). R(beta) = max over 0 < tau <= 1/beta of tau - (tau^2 / 2)(1 + tau beta). Then the least of the minor R x H at k units is >= R(beta) E. For a list of blocks with disjoint class sets on each row, TQ22 adds these, each with its own beta. Overlapping layers with sum of a b <= n, one common beta and the sum of E also hold, and the same proof works. For any head V this builds a coupling of K1 with higher entropy than s, so it is a floor of the form I(s) - I(pi) with pi depending on V.
Proof. Fix a competitor (t, V, c). Pi is the L2(b)-orthogonal projector on R^H onto the complement of 1 and V restricted to H. g_x = Pi That_x. For tau <= 1/beta let delta_xi = -(tau / p_x) a_x b_i g_xi, zero off the block, and pi_x = s_x + delta_x. (1) Pi_x is a distribution: <g, 1>_b = 0, and |g_xi| <= r_x / sqrt(b_i), so |delta_xi| / s_xi <= tau beta <= 1. (2) Moments: V^T delta_x = 0, because g is b-orthogonal to V on H. (3) Marginal: sum p_x delta_x = -tau b Pi (sum a_x That_x) = 0, by the a-weighted column centring. So pi is a coupling of K1. (4) K1 gives D >= sum p_x [H(pi_x) - H(s_x)] = sum p_x [-<delta_x, T_x> - KL(pi_x || s_x)]. On H, T_x is That_x plus a row constant plus a vector free of x, and both integrate out. So the first term is tau sum a_x |g_x|_b^2 =: tau E'. (5) Cost: with v = delta / s, phi(v) = (1 + v) log(1 + v) - v <= v^2 / 2 for v >= 0, and <= (r^2 + r^3) / 2 for v = -r. So KL cost <= ((1 + tau beta) / 2) sum (p_x delta_xi)^2 / n_xi, and (a b g)^2 <= n_xi a b g^2 by a b <= n. So cost <= (tau^2 / 2)(1 + tau beta) E'. Thus D >= E' R(beta). (6) E' = |M Pi~|_F^2 with Pi~ removing sqrt(b) and at most k more directions, and M sqrt(b) = 0, so E' >= E by Eckart-Young. Per-minor beta: the minor has n'_xi = p_x s_x[i] = n_xi, and its T differs by a row constant, so the block value on the raw table equals the value on the minor. QED.
Referee: correction: As written, with beta for layers defined as the max over x, i of the sum over l of a^l_x sqrt(b^l_i) r^l_x / n_xi. This statement now has a referee check. It is a real lower-bound tool, not tight at error 0, and it fills no slot.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ26 (the fixed-span dual and the row cap) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Q-A (the fixed-V dual, and H1's row cap is the same set). Fix V of rank <= k. For free codes, the least over (t, c) of D equals the max of sum p_x [H(q°_x) - H(s_x)] over rows q°_x in the simplex with V^T (q°_x - s_x) = 0 for each x and sum p_x (q°_x - s_x) = 0. Now take H1's row form with a tail number e and top class tau(x): q°_xi = e y_xi / p_x on the tail, q°_x,tau = 1 - e y_x / p_x. The conditions y >= 0 and the row cap e y_x <= p_x say exactly that q°_x >= 0. So the row-weighted form of H1 removes no dual point and adds no dual point. At fixed V it gives the exact value. Its only open step is the inf over V. A per-row e_x changes the parametrisation only.
Proof. The problem in (t, c) is convex and q° = s is a strictly positive feasible point of the dual, so Fenchel duality holds with no gap. Gibbs gives log sum exp(l) >= <q°, l> + H(q°). So KL(s || softmax l) >= H(q°) - H(s) + <q° - s, l>. The constraints make the sum of the last term over rows 0 for every l = t + V c. At a minimiser, q° = softmax(l) gives equality. The H1 identity is a change of variables. The envelope of H1 (m + 1) v0 - hbar drops the entropy of q°. QED.
Referee: correction: As stated, with 'least' read as an inf. The inf is attained because s > 0. Attribute only 'no admissible v0' to the round 2 referee.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ27 (the worst entry of a projected vector) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Q-B (the sharp worst entry of a projected vector). Let u be a unit vector in R^K, g perp u, and e' = e_i - u_i u, so |e'|^2 = 1 - u_i^2. Over all orthogonal projectors Pi on u-perp, the range of (Pi g)_i is exactly [(g_i - |e'||g|)/2, (g_i + |e'||g|)/2]. Both ends are attained with P of rank 1 inside u-perp.
Proof. Put v = Pi e'. Then <v, e'> = |v|^2, so v lies on the sphere with centre e'/2 and radius |e'|/2. Also (Pi g)_i = <v, g>, since g perp u gives <e', g> = g_i. Cauchy on the sphere gives both bounds. To attain: let v = e'/2 -+ |e'| g / (2 |g|) and w = e' - v. Then v perp w, so the projector off w maps e' to v. With scale gamma and V column w / gamma, a real competitor with k >= 1 realises it. QED.
Referee: correction: For K >= 3 the range is exactly the interval, with both ends at P of rank at most 1 inside u-perp. For K = 2 only the two ends occur. The bounds hold at every K. The K = 2 case has no effect on any use, because rectangles need K >= k + 3.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ28 (the weighted rectangle dual) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Q-C (the weighted rectangle dual, computable at any k). Rows x, weights p_x, table s > 0, n = p s, A = log s. A system is a family b of rectangles R x S, |S| = K, with weights W^b_xi > 0 on R x S and sum over b of W^b_xi <= n_xi at every entry. Each b also has a scale gamma > 0 on S, u = gamma / |gamma|, fixed vectors g_x perp gamma, and numbers rho_x in (0, 1]. Cap: gamma_i (sqrt(1 - u_i^2) |g_x| - g_xi) / 2 <= rho_x W_xi for all x, i. Let kap(rho) = ((1 - rho) log(1 - rho) + rho) / rho^2, kap(1) = 1, m_x = max_i gamma_i^2 / W_xi, f_x = gamma * A_x with its gamma part removed, B_b = -sym(sum g_x f_x^T) - sum kap(rho_x) m_x g_x g_x^T. Then L_free(k) >= sum_b [tr B_b - the sum of the k + 1 largest positive eigenvalues of B_b]. With kept units T, replace k + 1 by k + 1 + |T|. Three uses are computed. Q1: entry-disjoint rectangles with W = n. Q5: flat slices, W = p (t_l - t_(l+1)) on entries with s >= t_l. Then the cap holds with no entry of s in it, and the sum over slices is at most s. Q7: all rows on one class-tree node, W^N_xi = alpha_x(N), the row's least leftover on the node.
Proof. psi(e) = exp(e) - 1 - e >= 0, so D = sum n psi(e) >= sum_b sum W^b psi(e), with e = log q - A = L - A and L_x = t + V c_x - log Z_x. On S, L_x lies in span(t_S, V_S, 1_S). Let Pi be the orthogonal projector off gamma times this span. Its P part in gamma-perp has rank <= k + 1. Put Y_xi = gamma_i (Pi g_x)_i, h = Y / W. Q-B and the cap give h >= -rho_x for every competitor. Fenchel: W psi(e) >= Y e - W psi*(h), psi*(h) = (1 + h) log(1 + h) - h. psi*(h) / h^2 is decreasing in h (Bennett's function), so psi*(h) <= kap(rho) h^2 for h >= -rho. <Y_x, L_x> = <Pi g_x, gamma * L_x> = 0. So the block's sum is at least sum_x [-<Pi g_x, f_x> - kap m_x |Pi g_x|^2] = tr(Pi B). B vanishes on gamma. The inf over projectors of tr(Pi B) with rank P <= k + 1 on gamma-perp is tr B minus the k + 1 largest positive eigenvalues. Sum over b. QED.
Referee: correction: As stated. Covers free codes on any rows. On photo rows it also covers the read and the box through V_b >= L_free. It is not a slot result. As stated. It is stronger than stated: any valid certificate on such a rectangle has value at most 0, not only Q-C.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Proposition TZ29 (the ceiling on one rectangle) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Q-E (the ceiling on one rectangle, W = n, fixed gamma). Let a dual Y_x(V) = gamma * Pi_V g_x with fixed g_x stay >= -s_x at every competitor. Let a_i = 2 s_xi / gamma_i sorted, e* = sqrt(1 - max u_i^2). Then |g_x| <= Gamma_x = the least over j >= 2 with e* > 1 / sqrt j of a_(j) / (e* - 1 / sqrt j). The moved mass is mu_x <= |gamma| Gamma_x / 2. For any choice of g, the rectangle's inf over V is at most sum p [mu log(K - 1) + M h(mu / M)], M = the row's mass on S, h = binary entropy. So all duals linear in the projector are capped by the rows' j-th least ratio s_xi / gamma_i, for the gamma in use.
Proof. Q-B gives g_i >= sqrt(1 - u_i^2) |g| - a_i for each i. If |g| > a_(j) / (e* - 1 / sqrt j), the j smallest a_i each give g_i > |g| / sqrt j, so the sum of g_i^2 exceeds |g|^2, a contradiction. Cauchy: |y|_1 <= |gamma| |g|. At V = 0, t = 0, Pi is the identity on gamma-perp, so the value there is p [H_S(s + y) - H_S(s)]. Audenaert's bound on entropy against total variation (2007), applied on S with mass M, gives the rest. The inf over V is at most this value. QED.
Referee: correction: As stated, with the scope above. The numbers are ceilings only for the listed gamma and levels.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Proposition TZ30 (the block ceiling) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Q-F (the block ceiling). Consider any certificate of the form D >= sum_b D_b with weights sum W^b <= n, where D_b reads only rectangle b and is valid for every L of rank at most k + 2 on b with 1 in its row space. Then sum_b D_b <= sum_b inf over such L of sum W^b psi(L - A). If the rectangles lie inside row groups R_g, then sum_b D_b <= the sum over g of the least of the problem on the rows of R_g with its own k units. This is TQ22's sentence 'each minor gets all k units', and the mechanism of I8-F, stated for every dual of this form.
Proof. For each b, D_b <= its value at any allowed L, and Fenchel gives value <= sum W^b psi(L - A). Each L may differ per b, because D_b reads only b. For row groups, sum over b inside g of W^b psi(e) <= D on the rows of g at that group's competitor. QED.
Referee: correction: A false step in a first form: The theorem holds. Two readings fail. (1) The joint claim is true only on the six cuts run, J = 1, 2, 4, 8, 13, 36. It is the value of a fit aimed at the whole table. Theorem as stated. Add this monotone form. Any certificate on weights W <= n that holds for every L in a class is at most F_W(L) for each L in that class, with F_W = sum W psi(L - A). Next-step item 4 on this cover therefore cannot pass about 1.6% of the fit. It needs other weights.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ31 (the box as a floor at a span plus a distillation of codes) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** R1 (the box as floor at a span plus a distillation of codes) (under: none; any table with s > 0; V of full column rank modulo 1). For fixed V let (t°, c°) be the least free codes at V, q°_x = softmax(t° + V c°_x), and L_free(V) their loss. For every build with logits t' + V c'_x, gated or not: D = L_free(V) + sum p_x KL(q°_x || softmax(t' + V c'_x)). Hence V_b(k) = min over V of [ L_free(V) + E_b(V) ], with E_b(V) = inf over t', M, beta of sum p KL(q°(V) || softmax(t' + V relu(M z + beta))), and the same form holds for L_on. It is an identity and not a lower bound past L_free(V).
Proof. Stationarity of (t°, c°): V^T (s_x - q°_x) = 0 for each row, and sum p (s_x - q°_x) = 0. Then KL(s||q') - KL(s||q°) - KL(q°||q') = <s - q°, log q° - log q'> = <s - q°, l° - l'>, since <s - q°, 1> = 0. Here l° - l' = (t° - t') + V (c° - c'). Summing with p, the t part vanishes by the mean condition and the V part vanishes row by row. This is TZ10's fixed-span identity, stated at any V and any code class. Attainment: s > 0 makes D coercive modulo the kernel at fixed V. QED.
Referee: correction: A false step in a first form: Only the word 'min'. The identity itself holds and I checked each step. It is TZ10's fixed-span identity, so it is not new. V_b(k) = inf over V of [L_free(V) + E_b(V)]. At fixed V the inner infimum is attained: each unit's code set is a finite union of polyhedral cones, so the logit set is a finite union of polyhedra, and D is coercive modulo constants at s > 0. Only the outer infimum can fail.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ32 (four-term split over regions) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** R2 (four-term split over regions) (under: none; any table, any build, any partition into regions c). Let lbar_c be the p-mean of l_x on region c, qbar_c = softmax(lbar_c), d_x = l_x - lbar_c, sbar_c the region mean of s. Then D = A + E + N - T, with A = sum pi_c KL(sbar_c || qbar_c), E = sum p KL(s_x || sbar_c), N = sum p K_qbar(d_x) >= 0 where K_q(d) = log E_q e^d - E_q d, and T = sum p <s_x - sbar_c, d_x>. Real, 12000 photos, k = 14, top-class regions.
Proof. log sum e^(lbar + d) = A(lbar) + <qbar, d> + K_qbar(d), with A the log-sum-exp. Averaging over a region, sum p d = 0 removes <qbar, d> and <sbar, d>. Next -<s_x, l_x> = -<s_x, lbar> - <s_x - sbar, d_x> - <sbar, d_x>, and the mean of <s_x, log s_x> is E plus <sbar, log sbar>. Add the terms. Numerical identity check on real fits is below 1e-6. QED.
Referee: correction: The identity stands as written. Report T - N and A as a pair, because neither one alone is a share of E.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Theorem TZ33 (the signed cut program) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** R3 (the signed cut program, and its dual that depends on the competitor's cuts) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds). Rows x, positions s, zeta(x,s) = (1, z(x,s)). For a sign pattern sigma_j with y^j(x,s) = +1 on, -1 off, let F_j(x) = mean over s of 1[on] zeta(x,s). Lambda_+(V, sigma) = least over t, theta_j of D(t + sum_j v_j <F_j(x), theta_j>) subject to y^j(x,s) <zeta(x,s), theta_j> >= 0. This is convex with linear constraints. Then V_b(k) = inf over V, sigma of Lambda_+(V, sigma), exactly. Dual: Lambda_+(V, sigma) = max of sum p [H(r_x) - H(s_x)] over r_x in the simplex and mu >= 0 with sum p (r_x - s_x) = 0 and sum_x p_x <r_x - s_x, v_j> F_j(x) = sum over x,s of mu^j(x,s) y^j(x,s) zeta(x,s) for each j. So each unit's moment must lie in the normal cone of its cut's cell. Dropping the sign constraints (mu = 0) gives Lambda <= Lambda_+, a per-unit sharpening of J4.4 part 2. This removes J's free sign at fixed cuts: the hinge moment is >= 0 on the cell. It does not remove it over all V and sigma.
Proof. On the closed cell of sigma, relu(u) = 1[on] u at each position, so the family is exactly the set of builds with that pattern; the union over patterns is the box, which gives the equality. Fenchel: A(l) >= <r, l> + H(r) gives KL(s || softmax l) >= H(r) - H(s) + <r - s, l>. Sum with p. The term linear in theta_j has coefficient equal to the moment. By the dual constraint it equals sum mu y <zeta, theta_j> >= 0 on the cell. Strong duality: D is convex, differentiable and coercive modulo the kernel because s > 0, and the constraints are linear, so KKT holds at the minimiser with r = q. The trivial part is the equality; the content is the dual form. QED.
Referee: correction: As stated. It gives a lower bound only on builds with those V and those cuts.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).

**Lemma TZ34 (a perfect separator) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** R5 (a perfect separator on real tables). For any build whose code is constant on N's top-class regions: D = eps_const + region loss exactly, so such a build is at least eps_const + L_table(k). So J4.3 part 1's binary route loses to the read on these bits even at claim error 0. But relu on-levels must be constant on photos of a class, which R6 limits.
Proof. Constant q_c on a region: the mean of KL(s_x || q_c) = the mean of KL(s_x || sbar_c) + KL(sbar_c || q_c), since the cross term has zero mean. Reads of s_bar: the rest is the definition of L_table. QED.
Referee: correction: As stated, for region-constant builds only.
Lean: none, by hand (a round agent's proof, checked by a referee by hand).
