### B.Q.11 The general form is weighted low-rank fitting, and it is hard (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ11-2026-11-02.md)

Why this section. Lemma TQ20 says the exact problem is, at second order, a low-rank fit with one metric per row. This section proves that fact in full on a network whose every claim holds, and then proves that the problem is hard. It proves Conjecture DI1. Scope, said plainly: no result here is OPT-KL or fills a slot. The networks here have nearly all of each row's mass on one class, and their squeezes are in the quadratic regime of KL. Part C (round 2, measurement 6) reports that real tables are not in that regime. No hardness is claimed for tables with the confidence real networks have.

**Definition DQ16 (product tail claim) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ11; node R-prodtail).** A **product tail claim** names a partition A_1, ..., A_K of P and, for each region c, a set H_c of classes (its **near classes**). With pi_c and sbar_c as in Definition DQ10, its error is
   eps_prod = eps_const + the least over real numbers alpha_c and beta_i of sum over c of pi_c sum over classes i not in H_c of sbar_c[i] (log sbar_c[i] - alpha_c - beta_i)^2.
It is 0 exactly when s_x is constant on each region and, outside each region's near classes, the region's table is a row scale times a column scale. The scales are not part of the claim: the least is a weighted least squares problem, solved by linear equations. It uses logarithms, as the table of Definition DI1 does, and it is computed to any precision in polynomial time. It names no build, size or zoom. If every class is near on every region, the error is eps_const and the claim says no more than Definition DQ10. No theorem here uses this claim. Part C reports how far real tables are from it.

**Definition DQ18 (the weight-pattern network N(M, W; a, B)) (added 2026-11-02).** Let M be a real m x n matrix with entries in [-1, 1], not 0 (with M itself not the zero matrix; widened from [0, 1] on 2026-11-02: no result of this section uses M >= 0, since the sign enters only through |a M / 2| <= a / 2), and W an m x n matrix with entries in [1, d]. Write L_wj = log W_wj, E_W = sum over w, j of W_wj M_wj^2 and, for r >= 1,
   p*_r(M, W) = min over matrices X of rank at most r of sum over w, j of W_wj (M_wj - X_wj)^2.
The minimum is attained, since W > 0 makes this a norm, and p*_r <= E_W (take X = 0). N has one hidden layer and 2m units: for each w a **judgment unit** h_w and a **group unit** s_w, each reading one input coordinate with weight 1 and bias 0. P has 2m points of weight 1/(2m): x_w^- and x_w^+ are the inputs at which h_w has pre-activation 1, s_w has pre-activation 1 and 3 respectively, and every other unit has pre-activation 0. The classes are g, b_1, ..., b_m and 1, ..., n (the **tail**), so C = m + n + 1. With a > 0 and B > 1, the logits at x_w^+ and x_w^- (+ and - in that order) are
   y[b_w] = B, y[g] = B - 1, y[b_w'] = 0 for w' != w, y[j] = L_wj +- (a/2) M_wj.
They are linear in the units: h_w carries y at a = 0 minus a M_w on the tail, and s_w carries (a/2) M_w on the tail. The weights are rational when a, B, M and the L_wj are. Read as a network: each area is confident in its own class b_w, one shared class g is second, and what moves inside an area is the order of its unlikely classes. Write Z_0 = e^B (1 + 1/e), tau = 1/Z_0, eta = (m + 2 n d) e^(-B), alpha = a sqrt(E_W), and Gamma = a^2 tau / (8 m).
The map M_N holds, for each w, with A_w = {x_w^+, x_w^-}: the two districts ({h_w}, A_w) and ({s_w}, A_w), so that the group of Lemma TQ23.a is a union of districts in the trunk's words; their shelter claims; the judgment claim (A_w, {h_w}, 1); the branch claim ({s_w}); the on-inside claim (A_w, empty set, {h_w}) and the linear-read claim (A_w, {h_w}). It is a tree map. Every one of these claims has eps = 0, by reading the definitions at these 2m points: off an area each of its units has pre-activation and value 0, h_w is 1 on A_w, no hidden unit reads a hidden unit, and y on A_w is affine in s_w. It also holds the constancy claim of Definition DQ10 with the 2m points as regions, at eps_const = 0. Scope, said plainly: M_N is not complete in the sense of Definition DM6, whose item 5 asks for a pole claim at more than two logits.

**Lemma TQ23.a (the squeeze of N(M, W) is weighted low-rank fitting: areas kept) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-02).** Let N = N(M, W; a, B) with E_W >= 1, alpha <= 1/9 and eta <= 1/100. Let S be the group {s_1, ..., s_m}, T = {h_1, ..., h_m} kept, and k = r >= 1. Then
   (1 - 4 alpha - 6 eta) Gamma p*_r(M, W) <= L_free(r) <= V_b(r) <= L_on(r) <= (1 + 3 alpha) Gamma p*_r(M, W).
Proof. L_free <= V_b <= L_on is Proposition TQ11 part 1. On A_w a build has logits t_w + V c(x): h_w is 1 there and the other kept units are 0, so t_w is free for each w.
Facts on the table. For x in A_w let s_x = softmax(y(x)) and Z_x its normaliser. Then Z_0 <= Z_x <= Z_0 (1 + eta), and the mass off {b_w, g} is at most eta. For tail j, tau W_wj e^(-a/2) / (1 + eta) <= s_x[j] <= tau W_wj e^(a/2). Every class other than b_w has s_x at least tau e^(-a/2) / (1 + eta) >= 9 tau / 10, since a <= alpha <= 1/9. Also s_x[g] >= 1/4, and s_x[b_w] is the largest entry.
Upper side. Let X be a rank r matrix attaining p*_r, X = sum over l of u^l (v^l)^T. Let unit l of the box be relu(sum over w of (a/2) u^l_w z_(s_w) + beta), beta so large that it is on at all of P, with logit weights v^l on the tail and 0 elsewhere. Its value on A_w at x^+ and x^- is (constant on A_w) +- (a/2) u^l_w, since z_(s_w) - 2 = +-1. Choose the free t_w to cancel the constants and equal the logits of N at a = 0. Then d_x = (build's logits) - y(x) is +- (a/2)(X_w - M_w) on the tail and 0 elsewhere. Since W >= 1, every |M_wj - X_wj| <= sqrt(p*_r) <= sqrt(E_W), so the spread of d_x is at most alpha. Lemma TQ8 gives KL(s_x || softmax(y + d_x)) <= g(alpha) (1/2) sum over j of s_x[j] d_x[j]^2. Sum over the 2m points with weight 1/(2m): the loss is at most g(alpha) e^(a/2) Gamma p*_r <= (1 + 3 alpha) Gamma p*_r, using g(c) <= 1 + c and e^(c/2) <= 1 + c on [0, 1].
Lower side. Take any free-code choice (t_w, V, c) with loss D. If D > (1 + 3 alpha) Gamma p*_r there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, let d_x = (its logits) - y(x).
Step 1 (spread). Fix x in A_w. The loss bound gives KL(s_x || q_x) <= 2 m D <= (a^2 tau / 4)(4/3) E_W = alpha^2 tau / 3. Let i be a class other than b = b_w, P_i = s_x[i] / (s_x[i] + s_x[b]) <= 1/2, and e_i = d_x[i] - d_x[b]. The chain rule of KL on the pair {i, b} gives KL(s_x || q_x) >= (s_x[i] + s_x[b]) A(e_i), with A(e) = log(1 + P_i (e^e - 1)) - P_i e. A is convex with A(0) = A'(0) = 0, and A''(e) = P_i (1 - P_i) e^e / D_e^2 with D_e = 1 + P_i (e^e - 1). For |e| <= 1, D_e <= (1 + e^1) / 2, so A'' >= P_i / 19 and A(e) >= P_i e^2 / 38. For |e| > 1, convexity gives A(e) >= P_i / 38. So KL(s_x || q_x) >= s_x[i] min(e_i^2, 1) / 38, and with s_x[i] >= 9 tau / 10 this gives min(e_i^2, 1) <= 15 alpha^2 < 1. So |e_i| <= 4 alpha for every i, and the spread of d_x is at most 8 alpha. The price of a class and its gain have the same scale s_x[i], which is why no tiny number enters.
Step 2 (quadratic). By Lemma TQ8, KL(s_x || q_x) >= g(-8 alpha) (1/2) Var_(s_x)(d_x), and g(-c) >= 1 - c/3 for c >= 0.
Step 3 (the shared class pins the gauge). Var_s(d) = sum over unordered pairs {i, l} of s_i s_l (d_i - d_l)^2. Keep the pairs (b, j), (g, j) for tail j and (b, g). With f_j = d_j - d_g and y' = d_b - d_g, and (f - y')^2 >= (1 - theta) f^2 - (1/theta - 1) y'^2 with theta = eta / (s[g] + eta) <= 4 eta, the coefficient of y'^2 is s[b] (s[g] - (1/theta - 1) (sum over j of s_j)) >= 0. So Var_s(d) >= (s[b] (1 - theta) + s[g]) sum over j of s_j f_j^2 >= (1 - 5 eta) sum over j of s_j f_j^2. With the table's facts, Var_(s_x)(d_x) >= (1 - 6 eta) e^(-a/2) tau sum over j of W_wj (d_x[j] - d_x[g])^2.
Step 4 (two points). Let l' be the build's logits, and let G be the m x n matrix with G_wj = (l'(x_w^+)[j] - l'(x_w^+)[g]) - (l'(x_w^-)[j] - l'(x_w^-)[g]). t_w cancels, so G_wj = (V_j - V_g)^T (c(x_w^+) - c(x_w^-)), with V_j the row of V for class j, and G has rank at most r. Since d_x[j] - d_x[g] at x_w^+ minus the same at x_w^- is G_wj - a M_wj, and p^2 + q^2 >= (p - q)^2 / 2, the sum over w and the two points of the terms of Step 3 is at least (1/2) sum over w, j of W_wj (a M_wj - G_wj)^2 >= (a^2 / 2) p*_r. Collect the factors: D >= (1/(2m)) (1 - 8 alpha / 3)(1/2)(1 - 6 eta) e^(-a/2) tau (a^2 / 2) p*_r >= (1 - 4 alpha - 6 eta) Gamma p*_r. QED.
Lean: `tq23_two_points` (Step 4's inequality); `tq23_gauge` holds Step 3's inequality. Both are one line of algebra. The rest is by hand; the steps use Lemma TQ8 and the chain rule, and no new analysis.
Comment. Two parts of this proof carry the weight. A class's cost and its gain carry the same s_x[i] (Step 1), so a build cannot gain by pushing a tiny class far. And the free t_w per area makes the weight pattern free. On a table with no kept units it is not free, since the log of a fit's probabilities has rank at most k + 1 after row centring; Lemma TQ23.b pays for this with m - 1 units. The shared class g is needed: with own classes alone, V on b_w gives each row its own constant on the tail, so the fit would be rank r plus a free constant per row, a different problem.

**Lemma TQ23.b (the same with no kept units: the table) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-02).** Let N = N(M, W; a, B) with E_W >= 1, alpha <= 1/9, eta <= 1/100, m >= 2, and B >= 32 alpha m. Let S be all of the layer, T empty, and k = m - 1 + r. Let nu = 64 m E_W sqrt(m n d) (log d + 2) / B. Then L_table(k) = L_free(k) = V_b(k) = L_on(k), and
   (1 - 4 alpha - 6 eta) Gamma (p*_r(M, W) - nu) <= V_b(k) <= (1 + 3 alpha) Gamma p*_r(M, W).
Proof. The equalities are Theorem TQ14 part 6: the regions are single points, and the 2m vectors (z_S(x), 1) are independent. Upper side: take X and t_w as in Lemma TQ23.a. The rows are y^0_w +- (a/2) X_w with y^0_w = y at a = 0. They lie in y^0_1 plus the span of the m - 1 vectors y^0_w - y^0_1 and the r columns v^l, so they are a table build at k, with the loss bound of TQ23.a.
Lower side. Take a build l'_x = t + V c_x with loss D <= (1 + 3 alpha) Gamma p*_r. Steps 1 to 3 of TQ23.a are about one point at a time and use nothing about t_w, so they hold: |d_x[i] - d_x[g]| <= 8 alpha for all i, x. Let pi send a vector to its differences from coordinate g. The points pi l'_x lie in an affine space with direction space Lam of dimension at most k. Let p_w be the mean of pi l' on A_w, q_w = p_w - p_1 (w >= 2), and dhat_w = pi l'(x_w^+) - pi l'(x_w^-); all lie in Lam. On the coordinates b_2, ..., b_m, the vectors q_w form the matrix B I + E with |E_(w w')| <= 16 alpha, since y^0_w[b_w'] - y^0_1[b_w'] = B when w' = w and 0 when w' != w, for w, w' >= 2. So they are independent, and the restriction of Lam to these coordinates is onto R^(m-1). Let Lam_0 be the part of Lam that is 0 on them: its dimension is at most r. Write dhat_w = sum over w' >= 2 of c_(w w') q_w' + v_w with v_w in Lam_0. On the coordinates b_2, ..., b_m, N's own logits do not move inside an area, so |dhat_w| <= 16 alpha there, and |c_(w w')| <= 16 alpha / (B - 16 alpha m) <= 32 alpha / B. On the tail, |q_w'[j]| <= log d + 2. So on the tail dhat_w = v_w + xi_w with the matrix (v_w) of rank at most r and |xi_wj| <= kappa = 32 m alpha (log d + 2) / B. Step 4 of TQ23.a holds with G_wj = dhat_w[j], and the triangle inequality in the W norm gives
   sqrt(sum over w, j of W_wj (a M_wj - G_wj)^2) >= a sqrt(p*_r) - kappa sqrt(m n d).
Squaring, with p*_r <= E_W, the sum is at least a^2 (p*_r - nu) (when the right side above is negative, p*_r - nu is negative too, and the claim is empty). Collect the factors as in TQ23.a. QED.
Lean: `tq23_two_points`; the rest is linear algebra by hand.
Comment. Read as a network: the whole budget but r units goes to writing which area a photo is in, and this cannot be avoided, since those are the heavy classes. The fight is over the last r units. Using an area's own direction to help another area's tail is priced at B, on that area's own class. So B must be large against the tail's logits, and then the rest of the proof is that of TQ23.a.

**Lemma TQ23.c (padding: from rank one to any rank) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02, from REFEREE-BQ11-2026-11-02.md; it replaces a use of Remark 3 of Gillis and Glineur, whose sketch fails at rank 3).** Let M be the biadjacency matrix (m x n) of a bipartite graph G with |E| >= 1 edges, whose largest biclique has |E*| edges. Let r >= 2, t an integer with t^2 > 4 |E|, and d' >= max(2^14 |E|^6, 65536 r^2 |E|^3 m n). Let M' be the block diagonal of M and r - 1 blocks J_t (all ones, t x t), and W' = M' + d' (1 - M'). Then
   |E| - |E*| - 5/16 < p*_r(M', W') <= |E| - |E*|.
Proof. Write W for the block of W' on M. Lemma 3 of Gillis and Glineur at epsilon = 1/4 gives |E| - |E*| - 1/4 < p*_1(M, W) <= |E| - |E*|, since d' >= 2^14 |E|^6; its proof needs only real d' >= 1.
Upper side. Let X_1 attain p*_1(M, W). The block diagonal of X_1 and the J_t has rank at most r, cost p*_1(M, W), and no error elsewhere.
Lower side. Let X of rank at most r attain p*_r(M', W'), so its cost is at most |E|. Each J_t block has an entry in [1/2, 3/2]: otherwise the block alone costs at least t^2 / 4 > |E|. Take one such entry from each block, at rows p_1, ..., p_(r-1) and columns q_1, ..., q_(r-1). Every entry off the blocks has W' = d' and M' = 0, so |X| <= delta = sqrt(|E| / d'), and r delta <= 1/4. The pivot matrix D = X[p, q] has diagonal in [1/2, 3/2] and off-diagonal entries of size at most delta, so it is invertible, with the largest absolute row sum of its inverse at most 1 / (1/2 - r delta) <= 4. The Schur complement S = X[G, G] - X[G, q] D^(-1) X[p, G] has rank at most r - (r - 1) = 1. The entries of X[G, q] and X[p, G] lie off the blocks, so each entry of S differs from that of X[G, G] by at most (r - 1) delta 4 delta <= 4 r delta^2. In the W norm the difference is at most xi = sqrt(m n d') 4 r delta^2 = 4 r |E| sqrt(m n / d') <= 1 / (64 sqrt |E|). So sqrt(p*_1(M, W)) <= sqrt(p*_r(M', W')) + xi, and with p*_r <= |E|, p*_1(M, W) <= p*_r(M', W') + 2 sqrt(|E|) xi + xi^2 <= p*_r(M', W') + 1/16. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: a Schur complement and a triangle inequality, both standard.

**Theorem TQ23 (the least of a squeeze is NP-hard, on networks with every claim at error 0; this proves Conjecture DI1) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ11).** The maximum-edge biclique decision problem (given a bipartite graph G with edge set E, and K_0: is there a biclique with at least K_0 edges?) reduces in polynomial time to each of the following. Each is a threshold question on a network N with rational weights and rational P, on the map M_N of Definition DQ18, whose every claim has eps = 0.
1. (One unit, areas kept.) Decide V_b(1) <= theta, for S the group units and T the judgment units.
2. (A table, no kept units, k part of the input.) Decide L_table(k) <= theta, with 2m rows and T empty, which equals V_b(k), L_free(k) and L_on(k) there, at k = m.
3. (r units, areas kept.) For every r polynomial in the size of G, decide V_b(r) <= theta in the setting of part 1.
So no polynomial-time rule computes these leasts unless P = NP. In parts 1 and 3 this holds for approximation within an additive Gamma / 32, which is 1/poly. In parts 1 and 2 it holds within a factor 1 + 1/(8 m n), where M is m x n, so N has 2m units and m + n + 1 classes. On this family no constant factor is excluded. On other networks of Definition DQ18, Proposition TQ30 excludes one.
Proof. Remove isolated nodes. If G is a biclique, or K_0 < 1, or K_0 > |E|, answer directly. Otherwise |E| >= 2, m >= 2 and n >= 2. Let M be G's biadjacency matrix, X_0 = |E| - K_0, and L_0 an integer that is at least 14 log 2 + 6 log |E| and at most that plus 2, with d = e^(L_0), W = M + d (1 - M), so E_W = |E| and L_wj is 0 or L_0. Lemma 3 of Gillis and Glineur at epsilon = 1/4 gives |E| - |E*| - 1/4 < p*_1(M, W) <= |E| - |E*|. Take a = 1/(64 |E|^2), so alpha <= 1/(64 |E|^(3/2)) and 4 alpha <= 1/(16 |E|). Take B an integer that is at least log(96 |E| (m + 2 n d)) and at most that plus 2, so 6 eta <= 1/(16 |E|) and eta <= 1/192. In part 2 take also B >= 512 m |E| sqrt(m n d) (L_0 + 2), an integer of polynomial size, so nu <= 1/8 and B >= 32 alpha m. Let epsilon' = 4 alpha + 6 eta <= 1/(8 |E|).
If |E*| >= K_0, then p*_1 <= X_0, and the least is at most Gamma (X_0 + 3 alpha |E|) <= Gamma (X_0 + 1/8). If |E*| <= K_0 - 1, then p*_1 > X_0 + 3/4. Since X_0 + 3/4 <= 2 |E|, Lemma TQ23.a gives a least of at least Gamma (X_0 + 1/2), and Lemma TQ23.b, with nu <= 1/8, gives at least Gamma (X_0 + 3/8). Take theta rational within Gamma / 32 of Gamma (X_0 + 5/16).
Part 3. Replace (M, W) by (M', W') of Lemma TQ23.c, with t and an integer log d' of polynomial size, |E'| = |E| + (r - 1) t^2 in place of |E| in a and B, and m', n' in place of m, n. Then E_W' = |E'|. If |E*| >= K_0 the least is at most Gamma (X_0 + 1/8). If |E*| <= K_0 - 1 then p*_r > X_0 + 11/16, and since X_0 + 11/16 <= 2 |E'|, the least is at least Gamma (X_0 + 7/16). The same formula for theta works, with the padded network's Gamma.
Bit lengths. All of a, B, L_0, log d' are rational of polynomial size, so y is rational, and Gamma, which is not, is computed to the needed precision with polynomially many bits. In parts 1 and 3, B is a logarithm of a polynomial, so Gamma is 1/poly. In part 2, B is a polynomial, so Gamma is about e^(-B). The gap of Gamma / 4 or more gives the additive statement. For the factor: if least <= v <= (1 + delta) least with delta = 1/(8 m n), then at a yes instance v <= Gamma (X_0 + 1/8) (1 + delta) < Gamma (X_0 + 9/32), since X_0 + 1/8 <= 9 m n / 8, and at a no instance v >= Gamma (X_0 + 3/8). The maximum-edge biclique decision problem is NP-complete (Peeters 2003). QED.
Lean: none, since NP-hardness is a statement about all algorithms and the project has no complexity theory in Lean; the finite inequalities are in Lemma TQ23.a.
Label: a theorem about the general form, not one of the four labels. It fills no slot, and it does not meet the bar. Scope, said plainly. (a) These networks have tail mass at most eta and small a, so KL is quadratic there. Real tables are not there (Part C, round 2, measurement 6). (b) Part 2 needs B polynomial, so its tail masses are about e^(-B), and its hardness is about differences at probabilities exponentially small in the input. Parts 1 and 3 have a gap of at least Gamma / 4, with Gamma a small 1/poly. Nothing is claimed at constant accuracy. (c) Part 2 has k about half of the rows. Hardness at fixed k with T empty stays open. (d) In parts 1 and 3 the kept judgment units do the work of writing the weight pattern. In part 2 the group is the whole layer, and only the single-point constancy claim is used, which holds for every network. (e) Every claim of M_N holds, but the instance is not shown to be trained-like: its tail patterns are arbitrary bipartite graphs, and no training run produced them. So this meets the words "not possible" only for the general form. It says nothing about whether a real network's least can be computed.

**Corollary TQ23.1 (no polynomial-time closed form in general) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-02).** Unless P = NP, no rule that runs in polynomial time and reads N, P and a map of the types named in this paper computes the least at k_S = 1, on maps whose every claim has eps = 0, even where the areas, judgments and linear reads all hold.
Proof. Theorem TQ23 part 1, on the map M_N. A rule that computes the least decides the threshold question. QED.
Lean: none, as for Theorem TQ23.

**Corollary TQ23.2 (a limit on any exact claim type with a polynomial closed form) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ11).** Let a claim type have an error whose value 0 is decided in polynomial time. Suppose every network of Theorem TQ23 part 1 has a claim of the type of polynomial size with error 0, and from every such claim a rule gives the least within Gamma / 32 in polynomial time. Then NP = coNP.
Proof. How a map is found lies outside the trunk, so a claim can be guessed. Guess it, check that its error is 0, and compute the least to within Gamma / 32. Since the gap of Theorem TQ23 part 1 is at least Gamma / 4, this decides the threshold at finite precision, and it puts the threshold question and its complement in NP. Theorem TQ23 then puts an NP-hard problem in coNP. QED.
Lean: none, as for Theorem TQ23.
Comment. The trunk leaves "complete" to be defined in the paper. So this limits any definition of complete under which these networks are complete and the closed form takes polynomial time. The trunk's own "exact closed form" has no time bound, and node R-mixclean allows a one-time computation of any cost, so this does not contradict the trunk.

**Corollary TQ23.3 (no universal short certificate at this accuracy) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ11).** A certificate system is a polynomial-time verifier of triples (N, v, c) that accepts only when v is at most the least. Unless NP = coNP, no such system has, on every network of Theorem TQ23 part 2, an accepted c of polynomial size with v at least L_table(k) / (1 + 1/(8 m n)). The same holds for V_b(1) in part 1.
Proof. Such a system would put the no-instances of Theorem TQ23 in NP: a certificate at a no-instance shows a value of at least Gamma (X_0 + 3/8) / (1 + 1/(8 m n)) > Gamma (X_0 + 1/8), since X_0 + 3/8 <= 11 m n / 8, and no yes-instance has such a value. QED.
Lean: none, as for Theorem TQ23.
Comment. This excludes one named accuracy on this family. By itself it does not exclude a family of dual points good within a factor of 2 or of 10 on every table. Propositions TQ30 and TQ31 limit that on other networks, the second under a conjecture. So it does not show that the searches of B.Q.10 could not succeed, and it does not explain why their certificates miss real tables. It leaves node R-mixclean's choice (e) as written.

**Definition DQ19 (tree weight claim) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ11; node R-treeweight).** A **tree weight claim** names a partition A_1, ..., A_K of P with one class for each region (K = C), and a rooted binary tree on the classes. Let lca(c, i) be the lowest common ancestor. Its error is
   eps_tree = eps_const + the least over real alpha_c, beta_i, and f_v for each internal node v of sum over c of pi_c sum over classes i != c of sbar_c[i] (log sbar_c[i] - alpha_c - beta_i - f_(lca(c, i)))^2.
It is 0 exactly when s_x is constant on each region and every region's table, off its own class, is a row scale times a column scale times a number that depends only on where the two classes meet in the tree. The scales and the f_v are not part of the claim: the least is a weighted least squares problem. It uses logarithms and is computed to any precision in polynomial time. It names no build, size or zoom.

**Proposition TQ24 (a tree weight pattern without scales gives easy threshold graphs) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02; corrected after REFEREE-BQ11, which found that the first form named the wrong graph).** Let W_ci = f_(lca(c, i)) for c != i on the classes of a rooted tree, with f at a node at most f at each of its descendants, and W_cc at least f at c's parent. For a level theta, let H_theta be the bipartite graph between rows and columns (both the classes) with an edge (c, i) when W_ci < theta. This is the graph that the reduction of Theorem TQ23 reads, since there the edges are the low weights. Let B_1, ..., B_q be the leaf sets of the highest nodes with f >= theta, together with each other class c with W_cc >= theta as a set of one, and let s be the number of remaining classes. Then the largest biclique of H_theta has (x + s)(C_b - x + s) edges, with C_b the sum of the sizes |B_l|, maximised over sums x of some of those sizes. It is found by dynamic programming in time polynomial in C. The same holds when rows and columns are different sets of leaves, as they are in the networks of Theorem TQ23: with a_l rows and b_l columns in block l, and s_R rows and s_Q columns in no block, the largest biclique is the largest (s_R + the sum over A of a_l)(s_Q + the sum over the other blocks of b_l), over sets A of blocks.
Proof. The highest nodes with f >= theta are pairwise not nested, so the B_l are disjoint. If c and i lie in one B_l, they are equal or their lca is B_l's node or a descendant, so W_ci >= theta by monotonicity, and for c = i in a larger B_l, c's parent has f >= theta, so W_cc >= theta. If c != i do not lie in one B_l, let v be their lca. If f_v >= theta, then v lies at or below a highest node, whose leaf set holds both c and i, which is excluded. So W_ci < theta. So in a biclique no B_l supplies both a row and a column, every B_l can supply all its members on one side, and a class in no B_l can be on both sides. Sum over the sides. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: a short argument on a finite tree, with no analysis to check.
Comment. This excludes the reduction, not the problem: it does not say that weighted low-rank fitting with tree weights is easy. It covers monotone f only, and Definition DQ19 allows any f. It has no row or column scales. With scales the graphs are richer: at u = v = (1, 2, 4, 8) and W_ci = u_c v_i, the graph {W >= 8} has an induced path (row 1, column 4, row 2, column 3). Without scales that graph is a disjoint union of bicliques and isolated nodes, which has no induced path of 4 nodes. So this proposition does not cover the shape of Definition DQ19.

### B.Q.12 What gap-completion hardness can and cannot give at a fixed factor (added 2026-11-02; card 3-37)

Why this section. Theorem TQ23 excludes a fast rule only at accuracy about 1/(8 m n). Card 3-37 asks whether a fixed factor can be excluded. Propositions TQ30 and TQ31 answer this on clean networks: a fixed factor is excluded at k = 1. The first comes from vertex cover, the second from Max-Cut under the Unique Games Conjecture. Before them, Proposition TQ26 says why the direct lift of completion hardness fails, Lemma TQ27 is a tool that gives many bad rows, and Proposition TQ28 is an upper limit on such constructions. No result here fills a slot or carries one of the four labels. These are limits and tools. Their tables are tables of graphs, not shown to be trained-like.

**Proposition TQ26 (one bad entry cannot pay for the holes) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-02).** Let Omega be a set of entries of an m x n table, called exposed, and the others holes. Let N = N(M, W; a, B) of Definition DQ18, with M in {0, 1} on Omega, M = 0 on holes, W = d >= 1 on Omega, W = 1 on holes, a <= 1/9, eta <= 1/100, E_W >= 1. For a build write e_(x,j) = (l'_x[j] - l'_x[g]) - (y_x[j] - y_x[g]).
1. (The build.) Let X be a real matrix with X = M on Omega and |X_wj| <= 1 on holes, of rank at most r, and h the sum over holes of X_wj^2. Then L_on(r) <= (1 + 3 a) Gamma h.
2. (What a loss bound reads, entry by entry.) For a build of loss D, at x in A_w and a hole (w, j): (9 tau / 10) min(e_(x,j)^2, 1) / 38 <= 2 m D. Applied at the two points of A_w, with (p - q)^2 <= 2 (p^2 + q^2), it gives |G_wj| <= a theta on every hole, for G of Lemma TQ23.a and a theta < 2^(1/2), only for D <= 2 D_theta with D_theta = 9 tau a^2 theta^2 / (3040 m). Then 2 D_theta / (Gamma h) = 9 theta^2 / (190 h).
3. (Graphs.) Let m = n, let Omega be the diagonal and the adjacent pairs of a graph H on n >= 2 r vertices, and let X be any exact fit of rank at most r with entries at most 1 in size. Then h >= n^2 / r - n, since n = tr X <= r^(1/2) |X|_F. Let a NO instance on the same n have the property that X', Y' of row norm at most theta_row with X' Y'^T an epsilon-fit of H imply at most (4 theta_row^2 / (1 - epsilon) + 1)^(d_2) colors (Chawin and Haviv, Theorem 3.5), with chromatic number above that number. Then 4 theta_row^2 < n^(1 / d_2). An entry bound theta >= 1 + epsilon gives row norms with theta_row^2 = r^(1/2) theta, up to the factor of their Lemma 2.2, and their Theorem 3.5 needs theta_row >= 1, so theta^2 < n^(2 / d_2) / (16 r), and the ratio of part 2 is below 1. For the line digraph form (their Theorem 3.8), the same reading gives a smaller theta, with the exponent 1 / (d_2 m).
Proof. (1) This is the upper side of Lemma TQ23.a with X in place of the minimiser, with S the group units, T the judgment units kept, and k = r. Minimality was used only for the bound on the spread, and here the spread of the residual is at most a, since |M - X| <= 1 on every entry, and the sum over w, j of W_wj (M_wj - X_wj)^2 is h. (2) This is Step 1 of Lemma TQ23.a on the pair {j, g}, where s_x[j] <= eta <= 1/100 and s_x[g] >= 1/4, so P_j <= 1/2: KL(s_x || q_x) >= s_x[j] min(e^2, 1) / 38, and s_x[j] >= 9 tau / 10. The two points share the budget 2 m D, and G_wj = e_(x+,j) - e_(x-,j) on a hole. The arithmetic gives D_theta, and Gamma = a^2 tau / (8 m). (3) With r >= d_2 not assumed, use n >= 2 r: 9 theta^2 / (190 h) <= 9 n^(2 / d_2) / (16 r 190 (n^2 / r - n)) < 1. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: a substitution into Lemma TQ23.a and one inequality.
Label: a limit of method, like TZ24 and TZ30. Comment. The binding term is the bound on holes. An exposed entry pays d, which is free, so one bad exposed entry is not the problem. To read a low-rank fit in a completion theorem's terms, every hole must be bounded, and one hole's cost must then be above the loss of a YES build, which pays on every hole. The frame also assumes that a YES build fits every row. Proposition TQ30 drops this assumption, and that is why it has no such limit. This is a statement about this argument, not about the least.

**Definition DQ20 (conflict system) (added 2026-11-02).** A conflict system has a finite set of vertices with weights w(v) >= 0 of sum 1, a finite set of positions, and for each vertex a set of at most R positions it reads, with an answer in {+1, -1} at each. Two vertices conflict at a position when both read it with different answers. Its graph joins conflicting vertices. An independent set is a set of vertices with no conflict. For a position p, N(p) is the weight of the vertices that read p, N_+(p) and N_-(p) the weights by answer. The **conflict distribution** pi on ordered pairs is pi(u, v) = (1/Z) sum over positions p at which u, v conflict of w(u) w(v) / N(p), with Z = sum over p of 2 N_+(p) N_-(p) / N(p). For a set T, w(T) is its weight and pi(T) the mass of the ordered pairs inside T. The graph of a probabilistically checkable proof with R queries, in which vertices are a query and an accepted answer, is of this form (Feige, Goldwasser, Lovasz, Safra, Szegedy 1996).

**Lemma TQ27 (cleaning: a set with few conflicts holds an independent set) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** For a conflict system and any set T of vertices, the graph has an independent set inside T of weight at least w(T) - (R/2) sqrt(pi(T)). Consequently, if every independent set has weight at most alpha, then for every f-coloring of the vertices with f alpha < 1, the mass under pi of the pairs with one color is at least (4 / R^2)(1 - f alpha)^2 / f.
Proof. Fix T. At each position p let N^T_+ and N^T_- be the weights inside T by answer, r_p their minimum, and y_p = 2 N^T_+ N^T_- / N(p). Remove from T, at each p, the vertices with the minority answer (either one at a tie). The rest has no conflict, and its weight is at least w(T) - sum over p of r_p. Since N^T_+ N^T_- >= r_p^2, r_p <= sqrt(N(p) y_p / 2). By Cauchy-Schwarz, the sum of r_p is at most sqrt((sum N(p)) (sum y_p) / 2). Here sum N(p) <= R, since each vertex reads at most R positions, and sum y_p = Z pi(T), and Z <= sum N(p) / 2 <= R / 2, since 2 N_+ N_- <= N(p)^2 / 2. So the sum of r_p is at most sqrt(R (R/2) pi(T) / 2) = (R/2) sqrt(pi(T)). For the consequence, let T_1, ..., T_f be the color classes and rho the sum of pi(T_i). Adding the first statement over i: 1 - (R/2) sum sqrt(pi(T_i)) <= f alpha, and sum sqrt(pi(T_i)) <= sqrt(f rho). QED.
Lean: tq27_clean
What Lean covers: only the step N^T_+ N^T_- >= r_p^2. The sums and Cauchy-Schwarz are by hand.
Label: a tool. It says nothing about networks by itself. Comment. It turns an independence bound, which Huang 2013 gives at 2^(-Omega(K)) on a K^3-colorable graph, into a statement about a constant mass of edges, with no factor of the degree. A random f-coloring leaves mass about 1/f, so the bound is tight in f up to R^2.

**Proposition TQ28 (a build that fits nearly every row, on any graph) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Let H be the underlying graph of the line digraph of a graph with symmetric edge distribution pi, and let b(r) be the central binomial coefficient C(r, floor(r/2)). For every r, there is a matrix X in {0, 1}^(E x E) of rank at most r, whose entries at adjacent pairs are 0, whose diagonal is 1 except on a set of edges of mass at most 1 / b(r).
Proof. Color the vertices at random with b(r) colors. The expected mass of the pairs with one color is 1 / b(r), so some coloring has at most this mass. Let the graph G' keep the other edges. It has chromatic number at most b(r), so the underlying graph of its line digraph has chromatic number at most r (Poljak and Rodl 1981, in the form of Chawin and Haviv, Theorem 3.7). Let X be the Gram matrix of this r-coloring on the edges of G', and 0 on every other row and column. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: an expectation and the cited theorem.
Label: a limit of this construction. Comment. By the upper side of Lemma TQ23.a, an instance of this form with W on the diagonal proportional to pi has, at rank r, loss at most Gamma times the hole sum of X^2, plus the diagonal weight times about 1 / b(r). So a large factor needs hole weights far below 1 / b(r), when the YES and NO hole terms are comparable. This is a remark on the form, and it holds only as stated here.

**Proposition TQ30 (a fixed factor is hard with every claim at error 0: vertex cover) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds; part 3's last line under the Unique Games Conjecture) (added 2026-11-02, from REFEREE-BQ12; revised after its second round).** Let Q be a graph on n >= 2 vertices with at least one edge and vertex cover number vc(Q). For delta in (0, 1/100], let M = I_n, W_vv = ell >= n^2 / delta, W_uv = d >= ell n / (2 delta^2) for uv an edge of Q, in both orders, and W_uv = 1 otherwise.
1. ell vc(Q) (1 - delta)^2 <= p*_1(M, W) <= ell vc(Q) (1 + delta).
2. On N = N(M, W; a, B) of Definition DQ18, with a rational in [delta / (2 (n ell)^(1/2)), delta / (n ell)^(1/2)] and B with eta <= delta, with S the group units, T the judgment units kept, and k = 1: every claim of M_N has error 0, and L_free(1) <= V_b(1) <= L_on(1), with L_free(1) >= (1 - 10 delta)(1 - delta)^2 Gamma ell vc(Q) and L_on(1) <= (1 + 3 delta)(1 + delta) Gamma ell vc(Q).
3. Say a rule returns V_b(1) within F when least <= v <= F least. A polynomial-time rule within a factor F < 10 5^(1/2) - 21, about 1.3606, gives P = NP (Dinur and Safra 2005). A stronger factor, F < 2^(1/2), follows from the work of Khot, Minzer and Safra on 2-to-2 games, whose final step I have from a secondary source only. Under the Unique Games Conjecture, it holds for F < 2 (Khot and Regev 2008).
4. If the source's reduction is many-one, which I did not check at the source: unless NP = coNP, no system of polynomial-size certificates checked in polynomial time accepts, on every such network, a lower bound on V_b(1) within a factor below 1.3606.
Proof. (1) Upper side: let C be a least cover and I its complement, an independent set. X = 1_I 1_I^T has rank 1. It costs ell on each v in C, 0 on each v in I, 0 on each edge, since no edge lies inside I, and at most 1 on each other entry. So p*_1 <= ell vc(Q) + n^2 <= ell vc(Q)(1 + delta), since vc(Q) >= 1. Lower side: let X = u v^T attain p*_1, with cost at most ell n, the cost of 0. Put f_w = u_w v_w. For an edge wj, d ((u_w v_j)^2 + (u_j v_w)^2) <= ell n. Since x^2 + y^2 >= 2 |x y| and (u_w v_j)(u_j v_w) = f_w f_j, |f_w f_j| <= ell n / (2 d) <= delta^2. So {w : f_w > delta} holds no edge, and its complement C is a cover, with |C| >= vc(Q). Each w in C has f_w <= delta < 1, so it pays at least ell (1 - delta)^2. (2) E_W = n ell >= 1, and alpha = a E_W^(1/2) <= delta <= 1/9, and eta <= 1/100. Lemma TQ23.a gives the bounds, with 4 alpha + 6 eta <= 10 delta and 3 alpha <= 3 delta. Its upper side uses a through alpha only, and the factor in Gamma is exact. The claims hold by Definition DQ18, whose map is not changed. ell and d can be of the form e^q with q an integer of polynomial size, and a rational, so the weights are rational in the sense of Definition DQ18. B is O(log(n / delta)). Gamma and ell are needed only to relative accuracy delta, which takes polynomially many bits. (3) Take delta so small that F (1 + 3 delta)(1 + delta) < (1 - 10 delta)(1 - delta)^2 F', with F < F' below the source's factor. Then delta depends only on F, and an estimate of V_b(1) within F separates vc(Q) <= c from vc(Q) > F' c. (4) A many-one reduction from SAT through the gap to the network puts UNSAT in NP, as in Corollary TQ23.3. QED.
Lean: tq30_two_two
What Lean covers: only the two-by-two inequality of part 1's lower side. The rest is by hand, and the complexity statements have no Lean form here.
Label: a theorem about the general form, not one of the four labels. It fills no slot. Scope, said plainly. (a) The table is a table of a graph. Every claim of the map holds, but the network is not shown to meet the clean principles of Part A, and it is not shown to be trained-like. Its tail mass and movement are small, and V_b(1) is itself about 1/poly, so the factor sits on a tiny loss. Proposition TQ31's per-area form has no such limit. (b) M_N is not complete in the sense of Definition DM6, and no extension of it is complete at k = 1 for n >= 2: C = 2 n + 1 > 2 n = |P|, so a pole claim with K = C non-empty regions cannot exist. So this limits card 3-36's option (c), and it does not touch T5's exactness promise. The trunk's closed form has no time limit either. (c) It is at k = 1, with the areas kept. Comment. The gap sits in which rows the unit gives up: one unit can write its pattern only on an independent set of areas. No coloring, no line digraph and no size of entries enters, because the two-by-two identity replaces the factorisation. It corrects the end of Theorem TQ23, where no constant factor is excluded: that holds for the family of Theorem TQ23, not for N(M, W; a, B) in general.

**Definition DQ24 (per-area form of the weight-pattern network) (added 2026-11-02, after REFEREE-BQ12's third round).** N(M, W; a, (B_w), (p_w)) is N(M, W; a, B) of Definition DQ18 with one B_w > 1 for each area in place of B, and with weights p_w / 2 on the two points of A_w, where the p_w > 0 sum to 1. Its map M_N is the same, and every claim has error 0: each error is a p-weighted sum, ratio or maximum of terms that vanish at these points, for every p > 0, the parts of y that are constant on A_w are removed by the projection of the linear-read claim, and the constancy regions are single points. With rational p_w of polynomial denominator, P can be written as a list with repeats.

**Proposition TQ31 (every fixed factor under the Unique Games Conjecture, at any movement and tail mass, with the loss of the order of the uncut share) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds; part 3 under the Unique Games Conjecture) (added 2026-11-02, from REFEREE-BQ12's second and third rounds).** Parts 1 and 2 use no conjecture. Let G be a simple graph on n vertices with E >= 1 edges and no isolated vertex, and U(G) the least number of edges with both ends on one side, over all two-sidings. For D = e^q >= n, with q an integer, let M_uv = -1 and W_uv = D on edges, in both orders, M_vv = 1 and W_vv = e^(q_v) in [D deg(v), e D deg(v)] with q_v an integer, and M = 0, W = 1 otherwise. Let S_w be the sum of row w of W. Fix a rational a > 0, kappa > 0 and xi in (0, 1], and take D also with n - 1 <= xi S_w for every w and D >= 2 / kappa (D >= n gives the first for xi >= 1/2). Take N = N(M, W; a, (B_w), (p_w)), with B_w > 1 rational such that e^(B_w) (1 + 1/e) is within a factor 1 + 1/n of kappa S_w, and p_w rational within a factor 1 + 1/n of S_w / (the sum of all S_w). The constants below hold up to these factors, which tend to 1. With T = kappa + e^(a/2) + xi: for x in A_w, s_x[g] >= s_0 = kappa / ((1 + e) T), and (t' / S_w) W_wj <= s_x[j] <= (t'' / S_w) W_wj, with t' = e^(-a/2) / T and t'' = e^(a/2) / (kappa + e^(-a/2)). At every point the tail's odds lie within a factor depending on a alone of 1 / kappa, and all of the tail moves except the holes, whose mass is at most ((1 + e) / 2) n / S_w. So any tail mass in (0, 1) can be reached by kappa for fixed a, up to that factor. Let c = min(1, s_0 / t') = min(1, kappa e^(a/2) / (1 + e)).
1. (The matrix.) 2 D U(G) <= p*_1(M, W) <= 8 D U(G) + n^2.
2. (The network.) With S the group units, T the judgment units kept, k = 1, psi(e) = exp(e) - 1 - e, and g of Lemma TQ8, up to the rounding factors above:
      c t' psi(-a/4) D U(G) / (sum S_w) <= L_free(1) <= V_b(1) <= L_on(1) <= g(2 a) t'' (a^2 / 8) (8 D U(G) + n^2) / (sum S_w),
   and the sum of S_w lies between 4 D E and (2 + 2 e) D E + n^2. So for D >= n^2 / E, V_b(1) lies between a constant times U(G) / E and a constant times (U(G) / E + n^2 / (D E)), with constants that depend on a and kappa only.
3. (Hardness.) Under the Unique Games Conjecture, for every F, a polynomial-time rule that returns V_b(1) within F, on these networks at any fixed rational a and tail mass, gives P = NP. If the reduction is many-one, then unless NP = coNP, no polynomial-size certificate system accepts lower bounds on V_b(1) within F on every such network.
Proof. Call an entry with M != 0 violated by sign vectors (u, v) when u_a v_b M_ab < 0, and let frust be the least, over sign vectors, of the sum of W / D over violated entries, with W_vv read as D deg(v). (1) frust = 2 U(G). With u = v = sigma, the diagonal is never violated, and the violated entries are the two orders of each edge with both ends on one side, so frust <= 2 U(G). Conversely, given (u, v), let B_0 be the set of b with v_b != u_b. The diagonal pays the sum over B_0 of deg(b). The two-siding u has 2 U(u) ordered edge entries (a, b) with u_a = u_b. Those with b outside B_0 are violated by (u, v), and at most the sum over B_0 of deg(b) have b in B_0. So the total is at least 2 U(u) >= 2 U(G). Lower side: for X = u v^T real, take signs with 0 read as +1. A violated entry has X_ab M_ab <= 0, so (M_ab - X_ab)^2 >= 1, and p*_1 >= D frust. Upper side: u = v = a best two-siding pays 4 D on each of its 2 U(G) violated entries, and at most 1 on each hole.
(2) Upper side: as in Lemma TQ23.a with X = sigma sigma^T: the unit is relu((a/2) sum over w of sigma_w z_(s_w) + beta), with logit weights sigma on the tail, and kept units setting the area offsets. It is a class (b) build. The residual d_x is +- (a/2)(X - M), of size at most a, so its spread is at most 2 a. Lemma TQ8 gives KL <= g(2 a) (1/2) Var_(s_x)(d_x), g is increasing, and the variance is at most the second moment, which is at most (t'' / S_w)(a^2 / 4) times the sum over j of W_wj (X_wj - M_wj)^2. Multiply by p_w / 2 for each of the two points, with p_w = S_w / (sum S_w), and add over w. Lower side, with no quadratic regime. For a free-code build with kept offsets, let e_x[i] = log(q_x[i] / s_x[i]). Then KL(s_x || q_x) = sum over i of s_x[i] psi(e_x[i]), with each term >= 0, since q_x and s_x both sum to 1. Let f_x[j] = e_x[j] - e_x[g], and G_wj = (V_j - V_g)^T (c(x_w^+) - c(x_w^-)). G has rank at most 1. The kept units have one value on A_w, and y[g] is constant on A_w, so G_wj - a M_wj = f_(x+)[j] - f_(x-)[j]. Let V_w be the sum of W_wj over the entries of row w with M_wj != 0 and G_wj M_wj <= 0. By the count of part 1, the sum of V_w over w is at least D 2 U(G). At such an entry |G_wj - a M_wj| = a - G_wj M_wj >= a, so |f_x[j]| >= a/2 at one of the two points x of A_w. Fix an area w. If |e_x[g]| >= a/4 at one of its points, class g pays at least s_0 psi(-a/4) there, using psi(t) >= psi(-t) for t >= 0 and that psi(-t) increases with t. Since V_w <= S_w, this is at least c t' psi(-a/4) V_w / S_w. Otherwise each such entry has |e_x[j]| > a/4 at one point, and pays at least (t' / S_w) W_wj psi(-a/4). Each charge is a separate term (x, class), so nothing is charged twice. Each point has weight p_w / 2, and each charge is at one point, so the area pays at least (p_w / 2) c t' psi(-a/4) V_w / S_w. With p_w = S_w / (sum S_w), adding over w gives D_P >= c t' psi(-a/4) D U(G) / (sum S_w). The sum of S_w is the sum of W_vv, 2 D E on edges, and at most n^2 on holes.
(3) By Khot, Kindler, Mossel and O'Donnell (Corollary 2), under the Conjecture it is NP-hard for small eta to tell a weighted graph with cut at least 1 - eta from one with cut at most 1 - (2/pi) eta^(1/2). I read from their section 8.1, with rho rational, that the weights are rational with polynomial denominators for fixed eta; it is an inference, not their statement. Scale to integers. Self-loops add the same amount L to U in every cut. Drop them: if L exceeds the YES value, answer NO. If the new YES value u_0 is below 1, so that YES means U = 0, test bipartiteness directly. Otherwise u_0 >= 1, and the ratio of NO to YES only rises. Delete vertices left isolated. Replace each copy of an edge by a path of 3 edges with fresh inner vertices. By parity U is exactly unchanged, and the graph is simple. Take D >= n^2 / u_0, with the conditions on D above, polynomial in size. Thresholds are compared to finite precision, which is harmless, since the margin is a constant. Part 2's two sides then differ by the factor K (2/pi) eta^(-1/2), with K = c (t' / t'') psi(-a/4) 8 / (9 g(2 a) a^2), up to the rounding factors, and K does not depend on n or eta. This is above F for small eta. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: a count on a finite graph and one split of KL. Not yet in Lean.
Label: a conditional theorem about the general form, not one of the four labels. It fills no slot. Scope, said plainly. (a) It rests on the Unique Games Conjecture, which is open, so card 3-37's line I2 is met under that conjecture only. (b) It needs a kept judgment unit per area, as in Lemma TQ23.a. (c) On a YES instance the loss is of order eta, and on a NO instance of order eta^(1/2), so at fixed F, a and tail mass it is a constant, not 1/poly, and nearly all the tail moves. Every payment in the lower side is on an entry with |e| >= a/4, so at a >= 4 a part of any near-least build's loss sits at |e| >= 1. It does not show that most of the loss does. So card 3-37's I4 is met in the tail mass, the range and the size of the loss, and not fully in its shape. (d) The tables are tables of graphs, not shown to meet Part A's clean principles. (e) M_N is not complete, and no extension is: here C = m + n + 1 > 2 m = |P|, so a pole claim with K = C non-empty regions cannot exist, C > 2 rules out a blend claim, and k = 1 < c(S) = m for m >= 2, so DM6 item 5 asks for one of them. So T5's exactness promise is not touched. (f) A remark from a referee, from memory, not checked: least-uncut has a polynomial-time rule within O((log n)^(1/2)), so this family cannot give a factor growing past that. Comment. This limits card 3-36's option (c): under the conjecture, a certificate within any fixed factor needs a claim that leaves these networks out.

**Definition DQ25 (the family-table network) (added 2026-11-02; after REFEREE-BQ12's fourth round).** Let G be a simple graph on q vertices with no isolated vertex, with families F_v of t classes each, so n = q t classes and n areas, one area per class. There is no g and there are no own classes b_w: the classes are 1, ..., n. For a row r in F_v and a class b: b = r has M = +1 and W in [D t deg(v), e D t deg(v)]; a sibling b in F_v has M = +1 and 1 <= W <= D deg(v); b in F_w with vw an edge has M = -1 and W = D; otherwise M = 0 and W = 1. Units h_r, s_r, and points x_r^+-, as in Definition DQ18 with m = n, with y_x[b] = log W_rb +- (a/2) M_rb, where h_r carries log W_r - a M_r and s_r carries (a/2) M_r. Weights p_r / 2 on the two points of A_r, with p_r proportional to the row sum S_r of W. Its map holds the districts ({h_r}, A_r) and ({s_r}, A_r), their shelter claims, the judgment claim (A_r, {h_r}, 1), the branch claim ({s_r}), the on-inside claim (A_r, empty set, {h_r}), and the linear-read claim (A_r, {h_r}). Each has error 0, by the reading of Definition DQ18, and none of them mentions g or b_w.

**Proposition TQ33 (the same hardness on tables with families and no shared class) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds; part 2's last line under the Unique Games Conjecture) (added 2026-11-02, from a map agent; revised after REFEREE-BQ12's fourth round).** On the network of Definition DQ25, for D >= n, let the sum of S_r be S. For x in A_r, e^(-a) W_rb / S_r <= s_x[b] <= e^a W_rb / S_r. With one kept judgment unit per area, S the rest, and k = 1:
1. e^(-a) psi(-a/2) D t^2 U(G) / (2 S) <= L_free(1) <= V_b(1) <= L_on(1) <= g(2 a) e^a (a^2 / 8) (8 D t^2 U(G) + h) / S, with h the number of holes.
2. So the argument of Proposition TQ31 part 3 carries over, with K = e^(-2 a) psi(-a/2) 4 / (9 g(2 a) a^2), up to rounding p_r, and with D t^2 u_0 >= h. Under the Unique Games Conjecture no fast rule is within any fixed factor on these tables.
Proof. Bounds on s: every entry moves by at most a/2, so Z_x lies in [e^(-a/2) S_r, e^(a/2) S_r]. Upper side: X = sigma sigma^T, with sigma constant on families and a best two-siding of G. Own and sibling entries cost 0. A side entry pays 4 D if its edge is uncut, and there are 2 t^2 U(G) of those. Lemma TQ8 with spread at most 2 a, and the variance at most the second moment, then give the bound. Lower side: use e_x[i] = log(q_x[i] / s_x[i]) and KL = sum of s_x[i] psi(e_x[i]). In row r, let f_x[b] = e_x[b] - e_x[r], D_r = c(x_r^+) - c(x_r^-), and G_rb = D_r (V_b - V_r). On a side entry M_b - M_r = -2, so f_(x+)[b] - f_(x-)[b] = G_rb + 2 a. Call a side entry violated if G_rb >= 0. Then |f_x[b]| >= a at one of the two points. Fix any choice of one class from each family, and read the sign of D_r on these rows as a two-siding, with 0 read as +. It has at least U(G) uncut edges. On an uncut edge with chosen classes r, b, G_rb G_br = -D_r D_b (V_b - V_r)^2 <= 0, so one of the two is >= 0, and one of the two ordered entries is violated. Each ordered side entry is in the choice with chance 1 / t^2, so at least t^2 U(G) side entries are violated. Fix row r. If |e_x[r]| >= a/2 at some point x of A_r, own pays s_x[r] psi(-a/2) >= e^(-a) (D t deg(v) / S_r) psi(-a/2), which covers all t deg(v) side entries of the row. Else each violated entry has |e_x[b]| > a/2 at its own point, and pays e^(-a) (D / S_r) psi(-a/2) in its own term. Each charge is one term (x, class), and own terms of different rows sit at different points. With weight p_r / 2 per point and p_r = S_r / S, the sum is the left side. QED.
Lean: none, by hand.
Label: a conditional theorem about the general form, not one of the four labels. It fills no slot. Scope. M_N's completeness is not settled here: TQ31's count C > |P| fails, since C = n < 2 n = |P|. At k = 1 < c(S), DM6 item 5 asks for a pole claim with K = C = n regions, which needs s_x constant on n regions. If the 2 n vectors s_x are pairwise distinct, that claim has error above 0, so no extension is complete. Distinctness is not proved for every choice of sibling weights. Comment. Own class carries M = +1 and pins the gauge, so the shared class g of Lemma TQ23.a is not needed. The table's head holds a family and side links, as a map agent reads on ResNet-18.

**Proposition TQ32 (on a finite list, an information floor over all decoders is 0) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Let P be a finite list with distinct z(x) in R^d, and s_x any table. For every k >= 1 and almost every k x d matrix M, y = M z is one-to-one on P. So the least over every decoder q from y to distributions of the sum over x of p_x KL(s_x || q(y(x))) is 0. For a law on x, with i drawn from s_x, the same least is I(i; x | y) = I(i; x) - I(i; y), and for k < d and a law whose support is not countable this can be above 0.
Proof. For z != z', the set of M with M (z - z') = 0 is a proper linear subspace of the matrices, so it has measure 0, and a finite union of such sets has measure 0. Then set q(y(x)) = s_x. For a law: the chain rule gives E KL(s_x || q(y)) = I(i; x | y) + E KL(p(i | y) || q(y)), and the second term is 0 at q = p(i | y). QED.
Lean: none, by hand: a measure-zero union and a substitution.
Label: a limit of method, like TZ24 and TZ30. Comment. So any floor on the read through what k numbers can hold must use something beyond P alone. It must use the decoder's class (one linear map, or a limit on its size), or the law P was drawn from with a bound on the gap between P and the law. With many fewer free numbers than rows, a read cannot memorize P, which is why the read's loss is far above 0, while this quantity is 0. Part C reports a measurement on photos no fit has seen that points at the form of the law.

**Definition DQ22 (weight gap claim) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ12; node R-weightgap).** A **weight gap claim** names a partition A_1, ..., A_K of P and a set H of near classes common to all regions. With pi_c and sbar_c as in Definition DQ10, let W be the K x C matrix with W_ci = pi_c sbar_c[i] for i not in H and 0 otherwise, a and b its row and column sums, and Wtilde = D_a^(-1/2) W D_b^(-1/2) on the classes with b_i > 0. Wtilde has largest singular value 1, with singular vectors a^(1/2) and b^(1/2). The error is eps_gap = eps_const + sigma_2(Wtilde). It is 0 exactly when s_x is constant on each region and, outside H, the table is a row scale times a column scale. It is computed to any precision in polynomial time, and it names no build, size or zoom. Read as a network: sigma_2 is the largest correlation between a function of the region and a function of the class, under the joint law of W. It is not robust to rare pairs: a small entry that is the only link of a region and a class can hold sigma_2 near 1. Part C also reports sigma_2 with near sets that differ per region. That number is a measurement, not this claim's error, since a table with such zeros is never of rank 1. No theorem here uses this claim yet.

**Lemma TQ29 (KL is a variance along the path, at any amplitude) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02).** Let s, q be positive distributions on C classes, xi = log(s / q), and for t in [0, 1] let q_t be proportional to s^(1 - t) q^t. Then
   KL(s || q) = integral over t from 0 to 1 of (1 - t) Var_(q_t)(xi) dt.
On finitely many classes Var_(q_t)(xi) is constant in t only when s = q. For a sequence of pairs (s, q) whose log-moment functions K below converge to a nonzero quadratic on a neighbourhood of [0, 1], the ratio of KL(s || q) to (1/2) Var_s(xi) tends to 1. A zero limit does not give this: s = (1 - e, e), q = (1 - e exp(-x), e exp(-x)), with x fixed and e tending to 0, has K tending to 0, and the ratio tends to 2 (x - 1 + exp(-x)) / x^2. That is the sense in which a Gaussian xi gives equality. With kappa_j the cumulants of xi under s, KL(s || q) = (1/2) kappa_2 - (1/6) kappa_3 + (1/24) kappa_4 - ... when xi has spread below pi. The series can diverge at larger spread, and the integral form holds at any amplitude.
Proof. Let K(t) = log E_s[exp(-t xi)] = log sum over i of s_i^(1 - t) q_i^t. Then K(0) = K(1) = 0, K'(0) = -E_s[xi] = -KL(s || q), and K''(t) = Var_(q_t)(xi). Taylor's formula with integral remainder gives 0 = K(1) = K'(0) + the integral of (1 - t) K''(t) dt. The series is K(1) = 0 written in the cumulants of -xi. For |Im t| times the spread below pi, the terms exp(-t xi_i) lie in an open half-plane, so the sum has no zero, and the radius is at least pi / spread. If K'' is constant on [0, 1], then it is constant on the real line by analyticity. Yet K'' tends to 0 as t grows, since the tilt concentrates on the least value of xi. So the constant is 0, and xi is constant. The limit statement follows since K'' converges with K: exp K is bounded on complex strips by its values on the real line, so Vitali's theorem applies, and K''(0) tends to the nonzero constant. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: Taylor's formula on one smooth function of one variable.
Label: a tool, a true identity. It gives no lower bound over competitors: a large downward move on a class of small s changes Var_s by much more than KL. Lemma TQ8 bounds the ratio by the spread. This identity says what the ratio is. Comment. Part C measures the ratio of KL to (1/2) Var_s(xi) at real fits.

**Definition DQ23 (read curvature claim) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ12; node R-readcurv).** Let z be the pre-activations of a group S, whitened on P, let F_x = D_(s_x) - s_x s_x^T, and let H be the operator on C x |S| matrices with <W, H W> = sum over x of p_x Var_(s_x)(W z(x)), that is, H = sum over x of p_x F_x kron z(x) z(x)^T. It is the Fisher information of the softmax read at N's own outputs, one fixed operator on the read's weights, with no per-row free code in it. A **read curvature claim** names a partition A_1, ..., A_K of P. Its model is Hbar = sum over c of pi_c (F_c kron Sigma_c), with F_c the mean of F_x and Sigma_c the mean of z z^T on A_c. Since every s_x is positive, H and Hbar have the same range, the complement of the constant vector tensor the span of z. The error is the largest of |log lambda| over the eigenvalues lambda of Hbar^(-1/2) H Hbar^(-1/2) on this range. It is 0 exactly when H = Hbar. With K = 1 this says F_x and z z^T are uncorrelated under p. A partition into single points has error 0 for every network, so the claim says something only at small K. It is computed to any precision in polynomial time, and it names no build, size or zoom. For K = 1, a rank-limited least of the quadratic model is an SVD. No theorem here uses this claim yet. Part C reports how far real networks are from it.

### B.Q.13 The bar at a squeeze: KL for the developer's goal (added 2026-11-03; Trunk T6, card 3-40, node R-goalbar)

Why this section. Trunk T6 asks, at a squeeze, for a build that optimizes D_P for the developer's goal, judged against the best trained network of the same form on new inputs. It does not ask for the least over all networks. Theorem TQ23 and Propositions TQ30 and TQ31 stay true as they are, and Proposition TG4 says what they still imply for the new bar. This section gives what the new bar needs from mathematics: which part of a build is exactly optimal, that the goal's weights do what a developer means, why a score on a short list says nothing, and what passing the bar does not promise.

**Definition DG1 (goal, and the bar's words) (added 2026-11-03; revised after REFEREE-BQ13-2026-11-03.md).** A **goal** is a law Q on inputs. The list P, with weights p_x > 0, is a finite sample of Q. An input a developer does not care about has weight 0 under Q, so D_P does not depend on it. When Q has mass off P, **new inputs from the goal** are further draws from Q, not used by any fit. When Q is the finite list P itself, the new inputs are the list. Fix a group S in the last hidden layer, with pre-activations z(x) in R^d (the mean over positions, in a block with positions), and let h_T(x) be the kept units of that layer. The **read** of size k is the build y(x) = V M z(x) + A h_T(x) + t, with M of shape k x d, V of shape C x k, A the write of the kept units, and t in R^C. When T is empty, the term A h_T is absent. A read is a member of class (b) when each new unit stays on: relu(m . z + beta) with beta large enough for the inputs in question, and beta then moves into t. So it is always-on on that set of inputs only. Write s_x = softmax(y_N(x)), q_x = softmax(y(x)), and H for entropy. **Best trained network of the same form** means the lowest D_P on new inputs over reads fitted by a general optimizer from the trunk's starts. It is a reference, and it is an upper value on what the form can do.

**Definition DG2 (the goal read rule) (added 2026-11-03; revised after REFEREE-BQ13-2026-11-03.md).** Given a sample P of a goal, let the means and covariances below be taken under p, with z and y_N centred under p. When T is not empty, z and y_N are first replaced by their residuals after least-squares regression on h_T under p. Let F = E_p[D_(s_x) - s_x s_x^T], and let E = Sigma_zy F Sigma_yz. With Sigma_zz^(+1/2) the square root of the pseudo-inverse of Sigma_zz, let G_A = Sigma_zz^(+1/2) E Sigma_zz^(+1/2). Let U_k hold the top k eigenvectors of G_A, in order of falling eigenvalue, each with its entry of largest absolute value made positive, and let k be at most the rank of G_A, which is at most C - 1. The **goal read rule of size k** takes M_k = U_k^T Sigma_zz^(+1/2) and V_q = Sigma_yz Sigma_zz^(+1/2) U_k. It then minimises D_P over the write at that M_k, the convex problem of Lemma TG1, by one stated deterministic optimizer started at V_q and the mean logits. The least value is unique, and so are the logits on P, up to a constant across classes at each x, since lse is strictly convex modulo constants. The parameters are unique up to that gauge. Its variant with r rounds then alternates r times between the convex problem in (M, t) at fixed V and the convex problem in (V, t) at fixed M. One eigendecomposition serves every k, so the spans of one goal are nested when the top eigenvalues are distinct. A tie among them leaves the eigenvectors to the stated solver, which still gives the same output for the same input bits. There are no random starts. V_q M_k is a least of the quadratic E_p |F^(1/2)(y_N - X z - t)|^2 over maps X of rank at most k (Eckart-Young applied to F^(1/2) Sigma_yz Sigma_zz^(+1/2), whose B^T B is G_A), so the span alone is a closed form for another loss, node R-obj. Whether the build meets the bar is a question for Part C, and no theorem here says it does.

**Lemma TG1 (a fixed read or a fixed write is convex, with an exact check) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-03; revised after REFEREE-BQ13-2026-11-03.md).** Let P be a finite list with weights p_x > 0, and let the logits be linear in a parameter theta: y_x = L_x theta, with fixed matrices L_x. This covers theta = (V, A, t) at a fixed code c(x), including c(x) = M z(x), and theta = (M, A, t) at a fixed V. Let G(theta) = sum over x of p_x L_x^T (q_x - s_x).
1. D_P is convex in theta.
2. The least over theta is attained.
3. theta attains that least if and only if G(theta) = 0. Then the least equals the sum over x of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)).
4. (Weak duality.) For any distributions r_x with sum over x of p_x L_x^T (r_x - s_x) = 0, the least is at least the sum over x of p_x (H(r_x) - H(s_x)).
5. For any theta and any minimiser theta*, D_P(theta) - D_P(theta*) <= |G(theta)| |theta - theta*|.
Proof. KL(s || softmax(y)) = -H(s) - s . y + lse(y), with lse the log of the sum of exp. lse is convex and y_x is linear in theta. This gives 1, and D_P is finite everywhere, so it is closed and proper. For 2: along a direction d with logit moves u_x = L_x d, the recession value of the sum is the sum over x of p_x (max_i u_x[i] - s_x . u_x). Each s_x is positive and sums to 1, so a term is 0 only when u_x is constant across classes, and it is positive otherwise. Along a direction where every u_x is constant, softmax does not change, so D_P is constant. So the directions of recession form a subspace along which D_P is constant. On the orthogonal complement of that subspace, D_P has no nonzero direction of recession, so its level sets there are bounded, hence compact, and a minimum exists. For 3: G is the gradient, and a differentiable convex function is least exactly where its gradient vanishes. For the value, lse(y) = q . y + H(q) at q = softmax(y), so D_P = sum of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)) + sum of p_x (q_x - s_x) . y_x. The last sum is the inner product of G with theta, which is 0. For 4: lse(y) >= r . y + H(r) for every distribution r (Fenchel). So D_P(theta) >= sum of p_x (H(r_x) - H(s_x)) + sum of p_x (r_x - s_x) . y_x, and the last sum is 0 by the condition on r. For 5: convexity gives D_P(theta*) >= D_P(theta) + <G, theta* - theta>, and Cauchy-Schwarz gives the rest. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: the steps are convex analysis on finite sums, and Lean's library use here would outweigh the proof. `model/tg_goal.py` checks parts 3 and 4 on small cases.
Label: a tool. It says which part of a build is exactly optimal: the write at a fixed read, and the read at a fixed write. It does not say the pair is the least. Comment. The pair (M, V) together is not convex, and that is the choice the hardness results of B.Q.11 and B.Q.12 attack.

**Proposition TG2 (a goal's weights steer the optimum) (under: none) (added 2026-11-03; revised after REFEREE-BQ13-2026-11-03.md).** Let F be any set of builds, and let A and B be two goals, with losses v_A, v_B >= 0 on F. For lambda in [0, 1) let L_lambda = (1 - lambda) v_A + lambda v_B. On disjoint lists it is D_P of the goal that gives A total weight 1 - lambda and B total weight lambda.
1. If L_lambda(b) <= inf_F L_lambda + e, then for every b_A in F, v_A(b) <= v_A(b_A) + (lambda / (1 - lambda)) v_B(b_A) + e / (1 - lambda).
2. If 0 <= lambda < mu < 1, L_lambda(b) <= inf_F L_lambda + e and L_mu(b') <= inf_F L_mu + e', then v_A(b) - v_A(b') <= (mu e + lambda e') / (mu - lambda) and v_B(b') - v_B(b) <= ((1 - mu) e + (1 - lambda) e') / (mu - lambda). So with exact minimisers, where they exist, v_A(b) <= v_A(b') and v_B(b') <= v_B(b).
3. At lambda = 0, nothing about the list B enters the build's loss.
Proof. For 1: (1 - lambda) v_A(b) <= L_lambda(b) <= L_lambda(b_A) + e, since lambda v_B(b) >= 0. Divide by 1 - lambda. For 2: let a = v_A(b) - v_A(b') and c = v_B(b) - v_B(b'). The premises give (1 - lambda) a + lambda c <= e and -(1 - mu) a - mu c <= e'. Multiply the first by mu and the second by lambda, and add: (mu - lambda) a <= mu e + lambda e'. Multiply the first by 1 - mu and the second by 1 - lambda, and add: -(mu - lambda) c <= (1 - mu) e + (1 - lambda) e'. For 3: L_0 = v_A. QED.
Lean: goal_exchange_approx (part 2). Parts 1 and 3 are by hand: one line each.
Label: a tool. It holds for any set of builds at any size. Comment. Part 2 is what "more weight on dogs" can promise at a fixed size, for near-minimisers of each goal: no worse on dogs, and no better on the rest, up to the errors. A rule's build is not shown to be a near-minimiser, so this speaks about the optimum and not about a rule. It does not say at which size a given input stops being served. Part 1 has v_B(b_A) in it, and that term can be large: an input of weight 0 carries no promise of any kind, and a build for A may be confidently wrong on B.

**Lemma TG3 (a short list says nothing) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds) (added 2026-11-03).** If the list P has n <= k + 1 inputs whose z(x) are affinely independent, then some read of size k has D_P = 0, for every network N.
Proof. The n - 1 differences z(x_i) - z(x_1) are linearly independent in R^d, so a matrix M of shape k x d exists with M (z(x_(i+1)) - z(x_1)) = e_i for i <= n - 1. Let column i of V be y_N(x_(i+1)) - y_N(x_1), let the other columns be 0, and let t = y_N(x_1) - V M z(x_1). Then V M z(x_i) + t = y_N(x_i) on the list, so every KL term is 0. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: a linear interpolation on a finite list.
Label: a tool. Comment. So a small D_P on a short list alone is no evidence for any rule. The same holds more widely, when k reaches the rank of the logit differences modulo constants on the list. This is why line (a) of the trunk is on new inputs from the goal. Compare Theorem T28 part 2.

**Proposition TG4 (what passing the bar does not promise on hard tables) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds; part 2's last line under the Unique Games Conjecture) (added 2026-11-03, from REFEREE-BQ13-2026-11-03.md).** Take the networks of Proposition TQ30 or TQ31 at k = 1, with kept judgment units, and let the goal Q be the list P itself, so that the new inputs are the list. Let T be any training procedure and R a polynomial-time rule, both returning class (b) builds. Suppose D_P(R) <= c D_P(T) and D_P(T) <= K V_b(1) on every such network, with constants c >= 1 and K >= 1.
1. Then V_b(1) <= D_P(R) <= c K V_b(1).
2. So on TQ30's networks, c K < 10 5^(1/2) - 21 gives P = NP, and on TQ31's networks, any fixed c K gives P = NP under the Unique Games Conjecture.
Proof. Class (b) builds have loss at least V_b(1), which gives the left side of 1, and the right side multiplies the two premises. Part 2 is part 3 of each proposition, applied to the value D_P(R). KL holds logarithms, so that value is computed in polynomial time to a small relative accuracy, and the strict margin below the threshold allows this error. QED.
Lean: none, by hand: one multiplication and a citation.
Label: a limit. Comment. Line (a) of the trunk compares with training, not with the least. So these results do not stop a rule from meeting line (a). Deterministic polynomial-time training is limited too: unless P = NP, it is not within any factor below 10 5^(1/2) - 21 of the least on all of TQ30's networks, and under the Unique Games Conjecture, it is not within any fixed factor on all of TQ31's networks. For training with random starts, read NP in BPP in place of P = NP. A rule may be measured against that. The same two limits hold for any polynomial-time rule. So a rule that passes on such tables carries no promise of being near the least beyond what those limits allow. On TQ30's networks a fixed factor is available: naming a 2-approximate cover in TQ30's upper side gives a polynomial-time build within 2 (1 + O(delta)). Whether real goals behave like these tables is not addressed here, and these networks are not shown to be trained-like.

Comment on the hard step. In TQ30's upper side the build is direct once the areas given up are named (X = 1_I 1_I^T for the complement I of a cover), and in TQ31's upper side once the two sides are named (X = sigma sigma^T). These named builds are within 1 + O(delta) of the least in TQ30, and within a fixed constant plus a term of order n^2 / (D E) in TQ31. They are not shown to be the least. So those results locate the hard step in that choice, up to those factors.

# Part C: distance of InceptionV1 from each hypothesis

Each hypothesis gets one distance eps, defined before it is measured.

**Estimators, defined before any run.**

*H-sym (on photos, no network).* H-sym says the input law is invariant under rotations. A necessary consequence: for
every n >= 1, the orientation harmonic E_P sum_v m(v)^2 e^{i n psi(v)} is zero, where m and psi are the magnitude and
orientation of the image gradient at pixel v. (Proof: rotating the image by alpha multiplies the harmonic by
e^{i n alpha}; invariance for every alpha forces it to be zero.) Estimator: grayscale photos, gradient by Gaussian
derivatives (standard deviation 1.5 pixels), eps_sym(n) = |sum m^2 e^{i n psi}| / sum m^2 for n = 2 and 4 (undirected
edges have even harmonics; gravity predicts n = 2 and 4). Floor: the same estimator on white-noise images (an
isotropic law sampled on the pixel grid) measures the grid's own bias. Images: the first 2000 images of the train
split. This measures one projection of H-sym (second-order edge statistics), not all of it.

*H-contour (one InceptionV1 pass).* Members: the ten curve units at their angles theta_i recovered from the weights
(R1). Fields: 3b outputs before the pool, 28 x 28, stride 8 pixels. Co-activity: the covariance
Cov_ij(v) = E[h_i(x, p) h_j(x, p + v)] - E[h_i] E[h_j] over inputs and positions (independent curves and background
add zero covariance, so this removes the cross-curve floor). Frame: the R1 angles carry an unknown constant offset
(tangent or normal), so the tangent axis a_i of member i is defined as the principal axis of its own autocovariance
Cov_ii(v) (on one curve a detector co-fires with itself along the curve). Coordinates: x along image columns, y up.
Rotate the offset v by -a_i, giving (s, y); use s' = |s| and y' = y sign(s) (the statistic is the same for both
directions along the tangent). Keep |y'| <= s' (the short-arc region). Diagnostic: a_i should increase with theta_i
up to one constant.
Partner angle: phi = theta_j - theta_i wrapped to (-pi, pi]. Weight: the positive part of Cov_ij(v) (a choice:
negative co-activity is dropped). Statistic per s bin (bins of one cell, s from 1 to 6 cells): Dhat(s) = weighted mean
of (phi - 2 y / s)^2. The member angles are quantised (ten members), which adds a constant floor (absorbed in a).
Decision rule: fit Dhat(s) = a + b s^p + c / s^2 (s in cells, using s', y') with a, b, c >= 0, for p = 3 (curvature process) and p = 1 (direction
process). Decide for the law whose fit has the lower residual, only if the residual ratio exceeds 2. Otherwise
"undecided". Also report the weighted regression slope of phi on y / s per bin (2 for co-circular at short range).
Null: the same statistic with member angles shuffled must lose the structure. Missing lemma (stated after the smoke
run, from the third referee report): the step from network co-activity to D(s) needs H-shot (so that the covariance is
the single-curve pair term, by Campbell's theorem) and H-detector, and D(s) must be derived on the cut region
|y'| <= s', which the cut changes. Real members are tuned to curvature: Theorem T3 part 4 keeps the s^3 growth for
them, but the direction process has no curvature-tuned version, so the test should be one-sided (p = 3 or not). The
script also does not wrap phi - 2 y' / s'. Written expectation: the 3b receptive
fields are large compared with 1 to 6 cells, so receptive-field overlap may dominate (a large c / s^2 term), and
"undecided" is a likely outcome. If decided, p = 3 supports H-contour.

**Results.**
| Hypothesis | Result | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| H-sym (`pc_hsym.py`, 2000 train photos) | eps_sym(2) = 0.106 (se 0.006), eps_sym(4) = 0.073 (se 0.003); white-noise floor 0.0001 and 0.009; phase of the n = 4 harmonic -2 degrees | the photo law breaks rotation symmetry by about a tenth of the edge energy, toward horizontal and vertical edges (gravity), as written before the run. The harmonic is only a witness: a non-zero value shows that H-sym fails. It gives no bound on eps_sym as defined in A.3 |
| H-contour (`pc_hcontour.py`, smoke run, 64 images) | the frame diagnostic FAILED: the autocovariance axes minus the R1 angles scatter from -85 to +87 degrees (spread 35 degrees), not one constant | the estimator's frame rule is not valid, so the smoke run's fitted verdict (p = 1, residual ratio 2.49) is void. Stated reason "receptive-field overlap makes the autocovariance round" was checked with the one measurement it predicts (eigenvalue ratio above 0.8): REFUTED, ratios 0.34 to 0.84, 1 of 10 above 0.8. So each member's co-activity with itself is elongated, but not along a direction tied to its R1 angle. Open: a definition of each member's tangent axis that rests neither on the R1 labels nor on the autocovariance. The 2000-image run was not made. Two runs were made on this statement, so by the rule the next step is a definition in the paper, not a third run. Open note (not a conclusion): Dhat stayed between 1.1 and 3.4 rad^2. The flat-law reference is pi^2 / 3 + 4 / 3, about 4.6 rad^2 (phi uniform, and 2 y' / s' uniform on [-2, 2]), not pi^2 / 3 as first written here. So the weights do concentrate somewhat, more at short range. Whether this is enough power for the exponent test is open. Candidate definition for the next step (not yet adopted): the tangent axis of member i is its preferred arc normal plus 90 degrees, read from its responses to synthetic arcs at 36 orientations (`results_g0_tuning.npz`, already computed by `g0_tuning.py`; in `stimuli.py` an arc's orientation is the direction from its middle to its centre). This is a property of the feature (Definition D1), needs no new run, and must be stated in the paper before it is used |

**Toy chains (Part B.4), trained.** Code: `toy2/chain.py`. A gated chain (Definition D11) with N = 8 members per
family and depth 3 is trained by cross-entropy on a shape task on a polar grid (3 shape types x 8 orientations = 24
classes, so the readout has 3 orbits of 8 logits). H-gate and H-eq hold by construction (weight tying, group-averaged
gate kernels, circulant edges). H-symN holds exactly for the symmetrised training set (every image with all 8 exact
rotations). Students are builds of widths (k_1, k_2, k_3) with the teacher's gate path frozen and every value weight
free (no tying). They are trained by Adam on D2 over the training set, from a random start.
Predictions, written before the runs (`toy2/c1_core.py`, `toy2/c2_variants.py`):
| ID | Check | Prediction |
|---|---|---|
| Y1 | the T9 build and the T10 build at every strict-gap width, on the training law | D2 equals 1/2 sum_{j>k} mu_j to about 1e-12 relative, and the two builds have the same centred outputs |
| Y2 | trained students of width (k, k, k), random start, at each strict-gap width k <= 5 | final training D2 is at least the formula's D2 (a ratio below 1 by more than 1e-9 would refute T9) |
| Y3 | the formula as a start (local exactness test) | the gradient of D2 at the formula is zero to rounding, and 300 small Adam steps (lr 1e-4) do not lower D2 by more than 1e-9 relative |
| Y4 | depth: a student of widths (k, 8, 8) | it cannot beat the width-(k, k, k) formula either (T9: the optimum depends on min k_l only) |
| Y5 | the tree: merges between the strict-gap levels of the trained teacher | U_k U_k' U_k2 U_k2' = U_k U_k' to about 1e-12 |
| Y6 | held-out law (fresh symmetrised images) | no exact prediction (the formula is fitted on the training law). Written expectation: the formula stays within a few percent of the best trained student |
| Y7 | variant 'asym': the same teacher scored on an unsymmetrised sample of 24000 images (H-symN broken by sampling) | T9 stays exact (Y1 and Y2 hold for the T9 build). The harmonic T10 build is worse than T9 by a small positive amount |
| Y8 | variant 'relu1': each member of the first family also passes through its own ReLU (H-gate broken in one family, Proposition T1' applies) | T9's read is no longer a build: the read-then-one-ReLU build (unit a = g_1 relu(sum_i Lambda_{a i} z_i)) is not stationary: training from it lowers D2 by more than one percent, and random-start students beat it |
| Y9 (`toy2/c3_converge.py`, written after Y1-Y8) | does training converge to the formula? Random-start students of width (k, k, k) at k = 1, 3, 4, 3 seeds, 12000 Adam steps, logged at 12 points | at every logged point: the excess D2(B) - D2(B*) is >= 0, and the distance of centred outputs obeys T9 part 4 (no violation; these two are theorems). Expectation, not a theorem: excess and distance fall with training, and at the end the centred-output distance is below 10% of the formula's centred-output size |
