**Self-gated toy chain (Part B.5), trained.** Code: `toy2/chain.py` (variant `selfgate`, classes `SelfStudent`,
`t11_student`, `t11_1_build`), `toy2/c4_selfgate.py`. The toy of B.4 with the gate path removed: gate l is
relu(a_l t + b_l) of the orbit mean of the layer below (the first gate reads the orbit mean of z). So H-selfgate,
H-eq and H-symN hold exactly, and the forced read space is the all-ones vector (r = 1, Corollary T11.2). Students of
uniform width k are self-contained: a faithful student keeps unit 0 as the orbit mean (fixed kernel, fixed edge row) and
every gate reads it; a free-read student reads its gates through trained vectors.
Predictions, written before the runs (the teacher is trained first; the case of Y12 is written after the teacher's
lambda_n are computed and before any student runs):

| Y11 | faithful students, random start, uniform width k in {1, 2, 3, 4}, 2 seeds; and the same recipe started at the T11 build with small steps | never below the T11 value (a ratio below 1 by more than 1e-9 would refute T11 part 1). At k = 1 the student has no free weight in the first layer, so it equals the formula after its head and bias are fitted |
| Y12 | the cost of self-containment: T11 value against the T9 value (gates kept from the teacher, Theorem T9) at each k | the difference equals 1/2 (sum of the k largest lambda_n) - 1/2 (lambda_0 + sum of the k - 1 largest over n != 0) (Corollary T11.2 part 4). It is zero exactly at the widths where lambda_0 is among the k largest |

The ratio below 1 on dogs and cats does not show the rule is the optimum. Whether dog photos are easier for any read, apart from the goal, is not separated here. Agreement with N stays well below 1 at these sizes. Line (b) fails since the convex fit runs to a gain under 1e-6 per chunk, while training stops early on validation.

Reading, not proved. (1) With rows at most d, the whitened z of Definition DG2 is orthonormal on the list, so V_q M_k on the list is a rank-k principal part of the logits in F's metric for any z, and it says little about new inputs. This fits the random goals at k = 14 (fit about .29, sealed about 2.12). It does not explain why dogs and cats stay near 1 with the same row count. Network and row count are not separated here: ResNet-50 has 12 fit photos per class, against 30 for ResNet-18. (2) On all classes, the rule is also far above trained on its own fit rows on ResNet-18 at k = 14 (1.762 against 1.159), so the span in F's metric costs something apart from noise. This is compatible with the earlier finding that a dropped part can be large as a quadratic and cheap in KL.

Two references for line (a), found after the first write-up of these results. The script's line, fixed before the run, took the best of four starts: logitpca, rand0, rand1 and rule. Trunk T6 names only "starts from random and from B_j". Against those three, the rule passes on all 24 runs: ResNet-18 ratios .94 to 1.30, ResNet-50 ratios .94 to 1.24. Against the script's four, it passes on 18 of 24, as in the tables above. So all 6 failures come from the added start. A better read of the same form is known on those runs, so the stricter number is the one that says how far the rule is from what can be reached, and the table keeps it.

So photo count alone does not explain ResNet-50's failures. What remains is the network or the ratio of rows to d, and this run does not separate those two. Both sizes from it cost less than one random-start level on only 1 of 12 goal runs (all classes, ResNet-18). The lowest sealed value is selected over four starts, one of them this one, so its ratio of 1 is not an independent test. It is training, not a closed form.

# Part D: where the math leads

This part extrapolates. Each item is a conjecture with a route, or a program. Nothing here is claimed as proved.

## D.1 The chain from facts to an optimal subnetwork, with its missing links

The path of every result named in this table (the nodes of `DECISIONS.md` it sits under) is in `DECISIONS.md` section 6.
A link whose results sit under a node that Shonu has not decided is a side branch, not a step toward the trunk T\* (Part 0).

**D.1 in the language of Part B.S (2026-10-26).** The trunk asks for a point of the output set O_k(P) (Definition
D35) where the divergence D_P from N's outputs is least. Theorem T41 splits the problem into two parts: choose an
optimal pattern (a piece), then find the best point of that piece. For one hidden layer and two logits the second part
is 2^k convex problems (Corollary T41.1), so a rule's error is then exactly the price of a wrong piece (T41 part 4).
The open links of the table below then read as follows.

Known: under H-gate (an analogue class) the gate configuration is fixed (T9); with a gate in front, one sufficient condition (T39.1) and one counterexample (T40). For D_P on tree maps (Part B.I, 2026-10-31): closed forms for a group replaced by nothing (TI1) and for keep-or-drop groupings (TI2.1, node S-keepdrop); for 0 < k_S < rank Sigma open (TI3, TI4, Conjecture DI1) |

For D_P: Theorem TI2 (a group with k_S >= rank Sigma is within eps_lin / 4 of the least, 0 at eps_lin = 0) and Corollary TI2.1; side branch (nodes R-tree, R-branch, S-plainff, R-linread, S-keepdrop PENDING) |

Inside the gated class (H-gate, Part B.4), with the logit objective D2 in place of D_P, the following is proved. The
fold to any widths is an exact optimum over every build (Theorem T9, for every input law, with no H-kron hypothesis).
It is a read of the members and is built by real units (Proposition T7 with T9: links 8 and 9). It covers every layer
of a chain whose edges are pointwise in position (link 10 for that kind of edge). The optimal levels nest at widths with a strict gap (Theorem T6).
With H-eq, H-symN, Chat positive definite and a strict gap, the fold keeps the same Fourier modes at every layer, and the
data enters only through the floor(N / 2) + 1 numbers chat(n) and the constant E_P uhat (Theorem T10: links 2 to 4).
For D_P itself there is an upper bound (Corollary T10.2) and a comparison with every build whose logits have range at
most R, up to the factor n_y e^R / 2 (Corollary T10.3: a weak form of link 0). Part B.5 adds three things. (a) A lower
bound for the objective D2, for every map whose logits are affine in k numbers, under no hypothesis (Theorem T12). (b) With gates read from
the value path (H-selfgate) there is no gate path to keep: read-faithful builds have a closed-form optimum (Theorem T11),
r extra units below the top reach the bound of T12 (Corollary T11.1), and under symmetry r <= 1, the orbit sum
(Corollary T11.2, with invariant single-column reads). (c) With spatial edges (H-sgate), folding every layer down to
the raw input to its visible width reaches the bound of T12 for the top width (Theorem T13); the visible widths can be

## D.2 Conjecture D1: families as sampled fields with the network's own measure

The members need not be equally spaced, and their overlaps need not depend on the angle difference alone. So the
symmetric model should be generalised, not abandoned: the family is a field over the circle, sampled at the
network's angles theta_1, ..., theta_N, with the empirical measure mu_N = (1/N) sum_i delta_{theta_i}.
**Conjecture D1 (under: H-sym, H-kron, H-pool, and a sampled-field form of H-clean and H-read: C_ij = c(theta_j - theta_i)
and Phi_ij = phi(theta_j - theta_i) for continuous even positive-definite functions c, phi; CONJECTURE).** Let
mu_N converge weakly to a measure mu on the circle with a positive density. Let A be the operator on L2(mu) given by
A = C_mu^{1/2} Phi_mu C_mu^{1/2}, with C_mu and Phi_mu the integral operators with kernels c(theta - theta') and
phi(theta - theta') on L2(mu), and the square root taken as an operator. Then the best k-dimensional reads of T1a
part 1 (for the matrices C and Phi at the sampled angles) converge, as N grows, to the top k eigenfunctions of A
mapped by C_mu^{-1/2}, evaluated at the sampled angles. When mu is not uniform, the k = 1 read is not the uniform sum:
the network's emphasis (where it spends members) enters through mu.
Route: C and Phi are kernel matrices of the operators C_mu and Phi_mu discretised at mu_N. Nystrom perturbation
bounds control the distance between matrix eigenvectors and operator eigenfunctions, given a spectral gap of A.
A weights-only check additionally needs H-gram (C from the kernel Gram matrix), which Part C must measure first.

## D.3 Conjecture D2: the gated per-reader vector from the contour law

Lemma T1c leaves one N-vector per reader orbit: Lambda_j(i) = E[sum g_j h_i t] / E[sum g_j t^2], with g_j the gate of
reader j. If reader j is itself a detector of contour configurations (it reads the curve family), then its gate is
on exactly on certain configurations.
**Conjecture D2 (under: H-clean, H-sym, H-read, H-contour, H-detector; CONJECTURE).** For a reader whose gate is a
function of the contour through its position, Lambda_j(i) is a function of theta_i - psi_j only (psi_j the reader's
preferred angle), given by the Wiener integrals of Theorem T3 conditioned on the reader's configuration. The open
object of the gated setting is then a fixed function of the contour parameters (nu, sigma), not a free vector.
Route: condition the curvature process on the reader's event, then compute E[h_i t | event] with ideal detectors
(Definition D9). This is the concrete form of Conjecture T4 part 1.

## D.4 Program D3: depth, composition and selection rules

Theorem T5 is a selection rule for one layer: under a shared symmetry, coarse units of different families interact
only within one frequency. **Conjecture D3a (CONJECTURE).** Under H-read for every edge of a circuit (weights AND
gates equivariant), the composed edge maps of the circuit intertwine the group actions of its first and last
families, so the second-order objective of the whole circuit is block-diagonal by frequency.
Route: under H-read the weight block W_RF intertwines the actions (W_{., i+1} = R W_{., i}). A gate that is
equivariant (as in Lemma T1c) commutes with the actions too. A product of intertwiners is an intertwiner, and Schur's
lemma then gives the block structure. **Program D3:** (i) state H-clean for a circuit (a chain of families sharing one
group); (ii) prove D3a; (iii) count the data numbers per frequency per layer; (iv) find the condition under which the
k = 1 units of successive layers form a coarse circuit by themselves.

**Conjecture D3b (spatial edges) (under: H-sgate with a gate path, H-eq, H-symN; CONJECTURE).** Let the edges of a gated chain mix positions:
v_{l+1}(x, p) = g_{l+1}(x, p) sum_q w_l(q) v_l(x, p + q), with H-eq part 3 replaced by w_l(gamma q) = Pi w_l(q) Pi^T.
Context: Theorem T13 reaches the optimum for the top width at the visible widths of Definition D13. Theorem T14 shows
that, for chains in general, deciding the optimal value at width (1, 1) is NP-hard. T14's instances are not symmetric,
so this conjecture, which is about symmetric chains, stays open: symmetry may make the problem split into blocks, but a
block of multiplicity above one can still carry a hard instance. Route items, not proved here: for a fixed window
size the width-(1, 1) problem has only n_3 - 1 free variables after the inner maximisations (for fixed omega the best h
and kappa are the top singular pair of sum_q omega_q T_q), which suggests a polynomial algorithm for each fixed n_3;
orthogonally decomposable tensors have an easy best rank-1 approximation; for H-eq chains with only frequency 0 present
the problem may decouple. For the symmetric chain, the collapse of Lemma T8
still holds for each input, with u replaced by a sum over chains of positions, but the
member frequency is not conserved: a member mode n at layer l feeds mode n' at layer l + 1 through the angular harmonic
n' - n of the kernel w_l about the unit's position. The conjecture: the optimal fold of such a chain is a truncation in
the joint (member, offset) frequency, and the best reads then mix offsets, as Conjecture T2 asks for one layer.
Route: replace the member index by the pair (member, offset inside the window) at every layer. The edge maps are then
intertwiners of the joint action (a product of intertwiners is an intertwiner). The open step comes first: with spatial
edges the map from the build's weights to its output is a sum over chains of positions of products of the layers'
weights, so it is multilinear in the layers and not a single matrix of bounded rank. The rank reduction of Theorem T9
then fails, and a new argument is needed even before the symmetry is used. After that, the joint action has
multiplicity greater than one, so Schur's lemma gives blocks, not single modes, and the order of the blocks must be
computed.

## D.5 Program D4: other groups and other networks

The proofs of Theorem T1a part 3, Lemma T1b and Theorem T5 use a finite cyclic group that acts simply transitively on
the members (each member is moved to every other exactly once). They extend directly to any finite abelian group
acting simply transitively, with characters in place of Fourier modes (`perm_fixes_simple_eigvec` holds for any
permutation symmetry). Shifts and scalings act with infinite orbits, so they need a finite truncation (a torus of
positions, a band of scales) before the theory applies. **Program D4:** for each group, (i) name the family and its
readers, (ii) state H-clean and H-read for that group, (iii) apply T0, T1a, T5, (iv) measure the eps of Part C.
Hypothesis to test across networks: under the spectral premise of T1a part 3, the k = 1 unit of a family is its orbit
sum. The essay's report that small networks show coarser versions of the same units (one car unit instead of many)
would then be the statement that the orbit-sum unit is what survives at small width.

## D.6 Program D5: the HOW as a ridge-function approximation

Proposition T1' says a positive sum of ReLU members is not one ReLU unit where two hinges are crossed. The best single
unit for a target t = sum_i lambda_i relu(z_i) is the minimiser of the objective Q of Theorem T0 over single units
relu(<K', A> + b'), with the write re-optimised. Under a constant metric this is a weighted best approximation of a
sum of ridge functions by one ridge function. Approximation theory has results for this problem (ridge functions,
single-index models). **Program D5:** under H-contour, compute the best single unit for the summed read of the curve
family, and compare it with the circle detector of Conjecture T2. This is the step from the exact WHAT to a
buildable coarse unit.

## D.7 Builds that change their own gates: Theorem T15, Conjectures D7, D8 and D9

The existence question once stated here as Conjecture D6 is now Theorem T15: on an explicit chain the best
self-contained build lies strictly between the floor of T12 and the read-faithful value of T11.
**Conjecture D7 (under: H-selfgate with step gates phi_l(t) = 1[t > 0]; CONJECTURE).** The following decision
problem is NP-hard: given a self-gated chain with step gates and rational weights, a law uniform on finitely many
rational points, a width k and a rational r, decide whether the infimum of D2_P over self-contained builds of uniform
width k is at most r.
Route: reduce from training a single ReLU unit by squared error, which is NP-hard (Manurangsi and Reichman 2018). The
proof of T15 shows that a self-contained build of width 1 with a step gate, at one position, is a single ReLU unit
(through the origin) with a free sign and a free output bias. Three obstacles. (1) The teacher: the reduction needs a
self-gated chain whose logits equal arbitrary labels on the training points, and a chain with one position emits only
(a gate) times (a linear map). Routes: several positions, where the student becomes a sum-pooled ReLU and the
reduction must be redone for that class; or deeper teachers. (2) The student has a free sign and a free output bias,
while the cited hardness is for a zero-bias ReLU; the reduction must absorb both. (3) For a fixed input dimension the
problem is polynomial: on n points the activation patterns of a unit through the origin number O(n^{d-1}), and each
gives a problem over one chamber, which for n_y = 2 and k = 1 is a pair of convex problems (Comment after T16). So, for
n_y = 2 and k = 1, any hardness must come from growing dimension. Until this is settled, the exact optimum is known in
closed form only with r extra units below the top (Corollary T11.1, not at uniform width); at uniform width it is the
infimum of J_k over the effective reads (Theorem T16), for which no efficient algorithm is known.

Note (revision 7). D7 is about step gates. For affine gates under the premises of Theorem T17.2 the width-1 problem
reduces to the real roots of one polynomial; the affine-gate case on finite laws with n_y = 2, beta = 0 and one position
at width 1 is Conjecture D9. Other affine-gate cases (Gaussian laws outside the premises of T17.2, k >= 2) are in
neither.

**Conjecture D9 (linear gates on finite laws) (under: H-selfgate with phi(t) = alpha t; CONJECTURE).** The following
decision problem is NP-hard: given a self-gated chain of depth 1 with one position, one read column, the gate
phi(t) = alpha t and rational weights, a law uniform on finitely many rational points, n_y = 2, and a rational r, decide
whether the infimum of D2_P over self-contained builds of width 1 is at most r.
Route: with n_y = 2 and beta = 0, write z for the scalar P_perp y (up to a fixed unit vector), C = Cov(z, a a^T) and
D(kappa) = Var((kappa^T a)^2) = sum_i pi_i (kappa^T a_i)^4 - (kappa^T Sigma_2 kappa)^2 (pi_i the weights of the points,
Sigma_2 = E a a^T). After fitting the head and the bias the value is 1/2 [Var(z) D(kappa) - (kappa^T C kappa)^2] / D(kappa),
so "value <= r" holds for some kappa exactly when (Var(z) - 2 r) D(kappa) - (kappa^T C kappa)^2 <= 0 for some kappa != 0
(with D(kappa) > 0). Reduce from non-copositivity: deciding whether x^T C' x < 0 for some x >= 0 is NP-complete (the
complement of the copositivity problem of Murty and Kabadi 1987, literature table; x^T C' x over x >= 0 is the quartic
form sum_{ij} C'_ij y_i^2 y_j^2 over all y). Obstacles: (1) the quartic must be realised in the form
(Var(z) - 2 r) D(kappa) - (kappa^T C kappa)^2, a positive combination of fourth powers minus two squares of quadratic
forms, with C, Sigma_2 and D fixed by one law (a moment cone), which is the main difficulty; (2) the strict "< 0" must be
turned into "<= r" by a bit-size gap argument; (3) with beta != 0 the value involves forms of degree 6 in kappa, which is
why D9 is stated for beta = 0.

**Conjecture D8 (the best kept space at width k under H-gauss) (under: as Proposition T17.3; CONJECTURE).** For each
fixed k there is an algorithm that, given rational Sigma, M, s, alpha, beta, rho and a rational epsilon > 0, returns a
rational d x k matrix K' of rank k with F(col K') <= min_V F(V) + epsilon (the minimum over subspaces V of dimension at
most k), in time polynomial in d, the bit length of the input and log(1 / epsilon). (This is coordinate-free by Lemma
T17a; the maximiser of f in whitened coordinates is irrational in general.)
Route: (1) Proposition T17.3 part 4 reduces the problem to the supremum of h(p) over p != 0 on the sphere
|p|^2 = p^T stilde, compared with the value at p = 0; h contains the Ky Fan sum kappa_{k-1}(p) of a compression of Q.
(2) kappa_{k-1}(p) depends on p only through the span of stilde and p (two-dimensional except at p = stilde); study h on
the circles cut from the sphere by 2-planes through 0 and stilde, and through the eigenvectors of Q, as the resolvent
curve does at k = 1. (3) Check the fixed-point iteration "Pi -> the projection onto the top k
eigenvectors of G(Pi)" against the maximum of h on a small exact instance before claiming anything about it;
Proposition T17.3 does not say which k eigenvectors.

## D.8 Conjecture D17: a least build for two logits at every depth

Theorem T23 settles the case of three or more logits with one hidden layer: the least need not exist. Open: two
logits with more than one hidden layer (Conjecture D17), and three or more logits with more than one hidden layer
(where a wider class of builds might reach T23's limit; not studied here).

**Conjecture D17 (two logits: a least build exists at every depth) (under: two logits, a finite mix; CONJECTURE).** For every network N
with n_y = 2, every finite mix P and every width k, D_P has a minimum over plain ReLU builds (Definition D15) with any
fixed number of hidden layers of width k.
Route: (1) With two logits only the gap matters, and D_P is coercive in the gap vector by (l2). So it suffices to show
that the set of gap vectors of builds with L hidden layers is closed. For L = 1 this is Theorem T19. (2) For L = 2 the
data vector of a second-layer unit is relu of an affine map of first-layer data vectors: a finite union of images of
polyhedral pieces under bilinear maps. A second-layer unit can play the part of one output of a two-output network of
width k. Check whether the construction of Theorem T23 can be fed into one gap through a second layer. If it can, the
conjecture is false and T23's fork extends to two logits. (3) A margin argument handles the simplest limits: for affine
L and h on a finite set, s (relu(L + h / s) - relu(L)) tends to h 1[L > 0] + relu(h) 1[L = 0], which equals
relu(h + M L) - M relu(L) once M exceeds a bound set by max |h| and the smallest non-zero |L(x_i)|. T23 shows that
such re-writing can fail with two outputs, so the route must use the single gap.

## D.9 Conjecture D25: for clean networks, the optimum is a fold

**Conjecture D25 (fold optimality) (under: a perfectly clean network for Gamma, a full-rank first layer, a
Gamma-invariant mix; CONJECTURE).** Let N have one hidden layer, be perfectly clean for a finite group Gamma
(Definition D20), with first-layer weights that span R^d, and let the mix P be invariant under Gamma. Then for every
width k there is a least build over any new units (for D_P, and for D2_P) in which every hidden unit is equal on P,
up to a positive scale, to a covering fold (Definition D22) of one family (one Gamma-orbit of N's units).
Route: (1) Exact test first: small clean networks with cyclic symmetry in R^2 (one or two families of rotated units),
rotation-invariant mixes on rings of points, widths 1 and 2, D2 and KL, with the exact rule of Theorem T21, and a
linear program that decides whether a unit's data vector on P is that of a covering fold of one family. (2) If the
test passes: prove one family, width 1, D2, extending T20's exact computation, and find the structure of the fold
weights. (3) If it fails: the failing instance says what the optimum is instead (mixing families, negative weights,
or a raised offset), which answers the question of what distillation converges to for clean networks.

**Status of Conjecture D25 (2026-10-25): refuted exactly by Theorem T32 (D2, width 2); the cases below are at
solver accuracy.** The exact test of the route (step 1) gives,
for perfectly clean single-family networks with rotation-invariant mixes, least values over covering-fold builds
strictly above the least values over any builds. The clearest case: the family relu(w_i^T x - 1), w_i at angles
0, 120 and 240 degrees in R^2, the mix uniform on six points at radius 2 and angles 60 j degrees, width 2: for D2 the
least value over any builds is 1/36 and over covering folds 1/32 (computed by the exact rules of `model/trunk_exact.py`
at solver accuracy; `model/tf_fold_gap.py`), a relative gap of 1/8; KL shows a gap of the same size. At width 1 on
the same instance there is no gap. A second case (a family of four units, eight ring points and the centre, width 1)
also shows a gap (numerical, not used in any proof).
What the least builds do instead (`model/tf_clean_optimum.py`; numerical, not used in any proof; the exact
statement is Theorem T32): their units are non-negative mixes of the members'
pre-activations with a LOWERED threshold, so they fire where every member is silent; at width 2 the least build pairs
two such units along one member's direction, with output weights of opposite signs (a profile with two hinges along
that direction). So the condition "covers" (G3) is the wrong reading of a coarse unit for these networks: the
optimal coarse units are broader than the union of the fine units, which matches the essay's "coarser-grained
concepts" better than a narrower unit would. In R^2 three or more spread directions already make every direction a
non-negative mix, so these instances test only the threshold, not the sign of the mix.

**Conjecture D26 (broad folds) (under: a perfectly clean network for Gamma, a full-rank first layer, a Gamma-invariant
mix; CONJECTURE).** In the setting of Conjecture D25, for every width k there is a least build (for D_P and for D2_P)
in which every hidden unit is equal on P, up to a positive scale, to a **broad fold** of one family:
relu(sum_{i in F} m_i z_i + beta) with m_i >= 0 and any real beta (a non-negative mix of one family's pre-activations,
threshold free).
Route: test where the cone of a family's weights is a proper cone (for example a family of three units in R^3 whose
weights all lean the same way along the rotation axis, with a mix above and below the plane), comparing the least
values over any builds, over broad folds and over covering folds with the exact rules; then certify the gaps exactly
(D2 pieces are rational quadratic programs); then look for the structure (why lowered thresholds, and the paired
units at width 2).
First attempt at the route (`model/tf_broad_fold.py`, a family of three units in R^3 leaning up, six points above and
below): on these mixes one unit already copies N exactly, so the least value over any builds is 0 at widths 1 and 2
and the test does not separate any builds from broad folds (both reach 0). It does add one fact: covering folds stay
strictly above 0 there, even at width 1. A mix with more points is needed. Second attempt (twelve points: two rings of different radius above and
below, invariant under the rotation; width 1; two leans of the family): the least value over broad folds equals the
least value over any builds (to solver accuracy), while covering folds stay strictly above. Here the cone of the
members' weights is a proper cone, so the non-negative mix is a real restriction, and the least width-1 unit
satisfies it. This supported Conjecture D26 at width 1 (numerical, not used in any proof); Theorem T33 then refuted D26
exactly on another instance.

**Status of Conjecture D26 (2026-10-25): refuted exactly by Theorem T33 (width 1).** The least build there uses the
family's negative side: relu(-x_3 / 2), a non-negative mix of the negated pre-activations.

**Conjecture D27 (signed folds) (under: a perfectly clean network for Gamma, a full-rank first layer, a Gamma-invariant
mix; CONJECTURE).** In the setting of Conjecture D25, for every width k there is a least build (for D_P and for D2_P)
in which every hidden unit is equal on P, up to a positive scale, to a **signed fold** of one family:
relu(sum_{i in F} m_i z_i + beta) or relu(-sum_{i in F} m_i z_i + beta), with m_i >= 0 and beta free (the family's
positive or negative side, threshold free). This keeps both lessons of T32 and T33: coarse units fire more broadly
than the fine ones, and they may read the family's negative side (the essay: "The negative side tells us what
distinction matters").
Route: (1) with one family, a search over families leaning along a rotation axis found no case where any build beats
the signed folds (numerical); with two families, Theorem T34 refutes D27 exactly. (2) Try to prove it at
width 1 for D2, where the least build maximises the squared correlation of the unit with N's gap over the mix. (3) If
it fails, the one-family structure fails; folds of groups across families with free thresholds restrict nothing when
the layer's weights positively span R^d (Corollary T35), so the fold idea then has no content beyond Lemma T31 for
such networks: a fork for Shonu.

**Status of Conjecture D27 (2026-10-25): refuted exactly by Theorem T34 (width 1, two families).**

## D.10 Conjectures D29 and D30: the optimum of one family on rings

Setting (dihedral rings): a family of n units relu(u_i^T x - 1) in R^2, u_i = (cos(2 pi i / n), sin(2 pi i / n)),
logits (sum of the units, 0); a mix on rings of points whose angles are multiples of pi / n (with or without the
centre), invariant under the dihedral group D_n of the n rotations and n mirrors. The mirror axes are the lines at
angles multiple of pi / n: through a member, or exactly between two adjacent members.

**Conjecture D29 (the least width-1 unit lies on a mirror axis) (under: a perfectly clean network for Gamma, a
Gamma-invariant mix; CONJECTURE).** In the dihedral-ring setting, for D2 and for D_P, the least value over width-1
builds equals the least value over width-1 builds whose unit points along a mirror axis.
Route: exact test (`model/to_ring.py`): for each instance the global least (the exact rule of T21) against the least
with the unit's direction on each axis (a one-dimensional exact problem along the axis); then a proof for D2, where
the least unit maximises the squared correlation with N's gap.

**Conjecture D30 (the least width-1 unit fires where the family is silent) (under: a perfectly clean network for
Gamma, a Gamma-invariant mix; CONJECTURE).** In the dihedral-ring setting, if some point of the mix has every member
silent, the least value over width-1 builds is strictly below the least value over width-1 builds whose unit is
silent at all such points.
Route: the same exact test, with the restricted class given by the extra linear constraints w^T x + b <= 0 at the
silent points.

**Status of Conjectures D29 and D30 (2026-10-25): numerically contradicted, not refuted (`model/to_ring.py`; numerical,
not part of any proof).** D29: on several dihedral-ring instances (a family of three on two rings; a family of four on
one ring with the centre) the least width-1 value found along every mirror axis is above the global least found by the
exact enumeration with a numerical solver on each piece, for D2 and for KL. A refutation needs an exact certificate of
the gap (Lemma T32a's method applies for D2); none is written. D30: on every instance with silent points, no gap was
found at relative tolerance 1/10^6 between the least over all width-1 builds and the least over builds silent at those
points. A solver cannot refute a strict inequality; this only says the conjecture has no numerical support. T38 gives
a necessary condition on the least unit, not a symmetry or threshold rule.

## D.11 Conjecture D34: with a gate in front, the least coarse unit takes the gate's region

**Conjecture D34 (one gate, width 1) (under: two logits, a finite mix, first layer kept, H-front, H-flatgate, a
perfectly clean network for Gamma, a Gamma-invariant mix, Gamma fixes the gate; CONJECTURE).** In the setting of B.G,
for D2_P and for D_P, the infimum over all width-1 builds equals the infimum over width-1 gate folds (Definition D32).
When the condition of Lemma T39a holds, that value is L_G, reached by the fit on the gate's region with N's value off
it.
Route: (1) exact test on the instances I1 and I2 of B.G: the global least by the exact rule of T21
(`trunk_exact.exact_min`, on the points z_x, Lemma T39 part 0) against the least gate fold (the same convex piece
solver with the region fixed to G, both signs). (2) If the values agree, certify exactly with dual certificates (Lemma
T32a). (3) If they differ, read the least build's region against G, and fix the statement (rule 4).

**Status of Conjecture D34 (2026-10-26): refuted exactly for D2 by Theorem T40 (I1).** The numerical runs on I2 and
on KL are recorded in the Appendix ("Numerical record for D34"); they are not part of any proof. What is proved about
gates so far: Lemma T39 (the best build with the gate's region, by formula), Lemma T39a (when it is realisable),
Corollary T39.1 (one sufficient condition for an exact build from N's weights, in a case where the least build pays no
cost), Remark B.G.1 (even then the least build is not unique and need not read the gate), and Theorem T40 (one exact
instance where no gate fold is least). No theorem says which property of N inside the gate decides the case. On I1 the
gate rule's error against the least value is at least 7/182 - 5/182 = 1/91.

## D.12 Conjecture D47: the hardness for networks clean in the agreement form

**Conjecture D47 (proposed; nodes R-cleannet and R-explaw, PENDING).** Let AGREE-TRUNK be the decision problem of
Theorem T43 (input: a plain ReLU network N with two logits and one hidden layer, a compact convex domain X, a mix P
invariant under N's symmetry group, sizes (1), and eps; question as in TRUNK-1 of Theorem T22), restricted to networks
N that are perfectly clean in the agreement form of D45 under the uniform base law on X. Then AGREE-TRUNK is NP-hard.
(For almost every network the symmetry group is trivial, Theorem T44, so the mix condition is then no restriction.)
Route: step 0, show the class is non-empty. Step 1 (suggested by referee report 23): give each detector d_(j,i) of
D40 a nested helper b_(j,i) = relu(<x~_i, x_(j)> - r') with sqrt(1 - eta/2) <= r' < r and r' >= 1/2, read by the
same logit, with the readout rescaled so that the logit difference at a vertex point stays 2. The helpers are pairwise
apart (the argument of Lemma T43a part 2) and off at every midpoint and at sibling vertex points, so the logits on
T43's mix do not change and T43's reduction carries over. What remains is xi > 0 for all 2 kappa m units: each
detector co-occurs with its own helper, which Lemma T46d's identity rewards. If this works, the agreement form does
not remove the hardness either, and Shonu's conjecture needs a different principle.

## D.13 Conjectures D52 and D53: step by step, and the cost of an OR step

**Conjecture D52 (some tree makes step by step optimal; Hypothesis H-recur) (under: two logits, one hidden layer, a
finite mix, a perfectly clean network for Gamma; CONJECTURE).** For D_P and for D2_P: for every target grouping G\*
in which every group has at least two units and target size 1, there is a zoom G_0, ..., G_m = G\* with G_0 the grouping with no groups, in which every step changes exactly one group,
and that group has exactly two children and target size 1, and an (r) sequence along it (Definition D50) with
D_P(B_j) = V_b(G_j) at every level j.
Route: (1) on small detector networks, list every such zoom and compare the (r) value at the top with the least width-1
value (exact pieces for D2, T21); (2) describe the good zooms by their merges: Corollaries T59.1 and T59.2 say which
pairs merge for free; (3) state the description as a theorem for the detector networks, then try to prove it from the
principles of Part A.5. An instance where no zoom works refutes D52. The first numeric check is in the H-recur row of
Part C.

**Conjecture D53 (the cost of an OR step) (under: two logits, one hidden layer, a finite mix, a perfectly clean network
for Gamma, a Gamma-invariant mix; CONJECTURE).** For D2_P. Let the group be the whole hidden layer, one family that is
OR on P, with target size 1, and suppose that for every two members P holds a silent blend of their firing points (a
point x_0 as in Proposition T59 part 2). Then a least one-unit build fires, on P, only on the firing points of one
member (so it breaks the symmetry), and its affine piece is the fit of Corollary T38.1 on those points.
Route: T20 is the first instance: the least unit relu(x - 8/5) for D2 fires on {2, 3}, the points of the member
relu(x - 1) on P (Remark B.Z.1), and P holds the silent blend x = 0. Without the blend premise a statement of this kind fails, already for a group of two units: with kappa = 2 and m = 2, the group {d_(1,1), d_(2,1)} with P the two vertex points and the
origin merges exactly (the unit of T59.2) and fires on both members. Next: OR pairs and triples on rings
(`model/to_ring.py` instances), exact pieces for D2; then a proof from T38.1 and Proposition T59 part 2.

**Conjecture D57 (the kinds of coarse unit on the detector networks) (under: two logits, one hidden layer, a finite
mix, a perfectly clean network for Gamma; CONJECTURE).** On the detector networks with T43's mixes, for a grouping
whose groups have target size 1: (i) a free group has a least unit that is a presence unit (true: Corollary T59.2);
(ii) a conflicting group whose other units are kept has a least unit that is a presence unit firing on the vertex
points of a largest clique among its members; (iii) a zero-loss build at a grouping of conflicting groups has no
presence unit, and it exists only when every unit can pay, by switching, for the conflicting segments at one of its
own members (as in Theorem T62).
Route: (ii) from Corollary T62b: a least unit must pay for as many conflicting segments as it can without firing at a
silent midpoint, and the vertex points it covers then form a clique (T59.1); (iii) from the cycle argument of T62
applied to the graph of conflicting segments; the exploration of Remark B.W.4 is the first check (the same-block
pairing is the case where (iii)'s condition should fail).

**Conjecture D61 (for free families, the covering bound is reached) (under: two logits, one hidden layer, a finite
mix, a perfectly clean network for Gamma, H-freefam; CONJECTURE).** Let N be perfectly clean with families that are
free on P (Hypothesis H-freefam), and let G be a grouping of its families. Then the least total size of an exact (b)
build at G equals tau_b of N's strict dip lines (Theorem T65), and an exact build of that size is made of presence
units.
Route: T59.2 is the free-group case on the detector networks (clique groups, which are free but are not families
there): one presence unit per group, which is tau_b.
The comment after T65 shows that without freeness the bound is not reached (tau = 1, no exact width-1 build). Next:
families on rings (`model/to_ring.py`) with dense members, where blends of neighbours fire a member; then the
question for coarse circuits over several layers (Definition D60), where Proposition T66 shows that depth can beat
the one-layer count in general.

## D.14 Conjectures CM1 (false), CM2, CM3: the graded split, a claim inside a group, deeper layers (Trunk T5)

Conjecture CM1 (the graded split; FALSE as first stated, REFEREE-MAP-2026-10-28.md finding 6). It said that, under
TM1's premises with errors eps_dist, eps_shel and eps_judg, |V_b(G) - sum over S of L_S| is at most a function of these
errors that is 0 when they are all 0. Counterexample (one hidden layer, P = {a, b, c} in the plane in general position,
so every affine value table on P is realised; errors of A.7 normalised per unit): units s (region {a}), j1 (region {a}, h = 1 at a, 0 elsewhere), t1 (region
{b, c}, on only at b), j2 (region {b, c}, h = 1 at b and c); z_s = (1, -1, -1 + delta) at (a, b, c). Groups S = {s} at
size 1 and T = {t1} at size 0; j1 and j2 kept. Then eps_dist = eps_judg = 0 and eps_shel = 2 p_b p_c delta^2 / B_s with B_s the variance of z_s over P (positive, and bounded away from 0 as
delta -> 0). L_S = 0,
and L_T > 0 when N's class probabilities differ at b and c. The box unit relu((z_s + 1) / delta) is 0 at b and 1 at c;
with logit weight y_N(c) - y_N(b), and j1, j2 and the bias correcting a and b, the joint build is exact, so V_b = 0 for
every delta in (0, 1), while sum L_S = L_T stays fixed as the errors go to 0. The new unit takes the value 2/delta at a, and its weight
1/delta grows without bound as delta -> 0.

Conjecture CM1' (withdrawn 2026-10-28, REFEREE-MAP-2026-10-28.md round 2, findings 8 to 10). It added a weight bound
W. A variant of the counterexample needs no box (a kept unit j1 that is on at b with value delta, re-weighted by
1/delta), so a bound on boxes alone fails; a bound on every logit column fails at error 0 once N's own columns exceed W;
and with fixed N, P and M a function F(eps, W, N) that tends to 0 with eps says nothing beyond eps = 0. What the example
does prove is Proposition TM4. (2026-10-28, later: for the robust optimum of Definition DE2, node R-wellposed, a graded form exists, Theorem TE4,
as a side branch; its bound carries the swings of the clean assembly, and Proposition TE5 shows the errors DM2 to DM4 and
DM8 alone do not bound it.)

**Conjecture CM2 (a blend claim makes a group's least build fast to compute) (under: one hidden layer; two logits;
class (b) builds).** There is a claim type "no silent blend" for a group's districts, with an error computable in
polynomial time, such that (i) for a group S at any target size k_S whose districts have this claim at error 0, a least
build at the grouping {S} can be computed in time polynomial in the bit length of (N, P, k_S), and (ii) the claim is
not trivial: it has error 0 for every group without a bad pair on T43's instances (as DM7 does, Theorem TM5) and for
every AND group with non-negative gap weights (Definition D51, Proposition T59 part 3). With card 3-19 option (a), such claims would be among the
claim types that a map must hold for each group before the exact clause applies.
Route. On the instances of T43 the case k_S = 1 is already in Part B.W: a "blend" of two members u, v is the midpoint of
their vertex points, the mix holds exactly the midpoints of bad pairs, and a group whose members' midpoints are not in
P has no bad pair, so Corollary T59.2 gives the exact presence unit, while a bad pair blocks every exact build (Corollary
T59.1). The general claim must say "blend" without the coloured graph. Proposition T59 part 2 gives the form: a point x_0
of P whose pre-activation vector z_S(x_0) is a convex combination of the vectors z_S(x_k) of points where the group's
output t is larger than t(x_0). Its error can be the weight of such points (membership in a convex hull of finitely many
vectors is a linear program, so this is polynomial). On every instance of T43 the one big group has positive error
(two detectors of one block form a bad pair, their midpoint is in P, z_S is affine in x so the midpoint's vector is the
average of the two vertex points' vectors, and N's output there is 0 < 2), so on these instances the claim keeps the
exact clause from applying to the big group (Corollary TM5.1). With DM7 itself as the claim type, CM2 for general
networks would give a fast exact rule on any family of inputs whose groups have blend error 0, so it must be checked
against hard families other than T43's. Open: the closed form for k_S >= 2, and how a
group made of several districts gets its build from its districts' claims.
Lean: none, conjecture.

**Conjecture CM3 (the split in deeper layers) (under: class (b) builds).** First define class (b) builds and a group's
least loss on its regions for groups below the last hidden layer (node R-deep, pending: what "reads only its group"
means there). Then: let the groups of a grouping lie in hidden layers below the last, each group with its own regions, and suppose that no hidden unit descends (along N's edges) from
two groups (a block-sparse premise: in a dense network every later unit descends from every group, so it holds only
when the layers above split into separate blocks). If every group's districts have exact district and shelter claims, every unit that descends from a group is
off outside that group's regions, and every region has an exact judgment claim whose units are kept and do not descend
from any group, then the least loss is the sum of the groups' least losses on their own regions, with readers in
layers above each group re-fitting their biases and weights (nodes R-readbias, R-readweights).
Route: Proposition TU16 of `UNIT-BRANCH.md` (if no hidden unit descends from two sets, the joint build's logits are N's
plus the two single changes). Shelter makes each box constant outside its regions, as in TM1; the premise on
descendants makes each group's change at the logits vanish outside its regions; then TM1's lower bound and judgment
construction apply at the logits. The step to check is that re-fitting readers in the middle layers cannot carry one
group's change into another group's region (TA12's mechanism one layer up).
Lean: none, conjecture.

## D.15 Conjecture DV3: the signed carrying with norms (Part B.V.3; proved: Theorem TV15)

PROVED (2026-10-29, round 3): Theorem TV15 and Corollary TV15.3 (Part B.V.4) prove the statement below, and more: for
both forms of Definition DV1 and every Lipschitz activation, with the second order of the remainder for smooth sigma
(Corollary TV15.3 part 2). The route below worked as written, with step (i) in its premise-free form
(Lemma TV15.2 part 3). The statement as it was:
Conjecture DV3 (Proposition TV14 in the norm form; under: pure-stream networks; area cuts; sigma with a Lipschitz
derivative). In the norm form, with every eps'_l > 0, the logit change of a re-fit area cut that drops D
equals a signed sum Lambda_N computed from N, P, D and the cut's reads, in which each block's term and the logits'
term also carry the derivative of the norm n'_l at Pi h_(l-1)(x), up to a remainder rem(x) bounded point by point by
quantities from the same data and of second order in the leaks of Definition DM14.
Route (an outline of a proof; what is missing is writing it out): n'(a) = a / (|a|^2 + eps')^(1/2) is smooth for
eps' > 0, with derivative (I - n' n'^T) / nu'(a) and a second derivative bounded by a constant times 1 / nu'(a)^2.
(i) Along the segment from Pi h to ht, nu' can fall below rho_l: use nu'(z) >= max(eps'^(1/2), nu'(Pi h) - |delta|),
or a premise |delta| <= eta rho_l as in Proposition TV8, which gives the factor 1 / ((1 - eta) rho_l)^2. (ii) The
first-order term of each norm, the logits' norm n'_(L+1) included, joins the recursion of Proposition TV14 as one more
slope. (iii) The Taylor remainders join gamma_l. Whether the resulting remainder is small on trained networks is a
measurement, for Part C.

## D.16 Conjecture TH4: summaries passed up the tree (Part B.H)

**Conjecture TH4 (summaries passed up the tree) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups,
branch claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0; CONJECTURE).** For D2_P and a zoom of tree groupings whose steps are
sibling merges (creations included), there is for each node w a summary s_w, a list of rationals of bit length
polynomial in the bit length of (N, P), computable in polynomial time from N, P, M and the zoom when a polynomial
oracle for the least loss of one node's problem is given, such that L2_S of every group S at every level is a
function of the summaries of the w in W_S that is computable in polynomial time for each fixed k_S. In particular the
least build of every level is computed by one pass up the tree, each node reading only its children's summaries,
with no return to N's units.
Why the oracle: without it the statement asks too much, since one node with area P and k_S = 1 is already the problem
of Proposition T57, whose D2 version is NP-hard to approximate within the gap of T22; with summaries of unbounded
size it says too little, since a summary could store L2 for every k. The content is the merge map: whether a
parent's least loss is a fast function of its children's.
Route. (1) The case in which a least box of each group has units that are on at every point of its areas: there a
box acts on each area as a linear map of z_T, the least loss is the residual of the sum of the children's matrices
Sigma_w (the second moments of the part of P_perp y_N that is linear in z_T on w's area, as in the proof of
Proposition TH3) after its k_S largest eigenvalues (Eckart and Young), and s_w = (Sigma_w, the residual of w's area) is
a summary with no oracle needed. Before a proof this case needs a claim type for "on at every point of its area",
with a node (Rule 7). (Corollary TP1.1 proves this route with the premise on least boxes and no claim type; the
claim-type form is the linear-read claim of DP1, Theorem TP1, node R-linread.) (2) In the case of (1) with two logits, every Sigma_w has rank at most 1 on the one direction of
P_perp, so the sum has rank at most 1 and a sibling merge of size 1 has L2_(S') = sum of its children's L2. (Outside
the case of (1) this fails: two children whose units switch inside their areas, with gap weights of opposite signs,
need different kinks that one unit with one output weight cannot give.) (3) Boxes that switch inside an area:
Proposition TH3 shows the least unit of a child is not a summary; the candidate is the set of least boxes of the
child for every output direction (a curve, not a point). Check TH3's instance and `model/th_break.py` first.
Status (2026-10-29): Route (1) is proved as stated, for D2_P, as Corollary TP1.1 (Part B.P): among boxes on at every
point of their areas the least is Lin_S, the eigen-residual, for any linear-read error. Theorem TP1 adds a sandwich
(1/2) tail <= L2_S <= Lin_S that needs no premise on least boxes, exact when the linear-read claims of Definition DP1
hold. Route (2) under Route (1)'s premise is Corollary TP2.1. TP2 carries the recursion for sibling merges only; at a
lift the summary is computed again from N. Route (3), boxes that switch inside an area (large linear-read error), is
open, and there the one-node problem keeps the hardness of T57. Lifts (2026-10-29, later): at every node at or
below a node that meets the premises of Theorem TL3 (district, shelter, on-inside and judgment claims at eps = 0),
the linear-read error is 0 (Corollary TL3.1); Proposition TL4 carries the tables through lifts with one between
table, given the tables and means of the nodes of layer L, the nodes' masses and c_N; Corollary TL5 gives the least
of every such grouping in closed form. The box weights of a lifted group still read the build records of its nodes,
made from N in the one-time pass. With errors, Theorem TL6 bounds each node's linear-read error by absolute defects,
N's weight norms and the gates' margins; it bounds the gap to the least only where TP1 applies (Comment of TL6).
Lean: none, conjecture.

## D.17 Conjecture DI1: the open case of the KL least is hard (Part B.I)

**Conjecture DI1 (the KL least of a clean group with 0 < k < rank is hard; proved: Theorem TQ23 part 1) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a
tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0;
CONJECTURE).** Let TRUNK-KL be the problem: given N with rational weights, a finite mix P, a tree map M, a group S
with k_S = 1 whose nodes meet the premises of Theorem TI4 (every claim at eps = 0, linear-read claims included), and a
rational eps > 0, return a value within eps of L_S. Then a polynomial-time algorithm for TRUNK-KL, with n_y part of
the input, gives P = NP.
Why it matters: if true, the trunk's exactness clause cannot be met by a fast rule for KL at 0 < k_S < rank
Sigma_(W_S), even for groups whose every claim holds, unlike D2, where TP1 gives a closed form there. That is a
conflict of the TM3 kind, and it would go to Shonu as a card.
Route. (1) By Theorem TI4 part 1 the least is a^2 Phi + O(a^3), with Phi = (1/2) min over lines Q of
sum over w of psi_w(Q): a rank-one problem with a different metric H_w on each area. Show that this many-metric
rank-one problem is NP-hard, by reduction from weighted rank-one approximation (Gillis and Glineur 2011, literature
table): an area per column, its metric carrying that column's weights. (2) Realise the metrics: H_w must be the
Fisher matrix diag(sigma_w) - sigma_w sigma_w^T of a mean softmax, an (n_y - 1)-parameter family, smaller than all
positive definite matrices. This is the gap of the route: either the reduction uses only Fisher matrices (diagonal
weights in a basis of class contrasts), or it needs a different source problem. (3) Realise the tables Sigma_w and
the areas by a network with one hidden layer of gates and one judgment unit per area, every claim at eps = 0.
(4) Choose a with bit length polynomial in the input, small enough that the O(a^3) term of TI4 (with explicit
constants from its proof) is below the gap of the reduction.
Status (2026-11-02): PROVED as Theorem TQ23 part 1, with Lemma TQ23.a in place of the Route, whose gap (2) is closed by a shared class and an own class in each area; the statement is at the confident, small-movement networks of Definition DQ18. Take the conjecture's eps below Gamma / 32. Earlier status (2026-10-31): conjecture. TI5 part 2 shows the many-metric problem already has optimal directions that are not
D2's when the metric is not uniform; it does not show hardness.
Lean: none, as for Theorem TQ23.

**Conjecture DI2 (for KL a least box may switch inside its area) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map,
subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, every claim it uses has eps = 0; CONJECTURE).**
There is a group S meeting the premises of Theorem TI4 (every claim at eps = 0, linear-read claims included) with
L_S < L_S^on: some box whose units switch inside S's areas has KL terms below every box whose units are on throughout.
Candidate: N_a of Proposition TI5 part 2 with a = 1, k_S = 1 (`model/ti_open.py`, part D, finds such a box with a
local optimiser).
Route. (1) Certify the instance: give the switching box with rational weights and evaluate its terms with interval
arithmetic (an upper bound on L_S). (2) Bound L_S^on from below: for each line Q in the plane, a dual point of the
convex problem f_w(Q) of TI3 part 2 gives a lower bound; f_w is Lipschitz in the angle of Q (with a constant from the
data), so finitely many angles cover the circle. (3) Compare. Then the always-on form of TP1.1 and TL5 is a property of
D2_P, and a KL rule for 0 < k_S < rank Sigma must choose where its units switch, which is the problem of Proposition T57.
Status (2026-10-31): conjecture with a computed candidate.
Lean: none, conjecture.

## D.18 Conjecture DQ1: the packing bound is first-order tight for comparable confidence (Part B.Q)

**Conjecture DQ1 (the packing bound is first-order tight for comparable confidence) (under: plain feed-forward
networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, active-class summaries,
squeeze-complete groups, every claim it uses has eps = 0; CONJECTURE).** Let N_m be the network of Proposition TQ2
part 3 (two nodes, disjoint K_1, K_2, own-class ranks 1 = k_S), whose judgment weights m on both areas grow together,
so that both outside masses fall at the same rate e^(-m). Then L_S >= c (eps_act(A_1, K_1) + eps_act(A_2, K_2)) for
a c > 0 that does not depend on m.
Why it matters: Shonu's rule "graded is actually useful" asks for a bound that tracks the true gap. If DQ1 holds, the
packed bound is within a fixed factor of the least of row 3 for areas of comparable confidence.
Not for uneven confidence. The referee (REFEREE-BQ-2026-10-31.md, finding 9) sketches a family with the outside
logits falling by m on A_1 and by 2m on A_2 where a tilted direction (e_1 - e_2) / sqrt 2 + m^(-1/2) (e_3 - e_4) /
sqrt 2 has loss about e^(-m) / m while eps_act(A_1, K_1) stays of order e^(-m): the ratio grows like m. Unverified
here; if it holds, the packed choice must carry per-node scales: V = sum over w of lambda_w Pi^K_w U_w with c_w scaled
by 1 / lambda_w, whose envelope on A_w is (max over w' of lambda_(w') / lambda_w) rho_(K_w), minimised over lambda.
Route. (1) The chain rule of KL over a partition of the classes (proof of TQ2 part 3): on A_1,
KL(s || q) >= s(K_2) KL(s|K_2 || q|K_2), and s|K_2 is constant on A_1. (2) With one direction v, write v = v_1 + v_2
+ v_r by the blocks K_1, K_2 and the rest. The free amplitude alpha_x can fit the K_2 part of Y_2 on A_2 exactly with
alpha of size about a / |v_2|; the price is then paid by v_1 on A_2's outside classes, about
mu_2 min(1, (a / |v_2|)^2), and symmetrically by v_2 on A_1, about mu_1 |v_2|^2 Var(alpha on A_1). (3) Balancing |v_2|
gives a lower bound of order sqrt(mu_1 mu_2), which is of order mu when mu_1 and mu_2 are comparable. (4) Compare
with eps_act, which is at most 2 D_A mu (Definition DQ1, property (3)) and at least a constant times mu (rho_K >= a/2
at every point).
Status (2026-10-31): conjecture; `model/ts_tree.py` part E reports the ratio on this family (Part C).
Lean: none, conjecture.

**Conjecture DQ2 (the cost of sharing between two packed areas, to second order) (under: plain feed-forward networks,
a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, active-class summaries,
squeeze-complete groups, every claim it uses has eps = 0; CONJECTURE).** Let S have two nodes with disjoint K_1, K_2,
own-class ranks r^K_1 = r^K_2 = k_S = k, and no movement of N off its block on each area (on A_w, the logits outside
K_w vary only by one constant per point). Let a scale the movement as in TI4, sigma_w the mean softmax of N on A_w,
G_w = diag(sigma restricted to K_w) pulled back to w's box coordinates through the other area's fit, Sigma_w the
covariance of w's box coordinates, P = G_1^(1/2) Sigma_1 G_1^(1/2), Q = G_2^(1/2) Sigma_2 G_2^(1/2) (made precise in the
proof), and mu_w the outside masses. Then, with a tending to 0 first and then mu_1, mu_2 tending to 0 with mu_2 / mu_1
bounded above and below,
   L^on_S / a^2 = sqrt(mu_1 mu_2) (sqrt(p_1 q_1) + ... + sqrt(p_k q_k)) (1 + o(1)),
the value of Lemma TQ4 (with c = mu_2 / mu_1), attained by the reverse pairing.
Why it matters: it would give the cost of packing two areas, and how to line up the shared directions, in closed
form in this regime. Part C (H-active, per-area gauge) finds that this alignment is the missing piece of the packed
build on ResNet-18.
Route. (1) In the glued build of TQ3 part 2 with the own fits fixed, the freedom is an invertible k x k map T: area 1's
coordinates c_1 leak T c_1 onto block 2, area 2's leak T^(-1) c_2 onto block 1 (if V restricted to K_w is
Q_w A_w^(-1), T = A_2^(-1) A_1); and each fit's 1_(K_w) gauge, which changes lambda_w at first order and must be fixed.
(2) To second order in the leak, the cost is (a^2 / 2)(mu_1 tr(G_2 T Sigma_1 T^T) + mu_2 tr(G_1 T^(-1) Sigma_2 T^(-T)))
+ o(a^2 mu); the change of variables T = G_2^(-1/2) T' G_1^(1/2) gives Lemma TQ4's form. (3) Lemma TQ4. (4) A matching
lower bound: any box at k_S = k must reproduce each area's movement to this order, so its leak has this form; state it
as the mu -> 0 asymptotics of TI4's Phi, which is well defined for each mu.
Status (2026-10-31): conjecture; Lemma TQ4 (its step 3) is proved; first form (a "balancing" with Hankel singular
values) was wrong (REFEREE-BQ2 finding E2). If proved, label SECOND-ORDER, not OPT-KL.
Lean: none, conjecture.

Question (DQ2 beyond two areas, added 2026-11-01). In the second-order model of DQ2's Route step (2) with three or
more areas, is the least over all invertible maps always reached by a pairing of directions with scales? Part C
(H-active, `model/tq_ngauge.py`) reports instances where it is not; a proof would need an explicit instance with a
certified gap.

**Conjecture DQ4 (the leak least is hard in the number of areas) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map,
subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, active-class summaries, squeeze-complete groups,
every claim it uses has eps = 0; CONJECTURE).** Let LEAK be the promise problem: the input is a group S meeting the
premises of Theorem TQ5 with |K_w| >= 2 and own-class rank 1 on every area, no movement of N off its block (on A_w the
logits outside K_w vary only by one constant per point), k_S = 3, all data rational and written in binary, and a
rational e > 0 in binary; the output is a rational within e of Lambda_S. Then a polynomial-time algorithm for LEAK,
with the number of areas part of the input, gives P = NP.
Why it matters: Theorem TQ5 makes Lambda_S the leading term of a confident squeeze over always-on boxes. If DQ4 holds,
no fast rule computes that leading term for groups that share k units among many areas, even when every claim holds.
It would NOT yet show that the least L_S itself is hard: TQ5 gives no rate, and switching boxes are outside it
(Conjecture DI2). Whether groups with few areas make the leak problem easy is open.
Route. (1) Small movement: scale every Y_w by a, as in Theorem TI4; Lambda_S(a) = a^2 Lambda2 + O(a^3), where Lambda2
is the least of the quadratic form of Lambda (phi(t) = t^2/2 + O(t^3)). (2) Reduce Lambda2 to a weighted least over
n x n matrices X of rank at most k_S with unit diagonal of sum over w != w' of c_(w'w) X_(w'w)^2 (the Comment of
Lemma TQ6). (3) Reduce from min-rank (Peeters 1996, literature table): weight 1 on the pairs that must be 0 and a
small weight on the others. (4) Choose a small enough that the O(a^3) term of step (1) stays below the gap of step
(3). Gaps of the route, all open: (i) step (2) is not derived: the spills are vectors on each block, the own
directions must be centred on their blocks, and the reduction is exact only with equal odds inside each block,
otherwise two weighted problems bound Lambda2 from both sides (REFEREE-BQ3 finding G5); (ii) the lower side of step
(3): a quantitative separation (how large the least is when min-rank > 3) with polynomially many bits, which real
algebraic geometry gives only with bounds exponential in n; (iii) the upper side of step (3): the sizes of the entries
of a min-rank witness, which the small weights multiply; (iv) an explicit constant in the O(a^3) term of step (1);
(v) Peeters' convention (zeros at the non-edges, any field) must be matched to the pattern used here. For equal
weights there is no hardness: under the reduction of step (2), Lemma TQ6 gives the least in closed form.
Status (2026-11-01): conjecture. Lean: none, conjecture.

Question DQ6 (why the shared span works when the areas' metrics differ; added 2026-11-01). Proposition TQ7 says the
closed-form shared span is near the least, to second order, when the areas' Fisher metrics are close (eta small).
When each area is confident in its own block, eta is near 1 and TQ7 says nothing, while Part C (H-active, the shared
span) finds the closed-form span of the whole group's movement far better than the packed span on a trained network.
What is the property of N that makes the top shared directions of the group's movement (the top eigenvectors of
Sigma_(W_S) in the plain metric, as measured in Part C) near-optimal for the always-on KL least there?
A candidate, not yet defined as a claim (its error, computed from N alone, is still to be fixed): on each area, the part of the movement that
the area's own metric weighs (its own block) lies close to the span of the group's top shared directions; that is,
the areas' own movements are built from common patterns (the essay's reuse), not independent of each other. Route:
(1) by TI3 part 2, at a fixed span the always-on least is a sum of convex fits, so the question is only about the span; (2) in
the confident limit of TQ5, the spills enter with weight e^-m and the own blocks must be met exactly, so the
candidate claim, at error 0, would make the shared span the span of a leak point (Definition DQ5); its value is the
odds-weighted mismatch between that point's spills and N's own off-block movement, and by TQ5 part 2 it bounds the
always-on least at every m; what is missing is a matching lower bound; (3) a graded bound in the claim's error.

**Conjecture DQ8 (pinning of near-least builds, with constants from N; the small-tilt route) (under: plain
feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups, branch claims, on-inside claims, linear-read claims, every claim it
uses has eps = 0; CONJECTURE) (added 2026-11-02; restated after REFEREE-BQ5 finding E6).** In the notation of TQ10, let
   Psi = min over (Delta, M_w, beta_w) of sum over w and x in A_w of p_x KL(s_x || softmax(ybar_w + beta_w + Q0 (A_w + M_w) ztil_w(x) + Delta A_w ztil_w(x))),
the true KL of the family in which the shared span is tilted LINEARLY by Delta. Psi is the least of a convex problem
(logits affine in the unknowns, KL convex in the logits) and is attained, so it is computed exactly, with a dual
certificate, at any size. What is already proved by the Lipschitz step of TQ9 part 2 (|KL(s || softmax(l + e)) -
KL(s || softmax(l))| <= 2 |e|_inf): the build from a minimiser (Delta*, M*) of Psi, with the cross term restored, has
terms at most Psi + 2 sum p_x |Delta* M*_w ztil_w(x)|_inf; and every always-on build whose span is range(Q0 + Delta)
with code change m_x has terms at least Psi - 2 sum p_x |Delta m_x|_inf. (The two sides use different tilts: Psi's
minimiser on the upper side, the build's own on the lower side; with sines up to s, |Delta| <= tan(arcsin s).)
Conjecture: there are numbers theta(N) and mu(N), computed from N alone in polynomial time, such that every always-on
build within a constant factor of the least has its span within sine theta(N) of the shared span and its code change at
most mu(N). Then Psi sandwiches L^on_S within 2 tan(arcsin theta(N)) mu(N) (times a feature constant), in quantities of
N, which is the form the bar asks for.
Why it matters: when the dropped part is large in the quadratic sense but cheap in KL, the quadratic of TQ10 is the
wrong object, while Psi keeps the exact KL (Part C, H-active, measures both).
Route. (1) and (2) are proved above. (3) The pinning with explicit constants: TQ10 (3)(b) pins through pointwise
closeness, whose constants carry 1/s_min and 1/p_min; a weighted form (pinning in the norm of the head classes, the
chain rule over classes, Wedin's bound) is the route; the obstacle is that, in a block-confident network, the head
classes of each area are its own block, and there the packing freedom of TQ1 to TQ5 means no pinning holds.
Lean: none, conjecture.

**Conjecture DQ11 (the symmetric table with K = 2k: the pole build is the least) (under: none; CONJECTURE) (added 2026-11-01; first form false, see below; PROVED 2026-11-01 as Theorem TQ17 part 4, and kept here as the record).** In the setting of Proposition TQ16, L_table(k) equals the value of the pole build, with t = 0 mod constants. So in this case row 3 of ROADMAP.md, on a network that meets the premise of Theorem TQ14 part 6, has a closed form at a loss above 0.
First form, false. It claimed that an equiangular tight frame with codes tau times its own vectors is the least, when such a frame exists. Part C, TQ14: lower values from every random start on (K, k) = (6, 3) and (10, 5). (For K = 2k a real equiangular frame exists only when a symmetric conference matrix of order 2k does, so that form said nothing at k = 2 or k = 4.)
Route. (1) A certified optimum on the smallest case, K = 4, k = 2, where the span has two free angles (`model/tq15_cert.py`, Lemma TQ15). (2) Near the uniform table: at K = 4, k = 2, with r small, all spans tie at second order, and the third-order term (a fourth moment of the normal vector of the span, minus a square of its third moment) appears to pick out the pole span uniquely; to be re-derived before it enters the paper. (3) The limit b -> 0: a linear program for the coefficient of b log(1/b). (4) For every span V, the dual of Lemma TQ15 part 4 with the symmetric table. (5) When k is below K/2 the pole build does not fit, and the vertices of the codes form some other polytope in R^k: a discrete choice, left to the one-time computation (node R-mixclean, within modest hardware).
Lean: none, conjecture.

**Conjecture DQ15 (when families are confident, the squeeze's cost beyond its minors is a leak) (under: none; CONJECTURE) (added 2026-11-01; earlier forms, with the tail lumped, withdrawn: one was false and one's route failed; a later form was empty, REFEREE-BQ10).** Let a partition of the classes into families F_1, ..., F_J give minors with all rows. Take a family of tables along which each row's mass outside one family is e^(-m) times a fixed vector, with the conditional table inside that family fixed. Let L^(b) be the minors' leasts, and Lambda_S the leak least of Definition DQ5. Then L_Z(k) - the sum over b of L^(b)_Z(k) = e^(-m) Lambda_S + o(e^(-m)) as m grows, where Lambda_S is taken over the spans at which every minor reaches its least.
Why it matters: it would split a squeeze into family problems and one object that holds all the sharing of units between families. Part C finds that this sharing holds most of the loss at fine scale, on real tables.
Route: (1) Theorem TQ5 is the case where every minor's least is 0. Its proof splits the KL into each row's own block and its spill, at every confidence. (2) Theorem TQ3 gives the limit of the sum. (3) The lower side needs the spans pinned near the minors' minimisers, which holds if each minor has a unique minimising span (Theorem TQ18 part 2 may give that). (4) Real tables are not confident in one family, so a form at the network's own confidence is the real target; measure the share of the loss in the minors first (Part C). (5) A lower bound on the leak must read tail order: on a table near the identity, every top class can be placed at rank 2, classes on a circle, so top-class information alone cannot see the rank. One tool, with gaps: by Radon's theorem, any k + 3 classes have disjoint subsets A and B with positive weights such that the weighted sums of l' over A and B agree on every row, for a given competitor. So a row that ranks A above B misorders a pair. But (A, B) depends on the competitor, and the payment scales with the pair's mass.
Lean: none, conjecture.

**Conjecture DQ3 (the recursion of TQ3 down the tree) (under: plain feed-forward networks, a tree map, subtree groups,
branch claims, on-inside claims, active-class summaries, every claim it uses has eps = 0; CONJECTURE).** Let w be a
node whose children split A_w into sub-areas that favour pairwise disjoint sub-blocks of K_w. Then, along a family
where the sub-areas become confident in their sub-blocks (as in TQ3 part 3), the own-block least of w tends to the
sum of the children's own-block leasts.
Route. The lower side is TQ3 part 1 applied to the sub-areas. The upper side needs a box of w, one affine map of
z_(T_w) on all of A_w, to act as different maps on the sub-areas: a premise that the centred spans of z_(T_w) on the
sub-areas are linearly independent would allow it, or a KL form of the lift of Theorem TL2.
Status (2026-10-31): conjecture (the Remark of TQ3, demoted after REFEREE-BQ2 finding E3).
Lean: none, conjecture.

## D.19 Conjecture DQ17: at one unit, a least order respects a tree (Part B.Q.11; revised after REFEREE-BQ11-2026-11-02.md)

**Conjecture DQ17 (at one unit, a least order respects the tree) (under: tree weight claims; CONJECTURE) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ11).** Let the wall program V(n, 1) of Theorem TZ17 have n_ci = exp(f_(lca(c, i))) for c != i on the leaves of a rooted binary tree, with f at a node at most f at each of its descendants. Then the least over orders of the classes is attained at an order in which the leaves of every subtree are consecutive.
Why it matters: it would be the first statement that a tree on the classes cuts the search over orders, from K! to 2^(K-1). Whether a recursion over the tree then follows is open, since a cross pair reads the gaps inside each block. It is a limit in the confident regime, at k = 1, with T empty, so it is far from a real network.
Route: (1) K = 3 is proved: by Theorem TZ17 part (b) the cost of middle class b is 6 n_ac, so the least takes as ends a pair with the smallest n, and that pair holds the leaf that joins last. For larger K, n is symmetric, the objective is the sum of n_ci (2 S T - 2), with S and T the sums of u and of 1/u on the span from c to i, and an exchange argument on two adjacent blocks is the step to try. (2) With row and column scales the statement is false at K = 3: take the tree ((1, 2), 3), f = 0 at the root and one tenth below it, u = v = (1, 1, 10), n_ci = u_c v_i exp(f). By part (b), middle class 3 costs 6 exp(1/10) and middle class 1 or 2 costs 60, so the unique least order puts 3 between 1 and 2. Real tables have scales, so the statement that replaces this one is the real target. (3) Theorem TZ15 gives the rate on the value. A statement about the order at finite m also needs the value gap between orders to exceed that error, and no such gap is proved.
What this conjecture does not say, said plainly. It claims no polynomial algorithm and no exact promise. No tractability is conjectured at k >= 2. Level tables have a tree weight claim at error 0 for every tree, at every k. Restricted to V proportional to C, their limit asks for K points at pairwise distance at least 1 in R^k with the least total squared distance, a packing problem whose answers the paper knows only at a few sizes. That gives an upper bound on the limit, and whether the restriction loses anything is open for k >= 2. Also, by Proposition TQ25, no many-one NP-hardness can reach level tables with their numbers fixed, unless P = NP, so the absence of hardness there is no evidence of tractability.
Lean: none, conjecture.

**Proposition TQ25 (a threshold on a function of two sizes cannot be NP-hard) (under: none) (added 2026-11-02, from REFEREE-BQ11-2026-11-02.md).** Let v be any real function of (K, k), and A the set of (K, k, theta) with K and k written in unary, theta rational, and v(K, k) <= theta. If SAT reduces to A by a polynomial-time many-one reduction, then P = NP.
Proof. Search SAT's self-reduction tree level by level. Drop any node whose image is not of the form (K, k, theta). For each pair (K, k), keep only the node whose image has the largest theta. Each image has polynomial size and K, k are in unary, so at most polynomially many nodes stay at each level. If some node of a level is satisfiable, its image lies in A, so the kept node with the same pair has an image in A, and that node is satisfiable. So a satisfiable formula keeps a satisfiable node at every level. At the last level, evaluate. QED.
Lean: none, since this is a statement about all reductions and the project has no complexity theory in Lean.

## D.20 Conjecture DQ21: no fast rule within a fixed factor (Part B.Q.12; card 3-37)

**Conjecture DQ21 (every fixed factor is NP-hard, with no conjecture) (under: groups in the last hidden layer; class (b) builds; CONJECTURE) (added 2026-11-02; revised after REFEREE-BQ12).** For every F > 1 there is a k and a family of networks N(M, W; a, B) of Definition DQ18, with every claim of M_N at error 0, on which deciding V_b(k) <= theta against V_b(k) > F theta is NP-hard.
Why it matters: Proposition TQ30 proves this for F below about 1.36, and Proposition TQ31 proves it for every F under the Unique Games Conjecture. A proof with no conjecture would remove the condition. A claim with a polynomial-time closed form must exclude these families, within the factor proved. Card 3-37's line P2 sets no time limit, so that does not exclude every passing claim.
Route: three routes are open.
(1) At k = 1 with signed M, this asks for NP-hardness of least-uncut at every factor, a known open problem close to the Unique Games Conjecture. So this route is likely as hard as that. Sharpening TQ31's sandwich constant does not help with Hastad's gap, since a uniform charge cannot pass 2.89 on a triangle, and 3.2 is needed.
(2) k >= 2. At M = I and k = 2, an exact fit needs Q bipartite, so the limit form is odd cycle transversal. A robust form is not proved.
(3) The coloring pipeline. Source: Huang 2013, section 3: a conflict system with R = K, C K^3-colorable in the YES case, every independent set of weight at most 2^(-Omega(K)) in the NO case, with K large. Lemma TQ27 gives pair mass at least about 1 / (K^2 f) for every f-coloring, for f below 2^(Omega(K)). Rows and columns: the directed edges, exposed entries the diagonal and the adjacent pairs, weighted by the two-step path distribution. YES: the Gram matrix of an r-coloring of the line digraph, with b(r) >= C K^3. NO: a build of loss D has few bad exposed entries by mass, at most about 76 D / (Gamma M_e epsilon^2), with M_e the exposed mass. Choosing the sets E'_v of Chawin and Haviv's Theorem 3.8 from rows with few bad entries gives a coloring in which the pair mass with one color is at most gamma_0 + 2 (kappa m)^(1/2), with gamma_0 the mass of rows that fail a norm limit theta, kappa the mass of bad entries, m = m(2k, eps'), and f about theta^(4 k m). This step is a sketch and it needs its own Lemma, with G symmetrised and the diagonal normalised.
The limit of route 3. A second moment bound gives gamma_0 about theta^(-2): an L2 orthonormal basis or a balanced SVD gives the expected squared row norm in terms of the hole mean square. The first moment form, from Auerbach's lemma in l_1, gives only theta^(-1). The NO case needs gamma_0 below about 1 / (K^2 f), which fails for every theta >= 1, since 4 k m > 2. This is a limit of the Markov bound in this route: no build with such a tail is shown. A positive semidefinite fit has no such limit, since its rows have norm 1. What is missing in plain terms: is the chromatic number of G bounded by a function of the real minrank of its line digraph, with no norm limit?
What this conjecture does not say. Its tables are tables of graphs. By card 3-37 item I5, they are not shown to be clean in the essay's sense. So this conjecture, when proved, gives I1 and I2 with no condition. It does not by itself close row 3 as impossible. The trunk's closed form has no time limit, so it does not contradict the trunk.
Lean: none, conjecture.

**Referee report 17 and the fixes (Part B.O, D.10, H-dialfit).** Report and fix table: `REFEREE-BO-2026-10-25.md`.
Main findings: Remark B.O.2's reading ("the build is the best fit on each region, the average where no unit fires") is
false for two or more units unless the regions are nested or disjoint, so it is now stated at width 1; Theorem T38 is
a backfitting fixed point (each unit fits what the others leave) and is now proved with one-sided derivatives, without
the Clarke calculus; Corollary T38.2 holds among builds with output sign +1 only; D29 and D30 are numerically
contradicted, not refuted; H-dialfit now names its distance eps_dial and the slope-1 prediction, and states the two
premises of T38.2 that the crush does not meet.

**Numerical record for D34 (2026-10-26; `model/tg_gate_instance.py`, `model/tg_gate_instance.json`; numerical, not
part of any proof).** Predictions written before the run: D34 predicted equality on I1 and I2, each with off-gate
weight w_0 in {1/13 or 1/10 (uniform), 1/2}, for D2 and for KL. My own expectation was that I2 might fail. Result: on
all eight (instance, weight, objective) cases the least gate fold equalled the formula value L_G of Lemma T39, and the
global least width-1 build found by the exact enumeration with a numerical solver on each piece was below it, with a
firing set other than G. The least builds found break the rotation symmetry. Relative gaps between the least gate fold
and the least build found: between 1/8 and 3/7 of the least value found. On I1 with the uniform mix the build found is B* of
Theorem T40.

**Numerical record for Theorem T42 and Remark B.S.1 (2026-10-26; `model/ts_transfer.py`, `model/ts_transfer.json`;
numerical, not part of any proof).** Predictions written before the run: T42 parts 1 and 2 hold in every trial, with
the part-2 excess at most twice the distance; on I1 at least two optimal pieces, one rotation orbit. Result: 80 trials
(T20's bathtub and I1, 40 random perturbations each, D2, width 1): both parts held in every trial; the largest part-2
excess was about two thirds of the distance (the bound allows 2). On I1 the least value found equals 5/182 (the value
of B* in Theorem T40, so B* is least to solver accuracy; not proved). 56 closed pieces R(s, A) reach it, but they give
exactly two output vectors: B* and its turn by 90 degrees. The many pieces come from the closed cones (a point where
the unit's pre-activation is 0 counts in A or out of it with the same output). So in output space the optimum is one
orbit of two points, while in pattern space it is spread over many patterns.
